paras.en: After all, Elsa had magical abilities that no one in the kingdom had ever seen before.
paras.zh: 毕竟，艾莎拥有的魔力，王国里无人曾见。

paras.en: Or at least, no one alive had ever seen.
paras.zh: 至少，在世之人从未见过。

paras.en: In some of the old stories that were favorites of Queen Iduna’s, magic abounded.
paras.zh: 在伊杜娜王后钟爱的某些古老故事里，魔法比比皆是。

paras.en: She’d told tales about tablecloths that could produce banquet-sized feasts in the blink of an eye, and boots that could travel seven leagues in a single step—of shape-shifters who lived in an enchanted forest, and stones that could turn lead into gold…but those were made up.
paras.zh: 她讲过这样的故事：桌布能眨眼间变出一桌宴席，靴子一步能行七里格——还有住在魔法森林里的变形者，能把铅变金的石头……可那些都是编的。

paras.en: Make believe.
paras.zh: 是假想。

paras.en: Pretend.
paras.zh: 是假装。

paras.en: However, in the last three years, Anna had seen incredible things, impossible things, come to be.
paras.zh: 然而，过去三年里，安娜见过不可思议、不可能之事成真。

paras.en: A sister who could be one with the earth and sky and build ice palaces with a few breaths and some nimble flicks of her wrist.
paras.zh: 一个能与天地合一、几口呼气加几次灵巧的手腕翻转便筑起冰宫的姐姐。

paras.en: A queen who could harness the cold.
paras.zh: 一位能驾驭严寒的女王。

paras.en: If Elsa could exist, as Anna very much knew she did, then why couldn’t other impossibilities exist as well?
paras.zh: 既然艾莎存在——安娜再清楚不过——那为何其他不可能之事不能也存在？

paras.en: Why couldn’t there be a spell of sorts, or an enchantment, that could fix whatever was happening with the Blight?
paras.zh: 为何不能有某种咒语或魔魅，治愈枯萎病所发生的一切？

paras.en: Sure, Anna was hoping to find something in this room to help with the problem at hand, but after that, who knew?
paras.zh: 当然，安娜盼着在这房间找到应对眼前之困的东西，可那之后，谁知道呢？

paras.en: Maybe there was knowledge somewhere in there that could stop horseshoes from ever rusting, bread from ever going stale, or candles from ever melting down to stubs and going out.
paras.zh: 也许其中某处藏着知识，能让马掌永不生锈、面包永不发霉、蜡烛永不烧成残根熄灭。

paras.en: She’d be a hero. “Aha.” Anna pulled a thick volume from a shelf and plopped it down onto a bare worktable in the center of the room alongside the candle. “This one might have something helpful.” She tapped at the title and read it out loud to Olaf. “‘The Alchemist’s Almanac: A Guide to the Care and Keeping of Fields, Accurate Accounting of the Weather, and Wheat.’” Olaf looked down his pair of ice spectacles at Anna. “Not exactly my genre.” Anna smiled. “Ooh, this one seems cryptic and dense!” Olaf said, tugging out another thick book. “Here!
paras.zh: 她就成了英雄。“啊哈。”安娜从架上抽下一册厚书，啪地放到房间中央一张光桌面上，挨着蜡烛。“这本或许有用。”她敲着书名念给雪宝听。“《炼金术士年鉴：田地养护、天气精算与小麦指南》。”雪宝从冰眼镜上方俯视安娜。“不太合我口味。”安娜笑了。“噢，这本好像隐晦又深奥！”雪宝抽出另一本厚书说。“给！

paras.en: You might like it, too!” He held it up for Anna to see.
paras.zh: 你或许也会喜欢！”他举起来给安娜看。

paras.en: Its cover was a beautiful brown with black lettering.
paras.zh: 封面是美丽的棕色，配黑字。

paras.en: The title wasn’t written in an alphabet Anna recognized, but as she squinted at the book, a forgotten memory—more of an impression of sound and color, really—coalesced: The soft fabric of her mother’s dress beneath her cheek as Anna snuggled into her lap.
paras.zh: 书名用的不是安娜认得的字母，可当她眯眼盯着书，一段被遗忘的记忆——更确切说，是声音与色彩的印象——凝聚起来：安娜偎在母亲膝头时，脸颊下母亲衣裙柔软的布料。

paras.en: A warm pressure at her side—Elsa, who’d climbed up to join.
paras.zh: 身侧一股温暖的压迫——是艾莎，爬上来凑在一起。

paras.en: Words, low and gentle and hazy as her mother read out loud from a book, its cover the color of Anna’s new riding boots.
paras.zh: 话语低沉、温柔而朦胧，是母亲在念一本书，那书的封面是安娜新马靴的颜色。

paras.en: Lullabies about secret white rivers and Earth Giants and lost legends of yore…Could it be?
paras.zh: 关于秘密白河、大地巨人、失落的远古传说的摇篮曲……会是它吗？

paras.en: Setting the almanac back on the shelf, Anna cracked open the new book and saw the title again written in runes.
paras.zh: 安娜把年鉴放回架，翻开那本新书，见书名又一次以如尼文写成。

paras.en: Someone had written next to them, in pencil, the words Secrets of the Magic Makers .
paras.zh: 有人在旁用铅笔写着：《魔法创造者之秘》。

paras.en: Anna’s breath caught.
paras.zh: 安娜屏住了呼吸。

paras.en: It was her mother’s handwriting.
paras.zh: 那是她母亲的字迹。

paras.en: Anna would know it anywhere.
paras.zh: 安娜到哪儿都认得。

paras.en: This book.
paras.zh: 这本书。

paras.en: This room : her mother had known about it; she had been here.
paras.zh: 这房间：母亲知道它；她曾来过。

paras.en: These books and objects about magic were hers .
paras.zh: 这些关于魔法的书与物，是她的。

paras.en: Suddenly, Anna’s chest felt too small for her heart.
paras.zh: 忽然，安娜觉得胸口装不下自己的心。

paras.en: Or maybe her heart was too big for her chest.
paras.zh: 或许，是她的心对胸口来说太大了。

paras.en: Secrets.
paras.zh: 秘密。

paras.en: This castle was full of secrets she had not known—was not allowed to know.
paras.zh: 这城堡满是她不知、也不被允许知的秘密。

paras.en: Questions rattled through her: Why was Anna always shut out?
paras.zh: 一串问题在她脑中翻腾：为何安娜总被排除在外？

paras.en: Why had her mother collected all these books about magic?
paras.zh: 母亲为何收藏所有这些关于魔法的书？

paras.en: And…did Elsa already know about this room?
paras.zh: 还有……艾莎是否已知道这房间？

paras.en: Like when they were children, was Anna the last to know again? “Anna?” She felt a gentle pat on her shoulder. “Don’t judge a book by its cover.” At Olaf’s words, Anna felt her ribcage loosen, just a tad, but it was enough that she could breathe again.
paras.zh: 就像小时候那样，安娜又是最后一个知道的吗？“安娜？”她感到肩头被轻轻一拍。“别以貌取书。”雪宝的话让安娜的胸腔松了松，只一点点，却足以让她重新呼吸。

paras.en: Olaf had been the friend of both sisters; he was a little bit of Elsa and a little bit of Anna, created by them together.
paras.zh: 雪宝是两姐妹共同的朋友；他有一点艾莎、有一点安娜，是她们一起创造的。

paras.en: And looking around, Anna didn’t think Elsa knew about this secret room.
paras.zh: 环顾四周，安娜觉得艾莎并不知道这密室。

paras.en: After all, Elsa had been so good about filling Anna in on everything she had missed during the time when her head had been under the troll’s persuasion, when she’d been made to forget Elsa’s magic even existed.
paras.zh: 毕竟，在安娜被地精施法、被迫忘掉艾莎魔力存在的那段日子里，艾莎总把安娜错过的全都补给她。

paras.en: Elsa didn’t keep things from Anna, not anymore. “I’m not, Olaf.” Anna flung back a braid. “This book…it was my mother’s.” “Oh.” Olaf peered down through his spectacles. “Her reading selection appears to have been very specific .
paras.zh: 艾莎不再对安娜隐瞒，再也不了。“我没有，雪宝。”安娜甩了甩辫子。“这本书……是我母亲的。”“噢。”雪宝透过眼镜俯视。“她的阅读品味似乎非常专一。

paras.en: I’d rather check out this book.” He waved a slender black volume in his hand. “It’s about dangerous shape-shifters living in a cursed forest.” “Why don’t you give it a read?” Anna asked. “Who knows—maybe it’ll mention cursed animals, too.” “Holler if you need me!” Olaf plopped down at the worktable to page through it.
paras.zh: 我倒想翻翻这本。”他挥着手里一本细长的黑皮书。“讲的是住在被诅咒森林里的危险变形者。”“你何不读读看？”安娜问。“谁知道——也许它也会提到被诅咒的动物。”“需要就叫我校！”雪宝啪地坐到工作台前翻起来。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Anna’s eyes prickled.
paras.zh: 与此同时，安娜的眼睛刺痛起来。

paras.en: Her mother’s book.
paras.zh: 母亲的书。

paras.en: She flipped through the rest of the thick pages.
paras.zh: 她翻过其余厚页。

paras.en: The runes looked like meaningless constellations, but the translations next to them had been made by her mother, and she would follow her mother’s footprints, or fingerprints, as they were, anywhere.
paras.zh: 如尼文看似无意义的星座，可旁边的译文是母亲做的，她愿循着母亲的足迹——或说指纹——去任何地方。

paras.en: Secrets of the Magic Makers seemed to be a book of old tales, brief histories, and maps showing the way to the Valley of the Living Rock, but also a glossary of sorts, naming all kinds of creatures that only existed in lore.
paras.zh: 《魔法创造者之秘》似乎是一本旧故事、简史与通往活石谷之路地图的集合，也是某种词汇表，列出了只存在于传说中的各类生灵。

paras.en: Spirits of wind, water, and fire.
paras.zh: 风、水、火之灵。

paras.en: Earth Giants.
paras.zh: 大地巨人。

paras.en: Nattmara.
paras.zh: 夜魇（Nattmara）。

paras.en: Huldrefólk.
paras.zh: 胡尔德民。

paras.en: They all sounded so familiar, but it was like Anna was trying to stare through a bedsheet hung out to dry.
paras.zh: 它们听来都那么耳熟，可安娜像在透过晾着的床单使劲看。

paras.en: At some point in her life, she’d known what these bedtime-story words had meant in crystal-clear detail, but now she could not make out any more than the slightest shape.
paras.zh: 在她生命的某时，她曾清清楚楚知道这些睡前故事词汇的含义，可如今她连最模糊的轮廓都辨不出。

paras.en: Sadness crept over her.
paras.zh: 悲伤悄悄爬上她。

paras.en: Mother would have known.
paras.zh: 母亲本会知道。

paras.en: Anna hadn’t just lost her mother when the ship sank beneath the Southern Sea’s waves.
paras.zh: 当船沉入南海波涛下时，安娜失去的不只是母亲。

paras.en: The world had lost Queen Iduna’s stories and lullabies, and there was no way to recover them.
paras.zh: 世界失去了伊杜娜王后的故事与摇篮曲，且无从挽回。

paras.en: Or was there?
paras.zh: 还是说，有办法？

paras.en: Anna kept turning the pages.
paras.zh: 安娜继续翻页。

paras.en: There were too many emotions at war within her to settle on any one page, on any one definition.
paras.zh: 太多情绪在她心中交战，让她无法停驻于任何一页、任何一个定义。

paras.en: Faster and faster she flipped through the book until fragile pages slipped out and flitted to the floor.
paras.zh: 她越翻越快，直到脆页滑脱，飘落地面。

paras.en: Anna froze.
paras.zh: 安娜僵住。

paras.en: As carefully as she could, she picked up the papers to realize with relief that they weren’t pages from Secrets of the Magic Makers at all, but scraps of research that had not yet been bound in.
paras.zh: 她尽可能小心地拾起那些纸，松了口气：它们根本不是《魔法创造者之秘》的书页，而是尚未装订的研究残片。

paras.en: One page displayed some familiar-looking blueprints: it was Arendelle Castle.
paras.zh: 一页上有些眼熟的蓝图：是阿伦黛尔城堡。

paras.en: Anna squinted at the page.
paras.zh: 安娜眯眼细看。

paras.en: She, like Gerda, already knew all the secret passages and places that were marked, except for one that drew her attention now and the one she was currently in .
paras.zh: 她和格尔达一样，早已熟知图上标出的所有密道与密地，除了一处此刻吸引她注意的，以及她正身处的这一处。

paras.en: Below the castle, something called the Earth Giant’s Passage seemed to run from somewhere beneath the ice room next to the kitchen and then turn south, under the waters of Arenfjord, to…to somewhere.
paras.zh: 城堡之下，有条叫“大地巨人通道”的线路，似乎从厨房旁冰室下方的某处起，向南拐，钻过阿伦峡湾的水下，通往……某处。

paras.en: Anna couldn’t tell.
paras.zh: 安娜看不出来。

paras.en: The black ink ran off the page, unfinished.
paras.zh: 黑墨在页边断了，没画完。

paras.en: But instructions had been printed in the margins.
paras.zh: 但页边印着说明。

paras.en: Three flagstones in, two across. “ Fascinating ,” Anna whispered and set aside the blueprints.
paras.zh: 进三块石板，横过两块。“有趣，”安娜轻声说，把蓝图放到一边。

paras.en: As soon as she found something to help the animals, she would definitely be taking a trip to the ice room.
paras.zh: 一旦找到帮动物的东西，她定要去冰室一探究竟。

paras.en: She shuffled to the next piece of paper.
paras.zh: 她拖着脚走向下一张纸。

paras.en: It was a map of Arendelle and the land that surrounded it.
paras.zh: 那是阿伦黛尔及其四围之地的地图。

paras.en: Markings circled a black sandy beach and a place called the Dark Sea, and scrawled across it in that same clean flourish that distinguished her mother’s handwriting was one of her father’s many sayings.
paras.zh: 标记圈出一片黑沙海滩和一处叫“暗海”的地方，上面以她母亲特有的、干净利落的笔锋草草写着一个父亲常说的格言。

paras.en: The past has a way of returning.
paras.zh: 过去总会有回来的方式。

paras.en: It was underlined twice, as if it meant something important.
paras.zh: 它被划了两次下划线，仿佛意味深重。

paras.en: Anna squinted at the words, trying to make sense of them.
paras.zh: 安娜眯眼盯着那些字，想弄懂它们。

paras.en: But she was confused.
paras.zh: 可她困惑了。

paras.en: The past was the past, so how could it ever come back?
paras.zh: 过去就是过去，又怎会回来？

paras.en: And why would her mother have written it on a map…a map that was stored in this particular book in this secret room?
paras.zh: 母亲为何要把它写在一张地图——一张藏在密室里这本特定书中的地图上？

paras.en: Was it supposed to mean something?
paras.zh: 它该有什么含义吗？

paras.en: Anna yawned.
paras.zh: 安娜打了个哈欠。

paras.en: Maybe the words didn’t mean anything special at all.
paras.zh: 也许这些字根本没什么特别含义。

paras.en: Most likely, she was only looking for meaning because she so badly wanted meaning to exist.
paras.zh: 多半，她只是在寻找含义，因为她太渴望含义存在。

paras.en: And because she dearly missed her mother and, for a moment, had felt close to her again as she read her book.
paras.zh: 也因为她是那么思念母亲，且有那么一刻，在读母亲的书时又感到贴近了她。

paras.en: Or maybe it was because she was tired.
paras.zh: 抑或，是因为她累了。

paras.en: So very, very tired.
paras.zh: 如此、如此疲惫。

paras.en: Anna had no idea how much time had passed since she and Olaf had entered the secret room, and with no window, it was impossible to tell.
paras.zh: 安娜不知她和雪宝进密室已过多久，没有窗，根本无从判断。

paras.en: Tucking the map back inside the tome, she looked up to find Olaf balancing on a dusty wooden chair as he pulled a snow globe from a shelf. “Hey, look what I found!” Olaf called. “Snow that can exist in summer—just like me!” He plopped a kiss on the globe. “Hello, little pocket flurry.” Giving it a shake, he sent the glittering snow swirling around a miniature of Arendelle Castle carved from a seashell.
paras.zh: 把地图塞回书里，她抬头，见雪宝正立在一把积灰的木椅上，从架上取下一个雪景球。“嘿，看我找到了什么！”雪宝喊。“夏天也能存在的雪——就像我！”他往球上啵了一口。“你好啊，小口袋雪。”他摇了摇，让闪亮的雪绕着贝壳雕的阿伦黛尔城堡小模型打旋。

paras.en: It was pretty, and Anna had definitely seen that snow globe before: not the actual snow globe, but a sketch of it in her father’s sketchbook she still kept in a place of honor on her dressing table. “I think my father also knew about this secret room,” Anna said, “which means that there’s only one family member who might not know about it yet.” She snapped Secrets of the Magic Makers shut. “We have to go tell Elsa!” “Tell me what?”
paras.zh: 它很美，而安娜肯定见过那雪景球：不是真球，而是父亲素描本里的一幅速写——那本子她仍摆在梳妆台上尊贵的位置。“我想我父亲也知道这密室，”安娜说，“也就是说，只有一个家人或许还不知道它。”“我们得去告诉艾莎！”“告诉我什么？”

paras.en: ELSA HAD RETURNED.
paras.zh: 艾莎回来了。

paras.en: And though Anna knew her sister had been up since way before her, had held a meeting for the villagers, visited a farm, scoured the library, then visited another farm, she was still crisp and clean, her blond braid a streak of sunshine against the burgundy of their mother’s cozy scarf, which was now wrapped around her shoulders.
paras.zh: 尽管安娜知道姐姐比她早起得多，开过村民大会、走访过农场、翻过图书馆，又去了另一座农场，她却依旧清爽干净，金辫像一道阳光，衬在母亲那温暖的酒红围巾上——此刻围巾正搭在她肩上。

paras.en: Elsa stood still, her mouth open, staring in what could only be called astonishment at Anna and Olaf inside the secret room. “H-how?
paras.zh: 艾莎站着不动，张着嘴，只能用“惊愕”来形容地盯着密室里的安娜和雪宝。“怎——怎么？

paras.en: I mean, did you…” Elsa sputtered. “What is this place?” Happiness and relief washed over Anna.
paras.zh: 我是说，你们……”艾莎语无伦次。“这是什么地方？”喜悦与释然漫过安娜。

paras.en: From the expression on Elsa’s face and the way her voice shook, Anna knew—the same way she knew that ice was cold and fire was hot—that Elsa had not known about this particular secret.
paras.zh: 从艾莎脸上的神情和她发颤的声音，安娜知道——就像她知道冰是冷、火是热一样——艾莎并不知道这个特定的秘密。

paras.en: For once, Anna had not been the last to know. “We found a clandestine room,” Olaf said. “ Clandestine means secret.
paras.zh: 这一次，安娜不是最后一个知道的。“我们发现了一间秘密（clandestine）房间，”雪宝说。“clandestine 意思是秘密。

paras.en: But I guess now it’s not so clandestine.
paras.zh: 可我想现在它没那么秘密了。

paras.en: Unless you can keep a…what’s the noun form of clandestine ?
paras.zh: 除非你能保守一个……clandestine 的名词形式是什么？

paras.en: Keep a clandestiny ?” He still held the snow globe in his hands. “Do you mind if I show this to Sven?” And before the sisters could reply, he skipped out of the room. “I don’t know, exactly,” Anna said in reply to Elsa’s question. “But isn’t it wonderful ?” She gestured to the secret room’s shelves and fought the urge to giggle as Elsa took a few steps into the room and looked around, her eyes wide, taking in the dried herbs, the gleaming copper spyglass, and the creamy swirl of what appeared to be a narwhal tusk.
paras.zh: 保守个 clandestiny？”他还是把雪景球攥在手里。“介意我拿给斯文看看吗？”姐妹俩还没答，他就蹦跳着出了房间。“确切说，我也不知道，”安娜回应艾莎的问题。“可这难道不奇妙吗？”她指向密室的架子，强忍笑意——艾莎已走进房间几步，睁大眼环顾，打量着干草药、闪亮的铜望远镜，以及那卷像是独角鲸牙的乳白漩涡。

paras.en: Elsa moved closer to the shelves. “How did you find this place?” Elsa asked. “Olaf,” Anna said.
paras.zh: 艾莎凑近架子。“你们怎么找到这地方的？”艾莎问。“雪宝，”安娜说。

paras.en: She filled Elsa in on the items, the map, the notes, and the book she felt could hold the answers to their problems.
paras.zh: 她把那些物件、地图、笔记，以及她觉得可能藏着答案那本书，一一告诉了艾莎。

paras.en: At the mention of their parents having been in this room, Elsa gasped. “And so,” Anna concluded, “I bet we can find something in here about the Blight.” “I don’t know about that,” Elsa said. “But whatever is affecting SoYun’s cows is also affecting the Westens’ goats.
paras.zh: 一提到父母曾在此，艾莎倒吸一口气。“所以，”安娜总结，“我打赌我们能在这儿找到关于枯萎病的东西。”“这我可不敢说，”艾莎说。“但无论什么影响了小允的牛，也影响了韦斯顿家的山羊。

paras.en: I couldn’t wake them up.
paras.zh: 我没能叫醒它们。

paras.en: I tried everything.” “I mean, look at this title!” Anna plucked the Alchemist’s Almanac from the shelf and turned back to Elsa, but Elsa’s attention seemed to have snagged elsewhere, onto an old golden frame that had been carefully leaning against a wall.
paras.zh: 我什么办法都试了。”“我是说，看这书名！”安娜从架上抽出《炼金术士年鉴》转回身，可艾莎的注意力似乎被别处勾住——一幅小心倚墙而立的旧金框。

paras.en: The painting inside of it was muddied by grime, but Anna thought she could just make out a pair of eyes and a strong jaw: a portrait.
paras.zh: 框里的画被污垢糊住，可安娜觉得自己能勉强辨出一双眼睛和硬朗的下巴：一幅肖像。

paras.en: Picking it up, Elsa blew, and a puff of dust ballooned into the air, settling on Anna’s face.
paras.zh: 艾莎拾起它吹了吹，一团灰腾起，落在安娜脸上。

paras.en: Anna sneezed while Elsa held out the painting at arm’s length and squinted. “I think this is supposed to be Aren of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 安娜打了个喷嚏，艾莎则把画伸直手臂举着眯眼细看。“我想这该是阿伦黛尔的阿伦。

paras.en: The painting is so dirty, though, it’s hard to tell.” Anna placed the almanac back on the shelf and peered over Elsa’s shoulder. “What makes you think it’s Aren?” Aren was a legendary leader from times of old—the very, very old, before the last ice age, even.
paras.zh: 不过画太脏，难说清。”安娜把年鉴放回架，从艾莎肩后窥看。“你怎么觉得是阿伦？”阿伦是远古——极远古、甚至在末次冰期之前的传说领袖。

paras.en: So old, in fact, that it was most likely the famous warrior had never even existed. “See that?” Elsa pointed at a dark smudge. “I think that’s supposed to be Revolute, his sword with a ‘yellow diamond, bright as an eye.’” Anna stared at her sister. “Are you…quoting something?” “Yeah,” Elsa admitted. “That’s a line from the Saga of Aren , written by an unknown poet whom some claimed was actually Aren’s true love.” It sounded kind of familiar to Anna.
paras.zh: 事实上太古，那位著名战士多半根本不存在。“看见没？”艾莎指着一块黑斑。“我想那该是他的剑‘雷伏律特’，剑上镶着‘亮若眼的黄钻’。”安娜盯着姐姐。“你……在引用什么？”“对，”艾莎承认。“那是《阿伦 saga》里的一句，作者是个无名诗人，有人称她实为阿伦的真爱。”安娜听着有点耳熟。

paras.en: While she knew everything that there was to know about Arendelle, there were still some things, like these fine details, that she knew she’d once known but had forgotten.
paras.zh: 尽管她对阿伦黛尔无所不知，仍有某些细节——像这些——她知道自己曾知道却忘了。

paras.en: The things that she’d forgotten were usually stories her parents had shared.
paras.zh: 她忘掉的，通常是父母讲过的故事。

paras.en: Embarrassment crept through her.
paras.zh: 尴尬悄悄爬过她。

paras.en: She hated when she forgot things!
paras.zh: 她讨厌自己忘事！

paras.en: She tried to remember everything she could about Aren.
paras.zh: 她努力回想关于阿伦的一切。

paras.en: There were endless stories and epic poems about his brave deeds—from helping the Huldrefólk hide their tails to journeying under the sea to sing with mermaids or questing to mountaintops to meet the sun.
paras.zh: 关于他英勇事迹的故事与史诗无穷无尽——从帮胡尔德民藏尾巴，到潜海与美人鱼同歌，或登山顶会太阳。

paras.en: According to that particular story, Anna recalled, the sun had been so impressed with Aren that she’d given him a sword called the Revolute Blade.
paras.zh: 据那个特定的故事，安娜回想，太阳对阿伦如此倾心，便赠他一柄叫“雷伏律特之刃”的剑。

paras.en: With the sun’s sword in his hand, Aren had carved the fjord between the mountains.
paras.zh: 握着太阳之剑，阿伦在群山间凿出了峡湾。

paras.en: And not just any fjord, but this fjord: Arenfjord, the backbone of the kingdom of Arendelle. “Is that the one that goes, ‘Revolving moon and spinning sun, forged a crescent blade,’ and…something, something, something, ‘May the flags of Arendelle ever wave’?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: 且不止任何峡湾，正是这条：阿伦峡湾，阿伦黛尔王国的脊梁。“可是那句‘旋转的月，飞转的日，铸成弯月之刃’，然后……什么什么什么，‘愿阿伦黛尔的旗帜永飘’？”安娜问。

paras.en: Elsa nodded. “Exactly.” Anna’s embarrassment subsided as Elsa pointed a little above the smudge to a blur. “I think that might be the yellow diamond in the pommel, and then there”—she moved her hand—“see how the blade curves?
paras.zh: 艾莎点头。“正是。”艾莎指向黑斑上方一点的模糊处，安娜的尴尬消了。“我想那可能是柄头上的黄钻，然后那里”——她移手——“看见剑身怎么弯的吗？

paras.en: According to myth, the curve is where the sword first struck the earth.
paras.zh: 据传说，那弯处正是剑首次劈地之处。

paras.en: That’s how the sword got its name. ‘Revolute’ means ‘curved.’” “Magic swords are nice and all,” Anna said, tilting her head and fanning herself with her hand.
paras.zh: 剑名由此而来。‘Revolute’意为‘弯曲’。”“魔法剑什么的都好，”安娜歪着头，用手给自己扇风。

paras.en: It was getting hot in the windowless room. “But I don’t really see why it would be helpful to be able to make cuts into the earth.” Elsa fiddled with her braid as she looked at the painting. “Apparently, the sun bestowed Revolute with great powers, and with the sword in his hand, Aren became known as the protector of the people, unifying them against a dark fright.
paras.zh: 这无窗的房间渐热。“可我真看不出能切开大地有什么用。”艾莎拨弄辫子看着画。“据说，太阳赐雷伏律特以伟力，握剑在手，阿伦成了守护者，团结众人抵御黑暗恐惧。

paras.en: He was a great leader.” A strange expression settled on Elsa’s face. “History seems to be full of great leaders.” Anna glanced at her sister.
paras.zh: 他是位伟大的领袖。”一种奇怪的神情落在艾莎脸上。“历史似乎满是伟大的领袖。”安娜瞥了姐姐一眼。

paras.en: For some reason she did not quite understand, Elsa seemed to have left the room, even though she hadn’t physically gone anywhere.
paras.zh: 因某个她不太明白的原因，艾莎仿佛已离开房间，尽管她人没动。

paras.en: She no longer looked at Anna.
paras.zh: 她不再看安娜。

paras.en: Instead, her gaze was fixed on a shelf full of books, bottles, and jars. “Why were they studying magic?
paras.zh: 相反，她的目光定在满是书、瓶与罐的架子上。“他们为何研究魔法？

paras.en: And why did they seal off the room and never tell us about it?” Elsa asked, her voice so soft that Anna wondered if she’d meant to say anything at all.
paras.zh: 又为何封起这房间，从不告诉我们？”艾莎问，声音轻得让安娜怀疑她是否真想说出口。

paras.en: Elsa stood there, with her back impossibly straight, standing the way a queen should.
paras.zh: 艾莎立在那里，背挺得不可思议地直，正是女王该有的站姿。

paras.en: But at that exact moment, Anna didn’t see Elsa, queen of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 可就在那一刻，安娜没看见阿伦黛尔女王艾莎。

paras.en: She saw Elsa the lonely child, who’d spent her days alone in her room with only patterns of frost to keep her company.
paras.zh: 她看见孤独的孩子艾莎，终日独处房中，只有霜花图案作伴。

paras.en: Anna reached out to touch Elsa’s arm.
paras.zh: 安娜伸手碰了碰艾莎的手臂。

paras.en: Her sister was stiff, as if she didn’t just wield cold and snow, but were made of it. “I have the same question,” Anna admitted, glad they were in this together. “But think about it: why do people study art?” she asked. “Why does Baker Blodget spend her entire life in pursuit of baking the best butter biscuits in the world?
paras.zh: 姐姐僵着，仿佛她不仅掌控冰雪，本就是冰雪所造。“我也有同样的疑问，”安娜承认，庆幸他们同在此事里。“可想啊：人们为何学艺术？”她问。“面包师布洛杰特为何毕生追求烤出世上最好的黄油饼干？

paras.en: Why does Kristoff keep trying to sing?” Elsa remained silent, so Anna answered for her, reaching down to pick up Secrets of the Magic Makers . “Because talents are worth exploring.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫为何总想唱歌？”艾莎仍沉默，于是安娜替她答，弯腰拾起《魔法创造者之秘》。“因为才华值得探索。”

paras.en: Because butter biscuits are delicious, singing is fun, and your magic is beautiful, Elsa.
paras.zh: 因为黄油饼干好吃、唱歌有趣，而你的魔法很美，艾莎。

paras.en: Maybe they wanted to know more about it.” She slipped a hand in Elsa’s, and waited.
paras.zh: 也许他们想多了解它。”她把手滑进艾莎的手里，等着。

paras.en: A few seconds later, Elsa squeezed her fingers, and Anna squeezed back.
paras.zh: 几秒后，艾莎攥了攥她的手指，安娜也回攥。

paras.en: Without meeting Anna’s eye, Elsa moved away from her and toward the exit. “I need to go.” Elsa’s voice was quiet. “This place creeps me out.” “What do you mean?” Anna didn’t think she had ever been in a more beautiful room with still so much to explore.
paras.zh: 艾莎不与安娜对视，挪开身朝出口走去。“我得走了。”艾莎声音轻。“这地方让我发毛。”“什么意思？”安娜想，她从没待过一间如此美、却还有那么多可探索的房间。

paras.en: The possibilities were endless! “It’s all these things in jars.” Elsa waved her hands. “Contained and locked away.” “Well,” Anna said, tucking Secrets of the Magic Makers under her arm, “maybe that just means it’s time for them all to be brought to the light of day.” Excitement again rose within her. “The answers to how to stop the Blight could be in here!
paras.zh: 可能无穷无尽！“全是这些罐里的东西。”艾莎挥着手。“被装着、锁起来。”“唔，”安娜说，把《魔法创造者之秘》夹在臂下，“也许这正意味着，是时候让它们都见见天日了。”兴奋再次在她心中升起。“治愈枯萎病的答案可能就在这儿！

paras.en: Maybe there’s even more magic out there, magic that can actually help us!” Elsa flinched. “I—I didn’t mean it like that,” Anna said. “Your magic is really helpful.
paras.zh: 也许外面还有更多魔法，真能帮我们的魔法！”艾莎一缩。“我——我不是那个意思，”安娜说。“你的魔法真的很管用。

paras.en: Just not in this situation.” Elsa took a step back. “I need to help the livestock before we can start really delving into this room, okay?” Elsa said. “There’s no time to waste.
paras.zh: 只是不在此情此景。”艾莎退了一步。“在我们真正深挖这房间前，我得先去帮牲口，好吗？”艾莎说。“没时间可浪费。

paras.en: I…I have to go.” “Of course.
paras.zh: 我……我得走了。”“当然。

paras.en: But—but we …I can stay here and keep looking for clues,” Anna suggested. “We may be able to find the answers to what’s happening to—” Elsa shook her head. “I really think we should leave this place alone for now.” “Hold on,” Anna said, desperate to keep her plan in place, desperate to help. “There’s so much we haven’t uncovered!
paras.zh: 可——可我们……我可以留在这儿继续找线索，”安娜提议。“我们或许能找到正在发生之事的答案——”艾莎摇头。“我真的觉得，眼下我们该别碰这地方。“等一下，”安娜说，拼命想保住计划、拼命想帮忙。“还有太多我们没揭开！

paras.en: The books might have the answers!” “I have to go now.” Elsa’s voice was sharp as an icicle. “But we—” “ We should leave this room in the past.
paras.zh: 书里也许有答案！”“我现在得走了。”艾莎声音冷如冰锥。“可我们——”“我们该让这房间留在过去。

paras.en: There has to be a reason Mother and Father wanted to keep it secret.
paras.zh: 父母想保密，必有缘由。

paras.en: Besides,” she said as she gestured toward the door, “the answers to our problems are out there.” No , Anna thought, her fear big and full and pressing against her chest.
paras.zh: 再说了，”她朝门一指，“我们问题的答案在那儿外头。”不，安娜想，恐惧庞大而满溢，压着她的胸口。

paras.en: It was happening again.
paras.zh: 又来了。

paras.en: Her plan to prove herself to Elsa was falling apart!
paras.zh: 她向艾莎证明自己的计划要瓦解了！

paras.en: Who cared about being able to go on some silly grand tour?
paras.zh: 谁稀罕能去参加什么傻乎乎的环球巡游？

paras.en: Anna wanted to do what was best for everyone, but she seemed to have a knack for doing the complete opposite these days. “Stay away from this room, Anna,” Elsa continued, turning away from her and stepping toward the library. “It was left hidden for a reason.
paras.zh: 安娜想做对大家最有利的事，可近来她似乎有种反着来的本领。“离这房间远点，安娜，”艾莎继续道，转身朝图书馆走去。“它藏起来是有原因的。

paras.en: Let’s keep it that way.” “ Elsa —” “Leave it alone.” And when Elsa spoke in that tone, more like a queen than a sister, Anna knew there was no point in arguing.
paras.zh: 就让它那样吧。”“艾莎——”“别碰它。”当艾莎用那种语气——更像女王而非姐姐——说话时，安娜知道争辩无益。

paras.en: Silently, Anna nodded.
paras.zh: 安娜默默点头。

paras.en: As she placed Secrets of the Magic Makers back onto a shelf, Elsa returned to the library and strode to her next scheduled appointment.
paras.zh: 当她把《魔法创造者之秘》放回架，艾莎已回图书馆，迈步赶向下一场预约。

paras.en: But Anna couldn’t bring herself to leave—not just yet.
paras.zh: 可安娜无法让自己离开——至少现在不能。

paras.en: She let herself look one last time at this secret room, imagining how her mother might have sat at that worktable, translating symbols into words, while her father studied the objects on the shelves and cracked a clever joke.
paras.zh: 她让自己最后看一眼这密室，想象母亲如何坐在工作台前，把符号译成文字，而父亲研究架上的物件，讲个机灵的笑话。

paras.en: Without really thinking about it, Anna reached her fingers back toward Secrets of the Magic Makers , but they stopped just short of touching the soft leather.
paras.zh: 没多想，安娜伸手又朝《魔法创造者之秘》探去，却停在将触未触那柔软皮革之前。

paras.en: Elsa might be really upset with her if she found out what Anna was thinking, but Elsa would be even more upset if the animals kept getting sick.
paras.zh: 若艾莎发现安娜所想，或许会真生气；可若动物继续生病，艾莎会更气。

paras.en: It would be worth it, Anna told herself firmly, when everything had been fixed—when Anna had fixed things.
paras.zh: 一切都修好时——当安娜修好一切时——这便值得，安娜坚定地对自己说。

paras.en: Besides, Elsa had only said that Anna needed to stay out of this room, but she hadn’t said—or at least, hadn’t said specifically —that Anna couldn’t take some of the room with her.
paras.zh: 再说了，艾莎只说安娜需远离这房间，却没说——至少没明确说——安娜不能带走这房间的一点什么。

paras.en: And with that, Anna tugged her mother’s book free and hurried away.
paras.zh: 于是，安娜把母亲的书抽出来，匆匆离去。

paras.en: IT WAS VERY LATE NOW, and Anna was hungry.
paras.zh: 此刻夜已深，安娜饿了。

paras.en: Stopping to grab a plate of cheese, crackers, and apple slices from the kitchen, she chatted with the castle cooks, catching up on local gossip: who was most likely to grow the biggest pumpkin in the village patch this year, how many people would attend the annual harvest feast, and the very exciting rumor that an engagement ring had been purchased at the jeweler’s shop, but by whom?
paras.zh: 她在厨房顺手取了一盘奶酪、饼干和苹果片，与城堡厨师们闲聊，追着本地八卦：今年村园里谁最可能种出最大的南瓜，多少人会来一年一度的丰收宴，还有个极刺激的传闻——珠宝店卖出了一枚订婚戒指，可会是谁买的？

paras.en: Usually, Anna would have loved to stay and muse, but she knew the more time she spent down there, the less time she’d have to research.
paras.zh: 平时安娜会乐意留下神聊，可她知道在那儿耗得越久，研究的时间就越少。

paras.en: And so, excusing herself with her cheese plate, Anna rushed into her warm bedroom, clambered into her most comfortable pajamas, and began to read.
paras.zh: 于是，安娜端着奶酪盘告退，冲进温暖的卧室，套上最舒服的睡衣，开始阅读。

paras.en: Secrets of the Magic Makers was more than just a collection of stories.
paras.zh: 《魔法创造者之秘》不止是故事集。

paras.en: It almost seemed like a field guide, as if someone had traipsed through the wilderness collecting information on various mythological creatures while also gathering ingredients for turning flowers into frogs.
paras.zh: 它几乎像一本野外指南，仿佛有人踏遍荒野，收集各类神话生物的信息，同时也采集把花变蛙的材料。

paras.en: There were histories of enchanted forests, and things that looked like recipes.
paras.zh: 有魔法森林的历史，也有看似配方之物。

paras.en: And while several of the text passages had not been translated by her mother, many had.
paras.zh: 尽管有几段文字母亲未译，许多却译了。

paras.en: Anna followed her mother’s handwriting like a hungry bird trailing crumbs.
paras.zh: 安娜像一只循着面包屑的饿鸟，跟着母亲的笔迹。

paras.en: Crunching on her crackers, she read of shape-shifters who lived with herds of reindeer; talking trees; draugs; and boys who were no larger than a thumb.
paras.zh: 她咔嚓嚼着饼干，读到与驯鹿群同住的变形者、会说话的树、draug（僵尸），以及不比拇指大的男孩。

paras.en: There were pages and pages of the unknown language, and every so often an illustration accompanied the symbols.
paras.zh: 一页又一页的未知文字，偶尔有插图相伴。

paras.en: Anna wondered if Kristoff would know anything about the runes, or if he had ever come across anything in the Valley of the Living Rock that might help.
paras.zh: 安娜想，克里斯托夫会懂这些如尼文吗，还是他在活石谷曾见过什么有用的？

paras.en: Were they runes of the mountain trolls?
paras.zh: 它们是山地地精的如尼文吗？

paras.en: Or something else?
paras.zh: 还是别的？

paras.en: Her mother seemed to have skipped translating the pages with the more creepy-looking sketches.
paras.zh: 母亲似乎跳过了那些画风更可怖的页未译。

paras.en: Anna flipped past a sketch of a man seemingly screaming in agony, then one of another man lying on a stone table as blue smoke curled from his head and a troll stood over him with its arms held high.
paras.zh: 安娜翻过一张似在痛苦尖叫的男人速写，又翻过一张：另一男人躺在石桌上，蓝烟从头顶盘旋，一只地精高举双臂立在他上方。

paras.en: Finally, she landed on a page that, based on its illustrations, seemed to detail the Saga of Aren .
paras.zh: 终于，她落在一页上，从插图看，似乎详述着《阿伦 saga》。

paras.en: The physical features of the legendary hero were much easier to see in this book than they had been in the portrait Elsa had uncovered.
paras.zh: 这位传说英雄的体貌，在此书中比在艾莎揭出的肖像里清楚得多。

paras.en: Aren had a shaggy head of yellow hair and a bright blond beard with a few skinny braids tucked into it.
paras.zh: 阿伦顶着一头乱蓬蓬的黄发，亮金色胡须里掖着几缕细辫。

paras.en: His face was more square than it was round, and his hooked nose put Anna in mind of an eagle.
paras.zh: 他的脸偏方不偏圆，钩鼻让安娜想起鹰。

paras.en: Though there were only runes on the page—no translation—Anna recognized some of his more famous exploits.
paras.zh: 尽管页上只有如尼文——没有译文——安娜认得他几件更出名的事迹。

paras.en: In the corner was a sketch of the waterfall whom Aren had tricked into helping him breathe underwater.
paras.zh: 角落里是一幅瀑布的速写，阿伦曾骗它帮自己在水下呼吸。

paras.en: And just to the right of that, a sketch of the sun, each ray a delicate sword with a yellow diamond in its pommel, just like Aren’s famed Revolute Blade.
paras.zh: 就在其右，是一幅太阳的速写，每一道光芒都是柄精致的剑，柄头镶着黄钻，正如阿伦那柄著名的雷伏律特之刃。

paras.en: And in the last corner, far right and down, lounged a scrawled dragon.
paras.zh: 而在最右下角，懒洋洋趴着一条草草画的龙。

paras.en: Anna turned the page, and cringed.
paras.zh: 安娜翻页，瑟缩了一下。

paras.en: A sketch of a wolf, so realistic that Anna half thought she could feel its hot breath blasting from the pages, snarled up at her.
paras.zh: 一张狼的速写，逼真得让安娜半信自己能感到它从页中喷出的热气，正朝她龇牙。

paras.en: Her mother seemed to have only gotten to the very beginning of the page, and had translated only a single word: Nattmara .
paras.zh: 母亲似乎只译到这页开头，只译了一个词：夜魇（Nattmara）。

paras.en: Anna frowned.
paras.zh: 安娜皱眉。

paras.en: Yet another one of those once-known-now-forgotten words from her childhood.
paras.zh: 又是那些儿时曾知、如今已忘的词之一。

paras.en: In frustration, she flipped the page.
paras.zh: 她懊恼地翻过页。

paras.en: She’d had enough of not knowing—and enough, as a five-year-old, of that scary recurring nightmare, thank you very much.
paras.zh: 她受够了无知——也受够了五岁时那个吓人的反复噩梦，非常感谢。

paras.en: The next installment that made her pause her was a recipe.
paras.zh: 让她停下的是下一段：一张配方。

paras.en: It was a loose page, simply tucked into the binding, but it had been neatly titled in her mother’s handwriting: MAKE DREAMS COME TRUE .
paras.zh: 那是张散页，随意夹在装订里，却用母亲清晰的笔迹题了名：美梦成真。

paras.en: There was another word scrawled in the margins in the same handwriting: SPELL?
paras.zh: 页边用同一笔迹草草写着另一个词：咒语？

paras.en: Anna’s fingers traced the word spell .
paras.zh: 安娜的手指描过“咒语”二字。

paras.en: Not a recipe— magic .
paras.zh: 不是配方——是魔法。

paras.en: She had never known anyone other than Elsa to be able to use magic before, and Elsa certainly didn’t incant words or spells when she created and manipulated snow and ice.
paras.zh: 除了艾莎，她从不知别人能用魔法，而艾莎创造、操控冰雪时，绝不会念什么咒语。

paras.en: The magic was part of Elsa.
paras.zh: 魔法本就是艾莎的一部分。

paras.en: It ran within her.
paras.zh: 在她的血脉里流淌。

paras.en: Shortly after their reunion, Anna had asked Elsa what it felt like when she twirled her hands.
paras.zh: 重逢后不久，安娜问过艾莎，转手腕时是什么感觉。

paras.en: Elsa had described it as an overwhelming emotion, a feeling that would eventually grow so big it had to find release in some way. “Like when you want to cry but you hold on to it because you don’t want others to see?” Anna had asked. “Yes,” Elsa had said, “but not just crying.
paras.zh: 艾莎形容那是一种压倒性的情绪，终会涨大到必须以某种方式释放。“就像你想哭却忍着，因为不想让别人看见？”安娜问。“对，”艾莎说，“可不止哭。

paras.en: Sometimes, it’s the feeling of clamping in a giant laugh in a time you’re supposed to be quiet, like in the chapel.
paras.zh: 有时，是在该安静的场合——比如礼拜堂——憋住一场大笑的感觉。

paras.en: It seems that if I listen to the feeling, to the magic, and release it, I can manage it.” A poem in a book didn’t seem like the kind of magic Elsa possessed, but that didn’t necessarily mean these words would not hold any power.
paras.zh: 似乎只要我倾听那感觉、那魔法，并释放它，就能驾驭。”书中的诗不像艾莎那种魔法，可这不意味着这些字句毫无力量。

paras.en: These words.
paras.zh: 这些字句。

paras.en: This spell .
paras.zh: 这咒语。

paras.en: Excitement trilled through Anna.
paras.zh: 兴奋在安娜体内震颤。

paras.en: The more she looked at the words, the more certain she felt that everything they needed was right here, in their parents’ research.
paras.zh: 她越看这些字，越确信所需一切就在此处，在父母的研究里。

paras.en: She just wished she knew what knowledge lay behind the untranslated sections.
paras.zh: 她只愿自己知道未译部分背后藏着什么知识。

paras.en: Anna squinted at the symbols, as though by simply staring at them she would come to understand.
paras.zh: 安娜眯眼盯着符号，仿佛仅凭凝视便能懂。

paras.en: But no knowledge came, only heavy eyelids.
paras.zh: 可没来知识，只来了沉重的眼皮。

paras.en: She wondered if Kristoff had found out anything helpful on his trek to the valley.
paras.zh: 她想知道克里斯托夫去谷中的路上可发现了什么有用的。

paras.en: She wondered if SoYun was still out in the field, trying to keep her cattle awake through the night.
paras.zh: 她想知道小允是否还在田里，整夜试着让牛保持清醒。

paras.en: But most of all, she wondered what her parents would have done in this situation. “Anna and Elsa, always lean on each other for help,” Father had said.
paras.zh: 但最重要的是，她想知道父母在此境况会怎么做。“安娜与艾莎，永远互相依靠，”父亲说过。

paras.en: He’d have wanted her to tell Elsa about this spell, but first, she just needed to rest her eyes.
paras.zh: 他定愿她把这咒语告诉艾莎，可首先，她只需歇歇眼。

paras.en: Anna’s thoughts slipped over and past each other like darting fish as her eyelids drooped lower, and lower, and lower….She needed to fix the Blight….
paras.zh: 安娜的思绪像窜动的鱼般彼此滑过，眼皮垂得越来越低……她得治好枯萎病……

paras.en: The court of Royaume was just as beautiful as Anna had always dreamed, and she knew she was dreaming—not only because she’d never been to Royaume, but also because everything felt too perfect and fragile to be real.
paras.zh: 罗亚姆的宫廷美得一如安娜梦中所见，而她知道自己是在做梦——不只因为她从没去过罗亚姆，也因一切太完美、太易碎，不似真实。

paras.en: Besides, Elsa would never be caught dancing in real life, and there she was, spinning on the dance floor, arms flung wide as if she were trying to embrace the chandeliered ceiling above them.
paras.zh: 再者，现实里艾莎绝不会被撞见跳舞，可她就在那儿，在舞池旋转，双臂大张，像要拥抱头顶的水晶灯天花板。

paras.en: Anna grinned. “You look like a tree caught in a gale!” she shouted over the high song of violins and flutes. “And you look like you’re dizzy,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: 安娜咧嘴。“你像一棵被大风刮住的树！”她在提琴与长笛的高亢乐声上喊道。“你倒像晕了，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Anna shook her head. “Dizzy?
paras.zh: 安娜摇头。“晕？

paras.en: Why—oh!” Before she could finish her question, Elsa grabbed her hand and began to twirl her, her diaphanous white skirts fanning around her like a skein of sparkling snow.
paras.zh: 为什么——噢！”话没问完，艾莎抓住她的手开始转她，半透明的白裙像一缕闪亮的雪在她四周散开。

paras.en: Anna threw back her head and laughed, imagining what a sight they must make on the dance floor.
paras.zh: 安娜仰头大笑，想象她们在舞池该是多惹眼的景象。

paras.en: Elsa, dressed all in white spangled with pearl seeds, was the very embodiment of winter, while Anna’s headdress and gold skirts helped her masquerade as summer.
paras.zh: 艾莎一身白、缀着珍珠籽，是冬的化身；而安娜的头饰与金裙帮她扮成夏。

paras.en: The grand ballroom blurred around her, seeming to turn into streaks of paint.
paras.zh: 大舞厅在她四周模糊，仿佛化作画笔的条纹。

paras.en: Her head began to pound, but it was so rare to see Elsa silly and carefree that she didn’t want to tell her to stop.
paras.zh: 她头开始一跳一跳地疼，可难得见艾莎这般傻气无忧，她不愿叫停。

paras.en: Instead, Anna closed her eyes, trying to hold on to this moment, even if it was only pretend…but was it?
paras.zh: 于是安娜闭上眼，想抓住这一刻，哪怕只是假装……可它是吗？

paras.en: She was feeling really dizzy now.
paras.zh: 此刻她真觉得晕了。

paras.en: No matter how much fun Elsa was having, it was time to stop. “Hey, Elsa?
paras.zh: 无论艾莎玩得多开心，是时候停了。“嘿，艾莎？

paras.en: That’s enough!” Anna opened her eyes and gasped.
paras.zh: 够了！”安娜睁眼，倒吸一口气。

paras.en: Her sister was no longer twirling her.
paras.zh: 姐姐不再转她了。

paras.en: Instead, a tall stranger in coattails and a silver wolf mask stood where Elsa had been.
paras.zh: 取而代之的，是个穿燕尾服、戴银狼面具的高个陌生人，立在艾莎方才的位置。

paras.en: Anna stumbled to a halt. “Pardon me.” She removed her hand. “I need to find my sister.” The dancer bowed, the silver wolf mask nearly tipping off his nose. “As you wish, Princess Anna.” The blood in her veins turned to ice.
paras.zh: 安娜踉跄停住。“失陪。”她抽回手。“我得找我姐姐。”舞者鞠躬，银狼面具几乎从鼻尖滑落。“如您所愿，安娜公主。”她血管里的血成了冰。

paras.en: Anna knew that voice.
paras.zh: 安娜认得那声音。

paras.en: It was a voice she didn’t want to hear again.
paras.zh: 那是她不想再听到的声音。

paras.en: She peered uncertainly through the dark eyeholes of the mask. “Prince—Prince Hans?” “The very same.” A diamond ring suddenly materialized in his hand. “Your sister said I should give this to you when I ask for your hand.” “My—my hand?” Hans grabbed her wrist and jammed the ring onto her finger. “Your hand in marriage, of course.
paras.zh: 她不安地从面具的暗眼孔里窥看。“汉斯——汉斯王子？”“正是。”一枚钻戒忽然在他手中显形。“你姐姐说，我向你要手时，该把它给你。”“我的——我的手？”汉斯抓过她手腕，把戒指硬套上她手指。“当然是婚约。

paras.en: Your sister has given her blessing.
paras.zh: 你姐姐已赐下祝福。

paras.en: She has no use for you.” Anna yanked her hand away. “I don’t believe that,” she said, craning her neck to see if she could spot her sister in the glittering hall.
paras.zh: 她用不着你了。”安娜猛抽回手。“我不信，”她说，伸长脖子想在那闪亮的厅里找出姐姐。

paras.en: But no one was there.
paras.zh: 可没有人在。

paras.en: The decorations, the musicians, the dancers…all had vanished, leaving her completely alone with the prince of the Southern Isles—her villainous almost-husband, who had tricked her and the rest of the kingdom before Anna uncovered his awful plans to kill Elsa and take over Arendelle.
paras.zh: 装饰、乐师、舞者……全消失了，只留她与南方群岛的王子独处——那个险些成为她丈夫的恶棍，曾在安娜揭穿他欲杀艾莎、篡夺阿伦黛尔的恶计前，骗了她与举国上下。

paras.en: Hans laughed, an awful sound, made worse by the way it turned up into a howl at the end.
paras.zh: 汉斯笑了，一声可怕的音，末了还上扬成嗥叫，更显狰狞。

paras.en: As Anna watched, the silver hair of his wolf mask rippled in the draft as if it were real fur, and his nose elongated, becoming more and more snoutlike.
paras.zh: 安娜看着，他狼面具的银发在气流中起伏，像真毛，鼻子拉长，越来越像口鼻。

paras.en: More and more wolflike.
paras.zh: 越来越像狼。

paras.en: Until suddenly, there was no Hans, just a great white wolf with amber eyes and teeth the size of dinner knives.
paras.zh: 直到忽然，汉斯不见了，只剩一头琥珀眼、牙如餐刀般大的白狼。

paras.en: It was the same wolf that had stalked her childhood dreams.
paras.zh: 正是那头潜入她童年梦境的狼。

paras.en: But while most things from childhood seem to become smaller as one grows, the wolf had, in fact, only grown with Anna.
paras.zh: 可尽管童年之物常随人成长而变小，这狼实则只随安娜长大。

paras.en: He was fiercer now.
paras.zh: 他如今更凶。

paras.en: Hungrier.
paras.zh: 更饿。

paras.en: The wolf licked his maw and advanced.
paras.zh: 狼舔了舔嘴，逼上前。

paras.en: Wake up, Anna, she thought frantically, tripping on her skirts as she tried to scramble backward.
paras.zh: 醒来，安娜，她慌乱地想，被裙子绊着，想往后爬。

paras.en: Wake up!
paras.zh: 醒来！

paras.en: Wake up!
paras.zh: 醒来！

paras.en: Wake up— “Wake up!” Anna sat straight up.
paras.zh: 醒来——“醒来！”安娜猛地坐直。

paras.en: The sound of her own voice shattered her nightmare.
paras.zh: 自己声音击碎了噩梦。

paras.en: Relief, warm and sweet as fresh honey, coursed through her.
paras.zh: 如新蜜般温暖甘甜的释然流遍全身。

paras.en: It had been so long since she’d had this particular dream, this particular nightmare, and the fear it spawned was unfortunately as familiar as the ache of missing her parents.
paras.zh: 她许久未做这特定的梦、这特定的噩梦了，而它催生的恐惧，不幸地如思念父母的痛般熟悉。

paras.en: And this time, there was no Mother to tell her a distracting story or Father to bring her hot chocolate.
paras.zh: 而这一次，没有母亲讲个分神的故事，也没有父亲端来热可可。

paras.en: Always rely on each other for help.
paras.zh: 永远互相依靠。

paras.en: Leaning forward, Anna grabbed Secrets of the Magic Makers , which had slid to the foot of her bed.
paras.zh: 安娜前倾，抓起滑到床脚的《魔法创造者之秘》。

paras.en: She tucked it close to her chest and raced into her parents’ old bedroom.
paras.zh: 她把它紧贴胸前，冲进父母从前的卧室。

paras.en: Not because she thought they would be there, but because Elsa had moved into it after her coronation, abandoning her childhood bedroom.
paras.zh: 不是以为他们会在，而是因艾莎加冕后搬了进去，弃了童年卧室。

paras.en: But looking around the room and at the dying fire, Anna wondered why Elsa had not yet returned.
paras.zh: 可环顾房间与将熄的火，安娜疑惑艾莎为何还没回来。

paras.en: She reassured herself that sometimes queenly duties could last all night.
paras.zh: 她安慰自己，女王的职责有时能持续整夜。

paras.en: She walked back to her room.
paras.zh: 她走回房。

paras.en: Before clambering into bed, she stopped by her dressing table and took hold of her father’s sketchbook.
paras.zh: 爬上床前，她在梳妆台边驻足，拿起父亲的素描本。

paras.en: King Agnarr had been a talented artist, wielding both his pencil and sword with ease.
paras.zh: 阿格瑞国王是个有才的画家，铅笔与剑都使得从容。

paras.en: On the bad days, when Anna felt most alone, she liked to open his sketchbook up and see the world as he once had.
paras.zh: 在糟糕的日子，当安娜最觉孤独，她爱翻开他的素描本，看他曾眼里的世界。

paras.en: There were images of Arendelle Castle, as well as the far-off lands he’d seen on his grand tour.
paras.zh: 有阿伦黛尔城堡的画，也有他巡游所见远方之地的画。

paras.en: Elsa would leave on her own grand tour in just four—no, now three days—and if Anna could heal the animals before then, there was still a chance she’d be able to sail away with Elsa.
paras.zh: 艾莎再过四天——不，如今是三天——就要启程自己的巡游，若安娜能在那前治好动物，仍有机会随艾莎扬帆。

paras.en: Returning to her bed, Anna decided that she’d wake up extra early to show Elsa the spell first thing.
paras.zh: 回到床上，安娜决定明日格外早起，第一件事就把咒语给艾莎看。

paras.en: And so, with her father’s sketchbook on one side of her pillow and her mother’s book on the other, she at last dared to close her eyes.
paras.zh: 于是，父亲素描本在一侧枕边、母亲的书在另一侧，她终于敢合上眼。

paras.en: The wolf did not return.
paras.zh: 狼没有回来。

paras.en: ANNA HEARD THE SOUND of chimes and footsteps from somewhere in the castle.
paras.zh: 安娜听见城堡某处传来钟鸣与脚步声。

paras.en: Dawn had broken, spilling warm autumn sunlight across her face.
paras.zh: 黎明已破，温煦的秋日阳光洒在她脸上。

paras.en: Keeping her eyes closed, Anna stretched, enjoying the coziness of her quilt and the softness of her pillow.
paras.zh: 安娜闭着眼伸了个懒腰，享受被子的温暖与枕头的柔软。

paras.en: Just a few more minutes.
paras.zh: 再眯几分钟。

paras.en: She could afford to wait before she found Elsa, asked more about the Westens’ goats, and told her about what she’d found last night in their mother’s book.
paras.zh: 在去找艾莎、多问韦斯顿家山羊、并把昨晚在母亲书里的发现告诉她之前，她等得起。

paras.en: After all, she was so comfortable that it would be a crime to untuck herself, and— Her thoughts screeched to a halt.
paras.zh: 毕竟，她太舒服了，破窝而起简直是罪过，而且——她的思绪戛然而止。

paras.en: Secrets of the Magic Makers .
paras.zh: 《魔法创造者之秘》。

paras.en: The book with spells in it.
paras.zh: 那本有咒语的书。

paras.en: The book with a potential cure for the animals.
paras.zh: 那本可能治愈动物的书。

paras.en: Anna lurched up, eyes flying open—only to be blinded not by the light of dawn, but by golden mid-morning sun.
paras.zh: 安娜猛地弹起，眼睛睁大——却被刺盲的不是晨光，而是正午般的金色阳光。

paras.en: She’d overslept again!
paras.zh: 她又睡过头了！

paras.en: Faster than Sven could chomp a carrot, Anna tumbled out of bed before she could even untwist herself from her quilt.
paras.zh: 比斯文啃根胡萝卜还快，安娜还没从被子里挣脱就滚下了床。

paras.en: She grabbed Secrets of the Magic Makers , and with her blanket flapping behind her, she sprinted through the dressing room and downstairs.
paras.zh: 她抓起《魔法创造者之秘》，被子在身后拍打着，冲过更衣室奔下楼。

paras.en: Not bothering to knock, she flung open the door to her parents’ old bedroom.
paras.zh: 她懒得敲门，一把推开父母旧卧室的门。

paras.en: The bed was neatly made, the ashes cold in their hearth.
paras.zh: 床铺得齐整，壁炉里的灰已冷。

paras.en: Of course—her sister would have been up for hours at this point.
paras.zh: 当然——这会儿姐姐早起来了好几个钟头。

paras.en: Elsa, for some strange reason, enjoyed mornings.
paras.zh: 艾莎，出于某种奇怪的原因，喜欢早晨。

paras.en: She said they made her feel fresh as new snow, while they made Anna feel as fresh as chicken droppings.
paras.zh: 她说早晨让她如新雪般清新，却让安娜如鸡粪般“清新”。

paras.en: A headache pounded at her temples.
paras.zh: 一阵头痛在太阳穴处敲击。

paras.en: Even though she’d overslept by hours, it had been a restless sleep, as it had taken her long hours to relax after the return of the childhood nightmare.
paras.zh: 尽管她多睡了几小时，却睡得不安稳，因为童年噩梦回来后，她花了很久才放松。

paras.en: Think.
paras.zh: 想想。

paras.en: Where would Elsa be at this time of day?
paras.zh: 这会儿艾莎会在哪儿？

paras.en: Whirling from the bedchamber, Anna ran down the hallway to peer through open doors.
paras.zh: 安娜从卧室一转，跑过走廊从敞开的门里窥看。

paras.en: Elsa wasn’t in the library or council chambers.
paras.zh: 艾莎不在图书馆，也不在议事厅。

paras.en: Maybe the portrait gallery?
paras.zh: 也许在画像廊？

paras.en: Anna flew downstairs and made a sharp turn on the landing—and barreled into something warm and solid.
paras.zh: 安娜飞下楼，在楼梯平台急转——撞上什么温暖而结实的东西。

paras.en: Anna flew backward, sprawling onto the ground.
paras.zh: 安娜向后飞出，瘫倒在地。

paras.en: A dull pain rattled through her backside, but thankfully, the majority of her fall had been cushioned by the carpet.
paras.zh: 一阵钝痛窜过她的屁股，所幸跌落大部被地毯缓冲。

paras.en: Ow. “Hey!” the warm wall grumbled from above. “Watch where you’re going!” “You watch where you’re going!” Anna replied, and instantly regretted it.
paras.zh: 哎哟。“嘿！”那面温暖的“墙”在上方抱怨。“看路！”“你才看路！”安娜回嘴，旋即后悔。

paras.en: That’s not what someone hoping to be a royal ambassador on a grand tour should say. “I’m sorry,” she added, looking up to see the old, wrinkled face of Madam Eniola staring down at her. “Anna!” Madam Eniola bobbed a curtsy, her long brown skirt contrasting with the bundle of white ribbons she held in her arms. “My apologies, I didn’t recognize you in your…” Her eyes swept up and down. “Quilt?” Anna winced.
paras.zh: 想当巡游皇家使节的人不该这么说。“对不起，”她补了一句，抬头看见埃妮雪宝人那张布满皱纹的老脸正俯视她。“安娜！”埃妮雪宝人仓促行了个屈膝礼，她棕色长裙与臂中那束白“缎带”形成对比。“抱歉，我没认出你这身……”她的目光上下扫过。“被子？”安娜龇牙。

paras.en: Royal ambassadors should also probably remember to put on proper clothes before carrying out their important missions—and to comb their hair, too.
paras.zh: 皇家使节大概也该记得执行重要任务前穿上得体的衣服——还要梳头。

paras.en: Her hair didn’t look so much like hair as it resembled a bird’s nest. “That’s all right.” Anna clambered to her feet. “I should have been paying attention.” Like always.
paras.zh: 她的头发不像头发，倒像鸟窝。“没关系的。”安娜爬起身。“我本该专心些。”一如往常。

paras.en: She pulled her quilt tighter around her and hoped it looked more dignified than her ruffled pale green nightgown and bare feet.
paras.zh: 她把被子裹紧，但愿它比自己皱巴巴的浅绿睡衣和光脚看着体面些。

paras.en: Anna knew Eniola as one of the new villagers who’d moved to Arendelle from Tikaani, and specifically as the one who had taught Tikaani’s national anthem to Anna.
paras.zh: 安娜知道埃妮奥拉是从提卡尼迁来阿伦黛尔的新村民之一，确切说，是教过安娜提卡尼国歌的那位。

paras.en: Eniola lived in a cozy cottage on the outskirts of the farmlands.
paras.zh: 埃妮奥拉住在农地外围一间舒适的农舍。

paras.en: Holding her chin up, Anna asked, “What brings you to the castle, Madam Eniola?” Eniola sighed, and the creases on her face, which already held more lines than King Agnarr’s old sailing charts, seemed to increase tenfold as she frowned. “I’m here to speak to the queen.” She pursed her lips. “We all are.” Anna arched an eyebrow. “We?” Eniola stepped back to reveal more villagers lined up outside the Great Hall, staring at Anna.
paras.zh: 安娜抬着下巴问：“您来城堡有何事，埃妮雪宝人？”埃妮奥拉叹气，她脸上的皱纹本就比阿格瑞国王的旧航海图上的线还多，此刻一皱眉仿佛又增了十倍。“我来见女王。”她抿起嘴。“我们都是。”安娜挑起眉。“我们？”埃妮奥拉退后，露出大 hall外排成一队、正盯着安娜的更多村民。

paras.en: She recognized many of her friends—the candymaker, the farmer, the gas lamp lighter, the miller, the two blacksmiths, and many more.
paras.zh: 她认出许多朋友——制糖人、农夫、点灯人、磨坊主、两位铁匠，还有许多。

paras.en: Many, many more.
paras.zh: 许许多多。

paras.en: Anna’s eyes widened as she saw that the line of villagers extended from the double doors that led into the Great Hall all the way through the second great hall and into the portrait gallery.
paras.zh: 安娜睁大眼，只见村民的队伍从通往大 hall的双扇门，一路穿过第二大厅，直到画像廊。

paras.en: Anna’s mouth went dry, and she cleared her throat. “Why do you need to see Elsa?
paras.zh: 安娜口干舌燥，清了清嗓子。“你们为何要见艾莎？

paras.en: Erm, Queen Elsa?” she asked.
paras.zh: 呃，艾莎女王？”她问。

paras.en: Eniola held out her bundle of ribbons, which Anna saw now were not actually ribbons at all.
paras.zh: 埃妮奥拉伸出那束“缎带”，安娜这才看清它们根本不是缎带。

paras.en: They were strands of wheat, but instead of the long golden straws Anna was used to seeing from the tower window, these strands were short and mottled white—moldy and rotten all the way through and recognizable only by the heads of grains at the tops.
paras.zh: 它们是麦秆，却不是安娜从塔窗看惯的长长金秆，这些麦秆又短又斑白——从头烂到尾，只有顶端的麦穗还能认出。

paras.en: Even as Anna stared, a few seeds crumbled off into white dust.
paras.zh: 安娜正盯着，几粒种子已碎成白尘。

paras.en: First the animals, then the crops.
paras.zh: 先是动物，然后是庄稼。

paras.en: What was going on? “We woke this morning,” Eniola said, “and it’s all like this—everything!” The villagers grumbled in agreement behind her.
paras.zh: 怎么回事？“我们今早醒来，”埃妮奥拉说，“全都这样了——一切！”村民在她身后嘟囔着附和。

paras.en: Anna needed to tell Elsa about all these villagers— now . “Excuse me.” Anna tore her eyes away from the pitiful bundle in Madam Eniola’s arms and hurried downstairs in the direction of the Great Hall. “Pardon me, coming through!” The line shifted to allow Anna to wiggle by, and as she did, she saw that each and every person held white bundles similar to the one that Madam Eniola held: the pumpkins, usually the color of the sunset, had large unsightly splotches splashed across them, while the apples, usually red, round, and crisp, seemed to have the same consistency as raw dough.
paras.zh: 安娜得把这些村民的事告诉艾莎——马上。“失陪。”安娜把目光从埃妮雪宝人臂中那可怜的束上扯开，朝大 hall方向匆匆下楼。“借过，借过！”队伍挪动让安娜挤过，她看见每人都拿着与埃妮奥拉相似的白束：南瓜本是落日色，如今溅满难看的大斑；苹果本红润、圆实、脆生，此刻却像生面团般软塌。

paras.en: Up and down the line, Anna saw dried corn husks, white-mottled potatoes, and carrots as pale as cream.
paras.zh: 队伍上下，安娜看见干枯的玉米皮、斑白的土豆，和苍白如奶油的胡萝卜。

paras.en: Every crop, every vegetable, every grain Anna could think of, was destroyed.
paras.zh: 安娜能想到的每种庄稼、每种蔬菜、每种谷物，都毁了。

paras.en: Rotten.
paras.zh: 腐烂。

paras.en: The Blight.
paras.zh: 枯萎病。

paras.en: Anna picked up the pace.
paras.zh: 安娜加快脚步。

paras.en: Squeezing past a harried-looking woman, she at last made it through the doors and into the Great Hall.
paras.zh: 挤过一个神色慌张的女人，她终于穿门而入大 hall。

paras.en: The Great Hall, as its name suggested, was exactly that: great .
paras.zh: 大 hall，顾名思义，正是：大。

paras.en: It was the largest room in the castle, with tall windows and a gleaming chandelier, capable of fitting a hundred dashing lords and twirling ladies, Elsa’s throne, and a massive chocolate fountain all at the same time.
paras.zh: 它是城堡最大的房间，有高窗与闪亮的水晶灯，能同时容纳上百风度翩翩的贵族与旋转的淑女、艾莎的宝座，以及一座巨大的巧克力喷泉。

paras.en: Once, it had even hosted an entire ice skating rink when a late winter storm had threatened the annual ice dance competition.
paras.zh: 有一次，当晚冬风暴威胁年度冰舞赛时，它甚至容下过一整座溜冰场。

paras.en: But now, for the first time Anna could remember, the Great Hall felt small.
paras.zh: 可此刻，在安娜记忆里头一回，大 hall显得小了。

paras.en: The single file line cutting through the portrait gallery hadn’t prepared her for the absolute crush of people that filled the Great Hall.
paras.zh: 穿过画像廊的单行队伍，没让她准备好面对挤满大 hall的人潮。

paras.en: Even on the busiest market day on record—shortly after Elsa’s coronation, when everyone had come to see their new magical sovereign—there had not been this many people.
paras.zh: 即便在记载中最繁忙的市集日——艾莎加冕后不久，人人都来见新魔法君主时——也没这么多人。

paras.en: Or maybe there had been, but joy didn’t take up nearly as much room as fear.
paras.zh: 或许有过，但欢乐占的空间远不及恐惧。

paras.en: Fear filled the hall, as large and present as one of the Earth Giants in her mother’s tales.
paras.zh: 恐惧填满大厅，如母亲故事里的大地巨人般庞大而真切。

paras.en: The voices all around Anna were pulled tight, sounding as if they would break at any moment. “Everything is gone!
paras.zh: 安娜四周的声音绷得紧紧，仿佛随时会断。“全完了！

paras.en: It’s been ruined!” “My cattle!
paras.zh: 都毁了！”“我的牛！

paras.en: They won’t wake up!” “Never in all my days!
paras.zh: 叫不醒！”“我这辈子从没！

paras.en: It’s as if the very earth has gone awry!” “Do you think this has to do with the Northuldra?” “No,” someone grunted. “King Runeard, may he rest in greatest peace, made sure they would never trouble Arendelle again.” “And the animals…” Anna heard a strange noise from outside.
paras.zh: 仿佛大地都乱了套！”“你觉得这和北地人有关吗？”“不，”有人咕哝。“鲁内尔德国王，愿他安息，早确保他们再不会来烦阿伦黛尔。”“还有动物……”安娜听见外面传来怪声。

paras.en: It sounded like a mix of children learning how to play the violin crossed with the sounds of a zoo.
paras.zh: 那声音像学琴的孩子与动物园声响的混合。

paras.en: Peering through the window, Anna gasped.
paras.zh: 安娜从窗里窥看，倒吸一口气。

paras.en: The courtyard was just as full as the Great Hall, filled to the brim with farmers and animals.
paras.zh: 庭院和大 hall一样满，挤满了农夫与动物。

paras.en: Sheep had broken loose from their shepherds, and the herding dogs, usually so careful, seemed distracted, following something in the air that no one else could see.
paras.zh: 羊儿挣脱了牧人，平时那么谨慎的牧羊犬似乎分了神，追着空中别人看不见的东西。

paras.en: All the animals looked like walking ghosts, their fur and hides the same sickly yellow-white.
paras.zh: 所有动物都像行走的鬼，皮毛是同一种病态的黄白。

paras.en: And even as Anna watched, a cow and two horses knelt to the ground, their eyes as large and black as lumps of coal, their mouths open and tongues lolling out until, suddenly, they fell asleep.
paras.zh: 安娜正看着，一头牛和两匹马跪倒在地，眼睛如煤块般又大又黑，嘴张着、舌垂着，直到忽然，它们睡着了。

paras.en: Anna’s stomach turned. “Excuse me,” she said over and over again as she tried to wade her way to the front of the hall, toward the throne where Elsa must be.
paras.zh: 安娜胃里翻腾。“借过，”她一遍遍说，想挤过厅前，奔向艾莎必在的宝座。

paras.en: Grumbling people followed in her wake as she wove in and out of the crowd, and more than once, she had to tug her quilt from beneath someone’s boot.
paras.zh: 嘟囔的人跟在她身后，她在人群中穿进穿出，不止一次得从某人靴下拽回被子。

paras.en: But with one last push, she made it to the throne, relief washing over her as she found Elsa standing there, just as Wael, the local journalist, yelled out, “That’s not going to help us!” “Wael,” Elsa said, “if you would please only just—” “ Ah-hem!
paras.zh: 最后一推，她挤到宝座前，看见艾莎立在那里，如释重负——恰在此时，当地记者韦尔喊道：“那可救不了我们！”“韦尔，”艾莎说，“请你只——”“咳咳！

paras.en: Winter is fast approaching.” Wael’s ink-stained fingers gestured wildly. “We will have nothing to eat!
paras.zh: 冬天快到了。”韦尔沾墨的手指疯狂比划。“我们将无食可吃！

paras.en: We deserve answers—and it’s your responsibility as queen to give us answers and take care of your people!
paras.zh: 我们该有答案——而你作为女王，有责任给我们答案、照顾你的子民！

paras.en: We don’t have enough food to last the week!” A hush fell over the Great Hall at his words.
paras.zh: 我们的粮食撑不过一周！”他的话让大 hall一片肃静。

paras.en: Elsa stood tall, not backing down, but Anna knew her sister.
paras.zh: 艾莎高高站着，毫不退让，可安娜了解姐姐。

paras.en: She could see the overbright sheen of her eyes.
paras.zh: 她看得见姐姐眼中那过亮的光泽。

paras.en: It wasn’t just ice that could sparkle in chandelier light.
paras.zh: 能在水晶灯下闪烁的不只是冰。

paras.en: Tears could, too.
paras.zh: 泪也可以。

paras.en: Anger, bright and hot, swept through Anna. “Don’t speak to my sister that way!” she burst out as she reached Elsa’s side. “Anna,” Elsa said, her voice low, “I’ve got this, it’s fine—” Anna glared at Wael. “No, it’s not!” The man glared right back. “Elsa is doing her best,” Anna plowed on, her words coming fast and furious. “She has a plan!
paras.zh: 明亮而炽热的怒火扫过安娜。“别那样对我姐姐说话！”她冲到艾莎身边脱口而出。“安娜，”艾莎低声说，“我应付得来，没事——”安娜瞪着韦尔。“不，不是！”那人也回瞪。“艾莎已尽全力，”安娜继续，语速又快又烈。“她有方案！

paras.en: She’ll fix everything before she leaves on the grand tour!” Next to her, she heard Elsa’s breath catch. “Anna—” “That’s in just three days,” a tired-looking villager said, her arms full of what Anna thought was supposed to be emerald zucchini but now looked more like great white slugs. “Can the queen really—” “Anna—” Elsa tried again.
paras.zh: 她会在巡游前把一切修好！”身侧，她听见艾莎倒吸一口气。“安娜——”“就剩三天了，”一个面露倦容的村民说，怀里抱着安娜原以为该是翡翠色西葫芦、此刻却更像大白蛞蝓的东西。“女王真能——”“安娜——”艾莎又试。

paras.en: But Anna didn’t listen.
paras.zh: 可安娜没听。

paras.en: She was going to stick up for her sister.
paras.zh: 她要为姐姐撑腰。

paras.en: Elsa might be able to stand there and listen to people doubt her, but Anna wasn’t going to have any of it. “Of course Elsa can!” Anna said, holding on to their glowing secret, the promise of the mysterious book. “ANNA.” Elsa flung out her hand.
paras.zh: 艾莎或许能立在那儿听人质疑，可安娜绝不答应。“艾莎当然能！”安娜说，攥着她们发光的秘密、那本神秘书的承诺。“安娜。”艾莎甩出手。

paras.en: There was a time when icy spears would have sprouted from the floor, but Elsa had control of her magical powers now.
paras.zh: 曾几何时，冰矛会从地面冒出，可如今艾莎已能掌控魔力。

paras.en: Instead of a dangerously pointed ice spear, it was now just a gesture—to remind her sister to watch what she said. “I apologize for my sister,” Elsa said to the Great Hall at large.
paras.zh: 如今那不再是危险的尖冰矛，只是个手势——提醒妹妹说话小心。“我替妹妹道歉，”艾莎对大 hall众人说。

paras.en: Her chin had lifted in the exact same way Anna remembered her father lifting his during special ceremonies, when he was trying to be his most regal.
paras.zh: 她抬下巴的样子，和安娜记得父亲在特殊典礼上、想显出最王者风范时一模一样。

paras.en: Anna opened her mouth to protest, but one glance at Elsa’s expression squashed any words she had left.
paras.zh: 安娜张嘴想抗议，可瞥一眼艾莎的神情，就把剩下的话全压了回去。

paras.en: Her cheeks flushed.
paras.zh: 她脸颊发烫。

paras.en: Burning anger transformed into burning embarrassment.
paras.zh: 燃烧的怒火化成了燃烧的尴尬。

paras.en: What had she done? “I understand your concern,” Elsa continued, her voice steady and cool. “And I share it.
paras.zh: 她都做了什么？“我理解你们的担忧，”艾莎继续，声音平稳而冷静。“我也同此心。

paras.en: What I’ve been trying to say is, to show my commitment to solving the problem of the ruined crops and sick animals, I’m postponing my grand tour until I can sort out this troubling matter at hand.” “What?” Anna gasped before she could stop herself, shocked her sister would cancel her grand tour.
paras.zh: 我一直在说的是，为表明我解决庄稼毁坏与动物生病之问题的决心，我将推迟巡游，直到理清这眼前的麻烦。”“什么？”安娜没忍住倒吸一口气，震惊姐姐竟会取消巡游。

paras.en: She didn’t understand what Elsa was thinking—what if postponement convinced the dignitaries and people from other lands that Arendelle wasn’t, in fact, opening its gates, but closing them once again?
paras.zh: 她不懂艾莎怎么想——若推迟让各国使节与百姓以为阿伦黛尔并非敞开大门、而是再次关闭，怎么办？

paras.en: And from the shocked look on Wael’s face and the murmur of the crowd, Anna knew she wasn’t the only one surprised by this announcement.
paras.zh: 从韦尔震惊的脸与人群的低语，安娜知道自己并非唯一对这宣告吃惊的人。

paras.en: If they hadn’t been standing in front of a large crowd of stressed villagers, Anna imagined Elsa would be rubbing her temples and sighing right about now.
paras.zh: 若不是立在一大群焦虑村民前，安娜想，艾莎这会儿定在揉太阳穴、叹气。

paras.en: But they were standing in front of stressed villagers, and her sister never failed to live up to what was expected of her: she was queen, regal and unflappable. “Because,” Elsa said, speaking loud enough for all to hear, “the royal ship is loaded with rations of food, apples, wheat, dried vegetables, cheeses, cans of pickled herring, and sausages.
paras.zh: 可他们立在一大群焦虑村民前，姐姐从未辜负众望：她是女王，威严而镇定。“因为，”艾莎说，声音大到人尽可闻，“皇家船满载口粮：苹果、小麦、干菜、奶酪、腌鲱鱼罐头与香肠。

paras.en: We need to share our surplus, or else the villagers with Blight-stricken farms will suffer further.” Once again, Elsa had come up with the perfect solution—one so obvious Anna wondered why she hadn’t thought of it herself.
paras.zh: 我们需分享盈余，否则染上枯萎病的农场村民将更受苦。”艾莎又一次想出完美方案——简单得安娜奇怪自己怎没想到。

paras.en: Elsa was so good at seeing the larger tapestry, while Anna let herself get distracted by whatever thread was dangling in front of her at that very moment. “That amount of food will only last us all three days at the most ,” Wael protested. “And what makes you think the food on your ship hasn’t soured, Your Majesty ?” There was something about his all-knowing attitude that made Anna want to release Marshmallow, Elsa’s dangerous giant snowman—and Olaf’s little brother—on him.
paras.zh: 艾莎那么擅见大局，安娜却总被眼前晃的线头分神。“那些食物最多撑我们三天，”韦尔抗议。“您凭什么认为船上的食物没坏，陛下？”他那种万事通的态度，让安娜想放出棉花糖——艾莎那危险的巨型雪人、雪宝的弟弟——去对付他。

paras.en: But seeing as that wasn’t an option, since Marshmallow was currently the housekeeper for the ice palace on top of the North Mountain, she’d settle for glaring at Wael instead. “I’ll scour our kitchen here,” Elsa offered.
paras.zh: 可既然不行——棉花糖如今是北山冰宫的管家——她便满足于瞪韦尔。“我会清查这儿的厨房，”艾莎提议。

paras.en: Beside her, Kai scribbled a note onto a ream of parchment, while brown-haired and kind Olina, in charge of overseeing the kitchen staff, clasped her gloved hands together in deep thought.
paras.zh: 她身旁，凯伊在大幅羊皮纸上疾书，而棕发和善、负责监管厨房人员的奥丽娜，则十指交握、陷入深思。

paras.en: Nothing ever missed Olina’s careful eye, and Anna knew that she was probably already running through a mental list of food the castle kitchen could provide. “What if that food’s gone bad, too?” cried a voice from the crowd.
paras.zh: 没什么能逃过奥丽娜审慎的眼，安娜知道她大概已在心中列起厨房能供的食材清单。“万一那些食物也坏了呢？”人群中一声喊。

paras.en: Anna held her breath while everyone stared at Elsa.
paras.zh: 众人盯着艾莎，安娜屏息。

paras.en: Elsa, however, looked at only one person: Olina.
paras.zh: 可艾莎只看着一人：奥丽娜。

paras.en: The woman gave a slight shake of her head: the kitchen was still fine.
paras.zh: 那女人微微摇头：厨房尚好。

paras.en: Anna exhaled, thankful that at least this one piece of news wasn’t terrible. “As your queen,” Elsa said loudly, her voice strong, “I will see to it that you have food.” The crowd murmured, but Anna could hear the shift in tone.
paras.zh: 安娜舒气，庆幸至少这消息不糟。“作为你们的女王，”艾莎大声说，声音有力，“我必确保你们有食。”人群低语，可安娜听出语气变了。

paras.en: The conversation around her no longer vibrated with the intensity of a string pulled too tight.
paras.zh: 她身边的交谈不再如绷太紧的弦般颤栗。

paras.en: Instead, the words loosened and the conversation relaxed as the villagers considered Elsa’s proposal. “I think it’s a good idea,” Tuva called out. “My wife and I accept.” And the two blacksmiths nodded in agreement. “I accept, too,” Eniola called out, and soon other villagers voiced their agreement as well.
paras.zh: 相反，话语松了，交谈放松了，村民思量艾莎的提议。“我觉得是好主意，”图娃喊。“我和妻子接受。”两位铁匠点头同意。“我也接受，”埃妮奥拉喊，不久其他村民也纷纷赞同。

paras.en: All except for Wael, who only reluctantly nodded, but not before adding, “Fine—but the Village Crown will make sure that you keep Anna’s promise that the solution will be found before three days are up.” Pride filled Anna as Kai led the disgruntled villagers back out of the castle and toward the harbor to collect the supplies from the royal ship.
paras.zh: 除韦尔外都同意，他只不情愿地点头，却不忘加一句：“行——但村冠奖会确保你们守住安娜的承诺，三天内找出解法。”安娜满心骄傲，看凯伊领着不满的村民出城堡、朝港湾去取皇家船的物资。

paras.en: She felt like cheering, but instead she settled on a quiet squeal, and whispered to Elsa, “That was brilliant .” But Elsa didn’t smile back.
paras.zh: 她想欢呼，却只轻轻尖叫一声，对艾莎耳语：“太妙了。”可艾莎没回笑。

paras.en: Instead, she walked to one of the more secretive side entrances to the Great Hall, hidden from view by a tapestry. “Anna,” she said without turning around, “can we talk for a minute, please?” Anna’s smile slipped away as she followed her older sister.
paras.zh: 相反，她走向大 hall一处更隐秘的侧门，被挂毯遮住。“安娜，”她背身说，“我们能谈一分钟吗？”安娜的笑消失，跟着姐姐。

paras.en: She might not know why the farm animals were sleeping or why their fur was turning white, or why the kingdom’s food seemed to be turning to dust and ash, but she did know one thing: she was absolutely, completely, 100 percent in trouble. “Three days?!” Elsa whirled on Anna as soon as the tapestry fell back in place, obscuring them from view. “Anna of Arendelle, how on earth can I fix this mess, and so soon?” Even though Elsa didn’t raise her voice, Anna could hear her frustration boiling underneath. “Between this and Kristoff—” “Kristoff?” Anna interrupted, furrowing her eyebrows. “What about Kristoff?” Elsa closed her eyes and rubbed her temples, just as Anna had suspected Elsa had wanted to do earlier. “He’s not here.
paras.zh: 她或许不知农畜为何沉睡、毛为何变白、王国食物为何化尘成灰，可她确知一件事：她绝对、完全、百分之百有麻烦了。“三天？！”挂毯一落放回原位、遮住她们，艾莎就转向安娜。“阿伦黛尔的安娜，我到底怎么能在这么快修好这烂摊子？”尽管艾莎没提高嗓门，安娜却听出她压抑的挫败。“这事加上克里斯托夫——”“克里斯托夫？”安娜皱眉打断。“克里斯托夫怎么了？”艾莎闭眼揉太阳穴，正如安娜早先猜她想做的。“他不在这儿。

paras.en: I thought he’d be back by now, but…” Worry zipped through Anna, but she forced herself to shrug. “I’m sure he’s fine,” she said. “You know how happy Bulda is whenever he visits.” She smiled, thinking of the mountain troll who’d raised Kristoff as her own. “I bet you he’s delayed because he’s so full of mushroom stew that he’s too heavy for Sven to carry, and they have to walk.” But it seemed Elsa couldn’t be distracted from her worry, not even with the funny image.
paras.zh: 我以为他这会儿该回来了，可……”担忧窜过安娜，她却强迫自己耸肩。“我肯定他没事，”她说。“你知道布尔达每次见他多开心。”她笑着想起那位把克里斯托夫当自己孩子养大的山地地精。“我打赌他耽搁是因为蘑菇炖菜吃太撑，重得斯文驮不动，只好走回来。”可艾莎似乎无法被这滑稽画面分心。

paras.en: Elsa shook her head. “It’s so much pressure.
paras.zh: 艾莎摇头。“压力太大了。

paras.en: I don’t know what I can do.” “You mean, what we can do…with a secret book full of magic!” Anna said.
paras.zh: 我不知道能做什么。”“你是说，我们能做什么……用那本满是魔法的秘密书！”安娜说。

paras.en: Elsa groaned. “ Oh , Anna!” She shook her head. “I know you want it to be, but I don’t think magic is the answer to all of our problems.” “Okay, I hear you, but look .” Anna held out Secrets of the Magic Makers . “There is so much information in here.” She flipped through the pages until she found the one she was looking for. “See?
paras.zh: 艾莎呻吟。“噢，安娜！”她摇头。“我知道你希望如此，可我不觉得魔法能解答我们所有问题。”“好，我听到了，可你看。”安娜举起《魔法创造者之秘》。“这里面信息多着呢。”她翻到要找的那页。“看？

paras.en: This one grants your dreams .” Elsa sighed. “Anna, I told you not to go back in the secret room.” “I didn’t go back into it.
paras.zh: 这一条能成全你的梦。”艾莎叹气。“安娜，我让你别回密室。”“我没回去。

paras.en: I grabbed this book before I left the first time.
paras.zh: 我第一次离开前就拿了这本书。

paras.en: Look at it!” Reluctantly, Elsa glanced down at the page that had been pushed under her nose, but before she had a chance to skim, Gerda pulled back the tapestry, wearing her signature green skirt, jacket, and cap, and holding Elsa’s great big calendar. “Your Majesty, I’m sorry,” the woman said, and Anna could hear the sympathy in her voice, “but even with the grand tour postponed, this fiasco with the sickness has put us behind schedule.
paras.zh: 看这个！”艾莎不情愿地低头瞥了下顶到鼻尖的那页，可还没来得及略读，格尔达就拉开挂毯，穿着她标志性的绿裙、绿外套、绿帽，拿着艾莎那本大日历。“陛下，抱歉，”那女人说，安娜听得出她声里的同情，“可即便巡游推迟，这场病乱子还是让我们落后了日程。

paras.en: And now you must write explanations to all the different dignitaries and heads of countries to explain why you can’t make it.” Elsa took a deep breath. “Yes, of course, Gerda, you’re right.
paras.zh: 现在您得给各国使节与元首写说明，解释为何去不成。”艾莎深吸一口气。“对，当然，格尔达，你说得对。

paras.en: The work of a queen is never complete.” She glanced over at Anna, who held her breath. “Here.
paras.zh: 女王的工作永无止境。”她瞥了眼屏息的安娜。“给。

paras.en: Let me have that book.
paras.zh: 把那本书给我。

paras.en: Maybe you’re right.
paras.zh: 也许你是对的。

paras.en: I promise I’ll look at it as soon as I have a spare minute.” “Of—of course,” Anna said, happy to share.
paras.zh: 我保证一有空就翻。”“当——当然，”安娜说，乐意分享。

paras.en: But she would have been even happier if Elsa had told Gerda that Anna had found something important.
paras.zh: 可若艾莎告诉格尔达安娜发现了重要东西，她会更开心。

paras.en: That they were working on discovering a solution together . “I’d like to meet with an animal expert now to get their opinion,” Elsa said, and Anna noticed again that she was tugging on her fingers. “And a botanist.
paras.zh: 说他们正一起寻找解法。“我想现在见位动物专家，听听意见，”艾莎说，安娜再次注意到她在拽手指。“还有植物学家。

paras.en: I’m not sure what should be done first….” “If you need someone to write letters, I can help with that,” Anna offered. “I’ve read up on all the different etiquettes of each country.” “That should be just fine, dear,” Gerda said, her pencil already flying over the calendar to adjust it. “Just make sure Elsa signs them before you mail them.” “I will!” Anna promised, happy to help Elsa and happy to have something to do while she waited for Kristoff to return to the castle.
paras.zh: 我不确定该先做什么……”“若需要人写信，我能帮忙，”安娜提议。“我读过各国不同的礼仪。”“那就好，亲爱的，”格尔达说，铅笔已在日历上飞快调整。“只要确保艾莎签名后再寄。”“我会的！”安娜承诺，既高兴能帮艾莎，也高兴有事可做、等着克里斯托夫回城堡。

paras.en: She had so many things she wanted to ask him, starting with, How do the trolls say we can cure the Blight? and leading to, Do you know how to read the mysterious ancient runes in my mother’s book? “Thanks, Anna,” Elsa said as Gerda hurried away to arrange everything. “If that’s all taken care of, then I need to get going.
paras.zh: 她有太多想问他，先是“地精说我们怎么治枯萎病？”再到“你认得我母亲书里那些神秘古如尼文吗？”“谢了，安娜，”格尔达匆匆去安排时艾莎说。“若都安排好了，我得走了。

paras.en: I’ll make sure I visit you before I go to bed, okay?” But she turned before Anna could even nod.
paras.zh: 我睡前一定来看你，好吗？”可她转身时安娜还没来得及点头。

paras.en: And though Anna stood in the middle of a crowded castle still bursting to the brim with villagers, the sight of Elsa walking away from her had never made Anna feel more alone.
paras.zh: 尽管安娜站在挤满村民、仍满到溢出的城堡中央，看着艾莎离自己而去，她从未感到如此孤独。

paras.en: THROUGH HER BEDROOM WINDOW, Anna watched the exodus of the castle staff trailing over the Bridge of Arches and into the darkening village.
paras.zh: 安娜透过卧室窗，望着城堡仆从的队伍过拱桥、没入渐暗的村庄。

paras.en: That afternoon, Elsa had given the staff the option of taking off from work with pay so that they could go help their nearby relatives whose animals and crops were suffering from the Blight.
paras.zh: 那天下午，艾莎给了仆从带薪休假的选择，好去帮附近染上枯萎病的牲口与庄稼的亲戚。

paras.en: After she had written the letters, Anna had changed into her travel cloak and spent the rest of the day helping unload food from the royal ship and handing it out to the villagers amidst the groaning of sick animals.
paras.zh: 写完信后，安娜换上旅行斗篷，用那天余下的时间帮忙从皇家船卸粮、在病畜的呻吟中分发给村民。

paras.en: She’d wanted to cover her ears, but then she thought that would be the cowardly thing to do.
paras.zh: 她曾想捂住耳朵，却又想那太懦弱。

paras.en: She couldn’t just ignore the ugly things in the world around her.
paras.zh: 她不能对周遭丑陋之事视而不见。

paras.en: If people did that, no one would ever help at all, and nothing would become well again.
paras.zh: 若人人如此，便无人会帮忙，一切也永无好转。

paras.en: And so Anna had gone to help the farmers dab white fur with wet washcloths to try to keep their livestock alert.
paras.zh: 于是安娜去帮农夫用湿布轻拭白毛，试图让牲口保持清醒。

paras.en: She’d stroked a sad little foal’s fuzzy ears as it curled up next to the sleeping form of its mother, who did not so much as stir at the foal’s pitiful nickers.
paras.zh: 她抚过一匹伤心小马驹毛茸茸的耳，它蜷在沉睡的母亲身旁，母亲对马驹可怜的嘶鸣动也不动。

paras.en: Anna turned away from the window and paced, still in her travel cloak from earlier.
paras.zh: 安娜转离窗，踱起步，仍穿着早先的旅行斗篷。

paras.en: Just as she’d thought, Elsa hadn’t come to see her.
paras.zh: 正如所料，艾莎没来看她。

paras.en: She knew her sister was busy, but…Anna glanced out the window again, and made up her mind.
paras.zh: 她知姐姐忙，可……安娜又瞥向窗外，下了决心。

paras.en: Lighting an oil lamp, she quickly made her way through the now empty halls of the castle to Elsa’s council chambers.
paras.zh: 点起油灯，她快步穿过如今空荡的城堡长廊，去艾莎的议事厅。

paras.en: As Anna approached the doors, she was surprised to see no yellow light trickling out from beneath.
paras.zh: 安娜走近门，惊讶地发现门下没有黄光漏出。

paras.en: Her breath quickened.
paras.zh: 她呼吸加快。

paras.en: Maybe something else had gone wrong in the village, something so bad that it had pulled Elsa away from the signing of the dignitaries’ letters.
paras.zh: 也许村里又出了岔子，严重到把艾莎从使节信的签署中拉走。

paras.en: Anna knocked, and when there was no answer, she let herself in.
paras.zh: 安娜敲门，无人应，便自己进去。

paras.en: Elsa was nowhere to be found.
paras.zh: 哪儿都没有艾莎。

paras.en: But—Anna felt her mouth tighten.
paras.zh: 可——安娜感到嘴绷紧。

paras.en: There, lying unopened on the desk, was Secrets of the Magic Makers .
paras.zh: 桌上，未打开地躺着《魔法创造者之秘》。

paras.en: It was clear Elsa hadn’t touched it.
paras.zh: 显然艾莎没碰过它。

paras.en: But she needed to!
paras.zh: 可她必须碰！

paras.en: Anna knew people said she was too optimistic, naïve about the way the world worked, and maybe that was true, but she had faith in stories.
paras.zh: 安娜知道人们说她太乐观、对世界运作太天真，也许没错，可她相信故事。

paras.en: And she had faith that there was a solution to any problem, just as long as one kept looking.
paras.zh: 她也相信任何问题都有解法，只要不断寻找。

paras.en: She just needed to get Elsa to listen to her.
paras.zh: 她只需让艾莎听她。

paras.en: Anna hurried back through the castle, gripping Secrets of the Magic Makers .
paras.zh: 安娜攥着《魔法创造者之秘》匆匆穿回城堡。

paras.en: She looked everywhere for her sister, until her eyes grew heavy with sleep as the sky continued to darken outside the castle.
paras.zh: 她到处找姐姐，直到城堡外天色愈暗、眼皮愈沉。

paras.en: Maybe Elsa wasn’t in the castle at all.
paras.zh: 也许艾莎根本不在城堡。

paras.en: Reluctantly, Anna trudged back to her room.
paras.zh: 安娜不情愿地拖步回房。

paras.en: And then… Voices.
paras.zh: 然后……人声。

paras.en: Voices coming from Elsa’s bedroom.
paras.zh: 从艾莎卧室传来的声音。

paras.en: Anna pressed her ear to the bedroom door, and though she couldn’t make out the words, she recognized the low timbre of Kai’s voice as well as Gerda’s northern cadence.
paras.zh: 安娜把耳贴门，虽听不清字句，却认出凯伊低沉的嗓音与格尔达的北方腔调。

paras.en: Anna staggered from the door.
paras.zh: 安娜从门边踉跄退开。

paras.en: Elsa was having a meeting without her!
paras.zh: 艾莎在开会，没叫她！

paras.en: There was a time when Anna knew Elsa would have invited her to each and every single meeting, would have sought out her advice, but now…now it seemed Elsa no longer had any need for her little sister at all.
paras.zh: 曾几何时，安娜知道艾莎会邀她参加每场会、征求她的意见，可现在……现在艾莎似乎再不需要小妹妹。

paras.en: Elsa had chosen to shut her out once more.
paras.zh: 艾莎再次选择把她关在门外。

paras.en: With all the dignity she could muster, Anna walked slowly away from the door, but as soon as she was out of sight from Elsa’s bedroom, she broke into a run, trying to escape the emotion that threatened to overwhelm her.
paras.zh: 安娜用尽所能的尊严，缓缓走离门，可一离开艾莎卧室的视线，便拔腿狂奔，想逃开那要将她淹没的情绪。

paras.en: Rushing into the sanctuary of her own bedroom, Anna slammed the door shut and sat cross-legged on her shaggy pink rug, Secrets of the Magic Makers spread open in front of her.
paras.zh: 冲进自己卧室这方避难所，安娜砰地关上门，盘腿坐在毛茸茸的粉毯上，《魔法创造者之秘》摊在面前。

paras.en: She studied the book, which blurred slightly in her gaze from unshed tears.
paras.zh: 她研究着书，书在她含泪的视线里微微模糊。

paras.en: Anna flipped through it again, and a loose page fell out, one that looked like it was ripped from another book.
paras.zh: 安娜又翻，一页散页掉出，像是从别处撕来的。

paras.en: Reaching for it, Anna was reminded of the same loose page that had given her so much hope the previous night.
paras.zh: 她伸手去拿，想起昨夜给过她莫大希望的那张散页。

paras.en: The page with a spell to make your dreams come true.
paras.zh: 那是张让梦想成真的咒语页。

paras.en: Her tears dried up, and Anna felt her sadness replaced by another rising emotion, one growing so fast and so big that it seemed to take on a life of its own.
paras.zh: 她的泪干了，安娜感到悲伤被另一种升起的情绪取代，它涨得又快又大，仿佛有了自己的生命。

paras.en: For a moment, she thought she understood what Elsa experienced when she used her magic.
paras.zh: 有那么一刻，她以为自己懂了艾莎用魔法时的感受。

paras.en: Anna had to let this wild, untamed hope free—even if Elsa didn’t think it would work, there could be no downside to trying.
paras.zh: 安娜必须释放这狂野不羁的希望——即便艾莎觉得没用，试一试也无妨。

paras.en: And if it worked, maybe the doors to council meetings would reopen to Anna.
paras.zh: 若成了，也许议事厅的门会重向安娜敞开。

paras.en: Maybe the strained tension between Anna and Elsa would disappear.
paras.zh: 也许安娜与艾莎间的紧绷会消散。

paras.en: Because that was her dearest dream: Anna hoped she could help the people of Arendelle, working together with Elsa to find a solution that would make everything right again.
paras.zh: 因为那是她最深的梦：安娜希望帮阿伦黛尔百姓，与艾莎并肩找到让一切复原的解法。

paras.en: And in the process, Anna hoped Elsa would realize she needed her sister, just the same way that Anna needed Elsa.
paras.zh: 而在此过程中，安娜希望艾莎明白她需要妹妹，正如安娜需要艾莎。

paras.en: Tugging out the loose page, Anna whispered the words out loud: “Wild, awake!
paras.zh: 安娜抽出散页，轻声念出那些字：“荒野，醒吧！

paras.en: Wind and snow!
paras.zh: 风与雪！

paras.en: Plant the seed And watch it grow!
paras.zh: 种下种子，看它生长！

paras.en: Say this spell, And you shall see All your dreams Come to be!” A beat of silence.
paras.zh: 念此咒语，你将看见，所有梦想，皆会成真！”片刻寂静。

paras.en: Anna felt foolish.
paras.zh: 安娜觉得自己傻。

paras.en: What had she thought would happen after she read the spell?
paras.zh: 她念完咒语后，以为会发生什么？

paras.en: That her sister would materialize in front of her?
paras.zh: 姐姐会凭空出现在面前？

paras.en: Come racing in with open arms and lead her back to the secret room?
paras.zh: 张开双臂冲进来，领她回密室？

paras.en: Without her wild hope tugging her forward, Anna deflated.
paras.zh: 没了那股狂野希望牵引，安娜泄了气。

paras.en: She crumpled up the dream spell page and put it in her cloak pocket, not wanting to look at it anymore.
paras.zh: 她把梦境咒语页揉成一团，塞进斗篷口袋，不愿再看。

paras.en: From the dressing room, Anna suddenly heard footsteps followed by voices. “Poor thing, there is so much on her mind,” a voice floated through the door.
paras.zh: 从更衣室，安娜忽然听见脚步声伴着人声。“可怜的孩子，她心事太多了，”一个声音飘过门。

paras.en: Anna recognized it as Gerda’s. “She bears so much,” Kai agreed, his voice loud and clear as they passed right by her door.
paras.zh: 安娜认出是格尔达的。“她负担太重，”凯伊附和，声音洪亮清晰，正从她门外经过。

paras.en: The council meeting must be over by now.
paras.zh: 议事会这会儿该结束了。

paras.en: Which meant that at any second, there would be a knock on her door, and Elsa would ask to come in.
paras.zh: 也就是说，随时会有敲门声，艾莎会请求进来。

paras.en: Any second now, she’d tell Anna how sorry she was that it took her so long to listen to Anna’s suggestion and that Anna was right, they needed to look at the books in the secret room.
paras.zh: 随时，她会告诉安娜，她花了那么久才听进建议、很抱歉，是安娜对了，他们该看密室里的书。

paras.en: Then Anna would show her Secrets of the Magic Makers and the loose page with the spell, and they would fix everything.
paras.zh: 然后安娜会给她看《魔法创造者之秘》和带咒语的散页，一起修好一切。

paras.en: They would do it together.
paras.zh: 他们会一起做。

paras.en: After all, they were sisters.
paras.zh: 毕竟，她们是姐妹。

paras.en: Anna sat up straighter on her rug and waited…and waited.
paras.zh: 安娜在毯上坐直，等……等。

paras.en: The knock never came. —— Anna’s dreams were nightmare-tossed yet again.
paras.zh: 敲门声始终没来。——安娜的梦又被噩梦翻搅。

paras.en: She dreamed of dark shadows in treetops, Earth Giants destroying the village, and a shipwreck on a stormy sea.
paras.zh: 她梦见树梢的黑影、大地巨人摧毁村庄、风暴海上的沉船。

paras.en: And then—ice.
paras.zh: 然后——冰。

paras.en: Anna had told Elsa she did not remember the moments during which she’d turned to ice.
paras.zh: 安娜曾告诉艾莎，她不记得自己变成冰那几刻。

paras.en: But that was a lie.
paras.zh: 可那是谎。

paras.en: She would never forget the horror of warm flesh turning cold, then all sensation fleeing as her warm blood frosted into stone-cold crystal.
paras.zh: 她永忘不了温热血肉转冷、所有知觉逃逸、温血冻成冰冷水晶的恐惧。
