paras.en: She would never forget the last bit of heat escaping through her final breath, would never forget seeing her sister sob, and the unique pain of not being able to do absolutely anything at all.
paras.zh: 她永忘不了最后一丝热气随终息逃逸，永忘不了看姐姐啜泣，以及那种全然无能为力的独特痛楚。

paras.en: Tonight, Anna’s nightmares would not let her forget.
paras.zh: 今夜，安娜的噩梦不让她忘。

paras.en: And so Anna’s dream morphed….
paras.zh: 于是安娜的梦变了……

paras.en: She was a girl of ice, standing outside the castle, only able to peer into the window and never enter through the doors.
paras.zh: 她成了冰女孩，立在城堡外，只能从窗窥看，却进不了门。

paras.en: Inside, she could see Elsa reading aloud to a girl, whose glossy white hair was pulled back in two braids.
paras.zh: 里面，她看见艾莎给一个女孩朗诵，那女孩油亮白发梳成两条辫。

paras.en: Anna didn’t recognize the girl—her back was to the window—but she did recognize the girl’s dress, a soft green one with sunflowers embroidered on the hem.
paras.zh: 安娜认不出那女孩——她背对窗——却认得她的裙子，一条柔绿、裙摆绣着向日葵的裙。

paras.en: Anna’s birthday dress.
paras.zh: 安娜的生日裙。

paras.en: She could see Kristoff entering the room, strumming his guitar and smiling at the girl.
paras.zh: 她看见克里斯托夫进屋，弹着吉他冲女孩笑。

paras.en: Who are you?
paras.zh: 你是谁？

paras.en: Anna wanted to yell at the ivory-haired girl.
paras.zh: 安娜想朝那象牙发女孩喊。

paras.en: Turn around!
paras.zh: 转过来！

paras.en: But her frozen lips could not speak, and Anna had to wait, impatiently and horribly, until, at last, the girl turned around to reveal…Anna’s eyes.
paras.zh: 可她冻住的唇发不出声，安娜只能不耐又可怕地等，直到那女孩终于转身，露出……安娜的眼睛。

paras.en: Anna’s nose.
paras.zh: 安娜的鼻。

paras.en: Anna’s smile.
paras.zh: 安娜的微笑。

paras.en: The white-haired girl was Anna—but she wasn’t.
paras.zh: 那白发的女孩是安娜——又不是。

paras.en: Anna had been replaced.
paras.zh: 安娜被取代了。

paras.en: By this other person.
paras.zh: 被这另一个人。

paras.en: And no one in the room, not Kristoff, Olaf, Kai, Gerda—not even her own sister—realized it.
paras.zh: 屋里没人——克里斯托夫、雪宝、凯伊、格尔达——连她亲姐姐——都没察觉。

paras.en: Or maybe they did and they simply did not care.
paras.zh: 或许察觉了，却根本不在乎。

paras.en: A high howl pierced the air, and the ice shattered.
paras.zh: 一声高嗥刺破空气，冰碎了。

paras.en: It broke away from Anna like a suit of armor, revealing her true self beneath.
paras.zh: 它如铠甲般从安娜身上脱落，露出底下真实的她。

paras.en: Suddenly, she could run, but the castle had shifted into a wide white tundra, and there was no place to hide before the wolf appeared.
paras.zh: 忽然她能跑了，可城堡已变成辽阔白原，狼出现前无处可藏。

paras.en: Because it was already there.
paras.zh: 因它已在那。

paras.en: Without turning around, Anna felt the yellow eyes of the wolf fixed on her back.
paras.zh: 不用回头，安娜感到狼的黄眼钉在她背上。

paras.en: She ran.
paras.zh: 她跑。

paras.en: Yet, no matter how hard she pumped her legs or how fast her heart beat, nothing seemed to change.
paras.zh: 可无论她蹬得多狠、心跳多快，一切似乎不变。

paras.en: There was just a flat expanse of gray snow below her and even grayer sky above.
paras.zh: 脚下只是灰雪的平阔，头顶是更灰的天。

paras.en: The world was colorless and bleak and without hope, and then— An explosion of red pain burst through her vision as the wolf’s claws raked and sank into her back.
paras.zh: 世界无色、荒凉、无望，然后——狼爪划过、扎进她背，一阵赤红剧痛在视野中炸开。

paras.en: Anna expected to wake up—she always woke up.
paras.zh: 安娜以为会醒来——她总会醒来。

paras.en: But this time, she didn’t.
paras.zh: 可这次，她没有。

paras.en: Instead, the wolf flipped her over onto her back, opened its huge jaws, and swallowed her whole.
paras.zh: 相反，狼把她掀翻仰面，张开巨口，将她整个吞下。

paras.en: Anna’s eyes flew open.
paras.zh: 安娜猛睁眼。

paras.en: Sweat sheened her skin and she felt hollow, as if her insides had been scooped out, like a gutted pumpkin.
paras.zh: 汗覆皮肤，她感到空虚，像五脏六腑被掏空，如挖空的南瓜。

paras.en: Something prodded her back. “Troll’s toes!” Anna exclaimed to nobody as she pulled the book out from beneath her.
paras.zh: 有东西戳她背。“地精的脚趾！”安娜对着空处惊叫，从身下抽出书。

paras.en: Sometime in the night, she must have dozed off on the floor and rolled onto the book, its thick spine digging into her own, explaining the sharp pain of the wolf’s claws in her nightmare.
paras.zh: 夜里某时，她定是在地上打盹、滚到书上，厚书脊硌着自己背，解释了梦中狼爪的剧痛。

paras.en: Anna let her head sink back onto the floor and flung her hand over her eyes. “This is getting ridiculous,” she muttered, hoping the sound of her voice would chase away the lingering fear. “You’re too old for this kind of stuff.” Though, she didn’t feel old.
paras.zh: 安娜把头沉回地板，抬手遮眼。“这太荒唐了，”她嘟囔，盼自己的声音赶走余惧。“你太大了，不该这样。”可她不觉得自己老。

paras.en: In fact, that was kind of the problem.
paras.zh: 事实上，那正是问题。

paras.en: These last two days, she had felt oh so very young indeed.
paras.zh: 这两天，她确觉得自己太小了。

paras.en: And that ache that always lurked just beneath the sea of her thoughts surfaced, sending a ripple of sadness through her.
paras.zh: 那总潜于思绪之海下的痛楚浮起，送一阵悲伤的涟漪过她。

paras.en: How she missed her parents.
paras.zh: 她多想父母。

paras.en: Her mother would have fixed everything with a story or two about silly and magical things, like shaggy goats outwitting trolls, or an empress who forgot her clothes.
paras.zh: 母亲会用一两个关于傻气魔法之物的故事搞定一切，比如笨山羊智胜地精，或忘了穿衣的皇后。

paras.en: And her father, he would have chased away any lingering fear with a candle that crackled and emitted a sweet, soothing scent, or a warm mug of hot chocolate.
paras.zh: 父亲会用一支噼啪、散发甜润安神的蜡烛，或一杯温热可可，赶走余惧。

paras.en: Mmmm…hot chocolate…with marshmallows. “Come on, Anna.” She spoke out loud again, trying to shake the loneliness. “They’re not here, but you can definitely get your own mug of hot chocolate.
paras.zh: 嗯……热可可……加棉花糖。“加油，安娜。”她又出声，想甩掉孤独。“他们不在，可你绝对能给自己弄杯可可。

paras.en: It’s not like the wolf is hiding beneath the bed or something.” She let out a soft little “Ha!” for good measure.
paras.zh: 又不是狼藏在床下。”她为壮胆轻轻“哈！”一声。

paras.en: The sound wasn’t very convincing, but there was no one she had to convince but herself.
paras.zh: 那声音不太有说服力，可她只需说服自己。

paras.en: And so, she got off the floor, and the terrible, awful nightmare that had ended differently than it ever had before—with the wolf finally winning—slipped from her tired mind.
paras.zh: 于是她离了地，那场结局前所未有的可怕噩梦——狼终于赢了——从疲惫的心头滑走。

paras.en: Anna realized she was still in her travel cloak, but she didn’t care.
paras.zh: 安娜发现自己还穿着旅行斗篷，却不在意。

paras.en: She could change into her pajamas once she got back.
paras.zh: 回来再换睡衣也行。

paras.en: Taking a flickering candle from her bedside table, Anna was her own source of light in a castle of darkness.
paras.zh: 从床头柜取了支摇曳的蜡烛，安娜成了黑暗城堡中自己的光源。

paras.en: The flame was weak, yet just bright enough for her to make her way through the familiar halls and down to the kitchen.
paras.zh: 火苗弱，却恰好够她穿过熟悉的长廊、下到厨房。

paras.en: And—wait.
paras.zh: 然后——等等。

paras.en: What was that?
paras.zh: 那是什么？

paras.en: Lifting the candle up a little higher, Anna paused on the stairs.
paras.zh: 安娜在楼梯上停步，把蜡烛举高些。

paras.en: She thought she’d seen a bit of movement, a skim of white.
paras.zh: 她以为瞥见一点动静、一抹白。

paras.en: But as she strained her eyes to peer beyond the candle’s light, Anna didn’t see anything unusual or out of place or snarling with fangs.… “You’re being silly,” she chided herself. “Keep going.
paras.zh: 可当她眯眼望向烛光之外，安娜没见任何异常、错位或龇牙之物……“你真傻，”她责自己。“继续走。

paras.en: Remember: marshmallows!” Still, the memory of the nightmare resurfaced and trailed her through the corridors, down the stairs, and into the kitchen.
paras.zh: 记住：棉花糖！”然而噩梦的记忆复现，随她穿廊、下楼、进厨房。

paras.en: The kitchen was the beating heart of the castle, the cheery red-glow of its stoves producing delicious banquets and even more delicious heat that cut through the autumn’s creeping damp.
paras.zh: 厨房是城堡的跳动之心，炉子欢快的红光照出美味宴席，更美的热气刺穿秋日潜入的潮。

paras.en: Tonight, though, the kitchen felt oddly empty and quiet.
paras.zh: 可今夜，厨房怪异地空而静。

paras.en: The pots and pans, instead of being clanged around by busy cooks, were hanging quietly on their hooks in neat lines next to colorful garlands of garlic, dried peppers, and herbs that draped from the ceiling, dropping down to tickle the lids of jams, beets, and pickled herring.
paras.zh: 锅碗不再被忙碌的厨子敲响，而是静静挂在钩上排成行，旁是天花垂下的彩绳蒜串、干椒与香草，垂下来轻拂果酱、甜菜与腌鲱鱼的盖。

paras.en: Usually, at least one cook remained to keep an eye on the fire stoves, but Elsa had dismissed the cook staff, too, including Olina—which meant only Anna, Elsa, Olaf, Gerda, and Kai were sleeping in the castle that night.
paras.zh: 通常至少留一名厨子看炉，可艾莎也遣散了厨役，包括奥丽娜——也就是说那夜城堡里只睡安娜、艾莎、雪宝、格尔达与凯伊。

paras.en: Which explained why it felt particularly quiet, dark, and empty.
paras.zh: 这解释了为何格外静、暗、空。

paras.en: That—and the fact that Sven and Kristoff still weren’t back yet.
paras.zh: 还有——斯文与克里斯托夫仍未回来。

paras.en: At least, Anna didn’t think they were back yet—she didn’t know for sure.
paras.zh: 至少，安娜觉得他们没回——她不确定。

paras.en: Usually, outings to the Valley of the Living Rock didn’t last this long, and since he knew things weren’t going too well with the villagers, he’d know not to linger.
paras.zh: 通常去活石谷不会这么久，而且他知村民处境不妙，该知不可久留。

paras.en: He was a mountain man; he could take care of himself.
paras.zh: 他是山里人；能照顾自己。

paras.en: But still, Anna began to worry and hoped they had made it back.
paras.zh: 可安娜仍忧心，盼他们已回。

paras.en: Despite her optimism, she always worried for those she loved.
paras.zh: 尽管乐观，她总为所爱担忧。

paras.en: It was what made Anna…Anna.
paras.zh: 这正是安娜之为安娜。

paras.en: She sighed, heart heavy, and shuffled over to the stove.
paras.zh: 她叹气，心沉，拖步走向炉。

paras.en: Making hot chocolate was simple, and while she wasn’t great with cooking that required twenty different detailed steps and ingredients and lots of fine chopping, she was adept at mixing delicious chocolate powder with milk and setting it on the stovetop.
paras.zh: 做热可可简单，她虽不擅长需二十道精细步骤与配料、大量细切的烹饪，却擅于把美味可可粉与奶混匀、放上炉。

paras.en: But as Anna stirred the pot of warming milk to stop a skin from forming, she heard a soft clatter.
paras.zh: 可安娜搅着温奶防结皮时，听见一声轻响。

paras.en: She stopped stirring. “Hello?” she called hopefully. “Kristoff, is that you?” No response.
paras.zh: 她停搅。“你好？”她满怀希望地喊。“克里斯托夫，是你吗？”无人应。

paras.en: She thought she heard the sound of footsteps fading away, but from the other side of the kitchen leading toward the stairs.
paras.zh: 她以为听见脚步声渐远，却是从厨房另一侧、朝楼梯方向。

paras.en: Maybe Kristoff was wearing his earmuffs and hadn’t been able to hear her through the fluff.
paras.zh: 也许克里斯托夫戴了耳罩，隔着毛绒听不见她。

paras.en: Typical Kristoff.
paras.zh: 典型的克里斯托夫。

paras.en: Or maybe it was Olaf.
paras.zh: 也许是雪宝。

paras.en: Perhaps he was up for a night of reading a gripping passage about existentialism or a book on another -ism.
paras.zh: 或许他正打算夜读一段existentialism（存在主义）的扣人心弦段落，或一本别的“主义”书。

paras.en: Quickly, Anna turned off the stove and removed the milk.
paras.zh: 安娜迅速关炉、移开奶。

paras.en: The hot chocolate would have to wait.
paras.zh: 热可可得等等。

paras.en: The footsteps were too intriguing.
paras.zh: 那脚步太引人好奇。

paras.en: If it was Olaf, she’d leave it alone.
paras.zh: 若是雪宝，她便不管。

paras.en: But if it was Kristoff, she had to know what the trolls had said about the Blight.
paras.zh: 可若是克里斯托夫，她必知地精对枯萎病说了什么。

paras.en: Still…it wasn’t really cold enough yet for Kristoff to be wearing his earmuffs.
paras.zh: 不过……天还没冷到克里斯托夫戴耳罩。

paras.en: Like Elsa, the cold didn’t seem to bother him as much as it did the non-mountain folk.
paras.zh: 像艾莎，寒冷似乎不像烦扰非山民那样烦他。

paras.en: After all, he’d grown up in the cold.
paras.zh: 毕竟他在寒冷中长大。

paras.en: Taking the candle, Anna followed the footsteps up the stairs to the rest of the castle. “Kristoff?
paras.zh: 安娜持烛，随脚步上楼去城堡其余处。“克里斯托夫？

paras.en: Is that you?” she asked.
paras.zh: 是你吗？”她问。

paras.en: It sounded like the person was walking through the portrait gallery, then the second great hall, and finally, the Great Hall.
paras.zh: 听来那人走过画像廊，再第二大厅，最后大 hall。

paras.en: She stood in the doorway, lifting her candle as high as she could.
paras.zh: 她立门口，把烛举到最高。

paras.en: It only shed light on the polished wooden floor.
paras.zh: 它只照亮擦亮的木地板。

paras.en: She hadn’t heard the footsteps leave the Great Hall, which meant Kristoff, if it was him, was still there in the dark room with Anna.
paras.zh: 她没听见脚步离大 hall，也就是说若是克里斯托夫，仍在那暗室与安娜同在。

paras.en: She stepped inside, peering behind each column that lined the wall of the cavernous room.
paras.zh: 她步入，窥看空旷房间壁列每根柱后。

paras.en: She yanked at curtains and moved from one to the next. “Kristoff?” Anna called.
paras.zh: 她拽开帘，从一处移到下一处。“克里斯托夫？”安娜喊。

paras.en: Her candle’s flame danced this way and that.
paras.zh: 她的烛焰四舞。

paras.en: Nothing, nothing, nothing, two yellow eyes, nothing, nothing—Anna stopped breathing.
paras.zh: 没有、没有、没有、两只黄眼、没有、没有——安娜屏息。

paras.en: Two yellow eyes.
paras.zh: 两只黄眼。

paras.en: She brought the candle back around and saw the form of a wolf.
paras.zh: 她把烛转回，看见狼的身形。

paras.en: White and massive, exactly like the one in her nightmare.
paras.zh: 白而巨大，正如噩梦里的那只。

paras.en: Except this time, it was different.
paras.zh: 可这次，不同。

paras.en: Because Anna was awake.
paras.zh: 因为安娜是醒着的。

paras.en: ANNA HAD ONCE HEARD that when someone faced death, their life flashed before them.
paras.zh: 安娜曾听说，人临死时，一生会在眼前闪过。

paras.en: But as she stood there in the gloom of the Great Hall, with the yellow eyes of the wolf fixed on her, it wasn’t her life that flashed through her mind—it was the details of the Great Hall.
paras.zh: 可当她站在大 hall的幽暗里，狼的黄眼钉着她，闪过她脑海的并非自己的一生——而是大 hall的细节。

paras.en: The quivering red curtains that outlined each pillar.
paras.zh: 勾出每根柱的红帘在颤。

paras.en: The gleam of the curtain’s rod in the glow of the candle.
paras.zh: 帘杆在烛光里泛光。

paras.en: The heat of the candle wax as it dripped onto her skin.
paras.zh: 蜡滴到她皮肤上，烫。

paras.en: She noticed all of this in the breath it took for the wolf to growl.
paras.zh: 狼咆哮那一息间，她注意到这一切。

paras.en: Then it leapt at her.
paras.zh: 然后它扑向她。

paras.en: Anna jumped out of the way, the knife-sharp claws missing her by mere inches.
paras.zh: 安娜跳开，刀般利的爪只差寸许擦过。

paras.en: The wolf growled in frustration, and the sound seemed to reach into Anna and scrape against her insides, but she managed to drop her candle, grab the curtain, and tug—hard, sending the curtain’s rod clattering onto the floor.
paras.zh: 狼挫败地低吼，那声似探入安娜、刮过她内脏，可她丢下烛，抓住帘，猛拽——帘杆咣当落地。

paras.en: Snatching it up, Anna half ran, half stumbled toward the great double doors that seemed as far away as the moon.
paras.zh: 她抄起杆，半跑半踉跄奔向那仿佛远如月亮的双扇大门。

paras.en: One stride, then another, and then—she was through!
paras.zh: 一步、又一步，然后——她冲出去了！

paras.en: Slamming the doors shut, she pushed the curtain rod through the two handles, locking the doors in place just as the wolf threw its bulk against the other side with all its might.
paras.zh: 她砰地关门，把帘杆穿进两把手，锁住门，恰在狼用全力撞向另一侧时。

paras.en: THUMP!
paras.zh: 砰！

paras.en: The doors rattled, but stayed shut.
paras.zh: 门震了，却关着。

paras.en: THUMP!
paras.zh: 砰！

paras.en: THUMP!
paras.zh: 砰！

paras.en: THUMP!
paras.zh: 砰！

paras.en: How long would the curtain rod hold?
paras.zh: 帘杆能撑多久？

paras.en: Anna had never seen a wolf so large.
paras.zh: 安娜从没见过这么大的狼。

paras.en: Or rather, she had, but only in…Something stirred inside of her, something she knew she needed to examine closer, but the little feeling about what could have brought the wolf from her dreams into the castle would have to wait for when she wasn’t running for her life. “HELP!” Anna yelled as she sprinted away. “WOLF!
paras.zh: 或更确切说，她见过，但只在……她内心某物翻动，她知需细察，可关于什么把狼从梦中带入城堡的那点感觉，得等她不为逃命时再说。“救命！”安娜边奔边喊。“狼！

paras.en: BIG, MASSIVE WOLF!
paras.zh: 巨大、庞大的狼！

paras.en: IN THE CASTLE!” The only thing that beat faster than her heart was the single insistent question pounding through her brain: What to do?
paras.zh: 在城堡里！”比她心跳更快的，是脑中那唯一执拗的问题：怎么办？

paras.en: What to do?
paras.zh: 怎么办？

paras.en: What to do?
paras.zh: 怎么办？

paras.en: She’d faced a pack of wolves before, when she and Kristoff had journeyed to the North Mountain to try to find Elsa—but Kristoff and Sven weren’t here right now.
paras.zh: 她曾面对过狼群，那时她和克里斯托夫去北山找艾莎——可此刻克里斯托夫与斯文不在。

paras.en: She needed to find Elsa, and quickly.
paras.zh: 她需尽快找到艾莎。

paras.en: She flew up the stairs in the second great hall.
paras.zh: 她飞上第二大厅的楼梯。

paras.en: She needed to find help.
paras.zh: 她需找帮手。

paras.en: But as she sprinted down the hall that led to Elsa’s bedroom, she saw a flash of white up ahead.
paras.zh: 可当她冲向艾莎卧室的廊道，见前方一抹白光。

paras.en: The wolf—it had somehow escaped the Great Hall!
paras.zh: 狼——它竟逃出了大 hall！

paras.en: She groaned.
paras.zh: 她呻吟。

paras.en: It was just like in her dreams; the large-as-a-bull wolf seemed to outwit and outrun her at every turn.
paras.zh: 正如梦里；那大如牛的狼似乎每回都智胜、跑赢她。

paras.en: But how ?
paras.zh: 可怎么做到的？

paras.en: She knew wolves were fast, but they couldn’t possibly be this fast.
paras.zh: 她知狼快，却不可能这么快。

paras.en: Gasping for breath, Anna pivoted and sprinted down another hallway.
paras.zh: 安娜喘着气，转向冲进另一条廊。

paras.en: She turned left, right, and then left again.
paras.zh: 她左转、右转，再左转。

paras.en: She didn’t know exactly where her feet were taking her, but she realized she would be near Kai’s room if she made a final left.
paras.zh: 她不知脚带她去哪，却意识到若最后左转，会近凯伊的房间。

paras.en: Maybe she could hide in there!
paras.zh: 也许能躲那！

paras.en: As the castle’s steward, Kai had protocol for everything, from the right way to hold a teacup to the exacting ritual of snuffing out the candles and oil lamps one wick at a time.
paras.zh: 作为管家，凯伊凡事有规程，从端茶杯的正确姿势到逐根熄烛与油灯的确切仪式。

paras.en: There was a chance that maybe he already had a plan for a wolf breaking into the castle.
paras.zh: 或许他已有狼闯城堡的预案。

paras.en: A wolf!
paras.zh: 狼！

paras.en: A wolf!
paras.zh: 狼！

paras.en: A wolf!
paras.zh: 狼！

paras.en: Her breath came short and fast.
paras.zh: 她呼吸短促。

paras.en: From somewhere behind her, she thought she heard a howl.
paras.zh: 身后某处，她似听见嗥叫。

paras.en: Only twenty more feet until she reached Kai’s room…five feet…one foot… “KAI!” Anna catapulted into the steward’s room and bolted the lock behind her.
paras.zh: 离凯伊房只二十尺……五尺……一尺……“凯伊！”安娜弹进管家家，反手闩锁。

paras.en: She noticed his form lying in his bed. “Kai, wake up!
paras.zh: 她见他身形躺在床上。“凯伊，醒醒！

paras.en: There’s a wolf in the castle!
paras.zh: 城堡里有狼！

paras.en: What do we do?” But the man remained completely still.
paras.zh: 我们怎么办？”可那人纹丝不动。

paras.en: Unease trickled through Anna.
paras.zh: 不安流过安娜。

paras.en: It wasn’t as if she were being quiet.
paras.zh: 她可不是在悄悄。

paras.en: In fact, she was being very loud.
paras.zh: 事实上，她很吵。

paras.en: Why wasn’t Kai waking up?
paras.zh: 凯伊为何不醒？

paras.en: She lit a candle from his bedside to see.
paras.zh: 她借他床头点烛来看。

paras.en: Kai twisted and turned under his blanket, and as the light hit his eyelids, he muttered, “No, please…don’t!” He was in the middle of a nightmare.
paras.zh: 凯伊在被下翻来覆去，光落眼皮，他喃喃“不，求你……别！”他在噩梦正中。

paras.en: Anna knew from personal experience that no one should be woken in the middle of a bad dream.
paras.zh: 安娜凭经验知，不该在噩梦正酣时叫醒人。

paras.en: But there was a wolf now pawing outside the room.
paras.zh: 可此刻门外有狼在扒。

paras.en: Usual rules did not apply. “Kai, wake up !’ Anna shook the steward’s arm. “Please, please, please wake up.” Kai’s eyes snapped open, and Anna staggered back.
paras.zh: 常规则不适用。“凯伊，醒醒！”安娜摇管家臂。“求你、求你、求你醒醒。”凯伊猛睁眼，安娜踉跄退后。

paras.en: The steward’s eyes were usually the same brown-green color as changing autumn leaves or muddied creeks.
paras.zh: 管家的眼通常是秋叶或浊溪般的褐绿。

paras.en: But instead of looking into warm hazel eyes, she was staring into two inky pits.
paras.zh: 可她盯着的不是温暖的淡褐眼，而是两个墨坑。

paras.en: His pupils had swallowed his irises, turning his eyes completely black.
paras.zh: 他的瞳孔吞了虹膜，眼全黑了。

paras.en: Just like the cattle.
paras.zh: 正如那些牛。

paras.en: Suddenly, Kai sat upright, and screamed.
paras.zh: 忽然，凯伊坐直，尖叫。

paras.en: And screamed.
paras.zh: 又尖叫。

paras.en: And screamed.
paras.zh: 又尖叫。

paras.en: And screamed.
paras.zh: 又尖叫。

paras.en: He screamed as though long claws were tearing out his heart.
paras.zh: 他叫得像长爪在撕他的心。

paras.en: As though sharp teeth were sinking into his skin.
paras.zh: 像尖牙咬进他的皮。

paras.en: As though he were being eaten alive from the inside out.
paras.zh: 像正被从内到外活活吞掉。

paras.en: Anna placed a hand on his shoulder to try to comfort him, but he didn’t react to her touch.
paras.zh: 安娜把手放他肩想安抚，可他对她的触碰无反应。

paras.en: It was as though she were invisible.
paras.zh: 仿佛她隐形。

paras.en: Kai couldn’t see her—couldn’t sense her.
paras.zh: 凯伊看不见她——感觉不到她。

paras.en: He was lost.
paras.zh: 他迷失了。

paras.en: The pawing outside the door grew faster.
paras.zh: 门外扒抓更快。

paras.en: Hungrier.
paras.zh: 更饿。

paras.en: More desperate.
paras.zh: 更绝望。

paras.en: And as the scratching grew in intensity, Kai’s black eyes suddenly shifted again.
paras.zh: 抓挠愈烈，凯伊的黑眼忽然又变。

paras.en: One moment, they were black, and the next, they were yellow…and glowing.
paras.zh: 一瞬黑，下一瞬黄……且发光。

paras.en: Anna’s heart seemed to fly up into her throat and she almost choked as she staggered backward.
paras.zh: 安娜的心似飞上喉，踉跄退后几乎窒息。

paras.en: What was happening ?
paras.zh: 怎么回事？

paras.en: The scratching stopped.
paras.zh: 抓挠停了。

paras.en: Or had it?
paras.zh: 还是没停？

paras.en: Anna couldn’t be sure, as Kai’s scream continued to fill the room, making her clutch her ears.
paras.zh: 安娜不确定，因凯伊的尖叫仍充满房间，让她捂耳。

paras.en: She needed to get out of there.
paras.zh: 她需离开。

paras.en: She needed to find Elsa, Olaf, Kristoff, and Sven, to warn the others.
paras.zh: 她需找艾莎、雪宝、克里斯托夫、斯文，警告他人。

paras.en: The people of Arendelle were in danger.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔人危在旦夕。

paras.en: All of this was Anna’s worst fear, worse than her wolf-filled nightmare.
paras.zh: 这一切是安娜最深的恐惧，比狼的噩梦更甚。

paras.en: Because it was real.
paras.zh: 因它是真的。

paras.en: It was happening.
paras.zh: 它正发生。

paras.en: How and why, she would still have to think on later.
paras.zh: 如何与为何，她日后须想。

paras.en: She took a step toward the door.
paras.zh: 她朝门迈步。

paras.en: Kai’s yellow eyes stayed transfixed somewhere beyond her, as though witnessing unseen horrors.
paras.zh: 凯伊的黄眼定在她身后的某处，像在见证无形的恐怖。

paras.en: She crept by him and pressed her ear to the door.
paras.zh: 她溜过他，把耳贴门。

paras.en: Nothing.
paras.zh: 无声。

paras.en: Not so much as a yip.
paras.zh: 连一声吠都没有。

paras.en: But what if the wolf was out there, waiting for her in silence?
paras.zh: 可若狼在外，沉默地等她呢？

paras.en: And worse: what if it wasn’t out there, and was headed for others instead? “ELSA!” Her sister’s name ripped from her throat as she undid the lock and ran out of Kai’s room, leaving him screaming and writhing. “ELSA!
paras.zh: 更糟：若它不在外，而去了别人那呢？“艾莎！”她解开锁冲出凯伊房，留他尖叫扭动，姐姐的名字从喉中撕裂而出。“艾莎！

paras.en: ELSA!
paras.zh: 艾莎！

paras.en: ELSA!” she yelled.
paras.zh: 艾莎！”她喊。

paras.en: Minutes before, Anna had felt the quiet of her home.
paras.zh: 几分钟前，安娜还感到家的安静。

paras.en: But it wasn’t quiet anymore.
paras.zh: 可不再安静。

paras.en: Now she could hear more screams echoing throughout the castle.
paras.zh: 现在她听见更多尖叫回荡城堡。

paras.en: Screams she recognized as Gerda’s.
paras.zh: 她认出是格尔达的尖叫。

paras.en: Anna had the sinking feeling that if she went to her, she would be too late, that Gerda would have the glowing yellow eyes like Kai.
paras.zh: 安娜有种下沉感：若去，会太迟，格尔达会如凯伊般睁着发光的黄眼。

paras.en: She practically sobbed. “ELSA!” The door to their parents’ bedroom slammed open, and a moment later, Elsa appeared in the hallway, still in her work dress but wrapped in their mother’s scarf, and with heavy bags under her eyes.
paras.zh: 她几乎啜泣。“艾莎！”父母卧室门猛开，片刻后艾莎出现在廊中，仍穿着工作裙、裹着母亲的围巾，眼下挂着浓重的黑眼圈。

paras.en: Olaf waddled behind her, in a fuzzy yellow robe and with a matching sleep mask pushed up on his forehead.
paras.zh: 雪宝在她身后摇摇摆摆，穿毛茸茸黄袍，同色眼罩推上额。

paras.en: He also held the snow globe from earlier. “What’s wrong?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: 他还拿着早先的雪景球。“怎么了？”艾莎问。

paras.en: At the sound of her sister’s voice, Anna almost collapsed with relief that Elsa wasn’t asleep and screaming.
paras.zh: 听到姐姐的声音，安娜几乎因艾莎没在沉睡尖叫而虚脱般松了气。

paras.en: And Elsa’s eyes were blue—blue as the sky, and blue as a song. “A-a wolf!” Anna sputtered, wrapping Elsa and Olaf in a fierce embrace. “Wolf!
paras.zh: 艾莎的眼是蓝的——蓝如天，蓝如歌。“狼——狼！”安娜结巴，把艾莎雪宝紧紧抱住。“狼！

paras.en: Kai!
paras.zh: 凯伊！

paras.en: Gerda!” she gasped and then choked out, “Eyes!
paras.zh: 格尔达！”她喘息，然后哽咽道，“眼睛！

paras.en: Glowing yellow eyes!” “Elsa,” Olaf whispered, “she’s not making any sense.” The next second, Anna felt a cool hand on her forehead as her sister checked her temperature.
paras.zh: 发光的黄眼！”“艾莎，”雪宝低语，“她语无伦次。”下一秒，安娜感到一只凉手贴她额头，姐姐在探体温。

paras.en: At Elsa’s touch, Anna felt her frenzy subside, just a little.
paras.zh: 艾莎一触，安娜的狂乱稍退。

paras.en: She wasn’t sure if it was Elsa’s magic, or if it was just because the gesture was so familiar and comforting, but it made her want to cry.
paras.zh: 她不确定那是艾莎的魔法，还是因这动作太熟悉、太安慰，可它让她想哭。

paras.en: Their mother had done the same thing whenever Anna had woken up in a sweat from the fearsome nightmare that had plagued her childhood.
paras.zh: 每当安娜因折磨童年的可怕噩梦一身冷汗醒来，母亲总这样做。

paras.en: Anna managed to take a deep, shuddering breath. “That’s because nothing makes sense!” After they bolted upstairs into the council chambers and locked the doors, Anna told them what had happened.
paras.zh: 安娜勉强深吸一口颤气。“正因一切都不合理！”他们冲上楼进议事厅、锁上门后，安娜讲了经过。

paras.en: The story came out jumbled, details piling up all out of order.
paras.zh: 故事讲得乱，细节全无次序。

paras.en: Elsa didn’t interrupt.
paras.zh: 艾莎没打断。

paras.en: She listened, and when Anna at last came to the end of it, she gave her a firm and understanding nod. “Are you sure you didn’t just have a bad dream?” Elsa said. “It sounds like it,” said Olaf, pushing his sleep mask up a little higher.
paras.zh: 她听着，安娜终于讲完，她给了个坚定而理解的点头。“你确定不只是做了个噩梦？”艾莎说。“听来像，”雪宝说，把眼罩又推高些。

paras.en: Anna stared at Elsa. “What?
paras.zh: 安娜瞪着艾莎。“什么？

paras.en: No!
paras.zh: 不！

paras.en: There is a wolf in the castle!” Elsa rubbed her temples. “It’s late.
paras.zh: 城堡里有狼！”艾莎揉太阳穴。“晚了。

paras.en: We should get back to bed.” “What?” Anna pulled away from her sister. “You don’t believe me?” “Question.” Olaf had unbolted the lock and peeked through the doors. “Wolves usually have four paws, two eyes, and long, sharp teeth, right?” When the sisters nodded, he pressed a hand to his mouth and tilted his head. “Then I’m preeeetty sure we should believe Anna.” The door flew open, blowing off Olaf’s robe and mask, and sending the snow globe falling to the floor with a crack .
paras.zh: 我们该回去睡了。”“什么？”安娜从姐姐身边退开。“你不信我？”“问题。”雪宝已开锁，从门缝窥看。“狼通常有四爪、两眼、长利齿，对吧？”姐妹点头，他捂嘴歪头。“那我超确定该信安娜。”门猛开，吹掉雪宝的袍与罩，雪景球啪地落地的裂响。

paras.en: The wolf had found them.
paras.zh: 狼找到了他们。

paras.en: Its sharp shoulder blades jutted up and down as it moved, like some sort of terrifying carousel creature.
paras.zh: 它移动的尖肩胛上下耸，像某种恐怖的旋转木马兽。

paras.en: Its long legs brought it closer and closer, following Anna, Elsa, and Olaf as they backed up and skirted around the long table.
paras.zh: 长腿把它带得越来越近，跟着退着绕长桌的安娜、艾莎、雪宝。

paras.en: Before Anna could scream, a wall of ice erupted from the wooden floor.
paras.zh: 安娜还没喊，一道冰墙从木地迸出。

paras.en: Jagged crystals raced up to the ceiling in the center of the room, knitting themselves together to form a thick protective barrier, with Anna, Elsa, and Olaf by the doors and the wolf walled off on the fireplace end.
paras.zh: 嶙峋的晶体窜至天花板中央，自织成厚保护墙，安娜、艾莎、雪宝在门侧，狼被隔在壁炉端。

paras.en: Anna’s gasp of surprise turned white in the cold of Elsa’s magic. “ Now do you believe me?” Anna asked her sister.
paras.zh: 安娜惊喘在艾莎魔法的寒中变白。“现在你信我了？”安娜问姐姐。

paras.en: Elsa ignored her.
paras.zh: 艾莎没理她。

paras.en: Her eyes swept the room. “We need to go find—” But Elsa’s words were cut off.
paras.zh: 她的眼扫过房间。“我们得去找——”可艾莎的话被打断。

paras.en: THUMP.
paras.zh: 砰。

paras.en: THUMP.
paras.zh: 砰。

paras.en: SCREEEECH!
paras.zh: 吱嘎！

paras.en: Cobweb-thin lines scattered across the ice wall as the wolf pawed at it, its claws screeching.
paras.zh: 蛛网般的细纹散布冰墙，狼扒着，爪吱吱响。

paras.en: It was a terrible sound, even worse than the sound of teeth scraping against a fork, which until then Anna had thought to be the most awful sound imaginable.
paras.zh: 那声音可怕，比牙刮叉还糟——而那本是安娜以为可想的最可怕声。

paras.en: The ice wall wasn’t holding.
paras.zh: 冰墙撑不住。

paras.en: It was shattering. “Run!” Elsa shouted, raising both her arms.
paras.zh: 它在碎。“跑！”艾莎举双臂喊。

paras.en: Anna didn’t need to be told twice—and Olaf was already right by her side.
paras.zh: 安娜不用催第二遍——雪宝已贴她身侧。

paras.en: Sprinting out the doors of the council chambers, they made their way for the stairs, down toward the great front doors that would take them to the castle bridge.
paras.zh: 冲出议事厅门，他们奔向楼梯，下往通城堡桥的大前门。

paras.en: But as Anna and Olaf neared the landing to the first floor, two pairs of yellow eyes shone at them from the shadows, blocking their path to the front entrance.
paras.zh: 可当安娜与雪宝近一楼平台，两对黄眼在影中亮，挡了他们去前门的路。

paras.en: Kai.
paras.zh: 凯伊。

paras.en: Gerda.
paras.zh: 格尔达。

paras.en: Anna’s stomach twisted.
paras.zh: 安娜的胃拧起。

paras.en: She’d been right, but oh!
paras.zh: 她对了，可噢！

paras.en: How she wished she’d been wrong.
paras.zh: 她多希望自己错了。

paras.en: Gerda’s friendly face was now an oval of agony—her eyes and mouth were all wide and round as she screamed and lurched toward them, something glistening in her hand: a pair of sewing scissors.
paras.zh: 格尔达友善的脸如今是痛苦的椭圆——眼与嘴皆大睁圆，尖叫着踉跄逼近，手中闪着物：一把裁缝剪。

paras.en: And next to her, Kai clutched a red-hot poker. “Put out the flames.
paras.zh: 她身旁，凯伊攥着烧红的拨火棍。“灭掉火。

paras.en: The house is burning,” Kai croaked, jabbing the iron at them as though they were the phantom flames attacking him. “It’s burning!” he cried. “Well, this can’t be good,” Olaf whispered as Gerda stepped forward with the blades of the scissors snapping open and shut, open and shut.
paras.zh: 房子烧着了，”凯伊沙哑道，戳铁棍向他们，仿佛他们是攻击他的幻火。“烧着了！”他喊。“嗯，这可不妙，”雪宝低语，格尔达上前，剪刀刃开合、开合。

paras.en: The look in their yellow eyes was not human, but something else.
paras.zh: 他们黄眼里的神色非人，而是别的。

paras.en: Predatory.
paras.zh: 捕食性。

paras.en: Wolf like.
paras.zh: 狼一般。

paras.en: It’s a wolf pack, Anna realized with horror.
paras.zh: 是狼群，安娜惊恐地意识到。

paras.en: Suddenly, a great shattering sound erupted above them, as if a thousand crystal goblets had been smashed…or one gigantic wolf had managed to break through a magical ice wall.
paras.zh: 忽然，上方一声巨响，像千只水晶杯碎……或一头巨狼破开魔法冰墙。

paras.en: A second later, Anna heard her sister’s footsteps on the stairs behind her and Olaf. “KEEP GOING!” Elsa shouted down to them. “But Kai and Gerda want to prevent us from imminent escape and possibly cause us harm!” Olaf called back, darting behind Anna’s travel cloak and away from the hot poker. “Don’t stop!” Elsa called.
paras.zh: 一秒后，安娜听见姐姐在身后楼梯与雪宝上的脚步。“继续跑！”艾莎朝下喊。“可凯伊和格尔达想阻我们即刻逃脱、还可能伤我们！”雪宝回喊，窜到安娜旅行斗篷后避开热铁棍。“别停！”艾莎喊。

paras.en: Anna didn’t know what to do—Kai and Gerda were blocking the only path to escape the castle, and a massive wolf was barreling down the stairs toward them.
paras.zh: 安娜不知怎么办——凯伊与格尔达挡了逃出城堡唯一的路，一头巨狼正顺楼梯冲向他们。

paras.en: The only direction left was down —but there was no castle exit in the below-ground kitchen, and they would end up trapped there, or worse, in the ice room.
paras.zh: 只剩向下——可地下厨房无城堡出口，他们会被困那，或更糟，困冰室。

paras.en: Wait.
paras.zh: 等等。

paras.en: The ice room.
paras.zh: 冰室。

paras.en: There was something important about the ice room.
paras.zh: 冰室有要事。

paras.en: Something Anna had wanted to check out…the blueprints!
paras.zh: 安娜想查的……蓝图！

paras.en: The blueprints that had shown a secret passageway that led out from underneath the castle. “Elsa!” Anna yelled at the top of her lungs. “Meet us in the ice room!” Anna and Olaf practically flew down the rest of the stairs with Elsa bringing up the rear as she blasted the stair landing with mirror-smooth ice, making it difficult for the pack to follow them down the stairs.
paras.zh: 那蓝图显示一条从城堡底下通出的密道。“艾莎！”安娜扯嗓喊。“冰室见！”安娜与雪宝几乎飞下余阶，艾莎殿后，用镜面般的冰轰击楼梯平台，让狼群难追下楼。

paras.en: Anna didn’t turn around, not even when she heard two thuds and a whoosh that she assumed were Kai and Gerda slipping on the ice, unable to chase any farther.
paras.zh: 安娜没回头，即便听见两声闷响与一阵风声——她猜是凯伊与格尔达在冰上滑倒，追不动了。

paras.en: But that didn’t mean the wolf, with its large hooked claws, couldn’t navigate a bit of ice.
paras.zh: 可这不意味着那大钩爪的狼过不了点冰。

paras.en: Anna, Olaf, and Elsa continued racing downstairs.
paras.zh: 安娜、雪宝、艾莎续奔下楼。

paras.en: They burst into the kitchen, only to discover they weren’t alone.
paras.zh: 他们冲进厨房，却发现不孤单。

paras.en: Kristoff sat in the middle of the room at the long table, scarfing down a sandwich, and by the number of crumbs scattered in front of him, it wasn’t his first sandwich of the night.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫坐房中长桌旁，狼吞三明治，面前碎屑之多，显非今夜第一个。

paras.en: Relief washed over Anna: Kristoff was back, and he was okay!
paras.zh: 释然漫过安娜：克里斯托夫回来了，且安好！

paras.en: Anna took stock of the details.
paras.zh: 安娜细看。

paras.en: Kristoff’s blond hair was tangled, as if he’d spent the night in the woods or the mountains.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫金发凌乱，像在林或山过夜。

paras.en: His patched traveler’s pack, lantern, and pickax were slung across his shoulders, as if he’d been too hungry to wait even a second more.
paras.zh: 他补过的旅行包、提灯、镐挂肩，像饿得等不了一秒。

paras.en: Sven made happy munching noises as he buried his nose in a bag of carrots.
paras.zh: 斯文把鼻埋进胡萝卜袋，发出快乐的咀嚼声。

paras.en: They must have only just returned from the Valley of the Living Rock.
paras.zh: 他们定刚从活石谷回来。

paras.en: Horror collided with her relief.
paras.zh: 恐惧与释然撞在一起。

paras.en: Horror, because she’d thought—she’d hoped beyond hope —that Kristoff and Sven were far, far away from the castle and somewhere safe in the woods.
paras.zh: 恐惧，因她以为——她曾抱最大希望——克里斯托夫与斯文远在城堡之外、林中安全处。

paras.en: Relief, because she wouldn’t have to face this terror without him.
paras.zh: 释然，因她不必无他独面此恐。

paras.en: Kristoff looked up, a crumb dropping from his chin. “Hi, Kristoff!” Olaf darted into the kitchen and sprinted past the table. “Bye, Kristoff!” “RUN!” Anna yelled, barreling toward him.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫抬头，碎屑落下巴。“嗨，克里斯托夫！”雪宝窜进厨房、冲过桌。“拜拜，克里斯托夫！”“跑！”安娜喊，朝他撞去。

paras.en: With one hand, she grabbed Kristoff’s elbow and pulled him after her. “Mwaf?” he asked, his mouth full of sandwich.
paras.zh: 她一手抓克里斯托夫肘拖着他。“唔？”他满嘴三明治问。

paras.en: But Anna didn’t have time to explain, because the wolf was there, there in the kitchen.
paras.zh: 可安娜没空解释，因狼在那，在厨房。

paras.en: And though it was impossible—all of this was impossible! —the wolf seemed to have grown three feet since they had left it in the second great hall.
paras.zh: 尽管不可能——这一切都不可能！——狼似乎比他们在第二大厅留它时高了三尺。

paras.en: Its shoulders brushed the sides of the door as it swaggered into the room, eyes glowing, jowls drooling a thick slime.
paras.zh: 它肩擦门框大摇大摆进屋，眼发光，腮垂厚黏涎。

paras.en: Kristoff dropped his sandwich onto the floor. “MWAFFFF!” he yelled.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫把三明治掉地。“唔啊！”他喊。

paras.en: Now all five of them—Sven, Elsa, Olaf, and Kristoff, with Anna in the lead—sprinted toward the back of the kitchen, to the door that led into the ice room.
paras.zh: 此刻他们五个——斯文、艾莎、雪宝、克里斯托夫，安娜领头——冲向厨房后，通往冰室的门。

paras.en: Anna pushed open the heavy door and held it as Kristoff, Olaf, and Elsa ran through.
paras.zh: 安娜推开重门、把着，克里斯托夫、雪宝、艾莎跑过。

paras.en: But where was Sven?
paras.zh: 可斯文呢？

paras.en: Peering back, Anna’s heart stopped.
paras.zh: 安娜回头窥，心停了。

paras.en: Fear seemed to have frozen Sven in his tracks.
paras.zh: 恐惧似把斯文冻在原地。

paras.en: He remained still, a carrot in his mouth, as the wolf loped closer to him.
paras.zh: 他不动，嘴里叼胡萝卜，狼小跑近他。

paras.en: It knocked aside the long wooden table with an ear-bleeding screech of its legs against stone. “Sven!” Anna shouted. “Run!” But it was as if Sven couldn’t hear her.
paras.zh: 它撞开长木桌，腿刮石发出刺耳尖叫。“斯文！”安娜喊。“跑！”可斯文似听不见。

paras.en: Instead, his eyes remained fixed on the wolf’s glowing ones.
paras.zh: 相反，他的眼定在狼的发光的眼上。

paras.en: He lifted a hoof, and took a step… toward the wolf. “SVEN!” Kristoff yelled from over Anna’s shoulder.
paras.zh: 他抬蹄，迈步……朝狼。“斯文！”克里斯托夫从安娜肩后喊。

paras.en: At the sound of his best friend’s voice, the wolf’s strange hypnosis over Sven seemed to shatter.
paras.zh: 听挚友声，狼对斯文的奇异催眠似碎。

paras.en: Sven staggered backward, tripping over his hooves as he twisted on his haunches and stumbled through the door, leaving Anna just enough time to slam it shut on the wolf’s slick snout.
paras.zh: 斯文踉跄退，扭身绊蹄穿过门，安娜恰有时间把门砰上狼的光滑口鼻。

paras.en: Sven wobbled beside her, shaky but safe, and Kristoff threw his arms around him.
paras.zh: 斯文在她旁晃，颤却安全，克里斯托夫搂住他。

paras.en: Elsa blasted the door with ice to hold it, and with a wave of her hand, thirty or so blocks of ice scraped across the rough stone floor to settle in front of the door, for good measure.
paras.zh: 艾莎用冰轰门固住，挥手，约三十块冰擦过粗石地，堆门前，以防万一。

paras.en: But would it be enough?
paras.zh: 可这够吗？

paras.en: Elsa panted and tucked a loose strand of hair behind her ear. “It might be a strange wolf with glowing yellow eyes, but it has to have a hard time clawing through stone and ice!” The sounds of the wolf clawing and pawing against the door made it sound like perhaps, just maybe, it was making impossible progress. “Now what?” Elsa called, taking in the room. “Why did you want us in here?” “One second!” Anna said, squeezing her eyes shut, not just to try to keep out the mental image of the wolf hunting them, but to try to remember what the blueprints had said about the entrance to the Earth Giant’s Passage.
paras.zh: 艾莎喘着，把一缕散发掖耳后。“它或许是只发光黄眼的怪狼，可它总难抓穿石与冰！”狼抓扒门之声，听来似乎、也许、正取得不可能的进展。“现在呢？”艾莎打量房间喊。“你为何要我们来这？”“等一下！”安娜闭眼，不只为挡狼追他们的心象，更为记起蓝图说的巨人通道入口。

paras.en: Something about three flagstones … She counted three flagstones in, and two across, and hurried to one in the center of the room.
paras.zh: 关于三块石板……她数进三块、横过两块，匆匆到房中一块。

paras.en: As she knelt down and placed her fingers around the edge of the stone, she hoped with all her might that the blueprints had been complete, that they weren’t just a fanciful wish of her heroic grandfather King Runeard, who had built the castle.
paras.zh: 她跪下、手指绕石边，全力希望蓝图完整，而非建城堡的英雄祖父鲁内尔德国王的一厢情愿。

paras.en: Holding her breath, Anna pulled, and the flagstone lifted away, revealing carved stone steps leading down into darkness. “Yes!” Grinning, she gestured to the entrance. “Olaf, you first!” “Oh, I can’t wait to go somewhere new!” he said with an excited wave of his arms.
paras.zh: 屏息，安娜一拉，石板升起，露出雕石阶通向下暗。“成了！”她咧嘴指入口。“雪宝，你先！”“噢，我等不及去新地方！”他兴奋挥臂说。

paras.en: Arooooooooooooooooo!
The sound of the wolf’s howl seemed to burrow its way toward them, twisting and tumbling around Anna, surrounding her, becoming both up and down and around. “Me first!” Olaf hopped down the steps.
paras.zh: 狼的嗥声似钻向他们，在安娜周身扭翻、包围她，成了上与下与周。“我先！”雪宝跳下阶。

paras.en: Covering her ears to drown out the howling, Anna followed him, along with Elsa and Sven.
paras.zh: 安娜捂耳挡嗥，随他下，艾莎与斯文同下。

paras.en: Kristoff was last, and as he clambered down, he pulled the flagstone securely back over them, plunging them into utter darkness.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫最后，爬下时把石板牢牢拉回，罩他们入全黑。

paras.en: For a moment, Anna was aware of everyone’s breathing, and she wondered if they could all hear the pounding of her heart. “What was that thing?” Kristoff finally whispered.
paras.zh: 片刻，安娜觉众人呼吸，想知道他们是否都听见她心砰。“那是什么？”克里斯托夫终于低语。

paras.en: No one responded, but Anna knew.
paras.zh: 无人应，可安娜知道。

paras.en: It was not just a wolf.
paras.zh: 它不只是狼。

paras.en: It was a nightmare.
paras.zh: 它是噩梦。

paras.en: Her nightmare.
paras.zh: 她的噩梦。

paras.en: And it was coming for them.
paras.zh: 而它正冲他们来。

paras.en: ANNA’S HEAD POUNDED, her stomach twisted, and her heart hurt.
paras.zh: 安娜的脑袋突突直疼，胃里一阵阵翻搅，心也揪着痛。

paras.en: She wasn’t sick, and yet, in a weird way, she wished she were, because colds came and went of their own accord, but this—this aching feeling—she’d brought that upon herself. Just as she must have brought the wolf upon the castle. She wanted to believe it was a coincidence that the wolf had appeared after she’d read aloud the “Make Dreams Come True” spell, but she couldn’t.
paras.zh: 她并没有生病，可说来奇怪，她倒宁愿自己病了，因为感冒总会不治自愈，可这种——这种揪心的痛——是她自己招来的。就像城堡里的那只狼，一定也是她招来的。她多想相信这只是巧合——狼恰好在她念出那句“美梦成真”咒语之后出现——可她做不到。

paras.en: Anna had dreamed of the wolf her entire childhood. Now, Kai and Gerda—people who had loved and raised her—had yellow eyes and were trapped in their own nightmarish realities. Why hadn’t she listened? Elsa had told her to leave the secret room alone, that their parents had probably left it a secret for a reason. And now, Anna had unleashed her nightmare on Arendelle.
paras.zh: 从小到大，安娜梦里全是那只狼。如今，凯和格尔达——那些疼爱她、把她带大的人——眼睛泛着黄色，被困在各自噩梦般的现实里。她当初为什么就不听劝呢？艾莎明明告诫过她，别去碰那间密室，说父母把它藏着掖着，总归有原因。而今，安娜把自己的噩梦放进了阿伦黛尔。

paras.en: “It’s a good thing it’s so dark,” Olaf said from somewhere to Anna’s left. “If there are flesh-eating monsters down here, at least we can’t see them!”
paras.zh: “还好这么黑，”雪宝在安娜左手边不知哪个角落里说。“就算底下真有吃人的怪物，起码咱们看不见它们！”

paras.en: “Always looking on the bright side,” Kristoff’s voice called back. “Anna, what is happening? What is a wolf doing in the castle? And where are we now?”
paras.zh: “总是往好处想。”克里斯托夫的声音答道。“安娜，到底出了什么事？城堡里怎么会有狼？我们现在又是在哪儿？”

paras.en: “Elsa,” Anna said, fumbling in her cloak pocket for the scrap of spell with one hand, and reaching blindly out into the darkness for her sister’s shoulder. “I need to tell you something—”
paras.zh: “艾莎，”安娜一边唤，一边用一只手在斗篷口袋里摸索那张咒语残片，另一只手在黑暗中盲目地伸出去，寻找姐姐的肩膀。“我有件事要告诉你——”

paras.en: “One second, Anna,” Elsa’s voice said from a little further away. “Kristoff, can we get some light?”
paras.zh: “等一下，安娜。”艾莎的声音从稍远些的地方传来。“克里斯托夫，能弄点亮吗？”

paras.en: There was a rustling, followed by a scritch as Kristoff struck a match and lit the lantern clipped to the outside of his traveler’s pack. Usually, Anna felt better when there was light, but the wavering lantern flame cast huge shadows across the rough rock walls and across her friends’ faces, distorting their familiar features and turning them into strangers. And—Anna’s breath lodged beneath her ribcage—was that a glint of yellow she’d spotted in Kristoff’s eyes?
paras.zh: 一阵窸窣响过，接着是“嚓”的一声，克里斯托夫划亮火柴，点着了别在他行囊外侧的那盏提灯。平日里，有光安娜就会安心些，可这会儿，摇曳的灯火在粗粝的石壁上、在朋友们的脸上投下巨大的影子，把熟悉的面孔扭曲成了陌生人的模样。还有——安娜的呼吸卡在了肋骨底下——她刚才是不是在克里斯托夫眼里瞥见了一抹黄？

paras.en: “Seriously,” Kristoff said, his face twisting with frustration as he ran expert hands up and down Sven’s withers, and then peered into Sven’s ear. The poor reindeer was trembling from his close encounter with the wolf, and was standing so close to Kristoff he was almost on the mountain man’s toes. “Would someone please tell me what is going on?”
paras.zh: “说真的，”克里斯托夫说，懊恼地拧着眉，一双熟练的手顺着斯文的肩胛上下抚过，又凑近去查看斯文的耳朵。可怜的驯鹿方才与狼打了个照面，吓得浑身发抖，这会儿紧贴着克里斯托夫站着，几乎踩上了这山地汉子的脚尖。“能不能请哪位告诉我，这到底是怎么回事？”

paras.en: As he patted down Sven’s quivering legs, he turned his head, and the yellow speck Anna had thought she’d seen disappeared. It had only been the lantern reflected in eyes. Her panic dissolved, just a little, and she took in where she had led them. They were at the start of a tall, wide tunnel, hewn directly from the rough rock of the castle’s tiny island. The path led away from them, disappearing into more darkness.
paras.zh: 他拍着斯文颤个不停的腿，一侧头，安娜自以为瞧见的那点黄色便不见了。那不过是提灯映在眼里的反光。她的恐慌稍稍褪去，这才打量起自己把他们带到的这个地方。他们正站在一条又高又宽的地道口，地道是从城堡所在小岛的粗粝岩石里直接凿出来的。通道向远处延伸，没入更深的黑暗。

paras.en: “Where are we?” Elsa tilted her head back and looked up, wide-eyed.
paras.zh: “我们这是在哪儿？”艾莎仰起头，睁大眼睛朝上看。

paras.en: “It’s called the Earth Giant’s Passage,” Anna said. “It was on the blueprints in the…the secret room.”
paras.zh: “它叫大地巨人通道。”安娜说。“就在……那间密室里的蓝图上有画。”

paras.en: Elsa looked at her for a long moment. “You and that secret room.”
paras.zh: 艾莎盯着她看了好一会儿。“又是你和那间密室。”

paras.en: “What?” Anna said. “It was! And that secret room’s blueprints got us away from the wolf!”
paras.zh: “什么？”安娜说。“明明就是！而且正是那密室里的蓝图，救我们甩开了狼！”

paras.en: “So,” Elsa said, clasping her hands together, “do you know where this passage goes?”
paras.zh: “那么，”艾莎双手交握，问道，“你知道这条通道通向哪里吗？”

paras.en: “Not…exactly,” Anna admitted. “I think it goes under the fjord, but it wasn’t clear on the blueprints.”
paras.zh: “算不上……完全知道。”安娜承认。“我想它该是从峡湾底下穿过去，可蓝图上画得不明不白。”

paras.en: “So, you’re telling me it could lead to anywhere, including a dead end?”
paras.zh: “这么说，你是告诉我，它哪儿都可能通，包括死路一条？”

paras.en: Anna’s stomach twisted. “I…I didn’t think of that.”
paras.zh: 安娜的胃又绞紧了。“我……我没往那方面想。”

paras.en: Elsa sighed and shook her head. “It’s fine. I’ll think of a solution.”
paras.zh: 艾莎叹了口气，摇了摇头。“没关系。我会想出办法的。”

paras.en: The words stung Anna, as though Elsa had physically thrown them at her. Anna had let her down. If Elsa was this upset about just the blueprints, what would she say if Anna told her she had recited the spell? When exactly was a good time to admit to your sister you’d messed up big-time?
paras.zh: 这话刺得安娜生疼，仿佛艾莎是实打实地把它们掷到她身上的。安娜让她失望了。要是艾莎光为一纸蓝图就这么不快，那安娜若是告诉她自己念了咒语，她又该说什么？到底什么时候，才适合向姐姐坦白自己闯了大祸？

paras.en: Suddenly, Sven bellowed. His eyes rolled back, and Anna could see white ringing them. In that same instant, from high above, Anna could hear knives being sharpened. No, not knives. Claws, scraping against a flagstone floor. The wolf was digging for them.
paras.zh: 忽然，斯文发出一声嘶吼。他双眼上翻，安娜能看见眼珠周围环着一圈眼白。就在同一瞬间，安娜听见极高的头顶上方传来磨刀的声音。不，不是磨刀。是爪子，一下一下刮着石板地面。狼在刨土找他们。

paras.en: “We have to go. Now!” Elsa whirled away from Anna, transforming from annoyed sister to commanding queen. “I’ll go first, in case…in case there’s anything up ahead. Olaf, do you think you could…?”
paras.zh: “我们得走了。现在！”艾莎从安娜身边倏然转身，从恼火的妹妹变成了发号施令的女王。“我走前面，以防……以防前面有什么。雪宝，你能不能……？”

paras.en: “Put my eyes on the back of my head?” Olaf swiveled his entire head 180 degrees. “Already done.”
paras.zh: “把眼睛转到后脑勺上？”雪宝把整个脑袋转了一百八十度。“早就办妥了。”

paras.en: Elsa nodded. “Thanks. And if things happen, I want you all to run without stopping. Got that?” Without waiting for a reply, Elsa took the lantern from Kristoff and strode forward through the tunnel, the lantern scattering pale shadows across the rough stone walls.
paras.zh: 艾莎点点头。“谢了。要是真出了事，你们所有人都要不停地跑。明白了吗？”不等回答，艾莎从克里斯托夫手里接过提灯，大步走进地道，灯光在粗糙的石壁上洒下惨白的影子。

paras.en: Kristoff offered his shoulder to Sven, who rested his head on it. “What kind of things do you think Elsa meant?” he whispered to Anna.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫把肩膀让给斯文，斯文把头搁了上去。“你觉得艾莎说的‘事’，是指什么样的事？”他压低声音问安娜。

paras.en: “I think she means if anything goes wrong, we’re supposed to leave her to handle it,” Anna explained.
paras.zh: “我想她的意思是，万一出了岔子，我们该撇下她，让她自己应付。”安娜解释道。

paras.en: “Like, if there’s a cave-in,” Olaf added helpfully. “Or an avalanche, or if there’s a monster, or if you lose a nose, or if the wolf or Gerda or Kai attack us again, or if Kristoff’s eyes turn yellow—?”
paras.zh: “比如塌方，”雪宝热心地补充。“或者雪崩，或者冒出个怪物，或者你的鼻子掉了，或者狼、格尔达、凯又来袭击我们，或者克里斯托夫的眼睛变黄——？”

paras.en: Anna threw a hand over Olaf’s mouth, stopping the plethora of awful possibilities. “We’ll be fine if we just stick together.” She wished and hoped that was true. She withdrew her hand from Olaf, and smiled. “Besides, we have something the wolf doesn’t have.”
paras.zh: 安娜一把捂住雪宝的嘴，截断了那一长串可怕的可能。“只要我们待在一起，就没事。”她满心盼望这是真的。她把手从雪宝脸上挪开，笑了笑。“再说，我们有一样狼没有的东西。”

paras.en: Kristoff raised an eyebrow. “What’s that?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫扬起眉毛。“什么东西？”

paras.en: Sven’s ear perked also, waiting for an answer.
paras.zh: 斯文的耳朵也竖了起来，等着听答案。

paras.en: Anna nodded toward the light, and felt her own frustration fade. Even though her sister’s outfit was simple enough—a sensible heather-blue split dress perfect for long days at a desk or afternoons visiting a farm—it still glimmered where the lantern’s light kissed it, just the way that everything Elsa touched seemed to sparkle afterward.
paras.zh: 安娜朝光亮处一扬下巴，心头的烦乱也随之淡了。虽说姐姐的衣着再素净不过——一身得体的石楠蓝分裙，最适合整日伏案，或是午后去农庄做客——可凡是提灯光辉轻拂过的地方，衣裙便泛起微光，就像艾莎碰过的东西，过后总会闪闪发亮。

paras.en: Anna smiled. “We have Elsa.” And with that, she hurried to catch up.
paras.zh: 安娜笑了。“我们有艾莎。”说罢，她快步追了上去。

paras.en: They ran as fast as they could through the passage, which is to say not very fast at all. In part because the passage was so roughly hewn that it proved tedious to navigate, and in part because Sven still seemed shaken and terrified of the wolf, which was presumably still scrabbling at the flagstone somewhere far above them. Sympathy flitted through Anna. As terrified as she had been, it must have been a thousand times worse for a reindeer, whose greatest natural threat was the wolf. Anna noticed that Kristoff kept a hand on his best friend’s neck, and now and then, she caught an occasional note as Kristoff sang to him.
paras.zh: 他们在通道里拼命地跑，换句话说，其实根本没跑多快。一来通道凿得太粗糙，走起来步步艰涩；二来斯文似乎还惊魂未定，对那只狼怕得要命——那狼多半还在他们头顶极高处的石板上刨着。安娜心头掠过一丝怜惜。她自己已经吓得够呛，对一头驯鹿来说，那滋味恐怕还要糟上千百倍——狼本是它们天敌中最可怕的一个。安娜注意到，克里斯托夫一直把手搭在这位挚友的颈上，还不时低哼几句，唱给斯文听。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Olaf, his eyes facing backward, kept treading on the hem of Anna’s travel cloak. The third time it happened, Anna stopped, recalling how Elsa used to carry her long ago, and crouched in front of him. “Olaf, how about a piggyback ride?”
paras.zh: 与此同时，眼睛朝后的雪宝，老是踩到安娜旅行斗篷的下摆。第三次踩到时，安娜停下脚步，想起很久以前艾莎也是这样背着她，便在雪宝面前蹲下身来。“雪宝，要不要来个背背驮？”

paras.en: “Don’t mind if I do!” Olaf said. But without his eyes facing forward, it took him more than a couple of attempts, one of which knocked Anna flat onto her belly. “Ta-da!” Olaf climbed onto her back. “I did it!”
paras.zh: “那我就不客气啦！”雪宝说。可他眼睛不朝前，试了好几次才爬上来，其中一下还把安娜扑了个嘴啃泥。“当当——！”雪宝爬上了她的背。“我成功啦！”

paras.en: “You did,” Anna grunted. “Just stay put while I try to get up.”
paras.zh: “是啊。”安娜闷哼一声。“我起身的时候，你坐稳别动。”

paras.en: “Anna?” Olaf asked, sitting on her back. “Are you okay?”
paras.zh: “安娜？”雪宝坐在她背上问。“你还好吗？”

paras.en: Anna replied, somewhat breathlessly as she pushed down with her palms, “I’m fine.”
paras.zh: 安娜双手撑着地面，有点上气不接下气地答道：“我很好。”

paras.en: And that’s when Elsa screamed.
paras.zh: 就在这时，艾莎尖叫起来。

paras.en: “ELSA!” Anna cried as a new strength flooded through her. She launched to her feet. Pulse in her throat, she flew down the passage, Olaf clinging to her neck. The tunnel was dark but for the slightest halo of light.
paras.zh: “艾莎！”安娜大喊，一股新的力气涌遍全身。她一跃而起。脉搏直冲喉头，她抱着雪宝沿通道飞奔而去，雪宝紧紧搂着她的脖子。地道里一片漆黑，只有极远处浮着一圈微小的光晕。

paras.en: “Elsa! Kristoff! Sven!” Anna cried. “What’s wrong?!”
paras.zh: “艾莎！克里斯托夫！斯文！”安娜喊道。“出什么事了？！”

paras.en: Horrible thoughts stampeded through her mind, but Anna was able to slam them all out except for one: an image of the wolf, silent as the moon, stalking Elsa, while Elsa’s blue eyes drained of their color and shifted to a glowing yellow.
paras.zh: 无数可怕的念头在她脑海里横冲直撞，可安娜把它们统统关在门外，只留下一个：那只狼，悄无声息如月影，尾随着艾莎，而艾莎的蓝眼睛一点点褪尽颜色，化作灼灼的黄。

paras.en: The tunnel bent slightly, and then there they were: Elsa, Kristoff, and Sven. Anna scanned them for any signs of injury, but nothing seemed amiss. No one was bleeding. In fact, there was no sign of anything wrong. And, the more she thought about it, there was no way the wolf could have possibly passed her in the passage to have reached them up ahead.
paras.zh: 通道微微一弯，他们就在眼前了：艾莎、克里斯托夫，还有斯文。安娜把他们上下扫了一遍，查看有没有受伤的迹象，可似乎一切如常。没有人在流血。事实上，根本看不出任何不对劲。而且越想越明白：狼绝不可能从通道里越过她，抢先跑到前头去。

paras.en: “What’s happening?” Anna panted. “Why did you scream?”
paras.zh: “出什么事了？”安娜喘着气问。“你为什么尖叫？”

paras.en: “Sorry,” Elsa said, her cheeks flushed pink. “I guess I’m a little on edge, and then when I saw it, I, well…” She gestured behind her.
paras.zh: “抱歉。”艾莎说，双颊泛起红晕。“我大概是有点绷得太紧了，然后一看到那个东西，我就……”她朝身后比了比。

paras.en: The tunnel had widened into a chamber, though Anna could see that it narrowed again on the far side of the hall. It looked like a python that had swallowed a whole egg, the egg visible in its gullet. And in the farthest shadows of the chamber, Anna saw—
paras.zh: 通道在这里拓成了一间石室，不过安娜看得出，大厅的另一头又收窄了。整条通道活像一条吞下了一整颗蛋的蟒蛇，那蛋还卡在喉咙里清晰可见。在石室最深处的阴影里，安娜看见了——

paras.en: “A dragon!” Anna exclaimed, stepping backward only to tread on the hem of her cloak.
paras.zh: “一条龙！”安娜惊呼出声，往后一退，却踩到了自己斗篷的下摆。

paras.en: Olaf spun his head around to face forward again, prodding Anna’s ear with his carrot nose. “Silly Anna. It’s not a dragon, it’s a boat shaped like a dragon.”
paras.zh: 雪宝把脑袋转回来朝向前方，胡萝卜鼻子戳了戳安娜的耳朵。“傻安娜。那不是龙，是一艘形状像龙的船。”

paras.en: Kristoff rested a hand on Anna’s shoulder. “Don’t worry. Elsa thought it was a dragon, too,” he said with a kind smile.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫把手搭上安娜的肩。“别怕。艾莎刚才也当成是龙了。”他温和地笑道。

paras.en: Anna squinted in the dimness. It was a boat. Or a longboat, actually. Unlike the tall, multi-decked and multi-masted ships with butterfly-wing sails in the harbor above them, this boat was sleek, and laid long and low to the ground like a canoe. It had one simple mast, and its only height came at the front and back, where its wooden planks were swept up into the graceful point of a dragon’s tail at one end, and the dragon’s fearsome teeth at the other. It took her breath away—though part of that was due to jogging with a snowman on her back.
paras.zh: 安娜在昏暗中眯起眼睛。那是一艘船。确切地说，是一艘长船。不像头顶海港里那些高耸的多层多桅大船，挂着蝶翼般的帆，这艘船线条流畅，又长又低地贴伏在地，像一叶独木舟。它只有一根简朴的桅杆，高度全在首尾两端——木板向上扬起，一端收成龙尾优雅的尖梢，另一端则是龙口吓人的獠牙。它美得让安娜屏住了呼吸——虽说有一部分原因，是她背着一个雪人小跑得喘不上气。

paras.en: “This isn’t just a tunnel,” said Elsa. “I think it’s…a tumulus.”
paras.zh: “这不只是条地道。”艾莎说。“我想这是……一座坟冢。”

paras.en: “Oooh. A tummy what?” Olaf asked.
paras.zh: “噢——坟……什么？”雪宝问。

paras.en: Elsa smiled, but it seemed tinged with sadness. “It’s a burial mound,” she explained. “In the long-ago days, people used to build large dirt mounds called tumuli and lay their fallen leaders in their boats, along with everything they would need to take with them into the afterlife, favorite things like bronze shields, drinking goblets, and gold coins.”
paras.zh: 艾莎笑了，可那笑意里透着一丝哀伤。“就是墓葬土丘。”她解释道。“很久很久以前，人们会堆起巨大的土丘，称作坟冢，把逝去的领袖安放进船中，连同他们去往来世所需的一切，比如心爱的青铜盾牌、饮酒的金杯，还有金币。”

paras.en: “It’s beautiful,” Anna said, wanting to explore this unexpected treasure. She loved nothing more than answers, and a broken bit of pottery or a single glass bead from a long-ago age could tell a lot about the cultures and tales that had been lost to time.
paras.zh: “真美。”安娜说，很想探一探这份不期而遇的珍宝。她最爱寻根究底，而一块远古的残陶、一颗小小的玻璃珠，都能道出许多被时光湮没的文化与传说。

paras.en: Later, she told herself. One more reason you have to fix what you’ve done.
paras.zh: 以后再说，她对自己说。这也是你必须弥补过错的又一个理由。

paras.en: “I wish it were a real dragon,” Olaf said, interrupting Anna’s thoughts and pulling her back to the present.
paras.zh: “要它是条真龙就好了。”雪宝打断了安娜的思绪，把她拉回当下。

paras.en: “I think a wolf is more than enough to deal with right now,” Elsa said, already holding up the lantern again and taking a few steps away.
paras.zh: “眼下光一只狼就够我们对付的了。”艾莎说着，已重新举起提灯，往前走去。

paras.en: Kristoff nodded. “If we don’t move, this place may become a new grave site.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫点头。“我们要是再不动身，这地方恐怕就要添一座新的坟场了。”

paras.en: Olaf shook his head. “Poor Fredrick. I don’t think he’d like this place very much.”
paras.zh: 雪宝摇摇头。“可怜的弗雷德里克。我想他不会喜欢这地方的。”

paras.en: “Who’s Fredrick?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: “谁是弗雷德里克？”安娜问。

paras.en: “The wolf,” Olaf said, as though it were obvious. “He looked like a Fredrick, don’t you think?”
paras.zh: “那只狼啊。”雪宝说，仿佛这再明显不过。“他看上去就很像弗雷德里克，你说是不是？”

paras.en: “I wasn’t talking about the wolf,” Kristoff said, and shrugged his traveler’s pack higher onto his shoulder. “I was talking about us.”
paras.zh: “我没说狼。”克里斯托夫说着，把行囊往上耸了耸。“我说的是我们。”

paras.en: They continued to move, faster now and silent. They needed to save their breath to navigate the dark and twisting shadows of the passageway. After a few minutes, Anna thought she felt the ground begin to slope upwards, but she couldn’t be sure, and she didn’t want to get her hopes up.
paras.zh: 他们继续赶路，这回快了些，也安静了。他们得省着力气，才能穿过通道里那些扭曲昏暗的暗影。几分钟后，安娜觉得地面似乎开始向上倾斜，可她不敢确定，也不愿过早指望。

paras.en: “Do you hear that?” Elsa asked suddenly.
paras.zh: “你们听见了吗？”艾莎忽然问。

paras.en: Anna listened. She did hear something—a low rumbling. A sound that was almost like thunder, or what she imagined a sleeping Earth Giant’s snore would sound like, or—
paras.zh: 安娜侧耳去听。她确实听见了什么——一阵低沉的隆隆声。那声音几乎像雷鸣，又像她想象中沉睡的大地巨人打鼾的动静，再不然就是——

paras.en: “A waterfall,” Kristoff said. “I think we’ve gone under the waters of the Arenfjord and ended up on the other side.”
paras.zh: “瀑布。”克里斯托夫说。“我想我们已经从阿伦峡湾的水底穿了过去，到了对岸。”

paras.en: New energy quickened their steps. A few minutes later, they turned a corner to see a frothy curtain of water cascading down rock and a weak, gray not-quite-light trickling through into the tunnel. It was that time of night that wasn’t night at all, but the earliest moments of morning, the few minutes before the sun would break the line of the horizon.
paras.zh: 新的劲头让他们的脚步快了起来。几分钟后，他们转过一道弯，看见一幅翻腾着白沫的水帘顺着岩石倾泻而下，一缕微弱、灰蒙蒙、还算不上光的晨光渗进地道。那正是一天里那种已算不上夜的时辰，是清晨最初的片刻，距离太阳跃出地平线只剩几分钟。

paras.en: Night would soon be officially over, but…what other nightmares had Anna dreamed that could come true? Would her teeth start to fall out? Would she look down to see she was standing in only her underwear? Or maybe it would be a brand-new nightmare, one where Elsa exiled her from the kingdom once she learned about Anna’s wayward spell.
paras.zh: 黑夜很快就要正式落幕了，可是……安娜还做过哪些噩梦，是会成真的呢？她的牙齿会不会开始往下掉？她会不会一低头，发现自己只穿着内衣站在那儿？又或者，是一场全新的噩梦——艾莎得知安娜念了那句荒唐咒语后，把她逐出王国。

paras.en: The spell. Her stomach twisted. Anna didn’t like when secrets were kept from her, but holding her own secret made her feel like she’d eaten some of the Blight-stricken food. Now that they were leaving the tunnel, away from the wolf for at least a moment, she needed to tell Elsa. Maybe together, they could figure out a counter spell. Anna took a deep breath.
paras.zh: 那道咒语。她的胃又绞紧了。安娜不喜欢别人对她隐瞒，可自己揣着个秘密，又叫她觉得像吃了染上枯萎病的食物一样难受。既然他们正离开地道，至少这一刻甩开了狼，她得告诉艾莎了。也许两个人一起，能想出破解的咒语。安娜深吸一口气。

paras.en: “Elsa? I have something to tell you—”
paras.zh: “艾莎？我有事要告诉你——”

paras.en: Elsa held up her hand. “You don’t have to say it.”
paras.zh: 艾莎抬起一只手。“你不必说了。”

paras.en: Tilting her head, Anna squinted at her sister. “Say what?”
paras.zh: 安娜歪着头，眯眼打量姐姐。“说什么？”

paras.en: “‘I told you so,’” Elsa said with a small, tired grin. “I get it. You found the passage, and it was helpful. I’m not going to say otherwise. Can we please make a truce?”
paras.zh: “‘我早提醒过你’。”艾莎带着一丝疲惫的浅笑说。“我明白。你找到了这条通道，而且它派上了用场。我不会说不是。我们能休个战吗？”

paras.en: Anna gaped at her sister, not knowing what to do. On the one hand, she was pleased that her sister seemed happy with her. But on the other…Elsa didn’t know that all of this was Anna’s fault. And while Anna wasn’t exactly lying, the more seconds that ticked by, the more uncomfortable the omission made her feel, as though she were more of a scribble of Anna than an Anna who fully filled in all her lines. She hated to keep a secret—but she was more afraid of losing her sister. Oh, now what should she do?
paras.zh: 安娜张着嘴望着姐姐，不知如何是好。一方面，她很高兴姐姐似乎对她满意了。可另一方面……艾莎并不知道，这一切都是安娜的错。安娜倒也不算撒谎，可时间一秒一秒过去，这种隐瞒让她越来越不自在，仿佛她更像一幅潦草的安娜涂鸦，而不是那个把自己每一笔都描画完整的安娜。她讨厌守着秘密——可她更怕失去姐姐。哦，这下她该怎么办？

paras.en: But she was spared making a decision when Olaf emitted a squeal of glee directly into Anna’s ear. He jumped down from Anna’s back, and she stumbled slightly from the sudden lack of weight.
paras.zh: 可她还没来得及抉择，雪宝就在她耳边发出一声欢喜的尖叫，替她解了围。他从安娜背上跳下来，安娜因骤然卸了重负而微微一个趔趄。

paras.en: “Hooray!” Olaf cheered. “We’re not going to die in a tummy lice!” And then he sprinted down the path. Anna’s breath caught. He wasn’t really going to run straight through a waterfall, was he? Turns out he was, because in the next second, the water pounded on Olaf’s shoulders as he waded into it.
paras.zh: “好耶！”雪宝欢呼。“我们不会死在坟冢虱里啦！”说罢，他顺着小路飞奔而去。安娜一下子屏住了呼吸。他不会真要直直冲过瀑布吧？结果他真是，因为下一秒，雪宝蹚进水里，水哗地砸在他的肩上。

paras.en: “Oooh! A somewhat unpleasant massage!” he said, and then the snowman was through to the other side.
paras.zh: “噢——这按摩可有点‘不’舒服啊！”他说，随即雪人已经穿到了对岸。

paras.en: Anna heaved a sigh of relief. Sometimes when Olaf tried something new, he’d fall apart, and they’d have to take time to go looking for his arms or nose or other body parts. And there was no time to spare, not when the wolf could show up at any moment.
paras.zh: 安娜长舒一口气。雪宝尝试新鲜事物时，有时会散了架，他们就得花时间去寻回他的胳膊、鼻子或别的部件。而眼下片刻也耽搁不得，狼随时可能现身。

paras.en: Even though she didn’t think it could dig through solid rock, she couldn’t be sure of anything anymore. She glanced over her shoulder for the billionth time, just to check again.
paras.zh: 尽管她不认为狼能凿穿坚硬的岩石，可她如今什么都不敢断言了。她无数次地回头张望，只为再确认一遍。

paras.en: Kristoff reached out a finger to test the temperature of the waterfall. “Yikes!” He yanked his hand away, and the tip of his finger was bright pink. “That’s ice-cold, even by my standards!”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫伸出一根手指，试探瀑布的水温。“哎哟！”他猛地抽回手，指尖冻得通红。“这水冰得扎骨，连按我的标准都算冰！”

paras.en: “Hardly,” Elsa said, examining it. “Or else it would be frozen.” She smirked.
paras.zh: “才不呢。”艾莎端详着说。“不然它早就冻住了。”她抿嘴一笑。

paras.en: Kristoff made a face. “Touché.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫做了个鬼脸。“说得妙。”

paras.en: “I’ve got this.” With a flourish of Elsa’s lantern-free hand, an arch of ice appeared in the middle of the falls, sending water flying into the breaking dawn and scattering rainbows everywhere.
paras.zh: “交给我。”艾莎空着的那只手一挥，瀑布中央便现出一道冰拱，水花四溅，飞向破晓的天际，四处散落彩虹。

paras.en: And as Anna walked under the arch, leaving behind the shadows of the passageway, she felt her headache lift slightly. Her stomach untwisted just a bit, too.
paras.zh: 安娜从冰拱下走过，把通道的暗影抛在身后，只觉头痛轻了一些。胃里的拧结也松开了一点。

paras.en: Wolves did exist, yes, but so did rainbows and sisters. There had to be a way for Anna to fix her mistake. And there had to be a way she could fix it herself, without adding to Elsa’s pile of work. She just needed time—space—to think it through.
paras.zh: 狼确有其物，这没错，可彩虹和姐妹也同样存在。安娜一定有办法弥补自己的过错。也一定有一条路，让她亲力亲为地补救，而不必再往艾莎的担子上加码。她只需要时间——需要空间——把事情想个透彻。

paras.en: The Earth Giant’s Passage had deposited them on a small ledge that overlooked the village, and the group paused to take count. They were all there, though Anna noted in the dim light of dawn that Olaf’s twiggy hair seemed a bit bent out of shape, and new purple crescents had appeared under Elsa’s eyes. Kristoff, too, looked bedraggled, even by his usual standards. The cold, crisp air tugged at the fabric of Anna’s attire, giving her goosebumps. She pulled her travel cloak closer around her and was thankful she hadn’t changed into pajamas.
paras.zh: 大地巨人通道把他们送上一处俯瞰村庄的小小岩台，一行人停下脚步清点人数。人都在。不过安娜在黎明的微光里注意到，雪宝的树枝头发有点翘出了形，艾莎的眼下也添了新一轮紫色的月牙。克里斯托夫也是一副狼狈相，连按他平时的标准都算糟的。清冽干爽的空气扯动着安娜的衣料，激起她一身鸡皮疙瘩。她把旅行斗篷往身上裹紧了些，暗自庆幸自己没换成睡衣。

paras.en: “I think we should warn the village,” Kristoff said, shifting his weight as Sven moved his head onto his shoulder.
paras.zh: “我看该去给村里提个醒。”克里斯托夫说，一边随着斯文把头搁上他的肩而挪了挪重心。

paras.en: Anna’s headache returned with renewed vigor, but she tried to focus. Because Kristoff was right. “Yes! We warn the village! Tell them to stay inside!”
paras.zh: 安娜的头痛又来势汹汹，可她努力集中精神。因为克里斯托夫说得对。“对！我们去警告村民！叫他们待在屋里别出门！”

paras.en: Elsa shook her head. “You saw that wolf. I don’t think hiding is going to help.”
paras.zh: 艾莎摇摇头。“你也见到那只狼了。我看躲是躲不过的。”

paras.en: “Then we need to tell them to get far away!” Anna said as she tried to push her loose hair out of her eyes. She wished she’d thought to grab a spare hair ribbon so that she could wrangle her hair into manageable braids, instead of letting it hang loose and tangled around her shoulders.
paras.zh: “那我们得叫他们逃得远远的！”安娜一边说，一边想把散乱的发丝从眼前拨开。她真希望当初记得抓一根备用的发带，好把头发驯服成服帖的辫子，而不是任它蓬乱地披散在肩头。

paras.en: “But then again, what if the wolf is there now, prowling the village?” Kristoff asked, and then switched to Sven Talk. “What if he’s already full?”
paras.zh: “可话说回来，万一狼这会儿就在村里游荡呢？”克里斯托夫问，接着切换成了“斯文语”。“万一它已经吃饱了呢？”

paras.en: It was almost too horrible of a thought, and Sven’s ears, which usually pricked forward, seemed to droop like a pair of discarded socks as he swayed on his hooves, looking as though a sneeze from Kristoff would be enough to knock him over.
paras.zh: 这念头几乎可怕得让人不敢想下去。斯文那对平时竖得笔直的耳朵，此刻像两只被丢弃的袜子一样耷拉下来，四蹄摇摇晃晃，仿佛克里斯托夫打个喷嚏就能把他掀翻。

paras.en: Anna glanced at her sister, waiting for her to decide what to do. But Elsa didn’t say anything. Instead, she stared out across the Arenfjord toward the castle. And even though the castle looked the same, it didn’t feel the same. Anna knew all too well that things didn’t have to look different in order to be different. One morning, she’d gone to bed having two parents. The next morning, she’d woken up an orphan.
paras.zh: 安娜望向姐姐，等她拿主意。可艾莎什么也没说。她只是隔着阿伦峡湾，凝望着城堡。虽说城堡看上去还是老样子，感觉却全然不同了。安娜再清楚不过：一样东西不必变得看起来不同，才算是真的变了。有天夜里，她上床时还父母双全。第二天清晨醒来，她已成了孤儿。

paras.en: As she squinted at the castle, Anna caught a speck of white in the window of the guard tower. Beside her, Olaf had put his ice spectacles back on, and was staring at the castle windows as well.
paras.zh: 她眯眼凝望城堡，瞥见守卫塔的窗口有一点白色。她身旁，雪宝重新戴上了他的冰眼镜，也在盯着城堡的窗户。

paras.en: “Fredrick’s looking for us,” he said, adjusting the lenses so they sat better on his nose. “It doesn’t seem like he knows we’re gone…” Olaf lifted a hand to shield his eyes. “Oh, no, never mind. He does.”
paras.zh: “弗雷德里克在找我们呢。”他说着，把镜片调了调，好让它们架稳在鼻梁上。“看来他还不知道我们已经走了……”雪宝抬手遮了遮眼。“哦，不，收回。他知道。”

paras.en: “How do you know?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: “你怎么知道？”安娜问。

paras.en: Olaf pulled his gaze away. “Well, I think he misinterpreted why I raised my hand.”
paras.zh: 雪宝把目光挪开。“这个嘛，我想他误会了我抬手的意思。”

paras.en: “What does that mean?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: “那话是什么意思？”艾莎问。

paras.en: “He definitely took it as a friendly wave to come and join us. Which I think is what he’s going to do.”
paras.zh: “他准是当我是在友好地招手，叫他过来跟我们一块儿。我觉得他正打算这么做。”

paras.en: “Elsa?” Anna’s voice squeaked.
paras.zh: “艾莎？”安娜的声音发了尖。

paras.en: Elsa’s brow furrowed the way it always did when she was looking for something she’d misplaced, or, more likely, that Anna had removed and forgotten to put back. She seemed to be sinking deep within herself. Then, taking a deep breath, Elsa gave the lantern back to Kristoff and raised her hands, like a conductor about to direct a symphony.
paras.zh: 艾莎的眉头拧了起来，那副神情，和她每次找不着自己放丢的东西时一模一样——更可能的，是安娜拿走了又忘了放回去。她像是沉进了自己内心深处。接着，她深吸一口气，把提灯交还给克里斯托夫，举起双手，宛如一位即将指挥交响乐的指挥家。

paras.en: At first, Anna didn’t see any change, but then she noticed the waterfall’s roar had grown quiet. Looking behind her, Anna gasped.
paras.zh: 起初，安娜没看出什么变化，可随后她发觉瀑布的轰鸣安静了下来。安娜回头一看，倒吸一口凉气。

paras.en: The water was no longer in the waterfall.
paras.zh: 水，已经不在瀑布里了。

paras.en: Instead of trickling down the sides of the fjord and into the sea, the water was rushing upward, climbing the air as if it had been shot up from a geyser. It arced over the colored rooftops of the village below, its glittering tail reminding Anna of a comet. Her gaze followed its path to the castle, where it dipped and played around it, circling once, twice, three times, again and again until a dome of ice—seamless as an eggshell—covered the entire castle. Elsa had isolated their home inside of its own gigantic snow globe, preventing anyone from getting into the castle—but more importantly, keeping what was already there inside.
paras.zh: 水没有再顺着峡湾两畔淌入大海，而是向上奔涌，攀着空气直冲云霄，仿佛被间歇泉从地底射上了天。它划过下方村庄彩色的屋顶，那闪亮的水尾让安娜想起彗星。她的目光追着水流的轨迹到了城堡，水在那儿俯冲盘桓，绕着城堡嬉戏，一圈、两圈、三圈，一遍又一遍，直到一座冰穹——光滑得如同蛋壳——把整座城堡罩了起来。艾莎把他们的家封进了一只巨大的雪景球里，不让任何人踏入城堡——但更要紧的是，把里面已有的东西，也锁在了里头。

paras.en: She lowered her hands. Her pink cheeks flushed, but her eyes sparkled. Anna had always thought creating ice with magic seemed like it should be exhausting, like trying to run up a mountain in ten seconds, but Elsa always seemed the most Elsa after she’d wielded her magic. And she was only getting better at it with each passing day.
paras.zh: 她放下双手。她粉红的脸颊飞红，眼睛却亮晶晶的。安娜一直觉得，用魔法造冰该是件极耗心力的事，就像要十秒钟跑上一座山，可艾莎每次施展完魔法，反而最像“艾莎”本人。而且一天比一天更加得心应手。

paras.en: “That was beautiful,” Kristoff said, awe making his voice sound more solemn than usual, and Anna understood exactly how he felt.
paras.zh: “太美了。”克里斯托夫说，敬畏让他的嗓音比平时更庄重，安娜完全懂得他的感受。

paras.en: “Thanks.” Elsa bit her lip. “I just hope it holds the wolf. Now, we need to go warn the villagers, and get them to safety—just in case.”
paras.zh: “谢谢。”艾莎咬了咬嘴唇。“我只盼它能把狼关住。现在，我们得去警告村民，把他们带到安全的地方——以防万一。”

paras.en: Anna nodded her head in agreement, tearing her eyes away from the ice-domed castle. Elsa was right. They would go to the village, and then maybe she could—
paras.zh: 安娜点头赞同，把视线从冰穹笼罩的城堡上挪开。艾莎说得对。他们要先去村里，然后也许她就可以——

paras.en: But Anna’s thoughts jumbled up like crooked teeth as she looked away from the dome and back at her friends. The first true ray of morning sun had not just illuminated the beauty of Elsa’s creation; it had also brought to light something else: an unmistakable smattering of white in Sven’s dun coat.
paras.zh: 可当安娜把目光从冰穹移开、落回朋友们身上时，她的思绪顿时像歪七扭八的牙齿一样乱作一团。清晨第一缕真正的阳光，不仅照亮了艾莎杰作之美，也照出了另一样东西：斯文土褐色的皮毛上，分明斑驳着点点白色。

paras.en: The Blight had struck again.
paras.zh: 枯萎病又一次出手了。

paras.en: “SVEN!” KRISTOFF CRIED, holding up his friend, whose head lolled so low to the ground that his antlers skimmed the frost-covered grass.
paras.zh: “斯文！”克里斯托夫大喊，一把托住朋友，那颗脑袋垂得极低，鹿角几乎擦到了结霜的草地。

paras.en: Sven let out a rumbling groan, and the sound squeezed the breath out of Anna’s lungs. No—not Sven. He’d been fine only an hour ago!
paras.zh: 斯文发出一声低沉的呻吟，那声音把安娜肺里的空气都挤了出去。不——别是斯文。一个小时前他还好好的！

paras.en: “Mint,” Elsa said faintly, and when Anna turned to look at her sister, she saw that Elsa looked as shaken as she herself felt. “SoYun said that mint helped Hebert, and it was effective with the goats I saw the other day, too.”
paras.zh: “薄荷。”艾莎有气无力地说。安娜转头去看姐姐，发现艾莎的神色和自己一样慌乱。“SoYun说过薄荷救了赫伯特，我前两天见到的那些山羊，用了也有效。”

paras.en: “The botanist’s shop!” Anna said, tearing her eyes away from Kristoff’s devastated expression and looking out at the village below them. “Gabriella always has mint in her shop! And if that doesn’t work, Baker Blodget—”
paras.zh: “草药师的铺子！”安娜说着，把目光从克里斯托夫那张失魂落魄的脸上挪开，望向脚下的村庄。“加布里埃拉的店里一向备着薄荷！要是那不管用，还有面包师布洛杰特——”

paras.en: “It’ll work,” Elsa said, cutting in firmly. “I was there earlier to ask about herbal remedies, but no one was home,” she added. “She must be back by now.”
paras.zh: “会管用的。”艾莎斩钉截铁地打断。“我先前去过那儿问草药方子，可没人在家。”她补充道。“这会儿她总该回来了。”

paras.en: With that, they ran down the path to the village, Kristoff keeping a hand on Sven the entire time while Anna’s eyes remained fixed on the homes and shops ahead. The sooner they could evacuate the villagers, the sooner they could come up with a plan for how to defeat both the Blight and the wolf.
paras.zh: 说罢，他们顺着小路奔向村庄，克里斯托夫一路上始终有一只手搭着斯文，安娜的眼睛则死死盯着前方的房屋与店铺。越早把村民撤走，就能越早商量出办法，把枯萎病和那只狼一并解决。

paras.en: How much bad luck could a single kingdom have at once?
paras.zh: 一个王国怎么能一下子摊上这么多倒霉事？

paras.en: But it could be far worse. Anna knew that. Sven was still in the early stages of the Blight, after all. He could be doubling over in pain, he could be falling over, plunging into that unshakable sleep that would leave him unable to run from the wolf’s teeth.
paras.zh: 可情况本可能更糟。这一点安娜清楚。毕竟，斯文还处在枯萎病的初期。他本可能痛得弓下腰去，本可能一头栽倒，陷进那种再也挣脱不开的沉睡，从此躲不开狼的利齿。

paras.en: The wolf. Did it have anything to do with the Blight? Anna remembered the way Sven had stood still in the kitchen as the wolf stalked toward him, as if those yellow eyes had pinned him in place. But that didn’t make sense. The Blight came before the wolf, but maybe the wolf had so terrified Sven—had so rattled him to his reindeer core—that his body’s defenses had been jostled enough for the Blight to settle in and begin to creep through Sven like a thorny, resilient weed.
paras.zh: 那只狼。它和枯萎病有关吗？安娜想起斯文在厨房里僵立不动、任狼步步逼近的样子，仿佛那双黄眼睛把他钉在了原地。可这说不通。枯萎病出现在狼之前，但也许是狼把斯文吓得太狠——把这头驯鹿从骨子里吓乱了套——以至于他身体的防备被撼松了，枯萎病便趁虚而入，像一株多刺而顽强的野草，开始在斯文体内悄悄蔓延。

paras.en: But at least Sven was moving. He was still strong enough to trot, and he carried Olaf on his back, the snowman holding his own carrot nose in front of the reindeer’s muzzle on a string to keep Sven awake and motivated. Anna wished that she had something as simple as a carrot to cheer up Kristoff.
paras.zh: 但起码斯文还能走动。他还有力气小跑，背上驮着雪宝——雪人用绳子把自己的胡萝卜鼻子吊在驯鹿口鼻前晃来晃去，好让斯文保持清醒、提起劲头。安娜真希望自己也有那么简单的东西——比如一根胡萝卜——好让克里斯托夫振作起来。

paras.en: When she’d first met Kristoff, she’d thought he was just a perpetual grump, but as she spent more time with him, she realized that he was someone who loved to laugh and wore a smile easily. Now, though, she could see the solitary mountain man slowly returning. Worry carved lines into his face and his mouth tugged down.
paras.zh: 刚认识克里斯托夫时，她还以为他是个天生的臭脾气，可相处久了才发现，他其实爱笑，笑容来得毫不费力。可此刻，她眼看着那个独来独往的山地汉子又慢慢回来了。忧虑在他脸上刻出纹路，嘴角也向下耷拉着。

paras.en: Anna slowed to a walk and slipped her hand into his. “Hey. It’ll be okay. I promised we’d fix this mess in three days, and we will. Wolf and all.”
paras.zh: 安娜放慢脚步，把手悄悄伸进他的掌心。“嘿。会没事的。我答应过三天内收拾好这摊子乱子，我们说到做到。连那只狼一起。”

paras.en: Kristoff shook his head, brown eyes troubled. “I just don’t understand what’s happening. First the Blight, and then I couldn’t find the trolls, and then—”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫摇摇头，棕色的眼睛里满是愁绪。“我就是想不明白，这一切到底是怎么回事。先是枯萎病，然后我找不到岩精，再然后——”

paras.en: “Wait, what?” Anna gasped. “What do you mean, you couldn’t find the trolls?”
paras.zh: “等等，什么？”安娜倒吸一口气。“什么叫你找不到岩精了？”

paras.en: “They weren’t in the Valley of the Living Rock, and they didn’t leave behind any message,” Kristoff explained. He shrugged carelessly, but Anna could see the tension in his broad shoulders. “They’re mysterious creatures, I get it, but they usually at least leave me snail mail.” Snail mail, as Anna knew from experience, was notes written on the bottom of leaves with the help of friendly forest snails. They tended to be a bit difficult to read, and very, very sticky.
paras.zh: “他们不在活石谷，也没留下任何口信。”克里斯托夫解释道。他装作漫不经心地耸耸肩，可安娜看得出他宽阔的肩膀绷得紧紧的。“我知道他们是神秘的家伙，可他们起码总该给我留几封蜗牛信吧。”凭经验安娜知道，所谓蜗牛信，就是请友善的森林蜗牛帮忙，写在叶子背面的字条。那种字条向来有点难认，而且黏糊糊的。

paras.en: “Have they ever done that before?” Anna asked, but before Kristoff could answer, Sven’s head jerked up, his ears swiveling forward.
paras.zh: “他们以前这样过吗？”安娜问，可克里斯托夫还没来得及答，斯文的头猛地抬起，耳朵刷地转向前方。

paras.en: Kristoff dropped Anna’s hand. “What is it, boy?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫松开了安娜的手。“怎么了，老伙计？”

paras.en: But Anna thought she knew, as a soft, far-off wailing met their ears. It almost sounded like the wind, mournful and ghostly, but the pitch of it sent a rush of goosebumps cascading across Anna’s arms. Because it was not the wind. This was an utterly human sound—and it was coming from the village.
paras.zh: 可安娜觉得自己已经猜到了——一阵轻柔而遥远的哀嚎飘进了他们的耳朵。那声音几乎像风，哀怨而飘忽，可它的音调让安娜的手臂上霎时炸起一层鸡皮疙瘩。因为那不是风。这是彻头彻尾属于人的声音——而且是从村庄传来的。

paras.en: “No,” Elsa breathed, and Anna felt sick again. They sprinted the rest of the way.
paras.zh: “不。”艾莎低低地吐出一个字，安娜又泛起一阵恶心。剩下的路，他们是一路狂奔过去的。

paras.en: The village of Arendelle curved around the harbor, balancing along the bay like a flock of birds ringing the edge of a birdbath. Anna had always taken pride in the village’s vibrant homes, painted with bright splashes of color and trimmed with exquisite detail. Many villagers liked to add personal touches that matched the personality of those living inside—and Anna knew and loved each and every one of them. There hadn’t been one week in the last three years that she hadn’t made a trip into the village, even on the days when Elsa wasn’t able to join her.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔的村庄沿着海港弯成一道弧线，稳稳地伏在港湾边，像一群围着浅水盆边缘的小鸟。安娜一向为村里那些鲜活的屋子自豪，栋栋刷着明快的色彩，缀着精致的细部。许多村民喜欢添上些贴合屋主性情的个人点缀——而这里的每一处，安娜都认识，也都喜爱。过去三年里，没有哪个星期她不往村里跑一趟，哪怕有些日子艾莎无法同行。

paras.en: On a usual morning, the villagers woke early, gathering fresh loaves of bread for breakfast and exchanging news from the previous day. Anna much preferred the village to the castle, and she loved having friends. Friends like Baker Blodget, who always had a spare basket of fresh butter biscuits to share with the children—and, occasionally, Anna. Or Akim, the seamster who was deft with the knitting needles and had made Anna her very own hat with cat ears. And then there were the three sisters, Supriya, Deepa, and Jaya, who couldn’t wait to see Anna every week to discuss the latest books they’d read and turned into a play.
paras.zh: 平常的早晨，村民们起得很早，取来新鲜面包当早点，顺便交换头一天的新闻。比起城堡，安娜更喜欢村庄，她也喜欢有朋友环绕。比如面包师布洛杰特，他总有现成的一篮新鲜黄油饼干分给孩子们——偶尔也分给安娜。还有裁缝阿基姆，针线活灵巧无比，还给安娜织过一顶她专属的猫耳帽。还有三姐妹——苏普丽雅、迪帕和贾亚，她们每周都迫不及待地要见安娜，一起讨论新读的书，再把它改编成戏来演。

paras.en: That was how a usual morning looked. But this was not a usual morning. Not at all. The cobblestoned streets were empty of people, but full of their screams. Before the wolf had entered the castle, it must have attacked the village.
paras.zh: 平常的早晨，就该是这个样子。可今天不是平常的早晨。完全不是。鹅卵石街道上空无一人，却满是他们尖叫的回声。狼进城堡之前，一定先袭击了村庄。

paras.en: “NO—” Anna began to yell, but Elsa put a hand over her mouth, stifling her cry.
paras.zh: “不——”安娜刚要喊，艾莎一把捂住她的嘴，把叫声堵了回去。

paras.en: “Shhh.” Elsa pointed to a window. Peering inside, Anna saw Madam Eniola fast asleep, her nightcap askew on her gray hair. Her eyes were closed, but her mouth was open in a bloodcurdling scream. And Anna knew deep in her bones that if Madam Eniola’s eyes were to flutter open, they would be as bright yellow as the wolf’s. Like what happened to Kai and Gerda.
paras.zh: “嘘。”艾莎指了指一扇窗。安娜凑近往里看，只见埃尼雪宝人睡得正沉，睡帽歪扣在灰白的头发上。她双眼紧闭，嘴却大张着，正发出一声令人毛骨悚然的尖叫。安娜打骨子里知道，倘若埃尼雪宝人的眼皮颤颤睁开，那双眼睛一定会亮黄如狼眼。就像凯和格尔达那样。

paras.en: “If we provoke them,” Elsa whispered, “I think they’ll attack us.”
paras.zh: “要是惊动了他们，”艾莎低声说，“我想他们会攻击我们。”

paras.en: Anna nodded, sensing that her sister was right. “We just need to get some mint leaves for Sven,” she whispered. “Then we can go.”
paras.zh: 安娜点点头，觉得姐姐说得对。“咱们只要给斯文弄到薄荷叶。”她压低声音。“然后就离开。”

paras.en: “We don’t split up,” Elsa said, looking each of them in the eye and taking Olaf’s hand. “We stay together, we stay silent, and we keep moving.” Spoken like a true leader.
paras.zh: “我们不分头行动。”艾莎说，挨个直视他们的眼睛，牵起雪宝的手。“我们待在一起，不出声，一直走。”这话真有领袖的气派。

paras.en: They moved through the cobblestoned paths toward the market. Anna shuddered as they rounded every corner. Though there was no one in the streets, she had the constant feeling that someone was watching—as if all the windows were eyes staring at them.
paras.zh: 他们沿着鹅卵石小道朝集市走去。每转过一个街角，安娜都打一个寒颤。街上虽空无一人，她却始终觉得有什么在盯着自己——仿佛所有的窗户都成了凝视他们的眼睛。

paras.en: Or as though a wolf were in the shadows, just waiting to pounce.
paras.zh: 又仿佛暗影里蛰伏着一只狼，只等扑上来的时机。

paras.en: But, Anna assured herself, Elsa had sealed off the castle. The wolf, her nightmare wolf, was trapped inside, contained until Anna could figure out a better plan. Once they got help for the exhausted Sven—who now lifted each hoof as though it were heavy as a boulder—Anna would figure out a way to sneak back into the castle and read through each and every book in the hidden room, page by page, searching for a counter spell. There had to be one, even if she couldn’t remember having seen one. And if the counter spell’s runes hadn’t yet been translated…well, then she would just have to figure out how to decode the language, even if it took her twenty years.
paras.zh: 不过，安娜安慰自己，艾莎已经封死了城堡。那只狼，她梦里的那只狼，被困在了里面，在安娜想出更好的办法之前，出不来。等帮筋疲力尽的斯文——他如今每抬一次蹄，都像在搬一块巨石——找到救助，安娜就想法子溜回城堡，把密室里的每本书一页一页翻遍，寻找破解的咒语。一定有这么一道，哪怕她不记得见过。要是破解咒语的符文还没人译出来……那她就只好自己琢磨怎么破译那种文字，哪怕要花上二十年。

paras.en: Worry gnawed at her stomach. She knew she did not have twenty years. She might not even have a day. Who else would the wolf enchant with its nightmare bewitchment? What would happen to all of them in the end?
paras.zh: 忧虑啃噬着她的胃。她知道自己没有二十年。也许连一天都没有。狼还会用那噩梦的蛊术迷住谁？到头来，他们所有人会落得什么下场？

paras.en: They reached the forest-green doors of the botanist’s shop, and Elsa turned toward her companions. “Stay with Anna,” she instructed Kristoff, and before Anna could stop her sister, or join her, Elsa was inside Gabriella’s shop. Anna made to follow her.
paras.zh: 他们来到草药师铺子那两扇森绿色的门前，艾莎转向同伴们。“跟着安娜。”她吩咐克里斯托夫。安娜还没来得及拦住姐姐、或者跟上去，艾莎已经进了加布里埃拉的铺子。安娜抬脚要追。

paras.en: Kristoff stepped in front of her with a gentle smile. “Elsa said to stay,” he said.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫带着温和的笑，挡在她身前。“艾莎说了，留下。”他说。

paras.en: “I can’t let her go in there alone!”
paras.zh: “我不能让她一个人进去！”

paras.en: “I think she’s got it covered,” Kristoff said, even as he unhooked his pickax from across his shoulder. “She is queen.”
paras.zh: “我看她应付得来。”克里斯托夫说着，已把肩头的镐摘了下来。“她可是女王。”

paras.en: “She’s my sister first.” Anna looked at Olaf. “Please stay with Sven and make sure he doesn’t fall asleep.” Olaf saluted her as she went through the doorway, Kristoff just behind her. Inside the shop, a wailing scream reverberated, a sound so loud and clear and sad that Anna wished she could stick one of the many bunches of dried herbs in her ears to drown it out. Then—the screaming stopped. A moment later, Elsa came flying down the staircase.
paras.zh: “她首先是我姐姐。”安娜看向雪宝。“求你守着斯文，别让他睡着。”安娜穿过门口时，雪宝朝她敬了个礼，克里斯托夫紧随其后。铺子里回荡着一声哀哭，那么响亮、清晰又凄楚，安娜真想抓起挂着的哪一束干草药塞进耳朵，把这声音盖过去。接着——尖叫戛然而止。片刻之后，艾莎从楼梯上飞奔而下。

paras.en: “Go!” Elsa said, her voice wild with fear. “We need to leave now!”
paras.zh: “走！”艾莎说，声音里满是惊惶。“我们必须马上离开！”

paras.en: They hurried out and slammed the door, and then Elsa sealed its seams with ice, for good measure. “I accidentally woke the botanist,” Elsa said, panting. And indeed, Anna could hear footsteps as Gabriella moved inside.
paras.zh: 他们急忙出来，砰地关上门，艾莎又用冰封住门缝，以求万无一失。“我不小心吵醒了草药师。”艾莎喘着气说。果然，安娜听得见加布里埃拉在里头走动的脚步声。

paras.en: “Did you get the mint?” Kristoff asked.
paras.zh: “薄荷拿到了吗？”克里斯托夫问。

paras.en: Elsa held out her hand, flashing a bit of green leaf under Sven’s nose.
