paras.zh: 艾莎伸出手，在斯文鼻尖下晃出一片绿叶。

paras.en: Sven’s head jerked up, and Anna noticed with relief that his pupils contracted, ever so slightly as he inhaled the sharp scent.
paras.zh: 斯文的头猛地一抬，安娜欣慰地发现，他嗅到那股刺鼻的气味时，瞳孔微微收缩了一点点。

paras.en: “Then what are we waiting for?” Anna said. “Let’s go.” But before she could turn around, there was a flash of movement out of the corner of her eye.
paras.zh: “那我们还等什么？”安娜说。“咱们走。”可她还没来得及转身，眼角余光里就闪过一道动静。

paras.en: Kristoff had raised his pickax over his head. “Quiet,” he whispered, not taking his eyes from the road. “Something’s coming.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫已把镐举过头顶。“安静。”他低声说，眼睛一刻不离大路。“有什么东西过来了。”

paras.en: A shadow moved toward them across the cobblestones. Anna held her breath. A figure came into view. Tall, and quick. Elsa raised her hands, and then…
paras.zh: 一道影子踏着鹅卵石朝他们移近。安娜屏住呼吸。一个身影进入视野。高高的，动作飞快。艾莎举起双手，接着……

paras.en: “Hoo-hoo,” a voice whispered. “Girls, is that you?”
paras.zh: “嗬——嗬。”一个声音轻声说。“姑娘们，是你们吗？”

paras.en: “Oaken,” Anna whispered.
paras.zh: “奥肯。”安娜低声道。

paras.en: Sure enough, there stood Oaken, a large, powerfully built man with shoulders as wide as a rowboat and legs as thick as tree trunks. But despite his rather formidable height, Oaken’s round cheeks were as rosy as a porcelain doll’s, and his auburn beard and the frizz poking out from under his cap clashed gloriously with the green wool knit sweater that Anna knew his nan had made for him.
paras.zh: 果然，站在那儿的是奥肯——一个高大壮实的人，肩膀宽得像条划艇，腿粗得像树干。不过，尽管个子慑人，奥肯圆圆的脸颊却红扑扑的像个瓷娃娃，赤褐色的胡须和便帽底下翘出的卷发，与他那件安娜知道是他奶奶织的绿色羊毛毛衣相映成趣。

paras.en: Oaken lifted a finger to his lips. Then he clasped his fingers together. He looked as though he’d aged ten years since Anna had seen him just the other week during a visit to his trading post. Exhaustion sullied his face, and the cap on his head was askew. His ruddy muttonchops twitched as he blinked wide blue eyes. He beckoned.
paras.zh: 奥肯竖起一根手指抵在唇边。然后他十指交握。安娜不过几个星期前才去过他的商栈，可他看上去像是一下子老了十岁。疲惫笼罩着他的脸，头上的帽子也歪着。他眨着一双蓝莹莹的大眼，红褐色的络腮鬓胡跟着抽动。他招了招手。

paras.en: Together, they walked quietly but quickly through the empty streets, following the dirt path that Anna knew would take them down into a grassy valley surrounded by silver birch trees. But even though Anna knew the path well, everything seemed different. Trees that should have felt as familiar as old friends became just another potential place for a wolf to hide. Had it escaped the hold of the castle? As soon as they stepped out of the village, Elsa turned around, and again waved her hands, directing a rush of cold and a flurry of ice over the village.
paras.zh: 他们一起悄声却迅疾地穿过空荡的街道，沿着一条土路前行——安娜知道，那条路会引他们下行，走进一个银桦环绕的青草山谷。可尽管安娜对这条路再熟悉不过，一切却都变了样。本该像老朋友一样亲切的树木，如今成了狼可能藏身的又一处所在。它逃出城堡的封锁了吗？他们刚一出村，艾莎便转过身，再次挥动双手，把一股寒流和漫天冰凌倾泻在村庄上空。

paras.en: A minute later, the village, too, was encased in an ice dome, the screaming sobs muffled. Elsa didn’t say anything as she hurried to catch up with the group, but Anna could read the expression on her sister’s face clear enough: I had to. For their own good. And for ours. And Anna knew her sister was right. What if the wolf got out of the castle, and was feeling hungry? What if the sleepwalkers accidentally wandered out of the village toward the castle and freed the wolf? What Elsa had done was the right thing to do.
paras.zh: 一分钟不到，村庄也被罩进了一座冰穹，哭喊声被闷在了里头。艾莎什么也没说，急忙赶上来与大家会合，可安娜把姐姐脸上的神情看得一清二楚：我不得不这么做。为了他们好。也为了我们。安娜知道姐姐是对的。万一狼出了城堡，正觉得饿呢？万一那些梦游的人稀里糊涂地走出村庄、朝城堡去，把狼放了出来呢？艾莎所做的，是对的。

paras.en: Finally, it was safe for them to speak.
paras.zh: 终于，他们可以开口说话了。

paras.en: “Thank the glaciers you’re all right,” Oaken said. “We hoped you were okay when we saw the ice encase the castle.”
paras.zh: “感谢冰川，你们没事。”奥肯说。“我们看到冰把城堡封住，就一直盼着你们平安。”

paras.en: Anna’s hope, which had been slipping away from her since Gabriella’s shop, caught on his word.
paras.zh: 自打进了加布里埃拉的铺子便一路消散的希望，被他的话重新接住了。

paras.en: “We?” Elsa repeated excitedly, clearly thinking along similar lines. “So, not everyone is asleep?”
paras.zh: “我们？”艾莎兴奋地重复道，显然也想到了一处。“这么说，不是所有人都睡着了？”

paras.en: Oaken nodded. “A handful of us managed to flee to my Wandering Oaken’s Trading Post—”
paras.zh: 奥肯点点头。“我们几个设法逃到了我的‘流浪奥肯商栈’——”

paras.en: “And Sauna!” Olaf inserted. “Oh, I’d like to go into your sauna!”
paras.zh: “还有桑拿房！”雪宝插嘴。“哦，我真想进你的桑拿房！”

paras.en: “And Sauna, yes.” Oaken nodded. “That’s where we’re going now.” Oaken was a shopkeeper who sold a little bit of this and a little bit of that, from carrots to snow shovels to healing draughts and more. But most famous of all was his sauna, a room of cedarwood and steam that could make even the coldest winter nights feel like a balmy evening in the jungle.
paras.zh: “还有桑拿房，对。”奥肯点头。“我们现在就去那儿。”奥肯是个什么都卖一点的店主，从胡萝卜到雪铲，再到疗伤药水，应有尽有。但他最有名的，还得数那间桑拿房——雪松木与蒸汽织成的屋子，能把最冷的寒夜蒸得像丛林里温煦的傍晚。

paras.en: His shop sat in a small pocket in the forest, a little way off from a small creek that fed into a larger river and on the path that led to the North Mountain and the sparkling ice palace Elsa had crafted when she’d first experimented with her powers three years before. The little wooden cabin had been built with loving attention to detail, with geometric patterns carved into its logs, and tall windows fitted with diamond-paned glass.
paras.zh: 他的铺子坐落在森林深处一小块僻静的空地上，离一条汇入大河的小溪不远，正处在通往北山的路上——北山上闪着光的冰宫，是三年前艾莎初试魔力时亲手造的。那座小木屋的一木一石都造得情意满满，原木上刻着几何花纹，高窗镶着菱形格玻璃。

paras.en: Oaken took great pride in his shop. He’d once admitted to Anna that he used to think about becoming a designer before figuring out his real joy in life came from taking care of people and making sure they could get whatever they needed from him—for a fair price. Kristoff would disagree with that last part.
paras.zh: 奥肯对他的铺子极尽自豪。他曾向安娜坦言，从前想过要当设计师，后来才悟出自己人生真正的快乐，在于照料别人，确保他们能以公道的价钱，从他这儿买到所需的一切。末了那半句，克里斯托夫可不敢苟同。

paras.en: Oaken’s trading post was open around the clock, and weary travelers could always find the sauna and a pile of fluffy towels ready and waiting to warm them. But as they neared the shop, Anna saw that for the first time in three years, the curtains were drawn, and a little painted sign hung in the window: CLOSED.
paras.zh: 奥肯的商栈昼夜营业，疲惫的旅人随时都能找到桑拿房，和一堆蓬松柔软、暖意迎人的毛巾。可当他们走近铺子，安娜看见三年来头一回，窗帘拉上了，窗里挂着一块手绘小牌：歇业。

paras.en: “This way,” Oaken whispered, leading them around to a back entrance that Anna had only seen but never entered. He knocked on the door: one long tap, followed by three quick ones. Nothing happened, and then Anna spotted a tiny quiver behind the curtains.
paras.zh: “这边走。”奥肯低声说，领他们绕到后门——那道门安娜只远远见过，从没踏进去过。他敲了敲门：一下长敲，接着三下急叩。起初没有动静，随后安娜瞥见窗帘后微微一颤。

paras.en: “Password, please?” came a man’s voice.
paras.zh: “请对暗号。”一个男人的声音传来。

paras.en: “Surplus,” Oaken whispered.
paras.zh: “盈余。”奥肯轻声说。

paras.en: There was the sound of footsteps, then several clicks and a jangle of metal before the door creaked open.
paras.zh: 一阵脚步声，接着是几声咔哒和金属的碰撞，门吱呀一声开了。

paras.en: “Hurry, hurry,” Oaken whispered. He swept Anna, Elsa, Kristoff, Sven, and Olaf inside, then stepped into the cabin himself, twisting the doorknob to make sure it was locked. Satisfied with his work, he turned to face them, looking concerned. “Four-footed animals aren’t usually allowed inside Wandering Oaken’s Trading Post and Sauna. This is an exception, ja?”
paras.zh: “快，快。”奥肯低声催促。他把安娜、艾莎、克里斯托夫、斯文和雪宝一股脑儿扫进屋，自己才跨进门，拧了拧门把手，确认锁好了。他对自己的手艺颇为满意，这才转身面对众人，一脸忧色。“四条腿的动物，平时是不许进‘流浪奥肯商栈兼桑拿房’的。这回算破例，对吧？”

paras.en: “He’s very well-behaved,” Anna said of Sven. “I promise he won’t be a problem.”
paras.zh: “他很守规矩的。”安娜替斯文担保。“我保证他不惹麻烦。”

paras.en: Oaken’s expression shifted, and he nodded. At last, they were all safe.
paras.zh: 奥肯的神色缓和下来，点了点头。总算，他们都安全了。

paras.en: Metal screeched again as Oaken slid several bolts shut and clicked no less than seven padlocks. The shopkeeper wasn’t taking any chances of letting a wolf enter his cabin and mess up his tidy shop. Anna looked around. Well, what used to be his tidy shop.
paras.zh: 奥肯拉上好几道插销，咔哒咔哒挂了不下七把挂锁，金属又是一阵吱呀。这店主可不肯冒一点险，让狼闯进木屋、搅乱他整洁的铺子。安娜环顾四周。好吧，是他曾经整洁的铺子。

paras.en: “Oh, dear,” Elsa murmured.
paras.zh: “哦，天哪。”艾莎低声道。

paras.en: Oaken’s shelves, stuffed with an odd assortment of goods—flowerpots sitting on top of books, next to a corner of rakes and barrels of candied nuts—usually marched in straight lines throughout the shop. But now, the shelves and all their wares had been pushed to the edges. Reinforcements for the windows, Anna guessed. In case someone—or somewolf—tried to break in. It looked as though the cabin itself were preparing for a great war, and it wasn’t just the cabin that was ready for a fight. Looking around, she spotted two villagers in the storeroom. Tuva the blacksmith, her hammer dangling from a tool belt, stood guard at the front door, and at the counter, scribbling across old receipts, was Wael.
paras.zh: 奥肯的货架上堆着五花八门的杂货——花盆摞在书上，旁边一角立着耙子和一桶桶糖渍坚果——平日里在铺子中排成整齐的直线。可现在，货架连同所有货品，都被推到了四边。安娜猜，那是用来加固窗户的。以防有人——或某只狼——试图破门而入。整间木屋像在备战一场大战，而且严阵以待的不只是木屋。她四下张望，看见储藏室里有两个村民。铁匠图娃腰间的工具带上挂着锤子，守在前门；柜台边，韦尔正伏在旧收据上疾书。

paras.en: At the sight of him, Anna felt a twinge of embarrassment and an even stronger pinch of annoyance. If the journalist hadn’t goaded her yesterday, maybe she wouldn’t have promised everyone that Elsa could fix everything in three days, and then maybe Elsa wouldn’t have had a council meeting without her. And then maybe Anna wouldn’t have accidentally spelled the wolf out of her nightmare.
paras.zh: 一见到他，安娜心里先是一阵难堪，接着涌起更强烈的恼火。要不是那记者昨天出言相激，她也许就不会向所有人夸口，说艾莎三天内能解决一切；她不夸口，艾莎也许就不会背着她开议事会。而安娜也许就不会一失手，把狼从噩梦里念了出来。

paras.en: “Where is everyone else?” Olaf asked as he hopped off Sven, made his way into the center of the room, and peered behind overturned bookshelves. “Are they all in the sauna?”
paras.zh: “其他人都去哪儿了？”雪宝问着，从斯文背上跳下来，走到屋子中央，往翻倒的书架后面张望。“他们都在桑拿房里吗？”

paras.en: Tuva shook her head. “This is all of us. We’re the only ones left.”
paras.zh: 图娃摇摇头。“就我们这些了。我们是仅剩的人。”

paras.en: Anna froze. Earlier, she had assumed she’d find at least thirty or forty other villagers crammed inside. Not just two. She looked over at Elsa, but if her older sister had been expecting to find more villagers in there, her expression didn’t show it.
paras.zh: 安娜僵住了。方才她还以为，至少会有三四十个村民挤在里头。而不是只有两个。她看向艾莎，可即便姐姐原以为能在屋里见到更多村民，脸上也丝毫没有显露。

paras.en: Elsa nodded. “Okay. If this is what we have, this is what we have.” And though her voice was calm, Anna saw that she played with the tassels of their mother’s scarf. “Can someone please tell me exactly what happened?”
paras.zh: 艾莎点点头。“好。有多少人，就是多少人。”尽管声音平静，安娜却看见她的手指缠弄着母亲那条围巾的流苏。“谁能告诉我，这一切究竟是怎么发生的？”

paras.en: “I can.” Wael held up a piece of paper. “I’m writing everything down.”
paras.zh: “我来。”韦尔举起一页纸。“我一直在把一切都记下来。”

paras.en: Elsa, Oaken, and Tuva moved toward the countertop, but Anna made her way to the corner, where Oaken had dropped off a pile of thick wool blankets that Kristoff was now crunching into a soft nest around Sven.
paras.zh: 艾莎、奥肯和图娃都朝柜台那边走去，安娜却走向角落——奥肯在那儿扔了一堆厚实的羊毛毯，克里斯托夫正把毯子拢成一团松软的窝，围住斯文。

paras.en: “I don’t understand.” Kristoff shook his head. “He was fine when we were looking for the trolls, and even when we got back to the castle, he seemed good. I mean, hungry, but good.” He shook his head. “I know it sounds ridiculous, but it’s like he got the Blight by just looking at the wolf. He’s been out of sorts ever since!”
paras.zh: “我就是不明白。”克里斯托夫摇着头。“我们去找岩精的时候他还好好的，就是回到城堡时，他看上去也不错。我是说，饿了点，但还行。”他又摇了摇头。“我知道这听着荒唐，可就好像他只是看了狼一眼，就染上了枯萎病。从那以后他就一直不对劲！”

paras.en: “True.” Anna leaned close to Sven and waved the mint leaves under his nose. “Come on, don’t fall asleep!” she said.
paras.zh: “没错。”安娜凑近斯文，把薄荷叶在他鼻尖下晃了晃。“快，别睡着！”她说。

paras.en: But the reindeer’s eyes drooped. It was exactly as SoYun had described. The Blight was coming on quickly and horribly. Kristoff gently shook his muzzle again and again. There was nothing they could do.
paras.zh: 可驯鹿的眼睛还是耷拉了下去。这和SoYun描述的一模一样。枯萎病来得又快又凶。克里斯托夫一遍又一遍地轻摇着他的口鼻。他们无计可施。

paras.en: “At this point, we need a mystic,” Anna said, thinking of the magically inclined wise-folk who existed in legends.
paras.zh: “事到如今，我们需要一位秘术师。”安娜说，想起了传说中那些通晓魔法的智者。

paras.en: “Anna? Kristoff? Can you come here?” Elsa called.
paras.zh: “安娜？克里斯托夫？你们能过来一下吗？”艾莎唤道。

paras.en: Anna and Kristoff hurried over. As they neared, Wael held out mugs to them. “No one wants to fall asleep, just in case.”
paras.zh: 安娜和克里斯托夫赶紧过去。两人走近时，韦尔把杯子递给他们。“谁都不想睡着，以防万一。”

paras.en: “Just in case what?” Anna took a sip. She almost choked. It was the strongest cup of coffee she’d ever tasted, and she could practically feel the tips of her hair twist up as the coffee coursed through her. Based on Kristoff’s now red cheeks and the tremor of Elsa’s hand, Anna suspected that they, too, had not been ready for the jolt.
paras.zh: “以防什么？”安娜抿了一口，差点呛着。那是她喝过最浓的一杯咖啡，咖啡淌下喉咙时，她几乎觉得发梢都跟着卷了起来。看看克里斯托夫此刻通红的双颊，还有艾莎发颤的手，安娜猜他们俩也被这股猛劲儿打了个措手不及。

paras.en: “Everyone who was asleep when the wolf ran through town has stayed asleep,” Tuva said, her usually cheerful face somber. “Only the people who were up late at night avoided falling under its sleeping curse,” she continued. “That’s why we made the coffee so strong. Who knows what will happen if we fall asleep?” It was a terrible thought, made all the more terrible by the sudden exhaustion that washed over Anna. All she wanted to do was curl up and sleep.
paras.zh: “狼跑过镇子时睡着的人，到现在都没醒，”图娃说，一向开朗的脸上此刻一片凝重。“只有熬到深夜还没睡的人，才躲过了它的沉睡诅咒。”她接着说。“所以我们才把咖啡煮得这么浓。谁知道我们一旦睡着，会发生什么？”这念头可怕极了，而一阵骤然袭来的困倦更让它雪上加霜，安娜只觉浑身发沉。她一心只想蜷起来睡上一觉。

paras.en: “I was awake, but Gerda and Kai, well, they must have been asleep, because, I mean, they would never…” Elsa trailed off, at a loss.
paras.zh: “我当时醒着，可格尔达和凯，嗯，他们一定是睡着了，因为，我是说，他们绝不会……”艾莎的声音低下去，一时语塞。

paras.en: “Didn’t they attack us?” Olaf asked.
paras.zh: “他们不是攻击我们了吗？”雪宝问。

paras.en: “Well, they didn’t know it was us!” Anna rushed to clear her friends’ names. “And they weren’t exactly themselves….I think they thought we were part of their nightmares.” Speaking about them, Anna hoped Kai and Gerda were okay, and that the wolf hadn’t hurt them any more than it already had.
paras.zh: “哎呀，他们不知道那是我们呀！”安娜赶忙替朋友们辩白。“而且他们也不完全是自己了……我想，他们是把我们当成了噩梦的一部分。”说着说着，安娜只盼凯和格尔达平安无事，盼狼没再伤害他们。

paras.en: Tuva nodded. “Exactly the same with my wife. Ada attacked me, all the while screaming for me to come help her. And there was absolutely nothing I could do.” The expression on Tuva’s face broke Anna’s heart. She knew only too well what it was like to feel helpless. Tuva collected herself and continued. “I left her at home. She just kept screaming and screaming.…”
paras.zh: 图娃点点头。“我妻子也一模一样。艾达攻击我，一边还尖叫着，要我快去救她。而我什么也做不了。”图娃脸上的神情让安娜心都要碎了。那种无助的滋味，她再清楚不过。图娃定了定神，继续说。“我把她留在了家里。她就一直尖叫，尖叫个不停……”

paras.en: “Anna, you said we need a mystic, ja?” asked Oaken, tapping the tips of his fingers together. “Maybe Sorenson can help!”
paras.zh: “安娜，你刚说我们需要秘术师，对吧？”奥肯指尖相抵，敲着问道。“也许索伦森能帮上忙！”

paras.en: “Sore-what?” Olaf asked.
paras.zh: “索……什么？”雪宝问。

paras.en: “Sorenson,” said Oaken. “He’s what you’d call an expert in myths and lore. He’s the mystic of Miner’s Mountain.”
paras.zh: “索伦森。”奥肯说。“你们可以叫他神话传说的行家。他是矿工山的秘术师。”

paras.en: “No one lives on that mountain but bears and lynx,” Kristoff said.
paras.zh: “那座山上除了熊和猞猁，根本没人住。”克里斯托夫说。

paras.en: The coffee was way too strong. Anna could have sworn she’d just heard Oaken say that an expert in myths and lore—a mystic—lived on Miner’s Mountain.
paras.zh: 这咖啡劲儿实在太大了。安娜简直能发誓，她刚才是听见奥肯说，有个神话传说的行家——一位秘术师——住在矿工山上。

paras.en: Elsa tilted her head. “What?”
paras.zh: 艾莎偏了偏头。“什么？”

paras.en: Oaken started to say something else, but Anna was too distracted to pay attention. Mystics didn’t exist. They were just characters in stories Anna and Elsa’s mother would tell them before bed as young girls. Mystics were rumored to dabble in potions, enchantments, and powerful spells—but such people simply didn’t exist, or so Anna had thought.
paras.zh: 奥肯刚要再说什么，安娜却已心神大乱，没听进去。秘术师根本不存在。她们不过是安娜和艾莎小时候，母亲睡前故事里的角色。传闻秘术师摆弄药水、符咒和厉害的咒语——可这种人根本不存在，至少安娜一直是这么以为的。

paras.en: But if anyone would know how to reverse an accidental spell, it would be a mystic. Suddenly, finding Sorenson seemed more promising than returning to the secret room. Anna shook her head. If anyone had told her a week ago that she would be seriously considering seeking out a mystic, she would have laughed. But then again, she never would have believed that a nightmare wolf would be stalking the kingdom.
paras.zh: 可要说谁能逆转一道念错的咒语，那非秘术师莫属。刹那间，去找索伦森，似乎比回密室更有盼头。安娜摇了摇头。要是一周前有人告诉她，她会认真考虑去寻访一位秘术师，她准会笑出声来。可话说回来，她也从没料到，会有一只噩梦里的狼在王国里游荡。

paras.en: “Why haven’t we heard about Sorenson before?” Elsa demanded.
paras.zh: “我们以前怎么从没听说过索伦森？”艾莎追问。

paras.en: “He keeps to himself in a tall tower,” Oaken explained. “But if this is a curse, he could help!”
paras.zh: “他深居简出，住在一座高塔里。”奥肯解释道。“可如果这是诅咒，他能帮上忙！”

paras.en: “Is he…” Elsa waved her fingers, sending a dance of snowflakes twirling through the room. “Like me?”
paras.zh: “那他是不是……”艾莎挥了挥手指，一朵雪花在屋里打着旋儿飞舞。“像我一样？”

paras.en: “Why, no.” Oaken shook his head. “No one is like you.”
paras.zh: “嗐，不是。”奥肯摇头。“没人像你。”

paras.en: “We need to get to him!” Anna said, turning to her sister, who looked less than convinced. Anna whirled to Kristoff and, seeking backup, asked him, “Don’t you agree?”
paras.zh: “我们得去找他！”安娜说着转向姐姐，可姐姐一脸将信将疑。安娜猛地转向克里斯托夫，想寻个帮腔，问他：“你也不反对，对吧？”

paras.en: But Kristoff didn’t seem to have heard her. He was looking in Sven’s direction, and mumbled, “Why is this happening?” His coffee splashed out of his mug as his hands shook—from worry or from the coffee, Anna could not tell. “Where did it come from?”
paras.zh: 可克里斯托夫像是根本没听见。他望着斯文的方向，喃喃道：“为什么会这样？”他双手发抖，咖啡从杯里泼洒出来——是因为担忧，还是因为咖啡的劲儿，安娜分不清。“它是从哪儿来的？”

paras.en: “Magic,” Oaken said. “It has to be.” His words seemed to suck the air out of the room as Anna cast a glance at Elsa, only to see that her sister seemed to have, at the same time, both curled into herself and become rigid, like a nautilus’s shell.
paras.zh: “魔法。”奥肯说。“只能是魔法。”这话仿佛把屋子里的空气都抽干了。安娜瞥了艾莎一眼，只见姐姐仿佛同时缩进了自己心里，又僵直如石——像一枚鹦鹉螺的壳。

paras.en: “Did you do this?” Wael asked Elsa.
paras.zh: “是你干的吗？”韦尔问艾莎。

paras.en: Anna’s headache returned with furious force. “Elsa would never—”
paras.zh: 安娜的头痛卷土重来，来势汹汹。“艾莎绝不会——”

paras.en: “Of course she wouldn’t!” Tuva said. “And no one is saying she would. But between the rotten crops, the sleeping animals and people, and now the wolf—what else could it be but a curse or a spell of some sort?”
paras.zh: “她当然不会！”图娃说。“也没人说她会。可是烂掉的庄稼、昏睡的牲畜和人，再加上如今这只狼——除了诅咒或某种咒语，还能是什么？”

paras.en: At the blacksmith’s words, guilt surged through Anna. Now was the time for her to come clean. “Elsa?” she said tentatively. The entire room looked at her, and she winced. Her voice had gone very squeaky. “Er…could I…talk to you for a moment? In private?”
paras.zh: 铁匠这话一出，愧疚猛地涌上安娜心头。是时候坦白了。“艾莎？”她试探着唤了一声。满屋子的人都看向她，她缩了缩脖子。她的声音变得格外尖细。“呃……我能不能……单独跟你说句话？就我们俩？”

paras.en: “It’s not like this is a very big place,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: “这地方也不算大啊。”艾莎说。

paras.en: “Excuse me?” Oaken interrupted. “What did you say?”
paras.zh: “你说什么？”奥肯打断道。“你刚说什么？”

paras.en: Elsa gaped. “I mean, I didn’t—it’s lovely, but it’s not, you know, the biggest—”
paras.zh: 艾莎张口结舌。“我是说，我不是——这屋子挺好，但你知道，也不算最大——”

paras.en: Taking advantage of Elsa’s fluster, Anna pulled her sister away from the others and ducked behind the store counter. “We have to go see Sorenson,” Anna whispered, fumbling in her travel cloak pocket for the loose page from Secrets of the Magic Makers.
paras.zh: 安娜趁艾莎慌神的当口，把姐姐从众人身边拉开，躲到店铺柜台后面。“我们得去见索伦森。”安娜低声说，一边在旅行斗篷的口袋里摸索那页从《魔法制造者之秘》上撕下的散页。

paras.en: Elsa looked up at the ceiling and sighed. “Anna, I’ve told you, magic isn’t—”
paras.zh: 艾莎仰头望着天花板，叹了口气。“安娜，我说过了，魔法不是——”

paras.en: “I know, I know.” Anna nodded. “It’s not the solution. But it might be the reason.”
paras.zh: “我知道，我知道。”安娜点头。“它不是解决办法。但它也许正是原因。”

paras.en: “What?” Elsa asked. “Anna, what are you trying to say?”
paras.zh: “什么？”艾莎问。“安娜，你到底想说什么？”

paras.en: “Now, don’t get mad,” Anna said. “It’s just—you see, I heard you having a council meeting without me, which is fine, but for some reason it upset me. I took back Secrets of the Magic Makers for some light reading, you know, because Mother always used to tell us stories at night. So, I found this song, more of a poem really, well, maybe it was a spell, only it turns out that maybe, possibly, it just might have—”
paras.zh: “好了，别生气。”安娜说。“就是——你听我说，我听见你们背着我开议事会，这倒没什么，可不知怎么的，我心里很不是滋味。我就把《魔法制造者之秘》拿回去随便翻翻，你知道的，因为母亲以前总在夜里给我们讲故事。然后，我找到了一首歌，其实更像一首诗，嗯，也许是一段咒语，结果呢，也许、大概、可能——它说不定就——”

paras.en: “Anna.” Elsa sighed, burying her face in her hands.
paras.zh: “安娜。”艾莎叹了口气，双手掩面。

paras.en: “The point is…” Anna took a deep breath and held out the loose page from the book. “Arendelle is cursed…and…I may be the one who cursed it.”
paras.zh: “重点是……”安娜深吸一口气，把那页从书里撕下的散页递了出去。“阿伦黛尔被诅咒了……而且……可能诅咒它的人，就是我。”

paras.en: ANNA HELD HER BREATH as Elsa took the page, her eyes wide, scanning it line by line.
paras.zh: 安娜屏住了呼吸。艾莎接过那页纸，睁大眼睛，一行一行地扫过去。

paras.en: “Anna—did you see the small note at the bottom?”
paras.zh: “安娜——你看见底下那行小字了吗？”

paras.en: “No,” Anna said, turning red. “Why? What’s it say?”
paras.zh: “没看见，”安娜说，脸红了。“怎么了？上面写什么？”

paras.en: Elsa moved the paper in front of her, along with a magnifying glass made of ice that she’d crafted.
paras.zh: 艾莎把纸移到她面前，又取出一面她用冰雕成的放大镜。

paras.en: Peering through the ice, Anna read:
paras.zh: 透过冰镜，安娜读到：

paras.en: *SPELL NOT GUARANTEED TO BE EXACTLY WHAT YOU WISHED FOR.
paras.zh: ＊本咒语不保证恰好如你所愿。

paras.en: **IF NOT REVERSED, SPELL SHALL TAKE ROOT PERMANENTLY ON ITS THIRD SUNRISE.
paras.zh: ＊＊若不加逆转，咒语将在第三个日出时永久扎根。

paras.en: “Oh,” Anna said. “Yeah, I…definitely didn’t see that.”
paras.zh: “哦，”安娜说。“是啊，我……确实没看见。”

paras.en: Elsa bit her lip, and her eyes shimmered.
paras.zh: 艾莎咬住嘴唇，眼里泛起水光。

paras.en: “I’m sorry.” Anna shook her head, all the while hoping she could shake away the words. “I was only trying to help.”
paras.zh: “对不起。”安娜摇着头，只盼能把那些字摇出脑海。“我只是想帮忙。”

paras.en: Elsa sighed. “I know. I can’t be upset at you for that.”
paras.zh: 艾莎叹了口气。“我知道。我不能为这个生你的气。”

paras.en: There was something about Elsa’s words that made Anna want to curl up and cry. She almost would rather have had Elsa yell at her than sigh like she had. If Elsa had yelled at her, it would have meant that she thought of Anna as someone who had the ability to shape the kingdom’s future, but that sigh…it was the same sound her parents had made when a five-year-old Anna accidentally broke a clay figurine of a salamander over the mantel. “I thought it was a dragon,” a sorry Anna had told them. “I thought that it could fly!”
paras.zh: 艾莎的话里有种东西，让安娜想缩成一团哭出来。她宁可艾莎冲她吼，也不愿她这样叹气。要是艾莎吼她，至少说明艾莎还把她当成能左右王国未来的人；可那一声叹气……和父母当年一模一样——五岁的安娜不小心摔碎了壁炉台上那只蝾螈泥像时，父母就是这样。“我还以为它是条龙呢，”满怀歉意的安娜当时对他们说。“我以为它还会飞！”

paras.en: It’s okay, they had said. You didn’t know any better.
paras.zh: 没关系的，他们说，你那时候还不懂事。

paras.en: “Anna!”
paras.zh: “安娜！”

paras.en: Kristoff’s yell cut through Anna’s thought spiral. She shot to her feet. Kristoff never yelled like that. Not even the time Anna had set fire to his sleigh to save them from a pack of normal wolves, of the animal—not magical—variety.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫一声大喊，打断了安娜越陷越深的思绪。她猛地站起身。克里斯托夫从不会那样喊。连那次安娜为了把他们从一群普通野狼——是动物、不是魔法的那种——嘴里救出来、把他雪橇点着了的时候，他都没这样过。

paras.en: “What’s wrong?” she called. Because something had to be wrong for him to sound like that.
paras.zh: “怎么了？”她喊道。因为他这样喊，一定出了事。

paras.en: “Sven.” Kristoff’s eyes and hair were wild. “He fell asleep. He won’t wake up.”
paras.zh: “斯文。”克里斯托夫的头发和眼睛都乱了。“他睡着了。叫不醒。”

paras.en: Anna ran out from behind the counter, aware of Elsa following close behind. Sure enough, Sven’s eyes were shut and his sides heaved with ragged, labored breath.
paras.zh: 安娜从柜台后跑出来，知道艾莎紧跟在后。果不其然，斯文双眼紧闭，身侧随着粗重艰难的呼吸一起一伏。

paras.en: Kristoff rubbed Sven’s cheek with the back of his hand.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫用手背蹭了蹭斯文的脸颊。

paras.en: What to do, what to do, what to do!
paras.zh: 怎么办，怎么办，怎么办！

paras.en: But there was nothing Anna could do, except…“Elsa!” She whirled around to see her sister. “We have to meet this Sorenson person—he may be Sven’s only chance!”
paras.zh: 可安娜什么也做不了，只能——“艾莎！”她猛地转身面向姐姐。“我们一定得去见那个索伦森——他也许是斯文唯一的希望！”

paras.en: “But—”

“We can ask him about, you know.” Anna bumped a little against the word spell, not wanting to admit to everyone just yet who exactly was responsible for the wolf. “And we can see if he knows how to cure the Blight!”
paras.zh: “我们可以问问他……那个……的事。”安娜在“咒语”两个字上轻轻一撞便绕了过去，还不想当众承认那匹狼究竟是谁招来的。“我们还能看看他知不知道怎么治枯萎病！”

paras.en: At least the Blight wasn’t her fault. It had happened before Anna had said her spell, but still…it was rather curious that both the Blight and wolf shared similar symptoms: a strange kind of sleep and color-changing eyes. Anna felt like she was looking at a puzzle with a shifting picture. They could be related, but Anna wasn’t sure how.
paras.zh: 至少枯萎病不是她的错。它发生在安娜念咒之前，可还是……蹊跷的是，枯萎病和狼的症状如此相似：一种奇异的沉睡，和变色的眼睛。安娜觉得自己像在看一幅图案不断变换的拼图。它们可能有关联，可安娜说不清是哪种关联。

paras.en: “Oaken, where exactly in the mountain does Sorenson live?” Elsa asked as Anna hurried back over to the counter.
paras.zh: “奥肯，索伦森到底住在山里什么地方？”安娜快步回到柜台边时，艾莎问道。

paras.en: Oaken pulled out a map and spread it smooth in front of the register, then traced a path east, to Miner’s Mountain. He tapped his finger at the base of the mountain. “Follow the Roaring River past the Black Mountains until you see the signs for the abandoned mines. Beware. They’re dangerous.”
paras.zh: 奥肯抽出一张地图，在收银台前摊平，手指沿着一条路向东划去，指向矿工山。他在山脚下敲了敲。“顺着咆哮河走，过了黑山，直到看见废弃矿井的牌子。小心。那里很危险。”

paras.en: Kristoff leaned forward to get a closer look. “Dangerous how?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫探身凑近细看。“怎么个危险法？”

paras.en: “They’re known for awful cave-ins and terrible landslides,” Oaken said.
paras.zh: “那儿是出了名的塌方和山体滑坡，”奥肯说。

paras.en: “And the Huldrefólk who live in the heart of the mountain,” Tuva added. “They’re tricky. Sometimes, they help. Other times, they lure humans off the safest paths.”
paras.zh: “还有住在山心里的胡尔德精灵，”图娃补充道。“他们狡猾。有时帮忙。有时又把人从最安全的路上诱开。”

paras.en: Wael rolled his eyes. “The Huldrefólk aren’t real, you know. They’re just bedtime stories, an excuse for people who can’t follow directions and a scapegoat for when things go missing.”
paras.zh: 韦尔翻了个白眼。“胡尔德精灵才不是真的存在呢，你知道的。不过是哄孩子睡觉的故事，是给认不得路的人找的借口，也是东西丢了时的替罪羊。”

paras.en: “The Huldrefólk are dangerous,” Tuva continued, ignoring Wael. “You know the stories. They like to hide in the shadows. They’re thieves—they steal things.” The blacksmith dragged her eyes back to Elsa. “I think it would be wiser if you fled, Your Majesty. Maybe another country will have the answer, and they can bring help.”
paras.zh: “胡尔德精灵很危险，”图娃不理会韦尔，继续说。“你知道那些故事的。他们爱躲在阴影里。他们是贼——专偷东西。”铁匠把目光移回艾莎身上。“陛下，我想您还是撤走更明智。也许别的国家会有答案，能带人来相助。”

paras.en: Anna was too stunned to speak. She couldn’t believe Tuva was suggesting they leave their home when it needed them most. And from the look on Elsa’s face, she knew her sister felt the same way.
paras.zh: 安娜惊得说不出话。她不敢相信，图娃竟建议他们在王国最需要人的时候弃家而去。看艾莎的神情，她知道姐姐想的也一样。

paras.en: “Thank you for your advice.” Elsa stood up to pick up her cloak. “I appreciate it. But it’s my job to remain in Arendelle with everybody, and to find a solution, Huldrefólk or no. I’ll leave now.”
paras.zh: “谢谢你的建议。”艾莎起身去拿斗篷。“我很感激。但留下来与所有人同在、找出解决之道，是我的职责，不管有没有胡尔德精灵。我现在就走。”

paras.en: Anna shot up. “Don’t you mean we’ll leave now?”
paras.zh: 安娜腾地站起。“你不是说'我们'现在就走吗？”

paras.en: With a flourish, Elsa swirled her cloak onto her shoulders. “No, Anna. You heard them. It’s too dangerous. I think it would be best if you all left on the royal ship, at least until things are back to normal. I can protect myself.”
paras.zh: 艾莎潇洒地一挥手，把斗篷甩上肩头。“不，安娜。你听见他们说了。太危险了。我想最好你们都坐皇家船离开，至少等一切恢复正常再说。我能保护自己。”

paras.en: Anna could hardly believe her ears. She couldn’t leave Arendelle in such a state of danger. “It’s not about protection,” she said, her thoughts flying fast, trying to come up with a winning argument that could convince Elsa. “It’s about…about…” She looked down at the mug in her hand. “It’s about keeping you awake!” she finished. “You need at least one person with you who can keep you awake—”
paras.zh: 安娜简直不敢相信自己的耳朵。她不能在这种危急关头丢下阿伦黛尔。“这不是保护的问题，”她说，思绪飞转，想找出一条能说服艾莎的理由。“这是……这是……”她低头看了看手里的杯子。“这是为了让你保持清醒！”她接了下去。“你身边至少得有一个人能盯着你、不让你睡着——”

paras.en: “And another who knows the way of the mountains,” Kristoff added. Anna noted with gratitude that he’d already shouldered his traveler’s pack and added a coil of rope to his belt, even though he did cast a worried look at his sleeping reindeer friend. Anna knew how it must feel to volunteer to be separated from a sick and sleeping Sven, but she also knew that it would be even harder for Kristoff to not at least try to help. It was the way she felt, too, and part of the reason why she loved him so much.
paras.zh: “还得有一个认得山路的人，”克里斯托夫补了一句。安娜感激地注意到，他已经把行囊背上肩，腰间还多了一卷绳子，尽管他还是忧心忡忡地看了眼昏睡的驯鹿朋友。安娜明白，自愿离开病中沉睡的斯文是什么滋味；可她也知道，对克里斯托夫来说，连试都不试一下会更难受。她自己也是这种感觉，而这也正是她深爱他的部分原因。

paras.en: Olaf popped up from Sven’s blanket nest. “And a snowman who likes warm hugs!”
paras.zh: 雪宝从斯文的毯子窝里探出头来。“还有个爱暖抱抱的雪人！”

paras.en: For a moment, Elsa stood still, as though she’d been carved from ice. Anna had already started planning how she would sneak away from the royal ship if her sister ordered her aboard, but finally, Elsa raised her hands in surrender. “All right. Anna and Kristoff will come with me. Oaken,” she said, turning to him, “would you please lead the others to the royal ship? Set sail south as fast as you can, and stay there until you hear word from me.”
paras.zh: 有那么一刻，艾莎静静立着，像一尊冰雕。安娜已经在盘算，若是姐姐命她上船，她要怎么从皇家船上溜走；可终于，艾莎举起双手，做了个投降的姿势。“好吧。安娜和克里斯托夫跟我来。奥肯，”她转向他，“请你带其他人去皇家船，好吗？全速向南启航，待在那儿，直到收到我的消息。”

paras.en: “And if we don’t hear back?” Wael asked.
paras.zh: “要是我们等不到回音呢？”韦尔问。

paras.en: Anna stuck her chin up. “I promise you—you will.”
paras.zh: 安娜扬起下巴。“我向你们保证——你们会等到的。”

paras.en: Oaken lifted a thick finger and pointed out the window. “Then I suggest you leave now. The morning is almost over, and you’ll want to reach Sorenson’s before nightfall. And remember: beware the Huldrefólk!”
paras.zh: 奥肯竖起一根粗手指，指向窗外。“那我建议你们现在就动身。早晨快过去了，你们得赶在天黑前到索伦森那儿。记住：当心胡尔德精灵！”

paras.en: As Elsa and Kristoff did a final check of their supplies, Anna fidgeted with the crumpled spell in her cloak pocket. It might have caused trouble, but it was something her mother had touched, and the thought comforted her. Fastening her cloak, Anna went over to Olaf, who was shoveling a few more carrots into his own traveler’s pack.
paras.zh: 艾莎和克里斯托夫最后清点装备时，安娜摆弄着斗篷口袋里那张揉皱的咒语。它也许惹了祸，可那是母亲碰过的东西，这个念头让她心里安稳了些。安娜系好斗篷，走到雪宝身边——他正往自己的行囊里再塞几根胡萝卜。

paras.en: “I’m coming, too. I’m a snowman adventurer! A snoventurer!”
paras.zh: “我也要去。我是个雪人冒险家！雪险家！”

paras.en: Anna smiled and placed a hand on Olaf’s back. At least bravery existed in her snow friend, even if it was lacking in others. “I know you are, but Olaf…I need to ask you to stay here.”
paras.zh: 安娜微微一笑，把手搭在雪宝背上。至少她的雪人朋友有勇气，哪怕别人没有。“我知道你要去，可雪宝……我得请你留在这儿。”

paras.en: Olaf’s grin slid off his face. “You—you don’t want me to come?”
paras.zh: 雪宝脸上的笑容一下子垮了。“你——你不想让我去？”

paras.en: “I do,” Anna said, and it was the truth. Olaf might be silly, and he could occasionally lose his head, but he was wise in ways of the heart and he knew how to bring warmth to cold places. And Anna had a feeling that, soon, they would be in need of hugs more than ever. In fact, she could use one herself now. But the people standing before her could use him even more. She picked up his carrot nose and set it back in place. “Kristoff needs you here to keep an eye on Sven, and Elsa and I need you here to help the villagers stay awake as they carry Sven and head to the ship.” Anna ruffled his twiggy hair.
paras.zh: “我想的，”安娜说，这是真心话。雪宝也许傻乎乎，偶尔还会把脑袋弄丢，可他懂得人心的道理，知道怎么给寒冷的地方带去温暖。而安娜有种预感，很快他们就会比任何时候都更需要拥抱。其实，她现在自己就想要一个。可站在眼前的这些人，比她更需要他。她捡起他的胡萝卜鼻子，把它摆回原位。“克里斯托夫需要你在这儿照看斯文，而我和艾莎需要你在这儿，帮村民们抬着斯文去上船时保持清醒。”安娜揉了揉他树枝般的头发。

paras.en: “Oh, I already have tons of ideas to keep them awake!” Olaf assured her, brightening. “The question is: How will I choose which idea?” He began to tick off his repertoire on his fingers. “I could sing soothing lullabies, do an interpretive dance of falling autumn leaves, recite the names of all the best beaches in the world in alphabetical order—”
paras.zh: “哦，我已经有好多好多主意能让他们清醒了！”雪宝来了精神，向她保证。“问题是：我该怎么挑出哪一个主意？”他掰着手指头数起自己的看家本领。“我可以唱轻柔的摇篮曲，跳一支落叶纷飞的即兴舞，按字母顺序报出全世界最好的海滩的名字——”

paras.en: “Remember,” Kristoff interrupted as he came over, his traveler’s pack heaped with the added supplies from Oaken, “you’re trying to stop them from sleeping. Not put them to sleep.”
paras.zh: “记住，”克里斯托夫走过来打断，他的行囊里堆满了奥肯给的物资，“你是想让他们别睡着。不是哄他们睡。”

paras.en: Anna nudged Kristoff’s boot with her toe. “Hush,” she whispered.
paras.zh: 安娜用脚尖碰了碰克里斯托夫的靴子。“嘘，”她低声说。

paras.en: “I’ll start a rousing game of charades. Or, no. What about jokes?” Olaf said. “Everybody loves jokes. They’ll be laughing too hard to sleep. Ahem.” He straightened his top coal button. “What do snowmen eat for lunch?”
paras.zh: “我来发起一场热闹的猜词游戏。或者，不。讲笑话怎么样？”雪宝说。“大家都爱笑话。他们会笑得没法睡。咳嗯。”他正了正顶上的煤块扣子。“雪人午饭吃什么？”

paras.en: “What?” Oaken asked.
paras.zh: “吃什么？”奥肯问。

paras.en: “I’m not really sure. Snowmen really don’t eat anything, which is a bit perplexing. There was the time I tried eating fruitcake, but it kind of went right through me.”
paras.zh: “我也说不准。雪人其实什么都不吃，这有点让人费解。有一次我试着吃水果蛋糕，结果它差不多直接从我身上穿过去了。”

paras.en: Kristoff cocked an eyebrow while Anna giggled.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫挑起一边眉毛，安娜咯咯直笑。

paras.en: “Perfect. See, Olaf? You’ll be great!” Anna said. But as she followed Elsa and Kristoff to the door, the laughter within her faded. Dangerous things lurked outside these doors, and in the mountains. Dangerous things lurked within books, too. Dangerous power, it seemed, also lurked somewhere within Anna.
paras.zh: “完美。你看，雪宝？你会很棒的！”安娜说。可当她跟着艾莎和克里斯托夫走向门口时，心里的笑意淡了。危险的东西潜伏在这些门外，也潜伏在群山之中。书页之间也潜伏着危险的东西。而危险的力量，似乎也潜伏在安娜内心的某处。

paras.en: But here was her chance to fix things. Here was her chance to prove herself to Arendelle. To prove herself to Elsa. And if she didn’t, if she couldn’t, the nightmare would be complete.
paras.zh: 可现在，是她弥补过错的机会。是她向阿伦黛尔证明自己的机会。向艾莎证明自己的机会。而如果她做不到——如果她无力做到——这场噩梦就圆满了。

paras.en: The wolf would swallow the world, starting with everyone she loved.
paras.zh: 狼会吞下整个世界，从她所爱的每一个人开始。

paras.en: THE SUN SHONE with intensity in the sky, a bright flat disk that sparked the colorful splendor of autumn leaves.
paras.zh: 太阳明晃晃地悬在天上，像一只扁平的亮盘，把秋叶斑斓的盛景照得熠熠生辉。

paras.en: Usually, Anna loved nothing more than sunny fall days, those afternoons when the sky was as blue as could be and everything around her was golden. Usually. Today, though, the sun was too bright. It showed too many things: their footprints on the path, their shadows creeping across the ground, the bright gleam of Elsa’s hair. All were as visible as could possibly be. Beacons for the wolf that might as well have screamed DELICIOUS MEALS WENT THAT WAY.
paras.zh: 平常，安娜最爱晴朗的秋日，最爱那些天空蓝得不能再蓝、四周一片金灿灿的午后。平常而已。可今天，太阳太亮了。它照出太多东西：小径上的脚印、在地上爬行的影子、艾莎发间亮眼的光泽。一切都看得清清楚楚。简直像给狼点起的信标，恨不得大喊一声“美味大餐往这边走了”。

paras.en: Even though they had all guessed that the wolf would not move during the day, and that it was still trapped in the castle, there was no real way to be sure. So they stayed away from the cleared wagon path that followed the Roaring River, and instead stuck to the interior of the forest, picking their way over fallen logs and stumbling against rocks hidden by piles of leaves. Anna tripped more than a few times over wayward roots. Sneaking through the woods while imagining a wolf chasing her was all too familiar to Anna.
paras.zh: 尽管他们都猜狼白天不会动身，何况它还被困在城堡里，可谁也没法真正打包票。于是他们避开沿咆哮河延伸的大车路，改走森林深处，在倒木与埋在落叶堆下的石头之间磕磕绊绊地择路而行。安娜被任性的树根绊倒了好几回。一边想象着有狼在身后追赶、一边偷偷穿过树林——这种事对安娜来说再熟悉不过了。

paras.en: After a little while, an embarrassed Anna admitted to Kristoff what she had done. And instead of being upset at her, he hugged her. He understood that all she had wanted to do was help, and he was optimistic about their plan to save Sven.
paras.zh: 走了一小段，安娜红着脸向克里斯托夫坦白了自己的所作所为。他非但没有生她的气，反而抱了抱她。他明白她只是想帮忙，也对营救斯文的计划满怀乐观。

paras.en: “I don’t get it,” Anna said, trying to keep her voice quiet enough not to attract attention, but loud enough for Kristoff and Elsa to hear her over the crunching of leaves. “I have good dreams all the time. I’ve dreamed about flying, and living in a castle made of chocolate, and unicorn quests, and—”
paras.zh: “我不明白，”安娜说，尽量把声音压得既不引人注意，又能盖过脚下落叶的碎响，让克里斯托夫和艾莎听清。“我一直在做美梦啊。我梦到过飞翔，梦到过住在巧克力城堡里，梦到过独角兽的冒险，还有——”

paras.en: “And me, obviously,” Kristoff suggested with a cheeky grin.
paras.zh: “还有我，显而易见，”克里斯托夫咧嘴促狭地接了一句。

paras.en: Anna nudged his arm. “Focus,” she said, trying to sound stern, though she knew her cheeks were turning pink.
paras.zh: 安娜用胳膊肘碰了碰他。“专心点，”她说，努力装出严肃的样子，尽管她知道自己脸颊正在泛红。

paras.en: “I’m just glad you didn’t dream of something really scary—like a land-walking shark,” he said.
paras.zh: “我倒是庆幸你没梦到什么真正吓人的东西——比如上岸走路的鲨鱼，”他说。

paras.en: Anna smiled. “Is that your most terrifying nightmare?”
paras.zh: 安娜笑了。“那是你最可怕的噩梦？”

paras.en: “No.” Kristoff shook his head. “When I was little, I used to have nightmares about Bulda trying to spoon-feed me mushroom soup.”
paras.zh: “不是。”克里斯托夫摇了摇头。“我小时候，老做噩梦，梦见布尔达非要拿勺子喂我喝蘑菇汤。”

paras.en: Anna paused to unhook her cloak from a thorny bush. “That’s not scary at all.”
paras.zh: 安娜停下来，把斗篷从一丛荆棘上解下来。“那一点也不吓人。”

paras.en: Kristoff adjusted his traveler’s pack. “Have you ever had a troll try to spoon-feed you?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫拢了拢行囊。“你有过岩精拿勺子喂你的经历吗？”

paras.en: Anna giggled and turned to Elsa, trying to invite her to the conversation, but Elsa didn’t so much as crack a smile. She’d been practically silent since they’d left Oaken’s trading post, and Anna had the sinking suspicion her sister was upset with her.
paras.zh: 安娜咯咯笑着转向艾莎，想把她也拉进话题，可艾莎连一丝笑意都没有。自从离开奥肯的商栈，她几乎一言不发，安娜心里那种不祥的感觉越来越沉——姐姐在生她的气。

paras.en: “H-how about you, Elsa?” Anna tried to keep her tone light and airy. “What’s your worst nightmare?”
paras.zh: “那……你呢，艾莎？”安娜尽量让语气保持轻快。“你最可怕的噩梦是什么？”

paras.en: Elsa pushed back a branch. “I don’t have nightmares.”
paras.zh: 艾莎拨开一根树枝。“我没有噩梦。”

paras.en: From out of the corner of her eye, Anna saw Kristoff pick up the pace. He always liked to avoid spats whenever he could. And he, like Anna, could detect one brewing.
paras.zh: 安娜用眼角的余光瞥见克里斯托夫加快了脚步。他向来能避就避，不愿卷入争执。而且他和安娜一样，嗅得出一场争执正在酝酿。

paras.en: “Come on, Elsa.” Anna took a quick side step to avoid the branch whipping back toward her as Elsa released it. “Everyone has nightmares. I’m your sister. You can tell me. You all know my nightmare now—a massive, girl-stalking wolf.”
paras.zh: “得了吧，艾莎。”艾莎松开手，树枝弹了回来，安娜急忙侧身一闪，才没被扫到。“谁都有噩梦。我是你妹妹。你可以告诉我。你们现在也都知道我的噩梦了——一头巨大的、专盯着我追的狼。”

paras.en: Elsa flung their mother’s scarf over her shoulder. “I don’t know what to tell you, Anna, except that I don’t have nightmares.”
paras.zh: 艾莎把母亲的围巾甩到肩后。“我不知道该跟你说什么，安娜，只能说，我没有噩梦。”

paras.en: Anna’s sinking suspicion was no longer sinking. It had hit rock bottom, and anchored in the pit of her stomach. Elsa was definitely upset with her, and the worst part—the absolute worst part—was that Anna didn’t blame her. Anna was a little furious at herself.
paras.zh: 安娜心里那下沉的不祥预感不再下沉了。它已经沉到了底，锚在了她胃里最深的角落。艾莎肯定在生她的气，而最糟的——绝对最糟的——是安娜并不怪她。安娜反倒对自己有点恼火。

paras.en: Snowflakes drifted in the shafts of sunlight that trickled down through the trees. Anna looked up. The sky remained as blue as ever, which meant there could only be one other source of snow.
paras.zh: 雪片在从树叶间漏下的光柱里飘舞。安娜抬头望去。天空依旧湛蓝如故，这意味着雪只可能来自另一个源头。

paras.en: “Elsa, why are you making flurries?” Anna held out a finger to capture a miniscule ice crystal. “We can’t have snow. We’ll leave footprints. More than the ones we’re already leaving in the mud.”
paras.zh: “艾莎，你为什么要弄出雪花？”安娜伸出手指，接住一颗极小的冰晶。“我们不能下雪。会留下脚印的。比我们已经在泥地里留下的还多。”

paras.en: Elsa stopped and looked at her. “It’s not me.”
paras.zh: 艾莎停下脚步，看着她。“不是我。”

paras.en: “Then what do you call this?” Anna held out her finger.
paras.zh: “那你说这是什么？”安娜伸出手指。

paras.en: Elsa inspected the flake, and her pale cheeks grew even paler. “That’s not snow.”
paras.zh: 艾莎端详着那片雪花，本就苍白的脸颊愈发没有血色。“那不是雪。”

paras.en: “Anna! Elsa!” Kristoff yelled from ahead. He stood on top of a wooded knoll, looking down at something on the other side. “Come quick!”
paras.zh: “安娜！艾莎！”克里斯托夫在前头喊道。他站在一座林木葱茏的小丘顶上，俯望着另一侧的什么东西。“快过来！”

paras.en: They stopped caring who—or what—might hear them, and ran, coming to a halt beside Kristoff. Anna gasped. The forest ended on top of the knoll, and a red farmhouse sat before them, cradled by fields of wheat; wheat that was all white, translucent even, in the sun’s sharp light. As Anna looked, a breeze rippled through the field, dislodging the grains and sending up billows of what looked like ash.
paras.zh: 他们顾不得谁——或者什么东西——会听见，撒腿就跑，最后在克里斯托夫身旁刹住。安娜倒吸一口气。森林在小丘顶上到了尽头，眼前是一座红色农舍，被麦田温柔地环抱；麦子全白了，在烈日的锐光下甚至近乎透明。安娜正望着，一阵微风掠过田野，抖落谷粒，扬起一阵阵像是灰烬的白雾。

paras.en: The Blight was spreading.
paras.zh: 枯萎病在蔓延。

paras.en: “We can’t keep tiptoeing around,” Kristoff said, and Anna could tell he was thinking of Sven’s white coat that matched the terrible white powder. “All this darting and dodging is taking way too long. We have to move way faster!” He was right. But Anna didn’t know what to do.
paras.zh: “我们不能再这样蹑手蹑脚了，”克里斯托夫说。安娜看得出，他想起了斯文那身白毛——和这可怕的白粉一模一样。“这样东躲西藏实在太慢。我们必须快得多才行！”他说得对。可安娜不知道该怎么办。

paras.en: Even from this distance, she could spot little white huddles among the fields. Cows that had fallen asleep. Horses that had dropped in their tracks. Any animal that could take them farther or faster had fallen sick. The only thing that looked normal in the bleached autumn landscape was the navy thread of the Roaring River that wound its way to the base of Miner’s Mountain in the distance.
paras.zh: 即便隔着这么远，她也能看见田间一小团一小团白色的身影。睡着的牛。倒在半路的马。凡是能载他们走得更远更快的牲口，全都病倒了。在这片褪尽了颜色的秋景里，唯一看上去正常的，是远处那道藏蓝色的细线——咆哮河蜿蜒流向矿工山的山脚。

paras.en: “Can you freeze the river?” Anna asked Elsa. “Then maybe we could cross it.”
paras.zh: “你能把河冻住吗？”安娜问艾莎。“那样我们也许能渡过去。”

paras.en: “Huh.” Elsa tilted her head. “That’s an idea! Maybe these will help, too.”
paras.zh: “咦。”艾莎偏了偏头。“这倒是个主意！也许这些也用得上。”

paras.en: Elsa waved her hands, and Anna felt like she’d grown three inches. Looking down at her feet, she realized why: Elsa had transformed Anna’s walking boots into a pair of ice skates. Anna wobbled, but Kristoff grabbed her elbow, keeping her upright.
paras.zh: 艾莎一挥手，安娜觉得自己一下子长高了三寸。低头看向脚下，她才明白缘由：艾莎把安娜的步行靴变成了一双冰鞋。安娜摇摇晃晃，克里斯托夫一把抓住她的手肘，把她扶稳。

paras.en: Elsa nodded at the rushing river. “We can ice-skate.”
paras.zh: 艾莎朝奔涌的河流扬了扬下巴。“我们可以滑冰过去。”

paras.en: That was not what Anna had had in mind. She gulped. It was a good idea, but Elsa was the skater, not Anna. And when Anna did skate, she preferred to skate on smooth, solid ground. On a river, there was always the chance the ice could break, pitching her into icy water. “We’ll be exposed on the open river,” Anna said slowly. “We won’t be able to hide.”
paras.zh: 这可不是安娜心里想的那个办法。她咽了口唾沫。主意是好，可会滑冰的是艾莎，不是她。何况安娜滑冰时，向来偏爱平整结实的地面。在河上，冰随时可能破裂，把她掀进刺骨的冷水里。“在开阔的河面上，我们会暴露无遗，”安娜缓缓说道。“想躲都没处躲。”

paras.en: “Luckily,” Elsa said as she made her way down the knoll and to the river’s edge, “you’re traveling with an expert in ice. I can make the ice just thin enough that it’ll support our weight, but anything heavier—like a giant wolf—will crash right through it.” And with that, she stepped out onto the water.
paras.zh: “幸好，”艾莎一边走下小丘、朝河边去，一边说，“与你同行的是一位冰雪专家。我可以把冰做得薄到刚好托得住我们的体重，可任何更重的东西——比如一头巨狼——都会把它直接踏穿。”说着，她踏上了水面。

paras.en: As the toe of Elsa’s skate touched the surface, a bloom of ice crystals appeared on the river. The crystal blossoms doubled, then quadrupled, then further multiplied, until the entire surface of the river had transformed into a sheet of wild ice blossoms refracting over and over and over again in the blinding midday sun.
paras.zh: 艾莎冰鞋的鞋尖一触到水面，河面上便绽开一朵冰晶。冰花翻倍，再翻四倍，继而不断繁衍，直到整条河面化作一整片狂野的冰之花，在正午眩目的阳光下层层折射，熠熠生辉。

paras.en: It was, Anna admitted to herself, another one of Elsa’s great ideas and magical creations. But just not one she really cared for all that much. She trusted her sister, though, and so she moved to the river’s edge. The ice was so thin she could see straight through it, as though it were the delicate pane of her bedroom window.
paras.zh: 安娜不得不承认，这又是艾莎的一个妙想，一件魔法杰作。只不过，实在不是她有多喜欢的那一种。但她信姐姐，于是走到了河边。冰薄得能一眼望穿，仿佛她卧室里那扇纤薄的窗玻璃。

paras.en: “Come on, Anna,” Kristoff said, “we’re losing time!” He jumped out onto the river with his own ice skates. The sheet of ice jounced like a trampoline beneath him, but it held, just as Elsa promised it would.
paras.zh: “快呀，安娜，”克里斯托夫说，“我们耽搁不起了！”他蹬着自己那双冰鞋跳上河面。冰面在他脚下像蹦床一样颠了颠，却稳稳撑住了，正如艾莎所许诺的那样。

paras.en: “I won’t let anything happen to you, Anna,” Elsa said, reading her sister’s worried expression. “This is our best chance, and we don’t have much time to fix this nightmare.”
paras.zh: “我不会让你出事的，安娜，”艾莎读着妹妹脸上担忧的神情说道。“这是我们最好的机会，而要扭转这场噩梦，时间已经不多了。”

paras.en: Elsa was right. Anna had gotten them into this mess. And now she needed to fix it. Taking a breath, she stepped out onto the ice. Elsa led in front, each stroke of her feet scattering ice crystals across the surface.
paras.zh: 艾莎说得对。是安娜把大家拖进了这团乱局。现在她得亲手把它补好。她深吸一口气，踏上了冰面。艾莎在前领路，每一下蹬冰都把冰晶撒满水面。

paras.en: Lined on either side by trees in their autumn splendor, the river looked like a diamond necklace set against a cushion of red. And as Anna got her feet under her, she felt her heart lighten, just a bit. The rattling, windswept leaves sounded like applause. She took courage in the sound. It was as though Arendelle were cheering for her, wanting her to succeed. And she would. She wouldn’t stop until Arendelle was safe.
paras.zh: 两岸是盛装的秋树，河流宛如一条钻石项链，衬在红色的绒垫上。当安娜终于稳住双脚，她觉得心头轻快了些许。被风刮得簌簌作响的落叶，听上去像阵阵掌声。她从这声音里汲取勇气。仿佛整个阿伦黛尔都在为她欢呼，盼她成功。而她也定会成功。只要阿伦黛尔一日不安全，她就绝不罢休。

paras.en: Hours passed. Wind snarled Anna’s hair, and the constant rush of cold wind meant her nose had started to drip. Her feet were beginning to ache. Elsa’s magical skates usually fit just right, but today they squeezed a bit too tight, as though Elsa had forgotten Anna had grown up. Disheartened by the thought, she tried to shake away her melancholy. Anna hit a divot—and tripped. Before she could smash her nose into the ice, a hand caught her arm.
paras.zh: 几个小时过去了。风把安娜的头发搅得乱糟糟，凛冽的寒风不断灌来，她的鼻子开始淌水，双脚也渐渐酸痛起来。艾莎的魔法冰鞋平时总是刚刚合脚，今天却挤得有些紧，仿佛艾莎忘了安娜已经长大。想到这里她一阵沮丧，竭力想甩开心头的怅惘。安娜踩进一处凹坑——绊倒了。还没等她的鼻子撞上冰面，一只手拽住了她的手臂。

paras.en: “You okay there, Twinkle Toes?” Kristoff asked.
paras.zh: “没事吧，软脚虾？”克里斯托夫问。

paras.en: “Totally,” Anna said. “I meant to do that.” Even though her ice-skating had much improved since her first lesson with Elsa, she wasn’t winning a competition anytime soon.
paras.zh: “好得很，”安娜说。“我是故意的。”尽管自从第一次跟艾莎学滑冰以来，她的冰上功夫大有长进，但要赢得什么比赛，还遥遥无期。

paras.en: “Sorry,” Kristoff said. “I didn’t mean to ruin the Anna Axel.”
paras.zh: “抱歉，”克里斯托夫说。“我不是存心毁掉那记'安娜阿克塞尔'的。”

paras.en: Putting her nose in the air, Anna sniffed. “I guess I can forgive you.”
paras.zh: 安娜把鼻子一扬，哼了一声。“那我就原谅你吧。”

paras.en: Kristoff grinned, his hand slipping into hers. “Are you sure?” And then he was off, skating backward as fast as he could, pulling Anna after him. The world around them blurred as he whirled her around, as confident on the ice as he was on solid ground. Faster and faster they skated, balancing on a thin edge between control and out-of-control. Ahead of them, Elsa cruised with ease, not noticing them tilting, slipping, flying, until—
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫咧嘴一笑，手滑进她的掌心。“你确定？”话音未落，他已转身滑走，飞快地倒滑着，把安娜拽在身后。他带着她旋转，四周的景物都模糊了；他在冰上，和在坚实的土地上一样从容。他们越滑越快，在掌控与失控的薄刃之间寻求平衡。前方的艾莎自在地滑行，浑然不觉身后两人倾斜、打滑、飞掠，直到——

paras.en: “Look out!” Anna shouted as the river took an unexpected bend. But the warning came too late. Kristoff didn’t have time to pull them to a new course, and they skidded off the river and into a tall pile of maple leaves. Lying back, Anna watched as a swirl of golden leaves fell around them.
paras.zh: “小心！”河道毫无预兆地拐了个弯，安娜大声喊道。可警告来得太迟。克里斯托夫来不及带他们转向新航道，两人打着滑冲出河面，一头扎进一堆高高的枫叶里。安娜仰面躺着，看金色的落叶打着旋儿在身边飘落。

paras.en: “I meant to do that,” Kristoff said.
paras.zh: “我是故意的，”克里斯托夫说。

paras.en: “Mm-hmm. The same way I meant to do the Anna Axel?” she asked.
paras.zh: “嗯哼。就像我'故意'来那记安娜阿克塞尔一样？”她问。

paras.en: He nodded. “Exactly.”
paras.zh: 他点了点头。“一点不差。”

paras.en: “ANNA!” Elsa’s voice tore through the air.
paras.zh: “安娜！”艾莎的声音划破长空。

paras.en: “I’m here!” Anna stood up and shook out her travel cloak to send leaves skittering to the ground. “We had a bit of a misstep. Er, mis-skate.”
paras.zh: “我在这儿！”安娜站起身，抖了抖旅行斗篷，让叶子簌簌落回地面。“我们稍微失了一下足。呃，失了一下'冰'。”

paras.en: Elsa’s blade sent a spray of powder over them as she came to an abrupt stop in front of them. “This isn’t a time for game-playing!”
paras.zh: 艾莎的冰刀在两人面前骤然刹住，扬起一片冰粉，落在他们身上。“现在不是闹着玩的时候！”

paras.en: The world as Anna knew it slowed, then froze. And though Elsa hadn’t done any magic—there had been no twirl of her hand, no blast of her ice, no ice shard burrowing its way into Anna’s heart—Elsa’s words froze something deep within Anna. Her hope. And things that are frozen…shatter. Anna could feel the splinters of her broken hope tumbling through her like smashed glass, making every breath, every blink, painful as she looked at her sister, queen of Arendelle, who no longer had any place for her sister’s silly antics.
paras.zh: 安娜所熟悉的世界慢了下来，随即凝固。艾莎并没有施展任何魔法——没有手腕的回旋，没有寒冰的迸发，没有冰锥钻进安娜的心脏——可她的话，把安娜心底的某种东西冻住了。她的希望。而冻结的东西……会碎。安娜能感觉到，破碎的希望如玻璃碴一般在体内翻滚，每一次呼吸、每一次眨眼都疼得钻心。她望着姐姐——阿伦黛尔的女王，那里再也没有容得下妹妹傻气胡闹的位置。

paras.en: “I know it’s not a game,” Anna retorted.
paras.zh: “我知道这不是游戏，”安娜回嘴道。

paras.en: “I don’t think you do,” Elsa said, her voice carefully controlled. Anna wanted to shake her perfect sister, to see some sort of crack, to show her that she saw her as an equal. But that tone—that disappointed tone—revealed all too well exactly what Elsa thought of Anna. And then Anna was no longer hurt, no longer numb, no longer frozen. She boiled.
paras.zh: “我看你并不知道，”艾莎说，声音克制得一丝不苟。安娜真想摇醒这个完美的姐姐，想看她裂开一道缝，想让她明白，自己把她当作平起平坐的人。可那种语气——那种失望的语气——把艾莎眼里安娜的分量暴露得清清楚楚。刹那间，安娜不再受伤，不再麻木，也不再冰封。她沸腾了。

paras.en: “I’m not a child,” Anna said. She was grateful that the ice skates’ blades made her taller than she usually was. “Do you think I don’t know?” With each word, her voice got louder and louder until she practically shouted. “Do you think I haven’t been trying?”
paras.zh: “我不是小孩子，”安娜说。她暗自庆幸，冰鞋的刀刃让她比平时高出了几分。“你以为我不明白吗？”她的声音一字一句越拔越高，到后来几乎是在呐喊。“你以为我没有在努力吗？”

paras.en: And before she could hear Elsa’s reply, Anna flung herself out onto the ice.
paras.zh: 没等听到艾莎的回答，安娜便纵身冲上冰面。

paras.en: Digging the blades in deep, she pushed and pushed, going faster and faster. Anna felt too much. She was too much. That was the trouble. She was too distracted. Too carefree. Too ridiculous for anyone—even for her sister—to see how she could be helpful to the kingdom.
paras.zh: 冰刀深深咬进冰里，她一下又一下地蹬，越来越快。安娜感受得太多。她本身就是太多。麻烦就在这里。她太容易分心。太无忧无虑。太荒唐，让任何人——连她姐姐——都看不出她能为王国做点什么。

paras.en: The wind whipped her cloak behind her, but she leaned into it, wanting to feel the fresh iciness against her hot, angry skin. For a moment, she thought she heard Elsa calling out to her, but she didn’t stop. She wanted to skate away from it all. Away from that disappointed note in Elsa’s voice, away from Kristoff’s undeserved gentle kindness, and away from her own messy, tangled emotions.
paras.zh: 风把斗篷吹得在她身后猎猎作响，她却迎着风倾身向前，想让那股新鲜的寒意贴上自己滚烫恼怒的皮肤。有那么一瞬，她仿佛听见艾莎在喊她，可她没有停下。她只想滑离这一切。滑离艾莎话音里那抹失望，滑离克里斯托夫那不该来的温柔体贴，滑离自己心里那团乱麻般的情绪。

paras.en: Away from her giant, cursed mistake.
paras.zh: 滑离她那巨大而受了诅咒的过错。

paras.en: The ice groaned beneath her weight, her blades scratching out a mournful note that Anna couldn’t escape. Faster, faster, faster! If only she could skate as quick as the wind, maybe she’d melt into it and be swept away from all that she’d done.
paras.zh: 冰面在她的重量下呻吟，冰刀刮出一声声哀怨的调子，安娜怎么也逃不开。快些，再快些！要是她能滑得和风一样快，也许就能融进风里，被卷走，远离她闯下的一切。

paras.en: And that’s when the ice cracked.
paras.zh: 而就在这时，冰裂了。

paras.en: ONE SECOND, everything was cold and dry.
paras.zh: 前一秒，一切都又冷又干。

paras.en: The next second, everything was cold and wet.
paras.zh: 下一秒，一切都又冷又湿。

paras.en: The water dragged at Anna like it had fingers.
paras.zh: 水像长了手指一般，死死拽住安娜。

paras.en: She gasped once—a single great breath of air—before it pulled her under.
paras.zh: 她猛吸了一口气——一大口空气——随即被拖入水底。

paras.en: The world below the ice was dark and quiet, peaceful even, except for the wild scream that worked through Anna.
paras.zh: 冰层之下的世界黑暗而安静，甚至称得上安宁，唯有安娜体内那声狂乱的尖叫例外。

paras.en: She was cold again! She would freeze again! And if she died…would the wolf win? Anna kicked. She couldn’t let everyone down! But no matter how much she willed her feet to propel her back up to the surface, the heavy blades of her skates dragged her down…
paras.zh: 她又要冷了！她又要被冻僵了！而若是她死了……狼岂不是赢了？安娜拼命蹬腿。她不能让大家失望！可无论她多想叫双脚把自己推回水面，冰鞋沉重的刀刃却一个劲把她往下拖……

paras.en: down…
paras.zh: 往下……

paras.en: down into the dark.
paras.zh: 往黑暗深处沉去。

paras.en: Or was it up? Sideways? The dark, ice-cold quiet was disorienting, and her thoughts began to slow. And then, a beam of light shot past her as someone chopped through the ice from somewhere above. Anna felt the water underneath her move like a giant horse, a black wave of water that surged beneath her, and she was flying up through the water and toward the surface with all the strength of a geyser. The water didn’t have the temperature of a hot spring, though, but of an icy slush. Elsa. Moments later, after much spluttering and coughing, Anna was in the arms of Kristoff and Elsa.
paras.zh: 还是说，那是往上？是斜着？冰冷黑暗的寂静令人辨不清方向，她的思绪也慢了下来。就在这时，一道光柱从上方某处劈开冰层，掠过她身边。安娜感到身下的水像一匹巨大的马般翻涌起来，一股黑色的巨浪在身下隆起，她被喷泉般的力量托着，从水中朝水面飞升。可这水并非温泉的温度，而是冰碴般的刺骨。艾莎。片刻之后，在一阵呛水与咳嗽中，安娜落进了克里斯托夫和艾莎的怀里。

paras.en: “Thank you for saving me,” Anna whispered, shivering.
paras.zh: “谢谢你们救了我，”安娜哆嗦着低声说。

paras.en: But Elsa didn’t acknowledge her words. Instead, her sister said, “Kristoff, you need take her back to Oaken’s.”
paras.zh: 可艾莎没有接她的话。姐姐只说：“克里斯托夫，你得带她回奥肯那儿。”

paras.en: “What?! No,” Anna croaked. “I’m fine. I’ll be fine.”
paras.zh: “什么？！不，”安娜哑着嗓子说。“我没事。我会没事的。”

paras.en: “But Anna,” Elsa said, throwing her hands up in protest, “you almost drowned.”
paras.zh: “可是安娜，”艾莎摊开双手抗议道，“你差点淹死。”

paras.en: “Almost,” Anna protested. “I’ve almost done a lot of things. I have to help with this!”
paras.zh: “差点，”安娜争辩。“我'差点'做过的事多了去了。这次我必须帮忙！”

paras.en: Elsa shook her head. “I’m just not sure.”
paras.zh: 艾莎摇了摇头。“我只是拿不准。”

paras.en: “Why are you always trying to push me away?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: “你为什么总想把我推开？”安娜问。

paras.en: Elsa looked stung. “What? Anna, what are you talking about? When do I push you away?”
paras.zh: 艾莎像是被刺了一下。“什么？安娜，你在说什么？我什么时候推开过你？”

paras.en: Anna grew quiet. “I’m sorry. I…Please, I need to accompany you.” For a second, Anna thought Elsa would say no, but then something seemed to melt in Elsa.
paras.zh: 安娜安静下来。“对不起。我……求你了，我必须陪你去。”有那么一瞬，安娜以为艾莎会拒绝，可接着，艾莎心里像有什么融化了。

paras.en: She wrapped Anna in a hug. “I’m sorry, too. I didn’t mean to yell—I just…I’m upset, I guess.”
paras.zh: 她把安娜紧紧抱住。“我也要说对不起。我不是故意吼你的——我只是……我想，我是心烦。”

paras.en: “I didn’t mean to cast a spell,” Anna said, needing to get the words out now. “I had no way of knowing it would bring my nightmare about the wolf to life.”
paras.zh: “我不是故意念咒的，”安娜说，这些话现在非说不可。“我根本没法知道，它会把我那匹狼的噩梦变成真的。”

paras.en: Elsa shook her head. “It just…When did you start having the nightmares?”
paras.zh: 艾莎摇了摇头。“只是……你从什么时候开始做那些噩梦的？”

paras.en: “When I was a little girl, and then, this week the nightmare came back.” Ever since I realized that you were going to leave me behind for the grand tour. But Anna didn’t say that last bit out loud.
paras.zh: “我小时候就有，然后这一周，噩梦又回来了。从我意识到你要丢下我去巡游那时起。可最后这句，安娜没有说出口。”

paras.en: There was the scritch of a match as Kristoff lit a small pile of branches he’d gathered. He gestured the sisters over to the fire.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫划着一根火柴，嗤的一声，点燃了他捡来的一小堆树枝。他招手让姐妹俩到火边来。

paras.en: “When did you first have the nightmare?” Elsa prodded as they huddled close to the flames. Steam rose from Anna’s clothes as they slowly dried.
paras.zh: “你第一次做这个噩梦，是什么时候？”两人凑近火堆时，艾莎追问道。蒸汽从安娜的衣服上袅袅升起，衣物慢慢干着。

paras.en: Anna thought back. “I think it was the night you…you know.” She touched the spot in her hair where the white streak had once been, recalling once more when Elsa had accidentally struck her there with magic as a young girl. “I can’t believe you’ve never had bad dreams.”
paras.zh: 安娜回想起来。“我想……是你……你知道的那晚。”她摸了摸头发上曾有过白痕的地方，又一次想起小时候艾莎的魔法失手击中那里的情形。“真不敢相信，你从没做过噩梦。”

paras.en: Elsa shrugged. “The last time I had a bad dream, I must have been eight years old. I woke up and my entire room had turned into a winter landscape.” She shook her head. “I felt so bad! Everything got wet and they had to bring in new furniture and carpets for me.”
paras.zh: 艾莎耸了耸肩。“我上次做噩梦，应该还是八岁的时候。我一觉醒来，整个房间都变成了冬日的雪景。”她摇了摇头。“我当时难受极了！东西全湿透了，他们只好给我换了新家具和新地毯。”

paras.en: “And you never had the nightmare again?”
paras.zh: “那之后你就再没做过噩梦？”

paras.en: “No.” Elsa leaned her head back and looked up. “Father taught me a bunch of tricks to try to control my emotions, my magic. I remember he came into my room once with a mug of hot chocolate—”
paras.zh: “没有。”艾莎仰起头向上望去。“父亲教了我许多法子，试着控制我的情绪、我的魔法。我记得有一次，他端着一杯热可可走进我的房间——”

paras.en: “He used to do that for me, too!” Anna said.
paras.zh: “他也常那样对我！”安娜说。

paras.en: Elsa smiled, and Anna smiled back, enjoying the surprise bridge that linked them.
paras.zh: 艾莎笑了，安娜也回以微笑，享受着这道意外架起、连接两人的桥。

paras.en: “And Mother joined him and told me to imagine bunching up all the nightmares and throwing them out the window,” Elsa said. “I used to think that when I balled them up, I would throw them and pretend to feed them to the constellations in the sky.”
paras.zh: “后来母亲也来了，她让我想象把所有噩梦都揉成一团，从窗口扔出去，”艾莎说。“那时候我总想着，揉成团扔出去时，要假装把它们喂给天上的星座。”

paras.en: “I used to do that, too!” Anna said, feeling closer to her sister than ever. “I’d pretend to give them to Frigg the Fisherman so he could fish for them. But the trick didn’t stop me from having nightmares.”
paras.zh: “我也那样做过！”安娜说，觉得自己和姐姐从未如此亲近。“我会假装把它们送给渔夫弗里格，让他替我把噩梦钓走。可这法子并没能止住我的噩梦。”

paras.en: Elsa shrugged. “Mother’s trick worked for me. I haven’t had a nightmare since.”
paras.zh: 艾莎耸了耸肩。“母亲的法子对我管用。从那以后，我再没做过噩梦。”

paras.en: “I’m sorry to interrupt,” Kristoff said, “but speaking of stars…it’s getting late.”
paras.zh: “抱歉打断一下，”克里斯托夫说，“不过说到星星……天色不早了。”

paras.en: The sisters smiled, and Anna felt a little bit better, if not completely. Her clothes were still damp, but no longer dripping.
paras.zh: 姐妹俩相视而笑，安娜觉得好受了些，虽谈不上完全。她的衣服还潮着，但不再滴水了。

paras.en: After putting out the fire, Kristoff stepped back on the ice, and Anna followed after him. But the bright hope that had been so certain before now seemed to have been left behind in the maple leaf pile at the riverbank.
paras.zh: 灭了火，克里斯托夫重新踏上冰面，安娜跟在后面。可先前那份笃定的明亮希望，如今似乎被遗落在了河岸的枫叶堆里。

paras.en: Soon enough, the sun began to set, casting long shadows on the ice as they continued to skate up the rest of the Roaring River. Anna couldn’t help thinking that their shadows looked like drowning figures trapped beneath the ice.
paras.zh: 不久，太阳开始西沉，在他们继续滑完咆哮河余下的路程时，在冰面上投下长长的影子。安娜忍不住想，他们的影子就像被困在冰层之下溺水的人影。

paras.en: They were quiet as they skated. Anna didn’t want to accidentally step on the tenuous peace between her and Elsa, while Kristoff seemed to be lost again in his own worries. Kristoff’s birth parents had died long ago, and for the early part of his life, Sven had been his only family—until they’d both been adopted by the mountain trolls. The farther they glided away from Sven, the quieter Kristoff became, until, at last, it became unbearable for Anna. She needed a distraction—for all of them.
paras.zh: 一路滑行，他们默默无语。安娜不想不小心踩碎自己和艾莎之间那点脆弱的平和，而克里斯托夫似乎又陷进了自己的忧思。克里斯托夫的亲生父母早已离世，他生命最初的那些年，斯文是他唯一的家人——直到他们俩被山地岩精收养。他们离斯文越远，克里斯托夫就越沉默，到最后，安娜实在受不了了。她需要点话题来分散注意——为了他们所有人。

paras.en: “Kristoff, have you ever met the Huldrefólk?” she asked, blurting out the first thing she could think of. “Did they ever visit the trolls?”
paras.zh: “克里斯托夫，你见过胡尔德精灵吗？”她脱口而出，问出了脑子里蹦出的头一件事。“他们去过岩精那儿吗？”

paras.en: He shook his head. “Not that I know of,” he said. “The trolls like to hide, but the Huldrefólk—well, they really like to hide, right? I don’t think anyone’s ever seen one.”
paras.zh: 他摇了摇头。“据我所知没有，”他说。“岩精本来就爱躲，可胡尔德精灵——嗯，他们才真叫爱躲，对吧？我看没有人真正见过他们。”

paras.en: “They’re known for finding lost things, too,” Elsa said, slowing down so the other two could catch up with her. No one in Arendelle, or probably in the whole world, for that matter, was as comfortable on the ice as Elsa. While Elsa always moved with grace, when she skated, she was more than grace. She became someone with wind in her veins and wings on her feet. “It’s said that Aren of Arendelle once went to visit them.”
paras.zh: “他们还以能寻回失物而闻名，”艾莎说，放慢速度，好让另外两人赶上。整个阿伦黛尔，大概乃至全世界，都没有人比艾莎在冰上更自在。艾莎的一举一动向来优雅，可她一滑起冰来，就远不止是优雅了。她变成了一个血管里淌着风、脚下生着双翼的人。“据说阿伦岱尔的阿伦，曾去拜访过他们。”

paras.en: “But his adventures led him to many make-believe creatures,” Anna said as his tales gradually came back to her. “Like mermaids and dragons.”
paras.zh: “可他的冒险把他带向了许多虚构的生物，”安娜说，那些故事渐渐在她脑海里苏醒。“比如美人鱼和龙。”

paras.en: “Right,” Elsa said with a nod. “So maybe the Huldrefólk are like dragons and don’t exist at all. Maybe Aren never even existed.”
paras.zh: “没错，”艾莎点点头。“所以也许胡尔德精灵和龙一样，根本不存在。说不定连阿伦都从未存在过。”

paras.en: Kristoff made a face. “So why do you two know so much about this guy if he may or may not have existed? He’s just a legend, right? A myth?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫做了个鬼脸。“那如果他到底存不存在都两说，你们俩怎么对他这么了如指掌？他不过是个传说，对吧？一个神话？”

paras.en: “Possibly. It’s said he did a lot of great things for the land,” Anna said. “He carved Arenfjord himself, you know. Or so the old myths go.”
paras.zh: “有可能。据说他为这片土地立下过许多功绩，”安娜说。“要知道，阿伦峡湾就是他亲手开凿的。至少老神话是这么讲的。”

paras.en: Kristoff snorted. “Yeah, right. That’s the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever heard.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫嗤了一声。“得了吧。这是我听过最荒唐的话。”

paras.en: “You’ve never heard the story?” Anna asked in surprise. “I thought everyone knew it.”
paras.zh: “你没听过这个故事？”安娜惊讶地问。“我以为人人都知道呢。”

paras.en: Kristoff jabbed a thumb at his chest. “Raised by trolls, remember? Some of us didn’t have fancy lessons growing up.” There was something strange lurking in his voice, as though Anna had hit a nerve. It must have had to do with his worry for Sven. She turned to Elsa and asked, “You know the saga verbatim, right?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫竖起拇指，戳了戳自己的胸口。“岩精带大的，记得吗？我们有些人小时候可没上过那种精细的课。”他的声音里潜伏着一丝异样，仿佛安娜戳到了他的痛处。一定和他对斯文的担忧有关。她转向艾莎，问：“那篇史诗你能一字不差地背出来，对吧？”

paras.en: Elsa nodded. “It helped pass the time when I was growing up.” She paused a moment, seeming to collect herself, and then spoke the familiar lines that signified the beginning of a story: “‘A long time ago, in the time before time, a great darkness swept over the land…’”
paras.zh: 艾莎点点头。“小时候它帮我打发了不少时光。”她顿了顿，像是在凝神静气，然后念出了标志着一个故事开头的熟悉句子：“'很久很久以前，在时间之前的时代，一团巨大的黑暗席卷了大地……'”

paras.en: Anna held her breath as Elsa recited the ancient tale and described how an everlasting night had set over the mountains, and how humankind had fled to their boats for safety. Humans then lived on the waters for hundreds of years, until the day a strange sickness smote them. Scared, the people had asked the most ancient of water spirits for help, and the Water Spirit had told them that they were withering away without a place to plant their roots—they needed to return home. But all were too scared, except for a young boy.
paras.zh: 安娜屏住呼吸，听艾莎吟诵这古老的传说：永不消散的长夜如何笼罩群山，人类如何逃上船只避难。此后数百年，人类在水上生活，直到有一天，一种怪病降祸于他们。惊恐的人们向最古老的水灵求助，水灵告诉他们：没有扎根之地，他们正在渐渐枯萎——他们必须回家。可所有人都怕得不敢动，唯有一个小男孩例外。

paras.en: “‘Young as the morning, as fierce as a twig, Aren stepped out onto the land…’” Elsa recited.
paras.zh: “'如晨之稚，如枝之韧，阿伦踏上了陆地……'”艾莎吟诵道。

paras.en: They skated in rhythm to Elsa’s voice, a stroke of one leg, then the other, a beat that flowed through Anna, and calmed her. Impossible things had happened in the past. So why couldn’t they happen in the future?
paras.zh: 他们和着艾莎的声音，有节奏地滑行，一腿，又一腿，那节拍流过安娜的全身，让她平静下来。过去，不可能的事曾经发生。那么未来，为何不能再发生？

paras.en: She took heart as Elsa described how Aren had climbed up the highest mountain to bargain with night and bring back the sun, and how when he’d finally freed the sun, the sun had gifted him the Revolute Blade and told him how to bring his people home: by carving a new path for them, right between the protective mountains.
paras.zh: 听艾莎讲到阿伦如何攀上最高的山峰，与黑夜讨价还价、唤回太阳；讲到他终于释放太阳之时，太阳将回旋之刃赠予他，并告诉他如何带领族人回家——在拱卫的群山之间，为他们劈开一条新路——安娜的心为之一振。

paras.en: Elsa’s voice picked up speed as she reached the crescendo of Aren’s very first quest, and Anna couldn’t help mouthing along with the words as she suddenly remembered.
paras.zh: 讲到阿伦头一场冒险的高潮，艾莎的语速快了起来，安娜忽然想了起来，忍不住随着词句无声地跟着念。

paras.en: “‘Revolving moon and spinning sun, forged a crescent blade. From light and dark within the heart, the burnished sword was made. The curving arc of Revolute shimmered in his hand. He raised it high above his head, and smote the edge of land.’”
paras.zh: “'旋转的月，流转的日，锻出一弯新刃。由心中光与暗，铸成此柄亮剑。回旋之刃的弧光在他掌中闪烁。他将它高高举过头顶，劈向大地的边缘。'”

paras.en: Without missing a beat, Elsa reached out a hand for Anna, gesturing for her to join her on the final stanza of Aren’s first adventure, which Anna found herself happily able to recall. Together, the sisters finished telling the tale: “‘The sea rushed in as hidden power flowed from the gleaming sword, and shaped the rock and forest crown of the first majestic fjord!’”
paras.zh: 艾莎分毫不乱地伸出手，示意安娜同她一起念完阿伦首场冒险的最后一节——安娜惊喜地发现，自己竟还记得那些词句。姐妹俩齐声讲完这个故事：“'海水奔涌而入，隐秘的力量自闪亮的剑中流淌而出，雕琢出岩石与森林的冠冕，成就了第一道壮丽的峡湾！'”

paras.en: Their voices rang out as one, the words triumphantly echoing across the ice.
paras.zh: 两人同声唱和，词句胜利般地在冰面上回荡。

paras.en: “Not too shabby,” Kristoff said. “It kind of reminds me of the troll ballad about Dagfinn the Dusty, a troll who was allergic to mountains and would accidentally cause avalanches wherever he went by sneezing boulders out of his nose.”
paras.zh: “不赖嘛，”克里斯托夫说。“倒让我想起岩精们那首关于'尘土达格芬'的歌谣——那是个对山过敏的岩精，走到哪儿都打喷嚏，从鼻子里把巨石喷出去，弄得雪崩四起。”

paras.en: “Wait, what?” Anna giggled. “That’s what trolls say boulders are? Troll boogers?”
paras.zh: “等等，什么？”安娜咯咯笑了起来。“岩精管巨石叫那个？岩精的鼻屎？”

paras.en: Kristoff shrugged. “Well, yeah. I can sing it for you, if you’d like.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫耸了耸肩。“嗯，是啊。你要是想听，我可以唱给你。”

paras.en: “Maybe later,” Elsa cut in, stopping with a spray of ice. “We’re here.” She pointed up at a sign:
paras.zh: “回头再说吧，”艾莎插话，冰屑飞溅中停了下来。“我们到了。”她指向头顶一块牌子：

paras.en: MINER’S MOUNTAIN
paras.zh: 矿工山

paras.en: WARNING: KEEP OUT
paras.zh: 警告：请勿入内

paras.en: NO TRESPASSERS OR GOATS
paras.zh: 禁止擅闯者与山羊入内

paras.en: HULDREFÓLK ARE WATCHING!
paras.zh: 胡尔德精灵正在注视着你！

paras.en: Anna looked up at the sparkling summit of Miner’s Mountain. If she squinted her eyes just so, she thought she could make out the mystic’s tower. But it was so high up and so far away that from where she stood it looked more like a chimney that had been stuck on top of a roof rather than a tower on a mountain. It would take days to climb all that distance.
paras.zh: 安娜抬头仰望矿工山闪着微光的峰顶。倘若她眯起眼睛恰到好处，她觉得自己能辨认出那座神秘人的塔楼。可它实在太高太远，从她站的地方望去，那更像是搁在屋顶上的烟囱，而非山上的塔。爬完那段路，得花上好几天。

paras.en: For people who didn’t have a magical sister, that is.
paras.zh: 当然，这是对没有魔法妹妹的人而言。

paras.en: Elsa waited for Kristoff and Anna to step off the frozen river before she did so herself. As soon as Elsa was on the bank, the ice cracked, and blue water began to flow once more. With a twirl of Elsa’s hand, Anna’s ice skates melted away to reveal her boots beneath, but Anna hardly realized it because of the great whirlwind that kicked up around her, snow climbing into the air higher and higher, until solidifying into a grand icy staircase.
paras.zh: 艾莎等克里斯托夫和安娜先离开冻住的河面，自己才踏上岸。艾莎一上岸，冰面便碎裂开来，蓝色的河水重新流淌。艾莎手腕一旋，安娜脚上的冰鞋便融化消失，露出底下的靴子——可安娜几乎没察觉，因为一股巨大的旋风在她周围卷起，雪柱扶摇直上，越升越高，最终凝成一道巍峨的冰阶。

paras.en: Elsa had done it again. While the staircase of ice was long and ever so high, with nothing but a curving, slender handrail, it would be much easier to navigate than a treacherous and tedious rocky trail. There must have been at least a thousand steps in the ice staircase—Anna couldn’t be bothered to count. Either way, they were going to climb it, because, at the very top, answers were waiting for them.
paras.zh: 艾莎又露了一手。这道冰阶又长又高，仅有一道弯曲纤巧的扶手，却比那条险峻漫长、乱石嶙峋的小径好走得多。冰阶上想必至少有一千级——安娜懒得起数。无论如何，他们都要爬上去，因为在最高处，答案正等着他们。

paras.en: “Classic,” Kristoff said to Elsa.
paras.zh: “老一套，”克里斯托夫对艾莎说。

paras.en: “Thanks,” she replied.
paras.zh: “谢谢夸奖，”她答道。

paras.en: One step, then another, they ascended.
paras.zh: 一步，又一步，他们向上攀登。

paras.en: At first, Anna didn’t bother holding on to the fragile railing, but about two-thirds of the way to the top, she looked down and gripped it tight. The staircase was clear as glass, and Anna—though brave—wasn’t entirely comfortable with the sight of her feet seemingly dangling above thin air. From this height, the pines seemed to shrink, smaller and smaller and smaller. As they moved up, the sun moved down.
paras.zh: 起初安娜懒得去抓那脆弱的扶手，可爬到约三分之二处，她低头一看，便死死攥住了它。冰阶透明如玻璃。安娜虽然勇敢，可一想到双脚仿佛悬在半空之上，终究有些不自在。在这个高度，松树似乎在不断缩小，越来越小，越来越小。他们越攀越高，太阳越沉越低。

paras.en: At long last, in the blazing sunset, they reached the top. From there, the tower was much taller than Anna had realized—and much more jumbled. The rocks that made up the tower seemed to be haphazardly arranged, and certain stones seemed to be on the verge of slipping out of place. In fact, the tower did not look unlike the staggered piles of books Anna had left in the library. Elsa reached the door to the tower first, and paused. Her hand remained still, raised out in front of her, as if she couldn’t decide whether she should knock.
paras.zh: 终于，在灼热的落日余晖里，他们登上了顶峰。从这里看，那座塔比安娜想象的要高得多——也杂乱得多。构成塔身的岩石似乎胡乱堆叠，有几块石头眼看就要滑出原位。事实上，这座塔的模样，倒和安娜落在图书馆里那些东倒西歪的书堆有几分相像。艾莎率先走到塔门前，停住了脚步。她的手悬在身前，一动不动，仿佛拿不定主意该不该敲门。

paras.en: Anna pulled her cloak to her chest as the wind sang around them. “What’s wrong?”
paras.zh: 风在四周呜咽歌唱，安娜把斗篷拢向胸前。“怎么了？”

paras.en: “What do I say?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: “我该说什么？”艾莎问。

paras.en: “You knock and say hi, and we’ll go from there,” Kristoff called. “Hurry.”
paras.zh: “你敲门，打个招呼，其余的再说，”克里斯托夫喊道，“快点。”

paras.en: “What Kristoff said,” Anna said, watching the sun sink over the horizon.
paras.zh: “就照克里斯托夫说的办，”安娜说，望着太阳沉下地平线。

paras.en: Elsa threw back her shoulders and knocked.
paras.zh: 艾莎挺起肩膀，敲了敲门。

paras.en: Then the three of them stared at the door and waited, but nothing happened. Was no one home? The thought filled Anna with a heavy dread. They had come all this way, and Sorenson was not there.
paras.zh: 随后，三人盯着那扇门等啊等，却毫无动静。家里没人吗？这个念头让安娜心头坠满沉重的恐惧。他们千里迢迢赶到这里，索伦森却不在。

paras.en: Elsa knocked again. Nothing.
paras.zh: 艾莎又敲了一次。毫无动静。

paras.en: “Stand back,” Kristoff said. He moved in front of Elsa and put his shoulder to the door. But it was sturdier than it looked. He lifted his pickax high.
paras.zh: “退后，”克里斯托夫说。他挪到艾莎身前，把肩膀抵上门板。可这门比看上去结实得多。他高高举起鹤嘴锄。

paras.en: “Why don’t you try the handle?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: “你何不试试门把手？”艾莎问。

paras.en: Kristoff raised an eyebrow and did just that. The door swung easily open.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫挑起眉毛，照做了。门轻而易举地开了。

paras.en: “Huh,” he said as he put his pickax away. Without saying another word, he went inside.
paras.zh: “嘿，”他说着收起鹤嘴锄。他二话不说，走了进去。

paras.en: Anna exchanged an amused glance with her sister, and they followed him through the doorway and into the tower. From the outside, the tower had looked about to topple, but the inside seemed solid enough, made up of rock and wood and books.
paras.zh: 安娜和姐姐交换了一个忍俊不禁的眼神，跟着他穿过门洞，走进塔中。从外面看，这座塔仿佛随时会倾倒，里面倒还结实，由岩石、木头和书籍构成。

paras.en: Anna had always imagined a mystic to be exacting, the kind of person who might label the spices in their kitchen cabinet, but everything seemed to be randomly placed. Plants sprawled on top of books, and books on top of statues. On the far side of the circular room was a spiral staircase. There was practically everything under the sun in the tower room.
paras.zh: 安娜一向想象中的神秘人该是那种一丝不苟的人，会往厨房橱柜里的香料罐上贴标签；可这里的一切似乎都是随意乱放的。植物摊在书上，书摞在雕像上。圆形房间的另一头是一道螺旋楼梯。这间塔楼里几乎应有尽有。

paras.en: Except for a mystic.
paras.zh: 唯独没有神秘人。

paras.en: KRISTOFF GROANED, letting his traveler’s pack thump to the floor. “He’s not here. Now what?”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫咕哝一声，任凭行囊砰地砸在地板上。“他不在。现在怎么办？”

paras.en: “I’m sure he’ll come back,” Anna said, unclasping her cloak. The tower felt especially stuffy after being in the wind all day long. “In the meantime, we wait.”
paras.zh: “他肯定会回来的，”安娜说着，解开斗篷的搭扣。在风里跑了一整天，塔里显得格外闷。“眼下嘛，我们就等。”

paras.en: Arooooooooooooooo!
A long, low howl wrapped around the tower, carving a pit in Anna’s stomach—was it the wolf? Had it escaped Elsa’s ice dome?
paras.zh: 一声悠长低沉的嚎叫缠上高塔，在安娜的胃里剜出一个坑——是那只狼吗？它逃出艾莎的冰穹了？

paras.en: Kristoff, however, remained calm. “It’s just the wind. Trust me.” He picked up a small guitar that leaned next to a potted plant. “Growing up with trolls, you know what’s the wind, and what’s a wolf.” He strummed the guitar. The tinkling sound filtered through the air, pretty, if a bit off-key.
paras.zh: 可克里斯托夫镇定自若。“只是风罢了。相信我。”他拿起靠在盆栽旁的一把小吉他。“跟岩精一起长大，你分得清什么是风声，什么是狼嚎。”他拨响了琴弦。叮叮咚咚的乐声在空气中荡开，挺好听，只是有点走调。

paras.en: Anna’s fear receded a little, and she hoped he was right. “I’d rather the wolf be stalking us here and leaving the villagers alone,” she admitted.
paras.zh: 安娜的恐惧消退了些，但愿他没说错。“我宁可那只狼盯上我们，也别去烦村里的乡亲。”她坦言。

paras.en: “Very noble of you,” Elsa said. “We’ll stay, but just until we figure out a plan in case Sorenson doesn’t come back soon.”
paras.zh: “真够高尚的。”艾莎说。“我们留下，但只等到想出对策为止，万一索伦森迟迟不回来。”

paras.en: “Maybe there’s a book or something here that can undo the curse,” Anna said. “One that’s already been translated.”
paras.zh: “也许这儿有哪本书能解除诅咒。”安娜说。“最好是已经译出来的那种。”

paras.en: “That’s a good idea,” Kristoff said. “I’ll take the upstairs. You two search down here.” And with a nod at the girls, he lit his lantern and disappeared into the swirl of dark steps above them. Anna thought she knew why he wanted to search a floor by himself. When Anna was upset, she always sought company, but when Kristoff was upset, he liked to be by himself or with Sven. And with Sven in trouble, she knew Kristoff was having a hard time, too.
paras.zh: “好主意。”克里斯托夫说。“楼上的归我。你们俩搜下边。”他朝两个姑娘点点头，点亮提灯，消失在头顶那道盘旋而上的昏暗楼梯里。安娜想，她大概明白他为什么想独自搜一层。安娜心烦时总爱找人做伴，可克里斯托夫心烦时，却喜欢一个人待着，或者和斯文在一起。而如今斯文遭了难，她知道克里斯托夫心里同样不好受。

paras.en: Elsa sighed. “Ugh. I knew coming here was a bad idea.”
paras.zh: 艾莎叹了口气。“唉。我就知道来这儿是个馊主意。”

paras.en: Anna felt herself bristle like the gray barn cat, but she didn’t want to fight, not again, not so soon. They had come a long way, and they had more of a way to go. So she kept her voice light. “We don’t know that yet. Let’s just give this room a chance. Please?”
paras.zh: 安娜觉得自己像谷仓里那只灰猫一样竖起了毛，可她不想再吵——不要再吵，至少现在不想。她们已经走了很远的路，而前面的路还长。于是她把语气放得轻快。“这还说不定呢。先给这屋子一个机会嘛。好不好？”

paras.en: Elsa crossed her arms, but after a second, Anna knew she’d won. This round, anyway. They divided up the circular room. In the light of a dying fire, she could see the walls were plastered with detailed star charts and strange silver instruments that hummed, and a delicate gold miniature of the solar system that was so beautifully done, Anna thought it was a shame that she couldn’t study it for hours and tell the children of the village all about it. She also found a calendar with all the phases of the moon laid out, three miniature telescopes, powder-filled glass vials, and an old sundial, its copper face green from the years it must have spent out in the harsh elements. And last but not least, a hunk of blue-black rock that was labeled METEORITE.
paras.zh: 艾莎抱起双臂，可只过了一瞬，安娜就知道自己赢了。至少这一回合是。他们分头搜查这间圆屋。在将熄的火光里，她看见墙上贴满了精细的星图，摆着嗡嗡作响的奇异银器，还有一件精巧的太阳系金质模型，做得那样美，安娜都觉得遗憾：没法花上几个钟头好好研究，再讲给村里的孩子们听。她还找到一本列齐所有月相的历书、三架微型望远镜、装满粉末的玻璃小瓶，还有一座旧日晷，铜面绿锈斑斑，可见在风吹日晒里熬过了多少年头。最后但同样重要的是，还有一块蓝黑色的石头，上面标着：陨石。

paras.en: “This mystic seems to really like the night sky,” Anna called to Elsa.
paras.zh: “这位秘术师好像很喜欢夜空。”安娜朝艾莎喊。

paras.en: “I noticed,” Elsa said as she straightened a frame. “Did you see the ceiling?”
paras.zh: “我发现了。”艾莎边说边扶正一个相框。“你看见天花板了吗？”

paras.en: Anna tilted her head back and gasped. A star map had been painted above them in deep blues and indigos. Delicate lines of silver paint connected some of the stars, tracing the outlines of fantastical beasts, crowns, and heroes. They were familiar images, and Anna recognized them as constellations. But there was something else about the illustrations that seemed familiar to her, though she couldn’t quite place her finger on it….
paras.zh: 安娜仰起头，倒吸一口气。他们头顶绘着一幅星图，深蓝与靛青交融。银漆勾出的细线连起点点星辰，描出神话异兽、王冠与英雄的轮廓。这些图像似曾相识，安娜认出那是星座。可这些画里还有别的什么让她觉得眼熟，偏偏又说不上来究竟在哪儿见过……

paras.en: “It’s so pretty,” Anna said. “It’s the prettiest ceiling I’ve ever seen.”
paras.zh: “真美。”安娜说。“这是我这辈子见过最美的天花板。”

paras.en: Elsa nodded. “I like it, too. It even has my favorite constellation—Ulf.” She looked over at Anna and smiled. “Ulf the Wolf was always my favorite. I made Mother tell me all his stories.”
paras.zh: 艾莎点头。“我也喜欢。上面连我最爱的星座都有——乌尔夫。”她看向安娜，微微一笑。“乌尔夫狼向来是我的最爱。我总要母亲把他的故事讲个遍。”

paras.en: The sisters kept searching.
paras.zh: 姐妹俩继续搜寻。

paras.en: Sorenson’s thinking seemed random, and his shelves didn’t appear to be organized in any particular order that Anna could tell. Though, when she peeled back the first book’s cover, she wondered if maybe he had ranked them by stench. Many of the books had dark stains on their pages, and a couple of them even had their own furry patch of mold. But for someone who was known to be an expert in myths and lore, Sorenson didn’t appear to have many books on those topics. The closest thing was a small slate covered with strange symbols in chalk, but upon examining it, Anna saw it wasn’t magic, but physics.
paras.zh: 索伦森的心思似乎毫无章法，安娜看不出他的书架按什么特别的顺序排列。不过，当她翻开第一本书的封皮时，她开始怀疑，他没准是按臭味高低给书排的序。许多书的书页上留着暗色的渍痕，还有几本干脆长出了自己的一小片毛茸茸的霉斑。可一个以神话传说专家闻名的人，书架上这类题材的书却寥寥无几。最接近的，是一块用粉笔写满古怪符号的小石板，可凑近一细看，安娜发现那不是魔法，是物理。

paras.en: Wandering over to the last bookshelf, Anna skimmed the titles: Book of Later Han by Zhang Heng, Almanack by Richard Saunders, and Book of Optics by Hasan Ibn al-Haytham. Picking up the first title, Anna flipped through the pages to see sketches of instruments that looked quite similar to those sitting on the mystic’s shelves, along with annotations of water clocks and wind flows. No mention of curses, or of dream spells gone awry.
paras.zh: 安娜踱到最后一只书架，扫了扫书名：张衡的《后汉书》、理查德·桑德斯的《历书》，还有哈桑·伊本·海赛姆的《光学书》。她拿起第一本，翻了几页，见里面画着一些仪器的草图，与秘术师架上的摆设颇为相似，旁注还有水钟与气流的研究。只字未提诅咒，也没提走岔了的梦咒。

paras.en: “It’s funny,” Anna called out to Elsa as she tapped the book back onto the shelf. “I wouldn’t think that a mystic would have so many books on science. I thought he would have more spell books and stuff. You know?” She paused, waiting for her sister’s response. But when Elsa didn’t say anything, Anna called again. “Hey, Elsa?”
paras.zh: “有意思，”安娜敲敲书脊，把它插回架上，朝艾莎喊。“我没想到秘术师会有这么多讲科学的书。我还以为他多半是咒语书之类的呢。你说是不是？”她顿了顿，等姐姐回应。可艾莎没吭声，安娜又喊了一声。“喂，艾莎？”

paras.en: “Anna, can you come here?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: “安娜，你能过来一下吗？”艾莎问。

paras.en: Anna followed her sister’s voice to where she stood in a back room, more of an alcove really, that contained a tiny kitchen. Anna hurried over to her sister to find her gaping open-mouthed at a table. It looked ordinary enough, but then Anna saw it: on the center of the table was a pot of soup.
paras.zh: 安娜循着姐姐的声音走过去，她站在一间后屋里——说是个壁龛更贴切——里面安置着一方小小的厨房。安娜快步赶到姐姐身边，只见她张着嘴，愣愣地盯着一张桌子。那桌子看上去再普通不过，可紧接着安娜看见了：桌子正中央，摆着一锅汤。

paras.en: A steaming pot of soup.
paras.zh: 一锅正冒着热气的汤。

paras.en: Anna’s stomach flipped. For that twist of steam to exist, someone had to have been there recently.
paras.zh: 安娜的胃猛地一翻。既然有那缕蒸汽，就必定有人刚刚来过。

paras.en: “Where’s Kristoff?” Anna whispered. She’d planned on checking on him, but had become distracted by the many books and treasures. The mystic’s mind seemed just as distracted as her own. And now Kristoff had been gone upstairs for at least ten minutes, and he’d not come back down.
paras.zh: “克里斯托夫在哪儿？”安娜低声问。她本打算去看看他，却被满屋的书册和宝贝岔开了心神。这秘术师的心思，似乎和她自己一样容易走神。而此刻，克里斯托夫上楼至少有十分钟了，还没下来。

paras.en: “Anna,” Elsa whispered, “I don’t think we’re alone here.”
paras.zh: “安娜，”艾莎低声说，“我觉得这屋里不止我们。”

paras.en: “Exactly so,” said a low, raspy voice.
paras.zh: “说得一点不错。”一个低沉沙哑的声音响起。

paras.en: Anna spun around as a man stepped off the staircase landing and into the tower room. He was short, barely up to Anna’s shoulders, and he wore his long silver beard down to the floor. Anna had the fleeting thought that he looked a bit like the nisse from her mother’s tales, those tiny gnomelike creatures that would adopt a family to both hinder and help. The only thing he was missing was a nisse’s traditional pointy red hat, but he did have a sharp, glinting spear—and it was aimed directly at her heart.
