paras.zh: 安娜猛地转身，只见一个男人从楼梯平台走下，进了塔屋。他个子很矮，勉强够到安娜的肩膀，银白的长须几乎拖到地上。安娜脑中闪过一个念头：他有点像母亲故事里的尼瑟——那些小小的侏儒般的生灵，会认下一户人家，又帮又捣乱。他只缺一顶尼瑟传统的尖顶红帽，手里却实实在在攥着一杆寒光闪闪的尖矛——而且矛尖正对着安娜的心口。

paras.en: Anna stopped breathing. In the corner, she saw Elsa raise her hands. They were trembling. But there was Elsa, once again ready to step in. Anna knew better than anyone how much Elsa never again wanted to use her powers to harm another—not after the disastrous consequences that had occurred the last time, when she had turned Anna to ice by accident. But Anna also knew that Elsa would use her powers to protect Anna—and Anna could not allow that. Not when Anna could do something about it herself.
paras.zh: 安娜屏住了呼吸。角落里，她看见艾莎举起了双手。那双手在发抖。可艾莎又一次站在那儿，准备挺身而出。安娜比谁都清楚，艾莎多么不愿再用自己的魔力伤人——自从上次酿成大祸、失手把安娜冻成冰之后，她便再不愿了。可安娜也知道，艾莎会为了保护她动用魔力——而安娜绝不能容许那样的事。既然她自己能应付，就绝不能。

paras.en: “Hi! I’m Anna! This is Elsa!” Anna smiled, trying to inject as much cheer and goodwill into her voice as possible. “We’re sorry to intrude. We promise we weren’t going to eat your soup—it smells a bit funny—er, that’s so rude of me. I’m sorry. I mean, it doesn’t smell bad, but I’m not really sure I recognize that spice? But we’re not here for spices. Please don’t hurt us!”
paras.zh: “嗨！我是安娜！这位是艾莎！”安娜满面笑容，竭力往嗓音里灌进最多的欢快与善意。“打扰您真是抱歉。我们保证没打算喝您的汤——它闻着有点怪——呃，瞧我，多没礼貌。对不起。我是说，不难闻，只是那香料我实在认不出来？可我们不是为香料来的。请别伤害我们！”

paras.en: “Hurt you?” The man looked dizzy from trying to follow Anna’s words. “Why would you think I would want to hurt you?” His voice was deep and grating like gravel.
paras.zh: “伤害你们？”那人被安娜这串话绕得直发晕。“你凭什么觉得我要伤害你？”他的声音低沉粗粝，像碎石摩擦。

paras.en: “Umm.” Anna’s eyes flew to his hand. “Because of the spear you’re holding?”
paras.zh: “呃。”安娜的目光倏地落在他手上。“因为您手里那杆矛？”

paras.en: “What sp—? Oh!” The man lowered the point of his spear. “This isn’t a spear, it’s part of a weather vane. That mountain man upstairs broke it when he barged onto my peaceful observation deck unannounced! He’s exceedingly lucky I finished my Highly Flammable and Very Dangerous Combustion Powder last night, or he might not have ten fingers. Hmph.”
paras.zh: “什么矛——？哦！”那人放低了“矛”尖。“这不是矛，是风向标上的一截。楼上那个山地汉子，招呼都不打一声就闯上我安静的观测台，把它弄断了！他真是走运到了极点，我那罐‘高度易燃剧毒燃烧粉’昨晚刚做完，不然他未必还能保住十根手指。哼。”

paras.en: Anna blinked as the man shoved the pointed weather vane under her nose, and she took in the large golden N that twinkled in front of her. N for north. “Ha ha,” she said, and pushed the golden point away from her. “What a silly mistake. Is the, er, mountain man…all right?”
paras.zh: 那人把尖头风向标戳到安娜鼻子底下，她眨着眼，看清了迎面闪光的一个大大的金色“N”字。N，代表北方。“哈，哈。”她说着，把那个金尖从面前推开。“多蠢的一场误会。那位，呃，山地汉子……还好吗？”

paras.en: “He will be, once he cleans up the mess he made,” the short man said, shooting her a glare. “He’s also lucky he didn’t come next month and disturb my view of the meteor shower. But that’s what I’m doing here. I live here. Always have. My question is: what are you doing here?”
paras.zh: “等他把弄乱的摊子收拾干净，自然就好了。”矮个子男人说着瞪她一眼。“他还算走运，没赶在下个月来，搅了我看流星雨。可这儿是我住的地方。我住在这儿。一直都住在这儿。我倒要问：你们来这儿做什么？”

paras.en: “We’re looking for the great mystic Sorenson,” Anna said, trying to sweep a curtsy, but her knees were still shaky from misinterpreting the weather vane, and she almost knocked over a nearby bust of a man in round reading glasses. “We’re assuming that’s you?”
paras.zh: “我们是来找伟大的秘术师索伦森的。”安娜说着，想行个屈膝礼，可她的膝盖还因方才错认风向标而发软，差点撞翻旁边一座戴圆框老花镜的男子胸像。“我们猜，那就是您了？”

paras.en: The old man snorted. “I’m Sorenson, but I’m no mystic.”
paras.zh: 老者哼了一声。“我是索伦森，可不是什么秘术师。”

paras.en: Elsa stepped forward, her hands no longer raised, but now clenched in the folds of her cloak. “But the villagers say you are a mystic.”
paras.zh: 艾莎上前一步，双手不再举着，而是攥紧了斗篷的褶皱。“可村民们说您是秘术师。”

paras.en: “I’m a scientist,” the man said, using the weather vane to reach through his thick beard and scratch the underside of his chin. “Though I suppose the villagers might not see that much of a difference between me and the old mystics of legendary tales.”
paras.zh: “我是个科学家。”男人用风向标拨开浓密的胡须，挠了挠下巴底。“不过我想，在村民眼里，我跟传说里那些老秘术师大概也没多大分别。”

paras.en: A scientist. Anna tried not to let her disappointment show. It was great to be a scientist, but not when one needed a mystic to save a kingdom from a vicious magical wolf. How would a scientist be able to help with a terrible curse? “We’re sorry to have bothered you.” Anna stepped aside as Sorenson shuffled past her to check on his soup. “Oaken had told us that you’re an expert in myths and lore.”
paras.zh: 一位科学家。安娜竭力不露出失望之色。当科学家固然好，可眼下她们需要的是一位秘术师，把王国从恶毒的魔法狼爪下救出来，这就不好了。一个科学家，能帮上什么可怕的诅咒的忙？“很抱歉打扰您了。”安娜侧身让开，索伦森拖着步子走过她身旁，去照看他的汤。“奥肯告诉我们，您是神话传说的专家。”

paras.en: “Oh, but I am.” Sorenson gave his pot a stir. “Mythology and science are familiar friends—both seek for the why behind things. Both look to provide an explanation for the natural phenomena of the world around us. And all myths contain a kernel of hard truth.” He took a sip of his soup and winced before tossing in a pinch of salt. Only after he took another sip and nodded his head in satisfaction did he look back at the sisters. “Though I am curious as to why the queen and princess of Arendelle are here seeking an expert in myths and lore. Something must be truly wrong.”
paras.zh: “哦，这倒不假。”索伦森搅了搅锅。“神话和科学是相熟的老友——两者都在探求事物背后的‘为什么’。都想为周遭世界的自然现象寻一个解释。而所有的神话，都藏着一粒硬邦邦的真相。”他抿了口汤，皱了皱眉，撒进一小撮盐。直到再抿一口、满意地点了点头，他才回头看向姐妹俩。“不过我倒好奇，阿伦黛尔的女王和公主，为何跑到这儿来寻什么神话传说的专家。一定是出了不得了的大事。”

paras.en: “Because,” Elsa said, her voice low but steady, “Arendelle has been cursed.”
paras.zh: “因为，”艾莎说，声音低沉却平稳，“阿伦黛尔被诅咒了。”

paras.en: “And we need your help to figure out how to undo it,” Anna added, attempting to gloss over the fact that she’d been the one who’d cursed it. She tried not to look at anyone, but Elsa caught her eye and nodded. For a moment, it felt like an ember from the fireplace had broken away from the logs and settled somewhere in Anna’s heart. Even though snow and ice flowed through Elsa, she always made Anna feel the warmest. Maybe everything wasn’t lost, after all.
paras.zh: “我们需要您帮忙弄清怎么解除它。”安娜补上一句，竭力掩饰当初下咒的正是她自己。她尽量不看任何人，可艾莎迎上她的目光，轻轻点头。那一刻，仿佛壁炉里一粒火星脱离了木柴，落进安娜心底的某个角落。尽管艾莎体内流淌着冰雪，她却总能给安娜最多的暖意。也许，一切并没有全盘皆输。

paras.en: Except, Sorenson’s reaction wasn’t exactly encouraging. His bushy eyebrows shot up so fast that they almost skidded off his face, and Anna wondered for a minute if he would laugh. Instead, he opened an old trunk and began pulling out empty bowls.
paras.zh: 只可惜，索伦森的反应实在算不上鼓舞人心。他那两道浓眉飞快扬起，险些从脸上滑下去，安娜一时间还以为他要笑出来。谁知他却打开一口旧木箱，开始往外掏空碗。

paras.en: “In that case,” Sorenson said, “someone please fetch the mountain man from the observation deck and have him rebuild my fire. It seems as though you have a story to tell, and I’d rather be warm while I listen.”
paras.zh: “那样的话，”索伦森说，“劳驾哪位去把观测台上那个山地汉子叫下来，让他把我的火重新生起来。看来你们有个故事要讲，我宁可暖和着听。”

paras.en: A few minutes and a roaring fire later, Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff gathered around Sorenson’s table, each taking turns sharing all they knew. Anna heard Elsa describe the unnatural quiet that had befallen SoYun’s farm and the way the trees in the kingdom’s orchards were not only producing mushy gray apples, but had also become gnarled, as though they were twisting away from something—the wolf, Anna guessed—as it had passed by. But did that mean the wolf had been present before she read the spell? And if so, how?
paras.zh: 几分钟后，炉火烧得正旺，安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫围坐在索伦森的桌边，轮流把知道的一切和盘托出。安娜听艾莎讲起小允农场上那反常的死寂，讲起王国果园里的树不仅结出软塌塌的灰苹果，还长得虬曲扭曲，仿佛在躲避什么——安娜猜，是那只狼——躲避它经过时的气息。可这是不是说，早在她念出咒语之前，狼就已经在那里了？如果是，那怎么可能？

paras.en: Then it was Kristoff’s turn, and he described how the forest, too, had been quiet, though he did not mention the trolls or their surprising absence. Arendelle’s mountain trolls were private creatures, and for the most part, they liked to keep themselves hidden from humans, with a few special exceptions. Kristoff wouldn’t mention them to just any person, and though Sorenson was now feeding them warm soup that tasted of mushrooms and roots, Kristoff was still protective of the concealed trolls who had raised him as part of their family, and, after all, Sorenson had forced Kristoff to clean up his mess out on a chilly observation deck.
paras.zh: 接着轮到克里斯托夫，他讲起森林也曾陷入那样的寂静，只是没提岩精，也没提他们出奇地无影无踪。阿伦黛尔的山地岩精是怕生的生灵，大多喜欢避开人类，藏起身形，只有寥寥几个特殊的例外。克里斯托夫不会随便对什么人都提起他们；尽管索伦森此刻正端出蘑菇根茎味的热汤招待众人，克里斯托夫依旧护着那些把他当家人养大的隐居岩精——再说了，索伦森还逼着他在冷飕飕的观测台上收拾了半天残局。

paras.en: Finally, it was Anna’s turn. She began with the crumpled piece of paper with the “Make Dreams Come True” spell on it, and how she’d had a nightmare, and gone to the kitchen to make some hot chocolate. She told him how she’d seen something out of the corner of her eye and followed it to the Great Hall, where she’d seen a wolf—the same wolf from her nightmare. And how her friends’ eyes had turned inky black and then glowing yellow while they seemed to have lost themselves in the strong hold of a nightmare sleep. As she completed her tale, Sorenson stood and went to his shelves. Pulling out two books, he returned to the table, the wooden floorboards beneath his boots creaking slightly as he walked.
paras.zh: 终于轮到安娜。她从那张揉皱的、写着“美梦成真”咒语的纸讲起，讲她怎样做了个噩梦，去厨房煮热可可。她告诉他，自己怎样用眼角瞥见一晃而过的东西，一路跟到礼堂，看见了那只狼——和噩梦里一模一样的狼。又讲她的朋友们眼睛怎样变成墨黑，继而泛出幽幽的黄光，仿佛深陷噩梦的沉睡，再找不着自己。她讲完，索伦森起身走向书架。他抽出两本书回到桌边，靴子下的木地板随着脚步吱呀轻响。

paras.en: “I think,” Sorenson said, placing the books on the table and slipping back into his stool, “that the answer can be found in one of these.”
paras.zh: “我想，”索伦森把书放上桌子，坐回凳子，“答案就在其中一本里。”

paras.en: Anna looked at the books. One was a tome called Psychologia. The other was a slim leather volume with block letters stamped across its cover:
paras.zh: 安娜看着那两本书。一部是题为《心理学》的大部头。另一本是薄薄的皮面小册，封皮上烫着一行大写字母：

paras.en: NATTMARA
paras.zh: 纳特玛拉

paras.en: “‘Nattmara,’” Elsa read out loud. “I know that word.”
paras.zh: “纳特玛拉。”艾莎念出声来。“这个词我知道。”

paras.en: Anna knew the word, too. She’d heard the word before, long, long ago, but she had seen that word recently as well, as a non-translated entry in Secrets of the Magic Makers. A vision sprang to her mind: a sketch of a man screaming in agony, and the drawing of the wolf…
paras.zh: 这个词安娜也知道。她很久很久以前听过它，而最近也见过它——《魔法制造者之秘》里一条尚未翻译的条目。一幅画面在她脑海中跳了出来：一幅男人痛楚嘶嚎的素描，还有那只狼的图画……

paras.en: “Yes.” Sorenson nodded. “You probably do. Nattmara often show up in the sagas of old, and those stories are often told to children as warning tales.” Flipping open the ancient book, he pointed to an illustration of a child sleeping in bed. “Another name for a Nattmara is ‘Nightmare,’ because that’s what it is—the embodiment of our deepest fear.”
paras.zh: “没错。”索伦森点头。“你们多半知道。纳特玛拉时常出现在古老的萨迦里，那些故事常被当作警世之谈讲给孩子听。”他翻开那本古书，指向一幅孩童卧床安睡的插图。“纳特玛拉还有一个名字，叫‘噩梦’，因为它正是如此——我们心底最深处恐惧的化身。”

paras.en: “Embody-what?” Kristoff asked.
paras.zh: “化……什么身？”克里斯托夫问。

paras.en: “It means that nightmares can take on a physical shape and exist outside of your mind,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: “意思是，噩梦能够化作实体，存在于你的头脑之外。”艾莎说。

paras.en: “Precisely.” Sorenson held up his pointer finger. “The act of burying fear is what manifests the Nattmara. And eventually, the fear is too big to keep inside. They can take the shape of anything, and this particular one seems to have taken the form of a wolf. Nattmara tend to roam the world, leaching energy from all living things. Their very presence can cause trees to twist away from them. They feed on fear, and so they seek to create fear.”
paras.zh: “正是。”索伦森竖起一根食指。“把恐惧深埋起来，正是纳特玛拉成形的原因。而终有一天，恐惧大到再也藏不住。它们能化作任何形状，而这一只，偏偏取了狼的模样。纳特玛拉惯于在世间游荡，从一切活物身上汲取生气。单是它们的气息，就足以令树木扭曲着背过身去。它们以恐惧为食，所以才处心积虑地制造恐惧。”

paras.en: Anna’s eyes widened as she listened, trying to grasp onto the strange ideas.
paras.zh: 安娜越听眼睛睁得越大，努力想抓住这些古怪的念头。

paras.en: Sorenson flipped the page to another illustration, this one of a swirling storm of black sand. “A Nattmara is also able to turn itself into black sand in order to slip through cracks—cracks in doors, and cracks within the heart. There is no escaping them, unless you’re brave enough that there is no weakness for the Nattmara to enter through.”
paras.zh: 索伦森翻过一页，又是一幅插图，这回是一团盘旋翻搅的黑沙风暴。“纳特玛拉还能把自己化作黑沙，从缝隙里钻过——门上的缝，以及人心里的裂缝。谁也躲不开它们，除非你勇敢到没有一丝弱点，让它无从钻入。”

paras.en: He looked up, his brown eyes locking on Anna. “And if a Nattmara is allowed to run loose for too long, then a kingdom and everyone in it can fall into an eternal nightmare sleep. And as it grows more powerful, more people can become afraid, and it can gorge itself on fear, becoming bigger and bigger.” He tapped the page. “Or so the age-old myth goes.”
paras.zh: 他抬起头，棕色的眼睛锁住安娜。“而若放任纳特玛拉游荡太久，整个王国连同其中的每一个人，都会坠入永恒的噩梦沉睡。它越强大，害怕的人就越多，它便能饱餐恐惧，越长越大。”他敲了敲书页。“古老神话是这么讲的。”

paras.en: Anna blinked, breaking away from Sorenson’s deep gaze. “You don’t sound like you believe in this myth,” she said, puzzled. “But doesn’t what’s happening in Arendelle now prove that the myth is real?”
paras.zh: 安娜眨眨眼，从索伦森深邃的注视中回过神。“听你的口气，好像并不信这个神话。”她困惑地说。“可阿伦黛尔眼下发生的一切，不正好证明神话是真的吗？”

paras.en: “Not at all,” Sorenson said, shaking his head and sending his long beard swaying. “What do they teach in schools these days? The Nattmara is a creature of myth, and like all myths, it’s an explanation to a greater mystery. In this instance: where do nightmares come from?”
paras.zh: “全然不是。”索伦森摇头，长长的胡须跟着直晃。“如今学校里都教些什么？纳特玛拉是神话里的生灵，而它同所有神话一样，是对某个更大谜团的解释。就这一例而言，谜团是：噩梦究竟从何而来？”

paras.en: “Pardon me,” Elsa said, while Anna and Kristoff exchanged puzzled glances, “but I don’t understand your question.”
paras.zh: “恕我冒昧，”艾莎说，安娜和克里斯托夫满脸困惑地面面相觑，“我不明白您的问题。”

paras.en: Sighing, Sorenson shook his head. “Let’s look at it a different way. Did you see the signs for the mines that warn to be wary of Huldrefólk?” He paused, and when they nodded, he continued. “The mines were abandoned nearly twenty years ago, because of strange and mysterious things that kept going wrong. Cave-ins started to occur with increased frequency, and miners that had worked their entire lives in these tunnels began to get lost. Now, what was the explanation?” Sorenson looked from Anna to Elsa to Kristoff.
paras.zh: 索伦森叹了口气，摇摇头。“咱们换个角度看。你们看见矿上那些警告牌了吗？提醒人们当心胡尔德精灵的那种。”他顿了顿，见众人点头，才接着说。“矿井大约二十年前就废弃了，因为怪事邪事接连不断。塌方越来越频繁，在坑道里干了一辈子的老矿工，竟然也开始迷路。那么，当时人们怎么解释？”索伦森的目光从安娜移到艾莎，再到克里斯托夫。

paras.en: “Huldrefólk,” Anna said, thinking back to the sign they had passed and Oaken’s warning. “The mysterious, elf-like people known as the Huldrefólk are rumored to live throughout Arendelle in mounds and under rock. They are a mischievous bunch, not necessarily bad, but they enjoy pranks above all else. They have a bit of a reputation for being thieves, but some stories insist they are simply collectors, borrowers of lost things. But unlike the mountain trolls, they are just a story that parents tell their young ones to go to sleep.”
paras.zh: “胡尔德精灵。”安娜说，想起他们一路经过的警告牌，还有奥肯的叮嘱。“传说中，神秘的胡尔德精灵形似精灵，栖居在阿伦黛尔各地的土丘里、岩石下。他们是群促狭鬼，未必是坏，只是恶作剧排在心头的头一等。他们颇有几分贼名，可有些故事偏说他们不过是收藏家，只是把失落之物借走罢了。但与山地岩精不同，他们不过是父母哄孩子入睡的故事罢了。”

paras.en: “Exactly,” Sorenson nodded. “The miners believed the Huldrefólk were angry that they were impeding on their territory. They thought the Huldrefólk were creating the cave-ins to scare the humans away.”
paras.zh: “正是。”索伦森点头。“矿工们相信，胡尔德精灵恼恨他们侵占了地盘。认为那些塌方是胡尔德精灵一手造成的，好把人类吓跑。”

paras.en: “It seemed to have worked,” Kristoff remarked. “I noticed some boards over the mines’ entrance.”
paras.zh: “看来是吓跑了。”克里斯托夫说。“我瞧见矿口钉了几块木板。”

paras.en: “It did work,” Sorenson agreed. “And a good thing, too, because the mines had been overworked. The miners weren’t in danger from territorial Huldrefólk. The human miners were in the middle of a danger of their own making. It was their pickaxes that had made the rock walls too thin to hold the weight of a mountain. Nothing mythical about it; just old-fashioned greed.”
paras.zh: “确实吓跑了。”索伦森同意。“而且是好事一桩，因为这矿早就被挖过头了。矿工们的危险，并非来自抢占领地的胡尔德精灵。他们是自己亲手把自己推到了险境中央。正是他们自己的镐，把岩壁刨得太薄，撑不住整座山的重量。这里头没有半点神话，只有老掉牙的贪心。”

paras.en: “So,” Elsa said slowly, “you’re saying the Nattmara probably has a simple explanation, too?”
paras.zh: “所以，”艾莎缓缓地说，“您是说，纳特玛拉多半也有个简单的解释？”

paras.en: “A scientific one,” Sorenson clarified. “Most likely, our answer is in this.” He tapped the book labeled Psychologia with a grimy fingernail.
paras.zh: “一个科学的解释。”索伦森澄清。“答案多半就在这书里。”他用乌黑的指甲敲了敲那本《心理学》。

paras.en: Anna turned this information over. What Sorenson had said seemed simple enough, but she had seen the wolf. She had seen Kai’s and Gerda’s eyes. The “myth” had seemed very real as it had chased her and her friends through the rooms and halls of the castle.
paras.zh: 安娜在心里把这话翻来覆去地掂量。索伦森说的似乎浅白得很，可她亲眼见过那只狼。她亲眼见过凯和格尔达的眼睛。当那“神话”追着她和朋友们在城堡的厅堂房间间夺命奔逃时，它可真实得很。

paras.en: “But say it is a Nattmara that is doing all of this,” Anna argued, not wanting to leave empty-handed, not wanting to leave without at least one answer. “How can we defeat it?”
paras.zh: “可万一，干下这一切的真是纳特玛拉呢？”安娜据理力争，她不想空手而回，不想连一个答案都带不走。“我们怎样才能打败它？”

paras.en: “That’s easy enough,” Sorenson said, pulling out another book, this one titled Mythica Explainia. “You can only defeat a myth with a thing of myth. But it’s not like Revolute exists. None of it really truly does.”
paras.zh: “这个容易。”索伦森说着，又抽出一本书，这一本题为《神话释疑》。“打败神话之物的，只能是神话之物。可回旋之刃又不是真存在的东西。这些东西，没一样真正存在过。”

paras.en: “Revolute?” Kristoff asked. “That was Aren’s sword, right?”
paras.zh: “回旋之刃？”克里斯托夫问。“那是阿伦的剑，对吧？”

paras.en: “The very one.” Sorenson nodded. “Aren was said to have defeated many a mythical beast with his sword. The very sword, some say, that the sun herself gifted to him for ripping holes in the night sky so that she could watch her children during the day. Those rips, of course, are what we call stars.” He smiled up in the direction of his painted ceiling. “See? Another myth seeking to answer how things came to be.”
paras.zh: “正是那把。”索伦森点头。“据说阿伦用那把剑降服过许多神话里的猛兽。有人说，正是这把剑，太阳亲手所赠——因为他撕裂夜幕，好让她在白天也能守望自己的孩子。那些裂口呢，自然就是我们所说的星星。”他笑着抬头，朝绘满彩画的天花板望去。“瞧见没？又一个想解释‘万物从何而来’的神话。”

paras.en: “Great!” Anna felt hope lift within her for the first time since they’d arrived at the tower. “So we need Revolute! Where is it?”
paras.zh: “太好了！”自从来到这座塔，安娜的心头头一回升起了希望。“那我们就需要回旋之刃！它在哪儿？”

paras.en: Sorenson burst into laughter, but as he did, he took in the serious expression on her face, and shook his head. “I’m sorry, but it’s unlikely that Aren himself ever existed—or his mighty sword of myth. It’s likely that there was a strong warrior from way back when, but he probably never met the sun or faced a great dragon, or carved out the Arenfjord. That’s just legend—like the Huldrefólk or the mountain trolls.”
paras.zh: 索伦森放声大笑，可笑着笑着，看清她脸上认真的神色，又摇了摇头。“抱歉，可阿伦本人多半从未存在过——他那把神话里的神剑也一样。也许很久以前确有一位强悍的勇士，可他大概既没见过太阳，也没遭遇过巨龙，更没开凿出阿伦峡湾。那不过是传说——和胡尔德精灵、山地岩精一样。”

paras.en: “But the trolls exist,” Kristoff said with a shrug. “They raised me.”
paras.zh: “可岩精是真的存在。”克里斯托夫耸耸肩。“他们把我养大的。”

paras.en: Sorenson stared hard at Kristoff. Then he cupped his hand around his mouth and whispered in Elsa’s ear, “Is the mountain man okay?”
paras.zh: 索伦森死死盯着克里斯托夫。接着他拢起手掌，凑到艾莎耳边低声问：“那位山地汉子，脑子没事吧？”

paras.en: “Kristoff,” Anna corrected, “is amazing. And the trolls do exist. And the Nattmara exists. And the Huldrefólk, well, they probably exist, too!”
paras.zh: “他叫克里斯托夫，”安娜纠正道，“他厉害得很。而且岩精真的存在。纳特玛拉也真的存在。胡尔德精灵嘛，哼，八成也存在！”

paras.en: Sorenson sat back, snapping his book shut. “Magic and myth don’t exist,” he said.
paras.zh: 索伦森朝椅背一靠，啪地合上书。“魔法和神话都不存在。”他说。

paras.en: Elsa smirked and flicked her wrist. A second later, Anna felt a cold kiss on her cheek. She looked up to see a delicate snow flurry hovering above their heads.
paras.zh: 艾莎唇角一扬，手腕轻轻一弹。一秒之后，安娜的脸颊上落下一个冰凉的吻。她抬头望去，只见一阵细雪正悬在他们头顶，轻盈飘转。

paras.en: There was a loud clatter as Sorenson tumbled from his stool. “In all my days! The rumors are true!”
paras.zh: 哐当一声大响，索伦森从凳子上翻了下来。“我活了这么大把年纪！传言竟是真的！”

paras.en: Elsa smiled. “You haven’t come down your mountain in a very long time, have you, Sorenson?” And so, Elsa began to tell Sorenson all that had happened in the last three years. And with each new thing he learned, Sorenson had another question.
paras.zh: 艾莎笑了。“你已经很久很久没下过这座山了，对吧，索伦森？”于是，艾莎把过去三年发生的一切，从头讲给索伦森听。而每听完一件新鲜事，索伦森就冒出一个新的问题。

paras.en: Kristoff drummed his fingers on the table impatiently, and only when Anna laid her hand over his did he stop. “Sorry,” he whispered, “but while we’re talking, Sven is still sick!”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫不耐烦地用手指敲着桌面，直到安娜把手覆在他的手上，他才停下。“抱歉，”他低声说，“可我们在这儿说话的工夫，斯文还病着！”

paras.en: Anna knew that Kristoff was right. “Let’s keep looking,” she said quietly.
paras.zh: 安娜知道，克里斯托夫说得没错。“咱们接着找。”她轻声说。

paras.en: Kristoff crept over to the bookshelves while Anna cracked open the volume on the table. She skipped past passages about talking trees and a playful wind spirit until, finally, she found what she had been looking for: NATTMARA.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫蹑手蹑脚走向书架，安娜则翻开桌上的那本书。她跳过会说话的树、顽皮的风灵，一路翻下去，终于找到了要找的东西：纳特玛拉。

paras.en: Sure enough, all that Sorenson had said was written there, including a few additional pieces of information:
paras.zh: 果然，索伦森说过的那些，白纸黑字全在上面，还多出几条信息：

paras.en: The Nattmara is created when a child’s fear grows too big to be contained and the child’s fearful heart calls out to them.
paras.zh: 纳特玛拉诞生于孩子的恐惧大到无法遏制之时——那颗恐惧的心，向它们发出了呼唤。

paras.en: And then, a little below that:
paras.zh: 再往下几行，又写着：

paras.en: Trolls tremble at the Nattmara’s howl while the Nattmara flees from the sun like a shadow.
paras.zh: 岩精闻纳特玛拉之嚎而颤栗，纳特玛拉则如暗影般躲避太阳。

paras.en: Nothing in the section said anything about a spell that was able to manifest a Nattmara, or banish it. But it was useful to know that the Nattmara didn’t like sunlight. And it explained why the trolls had most likely gone missing. Frowning, Anna thumbed through the pages and reread an entry about the Huldrefólk. She stopped upon a line:
paras.zh: 这一节里，只字未提能召唤纳特玛拉、或是驱散它的咒语。但至少知道了纳特玛拉不喜欢阳光，这就有用。这也多半解释了岩精为何杳无踪影。安娜皱起眉，捻动书页，重读起一条关于胡尔德精灵的条目。她停在其中一行上：

paras.en: Huldrefólk always find that which is lost.
paras.zh: 胡尔德精灵总能寻回失落之物。

paras.en: That which is lost…Anna’s heart quickened. Maybe, she thought with rising excitement, that also meant the Huldrefólk could find a mythical sword that was lost to history. It was a slim hope, but a hope she clung to nevertheless. Maybe they needed to go to the mines to find the Huldrefólk—despite the warnings.
paras.zh: 失落之物……安娜的心怦怦加快。也许——她越想越兴奋——那也意味着，胡尔德精灵能找出一把失落于历史的神话之剑。这希望微茫，她却紧抓不放。也许他们正该去矿井寻找胡尔德精灵——哪怕警告就竖在那里。

paras.en: But they didn’t have much time.
paras.zh: 可他们的时间不多了。

paras.en: They only had two more sunrises left before the spell became permanent—and the night was no longer young.
paras.zh: 离咒语永久生效，只剩两次日出——而夜色，已然不早。

paras.en: “You know,” Sorenson said to Elsa, “your mother came here once, seeking answers. In fact, she was the one who painted my ceiling.”
paras.zh: “你可知道，”索伦森对艾莎说，“你母亲来过这儿一回，来寻求答案。事实上，我这天花板，就是她画的。”

paras.en: Anna froze. Their mother had been here? It couldn’t be. Why on earth would their mother come to visit Sorenson? Answers to what? And suddenly, she realized why the painted ceiling looked familiar. It reminded her of the painting of the northern lights and constellations that decorated the ceiling of the secret room.
paras.zh: 安娜僵住了。他们的母亲来过这儿？不可能。母亲究竟为什么要来拜访索伦森？寻什么答案？蓦然间，她明白了那画着的天花板为何如此眼熟。它让她想起密室天花板上那幅绘着北极光与星座的画。

paras.en: Slipping the book into Kristoff’s traveler’s pack, Anna opened her mouth to ask Sorenson more, and to tell the others her idea about going to the mines. But as Anna looked up, she noticed something strange across the tower room: an army of black ants pouring in from under the door. She shut her mouth.
paras.zh: 安娜把书塞进克里斯托夫的行囊，张口想再问索伦森几句，也想把自己去矿井的主意告诉大家。可她一抬头，却看见塔屋那头有桩怪事：一支黑蚁大军正从门底下涌进来。她把话咽了回去。

paras.en: No. Not ants.
paras.zh: 不。不是蚂蚁。

paras.en: Black sand.
paras.zh: 是黑沙。

paras.en: The Nattmara had found them at last.
paras.zh: 纳特玛拉，终于找到他们了。

paras.en: AS THE BLACK SAND trickled into the tower room from beneath the door, thoughts, dark and sticky, clung to Anna like oil.
paras.zh: 黑沙从门底渗进塔屋，一个个漆黑黏腻的念头，像油污一样粘上安娜。

paras.en: Thoughts like bugs crawling into ears, teeth rotting and falling out, waves black and drowning, and a door. A large white door with purple flowers repeating over and over again, each one telling her that she was not good enough, that she was not wanted, that she was shut out. And as the thoughts hit her, pounding as relentlessly as a stormy sea, Anna felt it hard to breathe. Her heart tightened as if something was pressing on her chest. The weight made it hard to speak, but she must—she had to warn her friends.
paras.zh: 虫子钻进耳朵的念头，牙齿烂掉脱落的念头，黑浪灭顶的念头，还有一扇门。一扇高大的白门，紫色的花一遍又一遍地重复，每一朵都在对她说：你不够好，没人要你，你被关在了门外。念头一阵阵砸向她，像风暴里的海，狠戾得没有一刻停歇，安娜觉得喘不过气来。她的心揪紧了，仿佛有什么死死压在胸口。那重量压得她难以开口，可她必须开口——她得警告朋友们。

paras.en: “Y-you guys,” Anna whispered, trying to get her mouth to work. But in those few precious seconds, the sand had spilled into the room, forming a dark puddle. The grains lifted and swirled into the air, as if each grain had its own pair of miniature wings, its own brain, and then they swarmed, creating the outline of a shadow. A wolf’s shadow.
paras.zh: “你、你们几个，”安娜低声说，拼命想让嘴听使唤。可就在这宝贵的几秒里，黑沙已漫进屋中，汇成一眼乌黑的洼。沙粒腾空而起，在空中打着旋，仿佛每一粒都生着一双小小的翅膀、有一颗自己的脑子，接着它们成群涌动，勾出一道影子的轮廓。一头狼的影子。

paras.en: Fear gave her strength. “Nattmara!” Anna yelled.
paras.zh: 恐惧反倒给了她力气。“纳特玛拉！”安娜大喊。

paras.en: The sand solidified into the great white wolf. Now the creature was as big as the length of wall. Its head practically scraped the painted ceiling.
paras.zh: 黑沙凝固成那头巨大的白狼。此刻这怪物已有一面墙那么长。它的头几乎擦着那绘满彩画的天花板。

paras.en: As if in slow motion, Anna saw the others turn. Kristoff’s mouth dropped open, while Elsa’s eyes widened in horror. But it was Sorenson—the old scientist who believed in the entanglement of science and myth, myth and science—who reacted first.
paras.zh: 仿佛慢镜头一般，安娜看见众人回过头来。克里斯托夫张大了嘴，艾莎则惊恐地瞪圆了眼。可最先做出反应的，是索伦森——那位相信科学与神话彼此纠缠、神话与科学难分难解的老科学家。

paras.en: “Close your eyes!” He bolted up and grabbed for one of the many glass vials near him.
paras.zh: “闭眼！”他腾地跳起来，抓起身边一只玻璃小瓶。

paras.en: Anna shut her eyes. A second later, there was a bright flash even through her closed eyelids, followed by the yelp of the wolf. No. Not a wolf, Anna corrected herself. Nattmara.
paras.zh: 安娜闭上眼睛。一秒之后，即便隔着合拢的眼皮，也有一道强光炸开，紧接着是一声狼嚎。不。不是狼，安娜在心里纠正自己。是纳特玛拉。

paras.en: “Upstairs!” Sorenson yelled. “Run!”
paras.zh: “上楼！”索伦森吼道。“快跑！”

paras.en: And even though she had closed her eyes to the flash, black dots still spotted her vision as she stood and ran with Kristoff toward the steps. Taking them two at a time, she was aware of screaming and a noise that sounded like sharpening knives. Glancing backward, she saw Sorenson at the bottom of the stairs, and beside him, Elsa, shooting ice javelins at the wolf again and again and again.
paras.zh: 虽说那道闪光她闭眼躲过了，视野里仍点点发黑；她爬起身，和克里斯托夫朝楼梯冲去。她一步跨过两级台阶，耳边是尖叫，还有一阵像在磨刀的声响。她回头一瞥，看见索伦森守在楼梯底下，他身旁的艾莎正一而再、再而三地朝那狼掷出冰矛。

paras.en: But the ice javelins, sharp and lethal, seemed to do as much harm as a toothpick plunged into water. Each time Elsa let loose an ice javelin, it soared through the air toward its target—but it never hit its target.
paras.zh: 可那些冰矛纵然锋利致命，落在狼身上，却像牙签插进水里，起不了半点作用。艾莎每掷出一支冰矛，它便破空飞向目标——却从未真正命中目标。

paras.en: The Nattmara didn’t seem to be made of fur or bone or muscle. Or anything solid, really. Because as ice javelins were about to pin its paws down in place, the wolf’s paws dissolved at their touch, shifting and morphing its shape like—like sand, Anna realized.
paras.zh: 纳特玛拉似乎不是皮毛、骨头或血肉做的。说真的，压根不是任何实体。就在冰矛即将把狼爪钉在原地的一瞬，那爪子一触即化，形体游移变幻，如同——如同沙，安娜恍然。

paras.en: It was as Sorenson had said. The Nattmara could take any form. Seep through the cracks in any door. Slip into the fragile spots of a person’s heart. It fed on fear, but how could they not be afraid of it? It was fear. A bit of black sand floated toward Anna, and her breath caught again. The sticky thoughts rushed back into her mind: She’d done this. She couldn’t do anything right. She never could. She’d failed Elsa.
paras.zh: 正如索伦森所说。纳特玛拉能化作任何形状。从任何门缝里渗过。滑进人心最脆弱的裂缝。它以恐惧为食，可他们又怎么可能不怕它？它就是恐惧本身。一缕黑沙朝安娜飘来，她的呼吸又一下噎住。黏腻的念头重新涌进脑海：这一切是她造成的。她做什么都不成。从来就不成。她辜负了艾莎。

paras.en: “ANNA!” Kristoff, his traveler’s pack dangling from his shoulder, pulled her arm. “KEEP GOING!”
paras.zh: “安娜！”克里斯托夫一把拽住她的胳膊，行囊还挂在肩头晃荡。“继续跑！”

paras.en: The sound of his voice—full of worry and care—snapped Anna back into herself. She ran with him, and didn’t stop racing up the dizzying, tight spiral of steps until she exploded out into the cold, open air of Sorenson’s observation deck.
paras.zh: 他的声音满是焦灼与关切，一下子把安娜唤回了自身。她跟着他跑，在那令人眩晕的紧凑螺旋阶梯上一刻不停地往上冲，直到一头扎进索伦森观测台寒冷开阔的夜风里。

paras.en: Any other time, she knew she would have loved to stay up there. The mountain air was so clear that the stars above pulsed bright. The moon overhead was round and ripe, just begging to be plucked from the sky and put into her pocket as a sweet treat for later. And in the center of the circular deck, standing like a newborn colt on spindly legs, gleamed a copper telescope. It pointed to the heavens, an instrument that helped seek answers in the celestial dance. It was all strange, fascinating, and beautiful. And a dead end.
paras.zh: 换作平日，她知道自己准会愿意在上面多待一会儿。山间空气清冽，头顶的星星亮得一颗颗直跳。头顶的圆月又圆又熟，简直惹人想把它从天上摘下来，塞进口袋里，当块甜点留着慢慢吃。圆形平台正中，一架铜望远镜闪着微光，立在细长的腿上，像一匹刚出生的小马驹。它指向苍穹，是一件帮人在天体之舞中寻找答案的仪器。这里的一切陌生、迷人，而又美丽。却也是条死路。

paras.en: Just like in Anna’s nightmare, there was no place to run.
paras.zh: 和安娜的噩梦里一样，无路可逃。

paras.en: The wolf, still behind them on the tower stairs, had cornered her, this time on a wooden deck, hundreds of feet in the air, and the only means of escape—jumping—definitely didn’t bode well for any of them. They were trapped!
paras.zh: 那狼还在身后的塔梯上，把她逼进了死角——这一次是在离地几百尺的木台之上，唯一的出路——往下跳——对他们谁都不是什么好主意。他们被困住了！

paras.en: Sorenson’s shoulder collided with hers as he shot past her to the edge of the deck. Leaning over the simple wooden railing, he grasped at the night air and then pulled back. In the light of the full moon, Anna could make out the silver glint of something in his palm: a wire cable—one so thin it seemed to vanish only a foot away from the tower.
paras.zh: 索伦森从她身边疾掠而过，肩膀撞上她的，直奔台边。他探身越过那道简朴的木栏，往夜空里一抓，又缩回手来。满月的光里，安娜辨出他掌心有样东西闪着银光：一根钢丝缆——细得离塔一尺远就仿佛凭空消失了。

paras.en: “Grab the tablecloth!” He gestured to the long wooden workbench that stood next to the telescope. It was covered in beakers, thermometers and barometers, pencils and quills, abacuses, rulers, flasks, and pages of calculations. And seemingly all of Sorenson’s life’s work sat on a little lavender tablecloth neatly embroidered with a crocus. If the tablecloth were pulled, all of that work—years and years of it—would smash onto the deck, lost forever. Anna hesitated.
paras.zh: “抓住桌布！”他朝望远镜旁那张长长的木工作台一指。台上摆满烧杯、温度计和气压计、铅笔和鹅毛笔、算盘、直尺、烧瓶，还有一页页的演算稿。而索伦森毕生的心血，似乎都摊在一条淡紫色的小桌布上，布上端端正正绣着一朵番红花。若是抽走桌布，那些心血——经年累月的心血——就会砸落在台面上，永远地毁了。安娜迟疑了。

paras.en: “Do it!” Sorenson roared at her.
paras.zh: “动手！”索伦森冲她大吼。

paras.en: But Anna couldn’t, she just couldn’t. It was a table of answers, the work of a lifetime of gathering information. So Kristoff reached behind her and tugged the tablecloth free. With a tremendous clash, the beautiful and strange devices fell to the floor, the sound something similar to the breaking of a heart.
paras.zh: 可安娜做不到，她就是做不到。那是一整桌的答案，是一个人一辈子搜集来的心血。于是克里斯托夫从她身后伸手，一把抽出了桌布。一声巨响，那些美丽而奇异的仪器纷纷坠地，那声音像极了心碎。

paras.en: “Now tear the cloth!” Sorenson commanded.
paras.zh: “现在把布撕了！”索伦森喝令。

paras.en: The sound of the wolf’s vicious barks and the scrape of ice filled the air. Elsa had made it to the observation deck and stood at the entrance, flinging her hand out again and again and again. With each flick of her wrist, the doorway filled to the brim with ice—fresh ice, new ice, ice without cracks.
paras.zh: 狼凶狠的吠声与冰的刮擦声塞满了空气。艾莎已经赶到观测台，守在入口处，一遍又一遍地甩手施法。她每弹一下手腕，门口便被冰填得严严实实——新冻的冰，崭新的冰，没有一丝裂缝的冰。

paras.en: For a moment, anyway.
paras.zh: 不过，也就能撑那么一小会儿。

paras.en: Because then the Nattmara would slam itself against it, sending cracks scattering across the surface, and a little more black sand wisped through the cracks each time.
paras.zh: 因为紧接着，纳特玛拉便会一头撞上来，裂纹霎时爬满冰面，而每一回，都有更多的黑沙顺着裂缝丝丝渗入。

paras.en: Smooth ice.
paras.zh: 平整的冰。

paras.en: Shattered ice.
paras.zh: 碎裂的冰。

paras.en: Smooth. Shattered. Elsa was holding the Nattmara and its sandy paws at bay, but even Elsa—brave, strong, wise, magical Elsa—couldn’t keep at it forever. Already, Anna could see the weariness in the slope of her shoulders. The snap of her wrist grew looser with each deft gesture.
paras.zh: 平整。碎裂。艾莎在抵挡纳特玛拉和它的沙爪，可就连艾莎——勇敢、坚强、睿智、身怀魔法的艾莎——也不可能永远撑下去。安娜已经能从她塌下的肩线里看出疲态。她的手腕每灵巧地一抖，弹势便比上一下松上一分。

paras.en: Riiiiiiip! Anna turned to see Kristoff obeying Sorenson’s orders and tearing the tablecloth into thick strips, but Anna didn’t offer to help. Instead, her mind had become preoccupied by something else. Each time Elsa flung out her wrist and filled the doorway with ice, Anna thought the Nattmara grew a little bigger. Smooth ice. Shattered ice. Smooth ice. Yes, Anna was sure of it now. Whenever Elsa shot a magical blast of ice at the creature of myth, its paws expanded, its teeth sharpened, and its strength doubled.
paras.zh: 哧啦————！安娜转头，看见克里斯托夫正照索伦森的吩咐，把桌布撕成粗粗的布条，可安娜没有上前帮忙。她的心思，已被别的事占满了。每次艾莎甩出手腕、用冰填住门口，安娜都觉得纳特玛拉又胀大了一分。平整的冰。碎裂的冰。平整的冰。是的，安娜现在敢肯定了。每当艾莎朝这神话之兽射出魔法冰暴，它的爪便鼓胀，牙便磨利，力气便翻倍。

paras.en: “Elsa!” Anna cried. “Elsa, stop! Your magic! It’s making it stronger!” But between the snarling of the Nattmara, the tearing of the cloth, and the sound of ice cracking again and again and again, Elsa couldn’t hear her. Their only way of surviving in this moment would be if they escaped.
paras.zh: “艾莎！”安娜喊。“艾莎，快停下！你的魔法！它在让它变得更强大！”可纳特玛拉的咆哮、撕布的声响，还有冰一遍又一遍碎裂的脆响交织在一起，艾莎根本听不见。此刻他们唯一活命的法子，就是逃出去。

paras.en: “Hurry!” Sorenson cried. “Take some!”
paras.zh: “快！”索伦森喊。“接一段！”

paras.en: Anna took a bit of tablecloth from Kristoff and stumbled toward the scientist. Grabbing the strip, Sorenson looped the cloth over the thin wire, making a U with the fabric.
paras.zh: 安娜从克里斯托夫手里接过一段桌布，踉踉跄跄地跑向那位科学家。索伦森抓过布条，在细钢丝上绕了一圈，用布兜出一个“U”形。

paras.en: “Hands,” he grunted.
paras.zh: “手。”他闷声说。

paras.en: Anna obliged, holding out her wrists as he tied the dangling ends of the cloth strip under Anna’s armpits to create a makeshift harness.
paras.zh: 安娜依言伸出手腕，他把布条垂下的两端在安娜腋下系紧，做成一个权宜的吊带。

paras.en: Sorenson patted the rickety wooden railing. “Climb up.”
paras.zh: 索伦森拍了拍那道摇摇晃晃的木栏。“爬上去。”

paras.en: Anna did as she was told. Only when she was balanced on the topmost rail, facing the mountain slope far beneath her, did Sorenson’s plan truly sink in. “Wait a second,” Anna said, twisting to face him. “You can’t be serious.”
paras.zh: 安娜照做了。直到她稳稳站上最高一根横栏，面朝脚下远远的山坡，索伦森的打算才真正砸进她的脑子里。“等等。”安娜说，扭过身来面对他。“你不会是认真的吧。”

paras.en: “Hang on tight!” Sorenson pushed her—hard.
paras.zh: “抓稳了！”索伦森猛地一推——用足了力气。

paras.en: With a squeal, Anna slipped off the observation deck in a rush of wind and stars. She screamed. Careening down the mountain nearly felt like flying, but definitely felt like falling. The cable jounced and jiggled as she sped down the mountainside.
paras.zh: 安娜一声尖叫，在一阵风与星光里冲下了观测台。她放声大喊。沿着山势直坠而下，几乎像飞，但完完全全像是在坠落。缆绳随着她飞速下滑一路颠簸摇晃。

paras.en: Wrapping her wrists in the tablecloth, she held on for dear life as her legs swung beneath her. From somewhere above, she could hear Elsa and Kristoff and Sorenson shouting as they zipped down behind her. Thank goodness they were safe!
paras.zh: 她把桌布死死缠在腕上，拼命抓牢，双腿在身下直晃。头顶什么地方，她听见艾莎、克里斯托夫和索伦森一路喊叫着，从她身后嗖嗖滑下。谢天谢地，他们都平安！

paras.en: Anna almost laughed—but the ground was rushing toward her, and coming up way too fast. Straining her eyes against the dark night, Anna followed the path of the rippling cable; it disappeared into the branches of a tree at the foot of the mountain, near the entrance to the mines. That much was good.
paras.zh: 安娜差点笑出声来——可地面正朝她扑来，快得吓人。安娜在沉沉夜色里眯起眼睛，顺着起伏的缆绳望下去：它消失在山脚一棵树的枝叶间，就在矿井入口近旁。这一点还算好。

paras.en: But what wasn’t good was how fast she was approaching the very solid trunk. If she hit the tree at this pace, she would definitely break a few ribs, and that was if she was lucky. She needed to slow down.
paras.zh: 不妙的是，她正以何等的速度撞向那根结结实实的树干。照这个势头撞上去，她非断几根肋骨不可——那还得算她走运。她得慢下来。

paras.en: “SNOW!” she yelled back at Elsa. “SNOW! SNOW SNOW SNOW!” She thought she heard Elsa shout back, but Anna couldn’t tell. The wind stole whatever words left her sister’s lips. She just had to hope and trust that her sister would know what to do, the way she always did.
paras.zh: “雪！”她回头朝艾莎喊。“雪！雪雪雪！”她好像听见艾莎回了话，可安娜分辨不出。风卷走了姐姐唇边吐出的每一个字。她只能盼望、只能相信，姐姐总会知道该怎么办，一如往昔。

paras.en: Ten feet away from the tree. Now five. Now two. Anna released the tablecloth and set herself free. She tumbled through the dark air for what felt like a year but was likely only a moment, and then—
paras.zh: 离树十尺。现在五尺。现在两尺。安娜松开桌布，放开了自己。她在黑暗的夜空里翻滚，仿佛过了一年，其实多半只是一瞬，接着——

paras.en: WOMP!
paras.zh: 噗！

paras.en: A cold tingle enveloped Anna, as refreshing and comforting as one of the bubbly drinks Oaken sold at his lodge. Soft, pillowy snowflakes had cushioned her fall. Elsa had done it again. But there was no time to catch her breath. Instead, Anna rolled out of the way as Elsa, Kristoff, and Sorenson plopped into the snow pile like ripe apples falling from a tree.
paras.zh: 一阵冰凉的酥麻裹住安娜，像奥肯客栈里卖的那种冒泡的饮料，又清新，又熨帖。柔软蓬松的雪花，稳稳垫住了她的坠落。艾莎又一次做到了。可她连喘口气的工夫都没有。安娜赶紧滚到一旁，艾莎、克里斯托夫和索伦森扑通扑通砸进雪堆，像熟透的苹果从树上掉下来。

paras.en: Anna shot up. “Everyone okay? Where is it?”
paras.zh: 安娜一跃而起。“大家都没事吧？它在哪儿？”

paras.en: Everyone nodded, then Kristoff pointed.
paras.zh: 众人纷纷点头，接着克里斯托夫一指。

paras.en: Anna turned. It was hard to see in the dark, but she could just make out a patch of shadow barreling down the mountain like an avalanche of black snow: the Nattmara. Still on the hunt.
paras.zh: 安娜转过身。黑暗中看不真切，可她勉强辨出一片影子正轰隆隆冲下山来，像一场黑雪崩：纳特玛拉。仍在追猎。

paras.en: “The mines!” Anna said. “Hurry!”
paras.zh: “矿井！”安娜说。“快！”

paras.en: “They’re not safe!” Sorenson said. “Cave-ins and toxic air—”
paras.zh: “那儿不安全！”索伦森说。“塌方，还有毒气——”

paras.en: “And Huldrefólk!” Anna said. “Elsa, remember the myth!”
paras.zh: “还有胡尔德精灵！”安娜说。“艾莎，还记得那个神话吗！”

paras.en: Elsa gasped. “‘Huldrefólk always find that which is lost.’ Aren’s sword!”
paras.zh: 艾莎倒吸一口气。“‘胡尔德精灵总能寻回失落之物。’阿伦的剑！”

paras.en: “It may be our only chance!” Anna said. “We have to find them and ask where the Revolute Blade is!”
paras.zh: “那也许是我们唯一的机会！”安娜说。“我们得找到他们，问出回旋之刃在哪儿！”

paras.en: “But—” Sorenson’s protest was cut off by a long howl, a howl that rose in pitch until the very air of the kingdom became a scream, and Anna staggered under its weight.
paras.zh: “可是——”索伦森的抗议被一声长嚎截断，那嚎声越拔越高，直到整个王国的空气都成了尖叫，安娜被它的重量压得一个踉跄。

paras.en: Clasping her hands over her ears, Anna ran past the warning posts, ripped back the wooden boards that had been nailed up over the entrance, and dove into the gaping mouth of the mines. Her friends followed her. The howl reached them even there, and Kristoff struggled with his traveler’s pack to light his lantern, but at last they could see.
paras.zh: 安娜双手死死捂住耳朵，冲过一块块警告牌，扯下钉在矿口的木板，一头扎进大张的矿洞之口。朋友们跟着她钻了进去。即便在这里，那嚎声也追了进来；克里斯托夫在手忙脚乱地翻行囊点提灯，他们总算能看清了。

paras.en: All around, there were passages: thin ones, wide ones, narrow ones, up and down and around. But which led to a dead end? And which led to chambers of poisonous gases or pits with sharp sticks or sleeping bears? Most importantly, which would take them to the Huldrefólk?
paras.zh: 四下里全是通道：细的，宽的，窄的，向上，向下，绕来绕去。可哪一条通向死路？哪一条通往毒气弥漫的洞室，或是插满尖桩的陷坑，又或是冬眠的熊窝？最要紧的是，哪一条能领他们找到胡尔德精灵？

paras.en: “Which one, Sorenson?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: “走哪条，索伦森？”安娜问。

paras.en: But the old scientist looked perplexed. His long silver beard tufted in all directions, as if it, too, were confused.
paras.zh: 可老科学家一脸茫然。他那把银白长须根根支棱，四下乱翘，仿佛连胡子也糊涂了。

paras.en: Standing beside Anna, Kristoff swung his lantern, sending arcs of light rippling across the walls and floor.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫站在安娜身旁，晃动提灯，一圈圈光弧在四壁与地上荡漾。

paras.en: Something glinted in the rock, and Anna looked down. She was standing on something long and metal: the tracks for mine carts!
paras.zh: 岩石间有什么一闪，安娜低头看去。她正踩在一根长长的铁家伙上：矿车轨道！

paras.en: “This way!” Anna said, taking off in a sprint as she followed the tracks.
paras.zh: “这边！”安娜说着，循着轨道撒腿便跑。

paras.en: A second later, they arrived in a large chamber where, at the far end, sitting comfortably as if it had been waiting for them all along, was a wooden mine cart.
paras.zh: 片刻之后，他们跑进一间宽阔的洞室，最深处端端正正停着一辆木矿车，安然自得，仿佛从始至终就在等他们。

paras.en: Kristoff gestured to it theatrically. “Ta-da! Your chariot awaits, m’lady.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫夸张地朝它一摆手。“当当！您的座驾候着呢，小姐。”

paras.en: “Why, thank you, kind sir!” Anna clambered in, with Elsa and Sorenson climbing in behind her.
paras.zh: “哎呀，多谢您嘞，好心的先生！”安娜手脚并用爬进车里，艾莎和索伦森跟在她身后。

paras.en: Kristoff pushed the cart, trying to get the rusty wheels to move forward. They rolled a bit then stopped, and Anna saw why. A rope had been tied around one end of the cart, anchoring it to a jutting boulder.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫推动矿车，想让锈住的轮子往前滚。轮子滚了几下便停住了，安娜看见了缘由。一根绳子捆在车头，把车拴在一块凸出的巨石上。

paras.en: “May I?” she asked him, reaching for his lantern.
paras.zh: “借我使使？”她问他，伸手去够提灯。

paras.en: He handed it to her. “You may.”
paras.zh: 他把灯递给她。“请便。”

paras.en: Anna held the lantern’s flame to the rope.
paras.zh: 安娜把提灯的火苗凑向绳子。

paras.en: The Nattmara’s howl was even louder now, impossibly so, and the tunnel shook.
paras.zh: 此刻纳特玛拉的嚎声更响了，响得不可思议，坑道都在震颤。

paras.en: It had arrived.
paras.zh: 它到了。

paras.en: Each step of its giant paws sent a tremor through the earth.
paras.zh: 它那巨爪每落下一步，大地便随之震颤。

paras.en: And Anna could see that her guess had been right—each time Elsa used her magic, the Nattmara seemed to have grown more fearsome and more horrible. It stood in the mouth of the cave, eclipsing the light of the moon, black sand sweeping around it as its eyes shone yellow.
paras.zh: 而安娜看得明白，自己的猜测没错——艾莎每用一次魔法，纳特玛拉便愈发狰狞可怖。它立在洞口，遮没了月光，黑沙绕着它打着旋，一双眼睛泛着黄光。

paras.en: In Anna’s hands, the rope charred—blackening, thinning. Finally, it snapped. But the cart stayed put.
paras.zh: 安娜手里的绳子焦了——渐渐发黑，渐渐变细。终于，绳子断了。可矿车纹丝不动。

paras.en: “Why aren’t we moving?” Elsa cried out.
paras.zh: “车怎么不走？”艾莎喊道。

paras.en: “We’re too heavy for it,” Anna said, desperation whirling through her. “Maybe if we rock a bit—”
paras.zh: “我们太重了。”安娜说，绝望在胸中打转。“也许晃一晃车——”

paras.en: “No need,” Sorenson interrupted.
paras.zh: “不必了。”索伦森打断她。

paras.en: “What do you mean?” Anna demanded.
paras.zh: “你什么意思？”安娜追问道。

paras.en: But the scientist only smiled—and then launched himself out of the cart. He sprinted toward the mouth of the mines…toward the Nattmara.
paras.zh: 可那位科学家只是笑了笑——随即纵身跳出了矿车。他朝矿井口飞奔而去——朝纳特玛拉冲了过去。

paras.en: “Noooooo!” Anna yelled, though she couldn’t hear herself in the ocean of the Nattmara’s howl.
paras.zh: “不————！”安娜大喊，可在纳特玛拉嚎声的汪洋里，她连自己的喊声都听不见。

paras.en: But Sorenson had done the trick. With his weight gone, the cart rose and the wheels rolled forward, slow at first, then faster and faster—and then the cart plunged, forcing Anna to drop Kristoff’s lantern. It crashed to the floor of the cart, but the light didn’t snuff out. Rough wood cut into her hands as she clung to the sides of the cart for dear life.
paras.zh: 可索伦森这一招奏效了。少了他那点分量，车身一抬，轮子向前滚动，起初慢，接着越来越快——然后车子猛地一沉，安娜只得撒手扔掉克里斯托夫的提灯。提灯砸在车板上，火光却没有灭。她死死扒住车帮，粗粝的木刺扎进掌心。

paras.en: It barreled down the tracks, screeching through jolting turns and sharp twists, threatening to buck them out at every turn.
paras.zh: 矿车沿着轨道狂冲而下，在颠簸的弯道与急转之间吱嘎嘶鸣，每一个弯都像要把他们整个甩出去。

paras.en: “We’re going too fast!” Elsa shouted. “Slow down!”
paras.zh: “太快了！”艾莎喊道。“慢一点！”

paras.en: “The brakes aren’t working!” Kristoff yelled back as he retrieved his lantern and held it out in front of them. “And the steering stick is stuck!”
paras.zh: “刹车不灵了！”克里斯托夫一边回喊，一边捞起提灯，伸到众人身前。“转向杆也卡死了！”

paras.en: Anna felt her mouth open in horror as she frantically tried to think of a solution.
paras.zh: 安娜惊恐地张大了嘴，脑子里疯狂地搜寻对策。

paras.en: “Lean right!” Kristoff bellowed.
paras.zh: “往右倾！”克里斯托夫吼道。

paras.en: Anna and Elsa flung their weight to the right, and the cart shifted on the track, following the curve of the rail. Kristoff continued to yell instructions. In this way—with Kristoff calling out and Anna and Elsa leaning this way and that—they were able to direct the cart, zigzagging down into the mountain’s core instead of dropping vertically. They would roll to a stop at some point. Wouldn’t they?
paras.zh: 安娜和艾莎把身子全力甩向右边，矿车在轨道上偏转，顺着弯道滑行。克里斯托夫不停地吼着指令。就这样——克里斯托夫喊一声，安娜和艾莎便左倾右斜——他们总算驾驭住了矿车，之字形地朝山腹深处俯冲，而不是一头直直栽下去。车总会在什么地方停下来的。会停下的，对吧？

paras.en: And then, suddenly, there was light up ahead. An exit!
paras.zh: 忽然间，前方亮起了光。一个出口！

paras.en: “What is that?” Elsa shouted. “We’re nowhere near morning!” She was right, and as Anna’s eyes drank in the light, she realized it held a strange aqua glow. Before she could wonder too much where it came from, Kristoff yelled, “LAKE!”
paras.zh: “那究竟是什么？”艾莎喊道。“离天亮还早得很呢！”她说得没错，安娜的目光饮着那片光，发觉其中泛着一种奇异的水蓝。她还没来得及细想光从何来，克里斯托夫已经大喊：“湖！”

paras.en: SPLASH!
paras.zh: 哗啦！

paras.en: In an explosion of lukewarm water, they careened into an underground lake. The cart rolled forward in the rippling water, then stopped, the surprisingly shallow body of water bringing their wild ride to an end. Kristoff’s lantern went out, smoke snaking off into the air.
paras.zh: 温吞的水花轰然炸开，他们一头冲进了一个地下湖。矿车在荡漾的水波里又滚了几步，停下了——湖水浅得出人意料，替这场疯狂的疾驰收了尾。克里斯托夫的提灯熄了，一缕烟袅袅升进黑暗。

paras.en: Anna allowed herself to be still. To feel the air in her lungs and hear the quiet of the subterranean world. But it wasn’t utter silence. Far from it.
paras.zh: 安娜允许自己静静不动。感受肺里的空气，聆听地下世界的安宁。可这里并非全然的死寂。远远不是。

paras.en: All around them was a soft splish-splash as stalactites dripped water into the reflective lake that was illuminated by the strange light. Anna looked down at the water and then up in wonder. She finally knew the source of the light. Dangling from the cave ceiling were a million tiny glowworms, each one giving off a gentle light the color of the bluest ice. They reflected onto the surface of the lake so that it looked they were in a bathtub under a galaxy of stars. It was a secret world of sound and water and light, both comforting and glorious.
paras.zh: 四周是一片轻柔的滴答泼溅，钟乳石把水滴进湖里，湖面映着那奇异的光，粼粼闪烁。安娜低头看看湖水，又满心惊奇地抬起头。她终于知道光是从哪儿来的了。洞顶垂挂着千千万万只小小的萤虫，每一只都发出最蓝的冰那种颜色的柔光。萤光倒映在湖面上，他们仿佛泡在星空下的浴缸里。这是一个由声音、水和光织成的隐秘世界，既抚慰人心，又华美壮丽。

paras.en: “Is everyone okay?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: “大家都没事吧？”安娜问。

paras.en: Kristoff winced slightly, but said, more or less cheerfully, “Yep!”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫微微龇了龇牙，却还算爽朗地说：“没事！”

paras.en: “Yes,” Elsa said. “I hope Sorenson is okay.”
paras.zh: “没事。”艾莎说。“但愿索伦森平安无事。”

paras.en: Anna hoped so, too, but she didn’t want her sister to worry. “I’m sure he’s fine,” Anna said, mustering as much enthusiasm as she could. “That scientist has more tricks up his sleeves than appointments in your schedule.” She stood up slowly. “And everyone will be okay once we have the sword to break the Nattmara’s curse.” Careful to keep her balance, she rose to her tiptoes and examined a glowworm. “Wow,” she breathed out. Each glowworm looked like a beaded necklace and hung like an icicle, beautiful and perfect.
paras.zh: 安娜也希望如此，可她不想让姐姐担心。“他肯定没事。”安娜说，竭力撑出满副兴致。“那位科学家袖子里藏的把戏，比你日程上的安排还多呢。”她慢慢站起来。“等我们拿到那把剑、破除纳特玛拉的诅咒，大家就都会没事了。”她小心稳住身子，踮起脚尖，细细端详一只萤虫。“哇。”她轻声赞叹。每一串萤虫都像一条珠链，如冰柱般垂悬，美丽得无可挑剔。

paras.en: There was the sound of swirling water. Anna looked over to see that Elsa had clambered out of the mine cart and stepped into the lake. It was shallow, only coming up to her sister’s waist. She didn’t bother to lift her cloak out of the water, but instead let it float up around her, so that it almost looked like she’d grown a twinkling mermaid’s fin. Now mermaids were something Anna wished were real. And maybe, just maybe, they were. Elsa waded to the rocky banks.
paras.zh: 一阵水声打着旋传来。安娜望过去，只见艾莎已经爬出矿车，蹚进了湖里。湖水很浅，只没到姐姐的腰。她懒得把斗篷拎出水面，任它在四周悠悠浮起，看上去几乎像生出了一条熠熠闪烁的美人鱼尾鳍。美人鱼，倒是安娜真心希望存在的东西。而——也许，只是也许——它们真的存在。艾莎蹚水走向石岸。

paras.en: “Where are you going?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: “你去哪儿？”安娜问。

paras.en: Elsa stopped to look up at the steep track they had careened down only moments before. “I can’t hear anything,” Elsa whispered, as though they were little girls again playing hide-and-find in the chapel and waiting for their parents to discover them.
paras.zh: 艾莎停下脚步，抬头望向他们方才一路狂冲下来的陡峭轨道。“我什么也听不见了。”艾莎低声说，仿佛她们又变回了小女孩，在小礼拜堂里玩捉迷藏，等着父母来找到自己。

paras.en: “That’s good, right?” Kristoff’s voice was hushed. “The Nattmara couldn’t have followed us. We were going impossibly fast, and there were too many tracks for it to know which ones we chose.”
paras.zh: “那是好事，对吧？”克里斯托夫压低了嗓音。“纳特玛拉不可能跟上来。我们快得离谱，轨道又那么多，它根本分不清我们走的是哪条。”

paras.en: “Look up,” Elsa said grimly.
paras.zh: “抬头看。”艾莎的声音沉了下来。

paras.en: Anna followed her sister’s gaze. In the glowworms’ light, she could make out a dozen different passages above them, each one leading to somewhere. To many somewheres. Anna tensed. They had lost the Nattmara. They had lost Sorenson.
paras.zh: 安娜顺着姐姐的目光望去。萤虫的微光里，她辨出头顶有十几条不同的坑道，每一条都通向某个地方。通向许多个地方。安娜的心绷紧了。他们甩掉了纳特玛拉。他们弄丢了索伦森。

paras.en: And now they were lost, too.
paras.zh: 而如今，他们自己也迷了路。

paras.en: ANNA, ELSA, AND KRISTOFF couldn’t stay in the cave of crystal-clear water and glowworm light forever.
paras.zh: 安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫不能永远待在这有清澈水潭和萤虫微光的洞穴里。

paras.en: Because now, even the quiet was dangerous.
paras.zh: 因为如今，连寂静都暗藏杀机。

paras.en: It had been nearly twenty-four hours since Anna had last slept, and judging from the dark bags under Elsa’s eyes, it had even been even longer for her. But it was Kristoff who was suffering from exhaustion the most. Looking for his troll family, he’d already done a hard day’s ride before arriving back at the castle, only to flee. He had been awake for too long. He needed sleep. They all did.
paras.zh: 安娜上次入睡已过去将近二十四小时；而从艾莎眼下的乌青来看，她撑的时间只怕更长。可最疲惫不堪的，还是克里斯托夫。为了寻找他的岩精家人，他在赶回城堡之前就已骑马奔波了整整一天，随后又仓皇出逃。他太久没合眼了。他需要睡眠。他们都需要。

paras.en: But if they slept, it might make it easier for the Nattmara to track them—and Anna knew it wouldn’t give up. That was the nature of a nightmare—one second, they were forgotten, and the next, they exploded into sharp memory. Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff had to keep moving through the mines. They had to keep their feet shuffling forward, their eyes open. If one of them slept, it could be the end of them all. They had so many people to save.
paras.zh: 可一旦睡去，纳特玛拉追踪他们就容易得多——而安娜知道它绝不会善罢甘休。这正是噩梦的本性——前一秒还被遗忘，下一秒便猛然炸成清晰的记忆。安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫必须在矿井里继续前进。他们必须让双脚不停向前挪动，让双眼一直睁着。只要有一人睡去，所有人都可能万劫不复。他们还有那么多人要救。

paras.en: And so, after gathering strands of glowworms to hang around their necks and wrists, they decided on a tunnel—not because it was familiar, but because it seemed to go more up than the others. Using the skills he’d learned on the mountain, Kristoff had been able to help them all scale the wall with his rope to reach the highest passageway.
paras.zh: 于是，采了几缕萤虫挂在脖颈和手腕上之后，他们选定了一条隧道——并非因为眼熟，而是因为它似乎比其他的更向上延伸。凭着在山上学来的本领，克里斯托夫用绳索帮大家攀上岩壁，抵达了最高处的那条通道。

paras.en: As they trudged forward, Anna tried to think about energizing things: sunrises, sledding, playing with the children in town, Olaf. But instead of making her feel excited and awake, they only made her feel sad and even more tired. She wondered if she would ever feel awake again. Kristoff stumbled beside her. Instead of catching himself as he normally would, he dropped to his knees and sank back onto his heels.
paras.zh: 他们拖着沉重的脚步前行，安娜努力想些令人振奋的事：日出、滑雪橇、和镇上的孩子们玩耍，还有雪宝。可这些非但没让她兴奋清醒，反而令她愈发伤感，也愈发疲惫。她怀疑自己是否还有再清醒过来的时候。克里斯托夫在她身旁踉跄了一下。他没有像往常那样稳住身形，而是双膝一软跪倒在地，整个人坐回了脚跟。

paras.en: Anna stooped beside him and rested a hand on his back. “Are you okay, Kristoff? You have to get up!” She nudged him.
paras.zh: 安娜在他身边俯下身，一只手抚上他的背。“你没事吧，克里斯托夫？你得起来！”她轻轻推了推他。

paras.en: Kristoff mumbled in reply and laid his head on the ground. “This rock is so soft.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫含糊应了一声，把头搁在了地上。“这石头好软啊。”

paras.en: Anna pulled on his arm, but instead of yanking him to his feet, she only succeeded in making herself more tired, and she, too, sank to the ground.
paras.zh: 安娜去拽他的手臂，却没能把他拉起来，反倒把自己累得更厉害，也跟着瘫坐在了地上。

paras.en: Kristoff was right. The rock was soft and still and it wanted her to lay her head down on it. It was warm, and from the depths of her sleep-addled mind, Anna remembered a lesson Gerda had taught her, about how the earth was a crust of dirt floating on top of hot magma, and that sometimes, little pockets of heat would spring warm water from the rocks underneath. Even though these carved tunnels within the mines had never seen the sun, they felt like a touch of summer—of lying on rocky beaches kissed by the sun. All Anna wanted to do was to stretch out her tired muscles and sleep there. Anna! From a long way away, she heard someone calling her name. Anna, get up!
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫说得没错。那岩石又软又静，仿佛在渴求她把头枕上去。它暖暖的，从昏昏欲睡的意识深处，安娜记起格尔达教过她的一课：大地不过是一层浮在炽热岩浆之上的泥土硬壳，有时，细小的热流会从底下的岩缝里涌出温泉。这些矿井里开凿的隧道虽从未见过天日，却透着一丝夏意——像躺在被阳光亲吻过的石滩上。安娜只想舒展开酸痛的四肢，就地睡去。安娜！很远的地方，她听见有人在喊她的名字。安娜，快起来！

paras.en: “Just a few more minutes,” Anna mumbled.
paras.zh: “再睡几分钟就好，”安娜嘟囔着。

paras.en: A slap of cold air hit her. Anna jolted upright. “Hey!” She wiped away what seemed to be the remnants of a snowball from her cheek.
paras.zh: 一股寒气迎面袭来。安娜猛地坐直了身子。“嘿！”她抹去脸颊上像是雪球残渣的东西。

paras.en: “What was that for?” Kristoff protested, snow also flecking his face.
paras.zh: “你这是干吗？”克里斯托夫抗议道，他脸上也落满雪沫。

paras.en: “I’m saving your lives,” Elsa said. She conjured another snowball, which she juggled. “On your feet, or it’s more ice in your face. We have a deal?”
paras.zh: “我在救你们的命，”艾莎说。她又变出一个雪球，在掌间抛玩着。“起来站好，不然你们脸上还有的是冰。成交吗？”

paras.en: “Blargh!” Kristoff sputtered. “Just let us sleep!”
paras.zh: “呃啊！”克里斯托夫喷着唾沫星子。“就让我们睡一会儿吧！”

paras.en: “Sorry, but I can’t do that.” Elsa shook head. “Anna! Oh, for goodness’ sake.”
paras.zh: “抱歉，这个我办不到。”艾莎摇了摇头。“安娜！哦，老天哪。”

paras.en: Anna felt another slap of cold snow and jerked her head up. “Sorry, sorry,” she mumbled, her tongue feeling too thick for her mouth. Snow glistened at Elsa’s fingertips, and something niggled at Anna’s mind. It was something important. It had something to do with Elsa and her magic. But what was it?
paras.zh: 安娜又挨了一记冷雪，猛地抬起头。“抱歉，抱歉，”她咕哝着，舌头在嘴里笨重得不听使唤。雪花在艾莎指尖闪着微光，安娜心里有个念头隐隐作痒。那是件很重要的事。与艾莎和她的魔法有关。可到底是什么呢？

paras.en: As Elsa wound her arm, ready to pitch another snowball at either one of them, Anna remembered. She shot up tall and nearly jumped.
paras.zh: 就在艾莎抡起手臂、准备再朝他们两人中的任何一个掷出雪球时，安娜想起来了。她腾地站得笔直，几乎跳了起来。

paras.en: “Elsa, stop!”
paras.zh: “艾莎，快停下！”

paras.en: Her sister dropped her snowball to the ground, where it landed with a small puff. “You promise to stay awake now? Because there’s more snow where that came from.”
paras.zh: 姐姐手中的雪球落到了地上，发出一声轻柔的噗。“现在你保证保持清醒了？要知道，这样的雪还多着呢。”

paras.en: But Anna was no longer sleepy. Far from it. “You can’t keep using your magic,” she said. “On the observation deck, I noticed that every time you did, the Nattmara grew.”
paras.zh: 可安娜已经丝毫不困了。恰恰相反。“你不能再用魔法了，”她说。“在观测台上，我注意到你每用一次魔法，纳特玛拉就会变大一圈。”

paras.en: “Oh.” Elsa folded her arms across her chest. “Great.”
paras.zh: “哦。”艾莎双臂环抱在胸前。“太好了。”

paras.en: Anna rooted around in Kristoff’s pack and pulled out the book, flipping open its pages to confirm her theory. But they were soaked through from the lake, the ink indecipherable. She sighed.
paras.zh: 安娜在克里斯托夫的行囊里翻找一番，掏出那本书，翻开书页想验证自己的猜想。可书页早已被湖水浸透，墨迹模糊难辨。她叹了口气。

paras.en: SNORFFF!
paras.zh: 呼噜——！

paras.en: The sisters looked down to see Kristoff’s eyes had closed again, a strangled snore escaping from him as his head drifted toward his chest.
paras.zh: 姐妹俩低头看去，只见克里斯托夫的眼睛又闭上了，脑袋朝胸口垂去，喉咙里发出一声压抑的鼾声。

paras.en: “What are we going to do about him?” Elsa asked.
paras.zh: “我们拿他怎么办？”艾莎问。

paras.en: “Umm.” Anna cast about for an idea—any idea. Usually, they came sharp and sure, but lack of sleep was making her feel fuzzy. All she could really focus on were their shadows thrown by the glowworms onto the cave wall opposite them. Shadows. Shadows similar to the famous shadow puppets of Zaria. She’d read how the puppeteers were often as famous as singers, and could fill whole theaters with their performances. If they could ever defeat the Nattmara and make everything right again, maybe she would invite some of the puppeteers to come give a performance in Arendelle. Everyone had liked it so much last year when Kristoff had performed his musical….
paras.zh: “呃……”安娜四处搜罗主意——随便什么主意都行。平日里，主意总是来得干脆而笃定，可睡眠不足让她的脑子发懵。她真正能凝神注视的，只有萤虫投在对面洞壁上的他们的影子。影子。类似扎里亚那闻名遐迩的皮影戏的影子。她读到过，皮影艺人往往和歌手一样声名显赫，一场演出就能让整座剧院座无虚席。如果他们真能打败纳特玛拉、让一切恢复如初，也许她会邀请几位皮影艺人来阿伦黛尔献艺。去年克里斯托夫上演他的音乐剧时，大家是那么喜欢……

paras.en: “That’s it!” Anna shouted. That’s it, it, it. Her words echoed down the rocky corridor. Crouching down to be at the same level as Kristoff’s fluttering eyelashes, she began to sing: “‘Goblin toes are ugly, and Hulder tails are sweet—but you would never catch me, sweep one off his’…paw!”
paras.zh: “有了！”安娜喊道。有了，了，了。她的声音在岩石走廊里回荡。她蹲下身，让视线与克里斯托夫扑闪的睫毛齐平，开口唱道：“'妖精的脚趾丑，胡尔德的尾巴甜——可你永远别想让我，去扫他一只'……爪！”

paras.en: It was a silly song that Kristoff had made up for the last spring festival. The children in the village had loved it, and had performed it for the kingdom under Kristoff’s encouraging eye. When Anna had first met the mountain man, he’d been snow-crusted and only grunted a few words to her. She never would have thought that underneath the rough exterior, and a dirt patch or two, his real language was song.
paras.zh: 那是克里斯托夫为去年春祭编的一首傻歌。村里的孩子们爱极了它，还在克里斯托夫鼓励的目光下为全国演过。安娜初遇这个山地汉子时，他浑身裹着雪壳，只对她咕哝过寥寥几个字。她万万没想到，在那粗糙的外表下，在一两块泥斑之间，他真正的语言竟是歌。

paras.en: Kristoff had a gift for melody, and though he didn’t mind the odd soup stain on his shirt and didn’t care about the difference between a salad fork and a dessert fork, he was sensitive about song lyrics. Particularly to songs he had written.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫有旋律方面的天赋；他不在意衬衫上偶尔沾着的汤渍，也分不清沙拉叉和甜点叉，可他对歌词却极其敏感。尤其是他自己写的歌。

paras.en: “Huh?” Kristoff’s eyes flew open. “It’s supposed to be ‘sweep one off his feet!’”
paras.zh: “啊？”克里斯托夫猛地睁开眼。“应该是'去扫他一只脚！'才对”

paras.en: Eyes sparkling, Elsa sang the next verse. “‘Goblins like to eat a lot, and Hulder like to sing—but you will never find one with a feathered’…nose!”
paras.zh: 眼中闪着光的艾莎接唱了下一节。“'妖精贪吃停不了口，胡尔德爱唱忘不了歌——可你永远找不到长着羽毛的'……鼻子！”

paras.en: “No!” Kristoff surged to his feet. “That doesn’t rhyme! And what does a feathered nose even mean?”
paras.zh: “不对！”克里斯托夫一跃而起。“这根本不押韵！还有，长羽毛的鼻子到底是个什么鬼？”

paras.en: “Now we got him,” Anna whispered to her sister, and she grabbed his hand. “Come on, Kristoff, sing it for us?”
paras.zh: “这下我们抓住他了，”安娜对姐姐耳语，一把抓住他的手。“来嘛，克里斯托夫，唱给我们听，好不好？”

paras.en: And Kristoff—poor, tired, sorrowful Kristoff—sang.
paras.zh: 于是克里斯托夫——这个可怜、疲惫、满怀哀伤的克里斯托夫——唱了起来。

paras.en: Together, the three of them moved forward through the darkness, their voices echoing so that they sounded like an entire choir rather than just three fatigued friends hoping to survive, hoping to save the kingdom that Anna loved more than anything. She gave herself over to the sound, letting it sweep her along.
paras.zh: 三人在黑暗中并肩前行，歌声回荡，听起来宛如一整支唱诗班，而不只是三个疲惫不堪的朋友——盼着活命，盼着救下这个安娜爱得胜过一切的王国。她把自己交付给歌声，任它裹挟着向前。

paras.en: They sang about the Huldrefólk. They sang about Aren and his gallant sword. And then they sang a silly ballad about a goose who fell in love with a duck.
paras.zh: 他们唱胡尔德精灵。他们唱阿伦和他那把英勇的剑。接着，他们又唱了一首傻乎乎的叙事谣曲，讲一只鹅爱上了一只鸭。

paras.en: As they reached the end of the song, Anna thought about how beautiful Elsa’s voice sounded. She hadn’t known her sister could hit quite such high notes, or even sing harmonies. Anna stopped singing, wanting to listen closer. And that’s when she realized that Kristoff had stopped singing…and so had Elsa.
paras.zh: 唱到歌曲末尾，安娜忽然想到，艾莎的嗓音是多么动人。她从不知道姐姐能唱出那么高的音，甚至还会唱和声。安娜停住了歌唱，想听得更真切些。就在那时，她发觉克里斯托夫已经不唱了……艾莎也不唱了。

paras.en: In fact, all three of them had fallen silent, and yet the song continued. It climbed around them, higher and higher.
paras.zh: 事实上，三个人都已悄然无声，可那歌声仍在继续。它在他们四周盘旋攀升，越来越高，越来越高。

paras.en: It was as though the rocks themselves were singing. But that couldn’t be—could it?
paras.zh: 仿佛是岩石本身在歌唱。可这不可能——难道可能吗？

paras.en: Elsa pointed down a passage to their left. “It’s coming from there.”
paras.zh: 艾莎指向他们左边的一条通道。“歌声是从那儿传来的。”

paras.en: Anna turned toward it.
paras.zh: 安娜转身朝那边走去。

paras.en: “Hold on!” Elsa grabbed her. “What makes you think we’re going that way?”
paras.zh: “等等！”艾莎一把抓住她。“你凭什么认为我们要走那条路？”

paras.en: “Why wouldn’t we?” Anna said. “We’re lost, and we need help. Besides, something so beautiful can’t possibly be dangerous!”
paras.zh: “为什么不走？”安娜说。“我们迷路了，需要帮助。再说，这么美的东西不可能是危险的！”

paras.en: Elsa stared at her. “Did you learn nothing from your engagement with Prince—”
paras.zh: 艾莎盯着她。“和王子订婚那一次，你就什么教训都没学到——”

paras.en: “Shh,” Kristoff interrupted. “The singing’s stopped.”
paras.zh: “嘘，”克里斯托夫打断了她。“歌声停了。”

paras.en: And so it had.
paras.zh: 果然停了。

paras.en: Anna whirled on Elsa. “We missed out on someone who could have helped us!”
paras.zh: 安娜猛地转向艾莎。“我们错过了一个本可以帮我们的人！”

paras.en: “Or maybe we missed out on whatever could have eaten us,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: “又或许，我们错过的是某个本可以吃掉我们的东西，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Kristoff gulped. “Or maybe they’re right behind you.”
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫咽了口唾沫。“又或许，它们就在你们身后。”

paras.en: “Very funny, Kristoff,” Anna told him.
paras.zh: “真会开玩笑，克里斯托夫，”安娜对他说。

paras.en: “No,” he protested. “I’m…serious. Look.”
paras.zh: “不，”他分辩道。“我是……认真的。你看。”

paras.en: While Anna had been talking with Elsa, they had walked into a new portion of the mines.
paras.zh: 趁安娜与艾莎说话的工夫，他们已走进矿井中一片新的区域。

paras.en: Unlike the other passageways, this one had never seen the tip of a pickax. Because all around were crystals—and not just any crystals. Each one was taller than Kristoff and as wide as a tree trunk. They jutted from the walls and the ceiling, angled every which way to form a forest of sparkling rock. Each crystal was a shifting white, as though when the crystals had formed, they’d been filled with smoke.
paras.zh: 与其他通道不同，这里从未见过镐尖。因为四周林立着水晶——而且绝非寻常的水晶。每一根都比克里斯托夫还高，粗壮如树干。它们从四壁和洞顶斜斜刺出，指向四面八方，构成一片晶莹闪烁的岩石之林。每一根水晶都流转着朦胧的白色，仿佛水晶成形之际，曾被灌入了烟雾。

paras.en: But it wasn’t the crystals’ unusual size or color that made Anna gasp or caused Elsa to grip her so hard that Anna could feel Elsa’s fingernails digging into her shoulder. Sitting astride a crystal as large as a pony was a little child.
paras.zh: 然而，令安娜倒抽冷气、令艾莎把她攥得生疼——安娜甚至能感到艾莎的指甲深深掐进自己肩膀——的，并不是水晶那罕见的尺寸或颜色。骑在一株小马大小的水晶上的，是个小小的孩童。

paras.en: At least, Anna thought it might be a child, as the figure was definitely child-sized, about as big as a three-year-old human. In the dim light of the glowworm bracelet she’d put on, Anna could just make out the gleam of an eye, and soft-looking gray leggings that glimmered slightly as the child kicked out their legs.
paras.zh: 至少，安娜猜那是个孩子，因为那身影分明是孩子的尺寸，约莫三岁人类孩童那般大小。借着戴上的萤虫手环的微光，安娜勉强辨认出一只眼睛的亮光，还有一条柔软的灰色紧身裤，在孩子蹬腿时微微闪烁。

paras.en: The child began to sing again, though the melody had no words. Just clear, round notes.
paras.zh: 孩子又开始唱了起来，只是那旋律没有歌词。只有清亮圆润的音符。

paras.en: With a gasp, Anna began to run toward the child, stubbing her toes and just missing occasional low-hanging rocks. But she didn’t care. All that mattered was that there was a child under the mountain who had been left alone. And Anna never wanted anyone to feel alone or left out—not ever. Not if she could help it.
paras.zh: 安娜倒吸一口气，朝孩子奔去，脚趾磕得生疼，还险些撞上偶尔低垂的岩石。可她毫不在意。重要的是，这大山深处有个孩子被人孤零零地丢下了。而安娜从不愿让任何人感到孤单或被遗忘——永远不愿。只要她力所能及。

paras.en: Worry pulsed through her, followed by guilt. She hadn’t even heard of a child missing from the village. She knew she’d been distracted with Elsa’s impending grand tour, but she couldn’t have been so busy as to not have heard about a missing child. She wondered how long the child had been down there, where the guardians were, or—she realized with a lurch—maybe the question should be, what had happened to them? Did the Nattmara get them?
paras.zh: 担忧在她胸中翻涌，随之而来的是愧疚。她连村里有孩子失踪的事都没听说过。她知道自己一直在为艾莎即将启程的盛大巡游分心，可再怎么忙，也不至于忙到连孩子走失都没听说吧。她想知道孩子在那儿待了多久，守护者们又在哪里，或者——她心头猛地一沉——也许该问的是，他们遭遇了什么？是纳特玛拉害了他们吗？

paras.en: But before she could get more than a few feet from the child, she felt someone tug on the back of her cloak, yanking her.
paras.zh: 可还没等她走出离孩子几步远，就感觉有人拽住她的斗篷后襟，猛地往回一拉。

paras.en: “Anna,” Elsa whispered, voice as low as could be, “do you see the ears?”
paras.zh: “安娜，”艾莎压得极低地耳语道，“你看见那双耳朵了吗？”

paras.en: Anna squinted, trying to see what Elsa saw. At first, she couldn’t, as the child’s curls bumped over where she expected the ears to be, except…
paras.zh: 安娜眯起眼睛，想看清艾莎看见的东西。起初她什么也看不见，孩子的卷发正隆起在她料想中耳朵的位置，只是……

paras.en: Anna squinted so hard now that she could see her own eyelashes.
paras.zh: 安娜眯眼眯得太用力，连自己的睫毛都映入了眼帘。

paras.en: And then, she saw them: the child’s ears rose to slender points, like the tips of a dragonfly’s wings.
paras.zh: 然后，她看见了：孩子的耳朵高高竖起，收成纤细的尖，宛如蜻蜓翅膀的翅尖。

paras.en: Suddenly, Anna remembered a bedtime story from a long, long time ago, back when she and Elsa had shared a room. They are tall and strong, with sharp ears. And they’re sensitive. Which is why, little Elsa, Mother had said with a tug on the hem of Elsa’s pajama bottoms, if you ever see one, you must not mention their tail! It’s rude.
paras.zh: 骤然间，安娜记起很久很久以前的一个睡前故事，那时她和艾莎还同住一室。他们高大强壮，耳朵尖尖。而且十分敏感。所以，小艾莎，母亲一边扯了扯艾莎睡裤的裤脚一边说，如果你见到一个，千万不可提他们的尾巴！那样很失礼。

paras.en: And if you do—a young Anna had popped up from behind her pillow fort, making a scary face and shaping her hands into claws—they might eat you!
paras.zh: 可你若是提了——小安娜从枕头堡垒后面探出头来，做了个吓人的鬼脸，双手弯成利爪——他们可能会把你吃掉！

paras.en: Elsa had burst into giggles, which had only made Anna wrinkle her face more and add an extra growl.
paras.zh: 艾莎咯咯笑个不停，这只会让安娜把脸皱得更凶，又添上一声低吼。

paras.en: All right, enough, Mother had said, scooping Anna up in one arm to plop her beside Elsa before she sat next to them on the bed. Cuddle close. Scooch in.
paras.zh: 好了，够了，母亲说着，单臂将安娜捞起来，放到艾莎身旁，然后挨着她们在床上坐下。挨紧些。往里挤挤。

paras.en: Anna had let her face fall back to normal, but she’d kept her fingers curled into claws as she cozied up next to her mother and sister and asked, Momma, what do their tails look like?
paras.zh: 安娜让脸上的凶相褪去，却仍把手指蜷成爪子，紧紧依偎在母亲和姐姐身边，问道：妈妈，他们的尾巴长什么样呀？

paras.en: No one knows, Mother had said, and fixed a ribbon in Anna’s ponytail. They keep them hidden under skirts or keep their backs to the wall at all times.
paras.zh: 没有人知道，母亲说着，替安娜理好马尾辫上的缎带。他们把尾巴藏在裙子底下，或是随时随地背靠着墙。

paras.en: But I wanna knoooow, Anna had whined, and her mother had kissed the top of her head and laughed.
paras.zh: 可我想知——道嘛，安娜哼哼唧唧地撒娇，母亲吻了吻她的发顶，笑了起来。

paras.en: Everyone is entitled to their secrets, she’d said. Especially the hidden people.
paras.zh: 每个人都有权保守自己的秘密，她说。尤其是那些隐世之人。

paras.en: The hidden people.
paras.zh: 隐世之人。

paras.en: Or, as the Arendellians called them…
paras.zh: 或者，用阿伦黛尔人的说法……

paras.en: “Huldrefólk,” Anna breathed. And as she spoke the name aloud, Oaken’s words came back to her, sharp as a stalactite.
paras.zh: “胡尔德精灵，”安娜轻声吐出。而就在她念出这个名字时，奥肯的话猛然浮上心头，尖锐如一根石钟乳。

paras.en: Beware the Huldrefólk.
paras.zh: 当心胡尔德精灵。

paras.en: THE CHILD’S—Hulder’s—melody flew off on invisible wings and faded again into silence.
paras.zh: 那孩子的——胡尔德的——旋律乘着无形的翅膀飞走，再度没入寂静。

paras.en: Anna burst into applause; she couldn’t help it. After all, the little Hulder didn’t seem dangerous.
paras.zh: 安娜忍不住鼓起掌来。毕竟，这个小胡尔德看上去并不危险。

paras.en: “That was incredible!” she exclaimed. “What’s your name?”
paras.zh: “太了不起了！”她惊叹道。“你叫什么名字？”

paras.en: For a moment, the Hulder seemed to stare at Anna in the glow-light, luminescent eyes boring into hers, and then the Hulder tumbled backward off the crystal.
paras.zh: 有那么一刻，胡尔德在幽光中凝视着安娜，发光的眼睛直直望进她的眼底，随后那孩子便从水晶上向后翻跌了下去。

paras.en: “No!” Anna said as she rushed behind the crystal to check on the child, hoping the tiny Hulder hadn’t hurt themselves.
paras.zh: “不！”安娜喊道，冲到水晶后面去查看孩子，盼着小胡尔德没有摔伤。

paras.en: But as she rounded the tree-trunk-sized crystal, she saw that the Hulder was no longer behind it. The child had disappeared, except for the sound of footsteps pattering down the dark passage up ahead. Without a second thought, Anna took off.
paras.zh: 可当她绕过那树干般粗的水晶，却看见胡尔德已不在后面了。孩子消失了，只剩前方幽暗通道里传来的细碎脚步声。安娜想也没想就追了上去。

paras.en: “Anna!” Elsa called from behind. “Wait! Slow down! You’re going too fast!”
paras.zh: “安娜！”艾莎在身后喊。“等等！慢点！你跑得太快了！”

paras.en: “Anna!” Kristoff shouted. Their warnings echoed off the rocks around them, but Anna disagreed with them both: she was going too slow.
paras.zh: “安娜！”克里斯托夫也喊。两人的警告在四周岩石间回响，可安娜对两位都不以为然：她明明跑得还太慢。

paras.en: The Hulder was quick—Anna wasn’t sure if it was footsteps she was following now, or just the quiet drip of stalactites in the distance. Still, they had come to look for the Huldrefólk, the only ones who might be able to help them find the Revolute Blade, the only ones of myth who might be able to save them all from Anna’s terrible mistake. And so Anna ran on, only just missing the occasional low-hanging rocks. Suddenly, the Hulder screeched. It sounded frightened, and Anna hoped the Hulder wasn’t in trouble.
paras.zh: 胡尔德动作极快——安娜已分不清自己追随的究竟是脚步声，还是远处钟乳石滴水的轻响。不过，他们本就是来寻胡尔德精灵的——只有他们或许能帮着找到回旋之刃，也只有这神话中的生灵，或许能把大家从安娜铸下的大错中解救出来。于是安娜继续奔跑，只险险避开偶尔低垂的岩石。突然，胡尔德尖叫了一声。那声音里满是惊恐，安娜盼着胡尔德没有遇上麻烦。

paras.en: “Hang on!” Anna shouted. She ran faster and faster, and then her foot caught—on a rock, a divot, or a root, it was too dark to tell—and she toppled to the ground, her hands out to cushion her fall.
paras.zh: “撑住！”安娜喊道。她越跑越快，随后脚下一绊——绊在石头、坑洞还是树根上，天太暗看不清——整个人向前栽倒，双手伸出去缓冲坠落。

paras.en: Pain cracked through Anna’s ribs as she slammed into the solid rock. She was going to have one giant bruise in an hour. Everything hurt. Everything but her right arm, which she’d flung out far in front of herself to try to break her fall. And as Anna looked at the glowworm bracelet dangling from her wrist, she saw why: her right arm had not hit any rock at all. All that hand had hit was thin air. Anna was glad she was already lying on the ground, because she thought she might faint if she were still standing. She’d followed the Hulder—and had almost run off a cliff and into an abyss.
paras.zh: 安娜撞上坚硬的岩石，肋部一阵剧痛迸裂。不出一个钟头，她准得青一大块。浑身都疼。唯有右臂不疼——她为了撑住身子，把右臂远远甩在了身前。安娜看着手腕上晃荡的萤虫手环，才明白缘由：她的右臂根本没撞上任何岩石。那只手碰到的，只有空气。安娜庆幸自己已经躺在地上了，因为若是还站着，她觉得自己非晕过去不可。她追着胡尔德——差一点就冲下悬崖，坠入深渊。

paras.en: She could still hear the Hulder’s cry. Tuva’s warning from the trading post came back to her. They’re tricky. Sometimes, they help. Other times, they lure humans off the safest paths. And maybe, Anna thought, lure them into an abyss. There was always a chance that the Hulder child had done this on purpose, had perhaps meant to distract Anna and Elsa and Kristoff away from the Huldrefólk’s home.
paras.zh: 她还能听见胡尔德的哭声。图娃在商栈的警告又浮上心头。他们诡计多端。 有时，他们会帮忙。有时，他们却会把人诱离最安全的路。 也许，安娜想，还会把人诱进深渊。胡尔德孩子这么做，说不定是有意的——也许就是想引开安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫，不让他们找到胡尔德精灵的家。

paras.en: But even as these dark thoughts gathered into a cloud, Anna scooted forward on her belly, toward the sound of the Hulder’s cry. It didn’t matter what the Hulder’s intentions had been—but it did matter that the Hulder was stuck and scared. Once she wiggled to the edge, Anna leaned her chin out and peered down. The Hulder had tumbled over the edge, but by some luck or miracle, the child had caught themselves on a small ledge five feet down. It would be easy for Kristoff to lean over and reach the Hulder, but even as Anna watched, the rocky ledge was crumbling away under the child’s weight.
paras.zh: 可即便这些阴郁的念头聚成了一团乌云，安娜还是趴在地上向前挪，朝着胡尔德哭声的方向。胡尔德的用意是什么并不重要——重要的是，胡尔德被困住了，而且正吓坏了。安娜扭动着凑到崖边，探出下巴往下望。胡尔德翻下了崖沿，但不知是侥幸还是奇迹，孩子卡在了下方五英尺处一小块突出的岩架上。克里斯托夫只要探身过去便够得到胡尔德，可就在安娜注视的当儿，那块岩架正在孩子的重压下簌簌崩碎。

paras.en: “Elsa! Kristoff! Help!” Anna shouted as she inched forward even more, letting herself dangle over the edge, her hand outstretched. “Grab my hand!” she called down.
paras.zh: “艾莎！克里斯托夫！救命！”安娜喊着，自己又往前挪了几分，半个身子悬在崖沿之外，手伸向下方。“抓住我的手！”她朝下喊。

paras.en: The Hulder raised a hand, but Anna was still too far away. She had to get closer. Wiggling forward, Anna lowered herself down inch by fraction of an inch. Just a little bit farther now…She strained her fingers forward, willing them to lengthen—and that’s when she felt the crumbling of the earth beneath her own weight. What was once solid ground turned to gravel, and Anna skidded forward, headfirst into the dark abyss. She screamed.
paras.zh: 胡尔德举起一只手，可安娜还是够不着。她得再靠近些。安娜一点一点往前蹭，一寸又一寸地放低身子。就差一点点了……她拼命把手指往前探，巴望着它们能再长一些——就在这时，她感到身下的泥土也开始在自己的重量下崩散。原本坚实的地面化作碎石，安娜一头栽进了黑暗的深渊。她尖叫起来。

paras.en: But before she could shoot past the Hulder and plummet into the vast void, two pairs of hands grabbed her ankles from above. Kristoff! Elsa!
paras.zh: 可还没等她掠过胡尔德、坠入那无底的虚空，上方两双手攥住了她的脚踝。克里斯托夫！艾莎！

paras.en: She lurched to a stop, face to face with the little cat-eyed Hulder, who was still mostly in shadow, and who, if Anna had to wager a guess, looked terrified of her.
paras.zh: 她猛地刹住，正对着那只猫眼小胡尔德——那孩子大半还隐在阴影里，若让安娜来猜，八成是被她吓坏了。

paras.en: “Hi,” Anna said, trying hard to iron out the quiver in her voice. “My name is Anna, and I’m not going to hurt you.” She offered out her hand. “Come with me!”
paras.zh: “嗨，”安娜说，努力抚平声音里的颤抖。“我叫安娜，我不会伤害你的。”她伸出手去。“跟我来！”

paras.en: The Hulder hesitated a moment, then gripped Anna’s palm. The child’s skin was smooth and dry, like one of the little lizards Anna had read about that populated the Chatho deserts. But even with the Hulder so close to her, it was hard to see them properly. It was almost as though the child had been made of shadow or carved from a mirror. Trying to make out the details was a little like trying to hold tight to a bar of soap: the harder one squeezed, the quicker the soap slid away; the harder one looked, the quicker the Hulder seemed to vanish.
paras.zh: 胡尔德迟疑了片刻，才握住安娜的手掌。孩子的皮肤光滑而干燥，像安娜在书里读到过的那种栖息在查索沙漠里的小蜥蜴。可即便胡尔德离她这样近，还是很难看清。那孩子几乎像是影子捏成的，或是从一面镜子里凿出来的。想看清细节，有点像要攥紧一块肥皂：你攥得越紧，肥皂溜得越快；你盯得越用力，胡尔德似乎消失得越快。

paras.en: Gripping the child with all her strength, Anna called, “Pull us up!”
paras.zh: 安娜用尽全力抓住孩子，喊道：“拉我们上去！”

paras.en: There was a grunt, and then Anna and the Hulder rose to safety, just as the little ledge deteriorated into nothingness. She and the child were dragged back onto solid rock. Before Anna had a chance to release the Hulder, Elsa and Kristoff wrapped Anna into a tight hug, and she leaned into their warmth.
paras.zh: 一声闷哼，安娜和胡尔德便被拉回了安全处——恰在那一瞬，那小块岩架碎成了虚无。她和孩子被拖回了坚实的岩石上。安娜还没来得及松开胡尔德，艾莎和克里斯托夫就紧紧抱住了她，她依偎进他们的温暖里。

paras.en: “Anna,” Elsa said, voice tight. “I couldn’t…I mean, you almost—”
paras.zh: “安娜，”艾莎说，声音发紧。“我没能……我是说，你差点就——”

paras.en: “Key word: almost,” Kristoff cut in with a wink.
paras.zh: “关键词：差点，”克里斯托夫眨着眼插话。

paras.en: Anna smiled at him. He always seemed to understand her, to know that if she thought too much about what had just almost happened, she would sit there forever and turn into a fossil.
paras.zh: 安娜冲他笑了。他似乎总能懂她，知道她若是对刚才那险些发生的事想得太多，就会一直坐在那儿，坐成一块化石。

paras.en: “I’m here,” Anna said. She could have stayed there forever in their arms, but for the wiggling Hulder she held.
paras.zh: “我没事，”安娜说。她本可以永远待在他们怀里，若不是怀里还抱着一个扭来扭去的小胡尔德。

paras.en: The child pushed out of the group and plopped onto the floor—still far enough away that all Anna could really make out was a pointy elbow, but in more detail than before. Now Anna could see that the Hulder’s skin was the exact color of the bluish rock that filled the mines. Anna frowned. When she’d first spotted the Hulder, she’d thought the child’s skin was a smoky white, similar to the crystal the Hulder had been sitting on. A funny, tickling idea crawled into Anna’s mind: she’d been right both times. The Hulder had been smoky white and then a bluish gray. The Hulder’s body had first looked smooth, then as rough as the stone wall. Maybe the Huldrefólk were like octopuses in the deeps of the Southern Sea, able to change not only their color but also their texture.
paras.zh: 孩子从人堆里挣脱出去，一屁股坐到地上——仍离得够远，安娜能看清的不过是一只尖尖的胳膊肘，但已比先前清楚些。这下安娜看出来了：胡尔德的皮肤和矿井里那种泛蓝的石头一模一样。安娜皱起眉。她刚发现这胡尔德时，还以为孩子的皮肤是烟白色的，和胡尔德坐着的那块水晶相似。一个有趣而撩人的念头爬进了安娜的脑海：她两次都没有看错。胡尔德先是烟白色，而后成了蓝灰色。胡尔德的身体起初看着光滑，随后又粗粝得如同石壁。也许胡尔德精灵就像南海深处的大章鱼，不仅能变色，还能改变肌理。

paras.en: “Wow,” Anna said, trying to collect herself even as a stream of rapid thoughts dashed through her mind. First thought: This is so cool! She was thrilled to learn about this wonderful trait of the Huldrefólk. The second thought came fast on the heels of the first: if Anna could change color and texture, she’d head to the portrait gallery, stand in front of all her favorite paintings, and feel what it was like to be Lieutenant Mattias, her father’s old official Arendellian guard, for an afternoon. And finally, her third thought: the last time she’d been in the castle, she’d seen the wolf, and everything had changed. A shudder ran down her spine.
paras.zh: “哇，”安娜说，一边努力定下神来，脑中却已掠过一串飞快的念头。第一个念头：这太酷了！能了解到胡尔德精灵这种奇妙的特质，她兴奋极了。第二个念头紧跟着第一个冒了出来：倘若安娜也能变色变肌理，她就要去画像长廊，站在所有最心爱的画作前，体会一个下午当马提亚斯中尉——父亲那位阿伦黛尔老侍卫——是什么滋味。而最后，第三个念头：她上一次在城堡里，是见到了那只狼，然后一切都变了。一阵寒意顺着她的脊背窜下。

paras.en: Elsa knelt before the child. “Hi there, little one. I’m Elsa. What’s your name?”
paras.zh: 艾莎在小家伙面前跪下。“嗨，小不点。我是艾莎。你叫什么名字？”

paras.en: The little Hulder burst into tears that sparkled like gems.
paras.zh: 小胡尔德突然放声大哭，眼泪像宝石般闪闪发亮。

paras.en: “Oh, no.” Elsa jerked back. “Here!” She conjured a snowflake and presented it.
paras.zh: “噢，不。”艾莎猛地往后一缩。“给！”她变出一片雪花，递了过去。

paras.en: “Elsa,” Anna hissed. “No magic, remember?”
paras.zh: “艾莎，”安娜嘶声道。“不能用魔法，忘了？”

paras.en: The snowflake burst into water droplets. Elsa’s cheeks turned pink and her hands clenched at her sides. “I’m sorry,” she whispered. “I forgot.” It was sad that Elsa had spent most of her life trying to suppress her magic. It truly seemed a part of her, as natural as breathing and blinking. Having to refrain from using it again was probably taking some getting used to.
paras.zh: 雪花啪地炸成一片水珠。艾莎的脸颊泛起红晕，双手在身侧攥紧。“对不起，”她低声说。“我忘了。”艾莎大半生都在竭力压抑自己的魔法，想来真叫人心酸。那魔法分明是她的一部分，自然得如同呼吸和眨眼。如今又要克制着不用，恐怕得慢慢习惯才行。

paras.en: Anna felt sorry about it. She took a deep breath. They had to get out of there. They had to find Revolute and defeat the Nattmara, not only for Arendelle, but for her sister. She couldn’t let Elsa shut herself away again.
paras.zh: 安娜为此替她难过。她深吸了一口气。他们必须离开这里。他们必须找到回旋之刃，打败纳特玛拉——不只是为了阿伦黛尔，也是为了她的姐姐。她不能让艾莎再次把自己封闭起来。

paras.en: “Ow!” Elsa yelped.
paras.zh: “嗷！”艾莎叫出了声。

paras.en: Looking down, Anna saw her sister’s thick braid held tight in a chubby fist.
paras.zh: 安娜低头看去，只见姐姐粗粗的辫子被一只胖拳头攥得紧紧的。

paras.en: “Ow-ow!” the little Hulder repeated, and gave another pull, as if Elsa’s braid were a rope.
paras.zh: “嗷——嗷！”小胡尔德重复着，又扯了一下，仿佛那辫子是根缰绳。

paras.en: “Owowowow!” Elsa unwound her hair from the child’s fists. “I’m not a horse.”
paras.zh: “嗷嗷嗷嗷！”艾莎把头发从孩子的拳头里解了出来。“我不是马。”

paras.en: “Horse!” the little Hulder said. “Horse! Horse! Horse!”
paras.zh: “马！”小胡尔德说。“马！马！马！”

paras.en: Elsa sighed while Anna covered her mouth to hide a giggle. She understood the Hulder’s fascination with Elsa’s braid. When she’d been little, she, too, had pretended Elsa was a racehorse and had ordered her sister to charge up and down the castle hallways. Once, she’d even gotten Elsa to neigh.
paras.zh: 艾莎叹了口气，安娜则捂住嘴，藏起一声咯咯的笑。她懂胡尔德为什么对艾莎的辫子如此着迷。她小时候也曾把艾莎假想成一匹赛马，命令姐姐在城堡的走廊里来回冲刺。有一回，她甚至逗得艾莎嘶叫出声。

paras.en: The little Hulder let go of Elsa’s hair and toddled over to Kristoff. “Horse!” the child proclaimed.
paras.zh: 小胡尔德松开艾莎的头发，摇摇晃晃地走向克里斯托夫。“马！”孩子郑重宣布。

paras.en: “Hey,” Kristoff protested as the Hulder ran around him. “You’re one to talk.”
paras.zh: “嘿，”克里斯托夫抗议道，胡尔德正绕着他跑圈。“你也好意思说我。”

paras.en: “Hey! Hey! Hey!” the little Hulder said. “Talk, talk, talk!” Though the Hulder was running in circles around Kristoff, the child ran sideways, long gallops, keeping their back to the wall at all times.
paras.zh: “嘿！嘿！嘿！”小胡尔德说。“说话，说话，说话！”胡尔德绕着克里斯托夫兜着圈子，却始终侧着身子、迈着大步，背一直贴着墙。

paras.en: To hide the tail! Anna realized with delight. Maybe she would finally be able to find out the answer to her childhood question about whether they all had tails.
paras.zh: 为了藏尾巴！安娜欣喜地醒悟过来。也许她终于能找到童年那个问题的答案了——他们是不是人人都有尾巴。

paras.en: “They’re a bit…hyper?” Elsa tugged her cloak so that it would hang neatly again.
paras.zh: “他们有点……太亢奋了？”艾莎拽了拽斗篷，让它重新垂得整齐。

paras.en: “No more than any other child,” Anna said, thinking of the children she’d often run into in the village. “But most children wouldn’t know how to get around a cave, while this little one might be able to lead us to the older Huldrefólk who can help us.”
paras.zh: “不比别的孩子闹，”安娜说，脑中想起在村里时常撞见的那些孩子。“可大多数孩子不认得怎么在洞穴里穿行，这个小家伙说不定能带我们去找年长的胡尔德精灵帮忙。”

paras.en: Tucking strands of hair back into her braid, Elsa looked doubtful. “Maybe?”
paras.zh: 艾莎把几缕散发塞回辫子里，一脸狐疑。“也许吧？”

paras.en: Taking note of what had happened to Elsa, Anna pushed her own hair back to make sure it wasn’t easily accessible before getting on her hands and knees. “Hi,” she said. “Do you remember my name?”
paras.zh: 吸取了艾莎的教训，安娜也把自己的头发往后拢好，确保不会被轻易抓住，然后手脚并用地趴下身来。“嗨，”她说。“你还记得我的名字吗？”
