paras.en: “Anna! Anna! Anna!” the Hulder screeched.
paras.zh: “安娜！安娜！安娜！”胡尔德尖声叫道。

paras.en: Anna blinked. She hadn’t been expecting quite so much enthusiasm. “Yes, that’s right. What’s your name?”
paras.zh: 安娜眨了眨眼。她可没料到会有这么大的热情。“对，没错。那你叫什么名字？”

paras.en: “What’s your name?” the Hulder repeated.
paras.zh: “你叫什么名字？”胡尔德重复道。

paras.en: “Anna,” Anna said.
paras.zh: “安娜，”安娜说。

paras.en: “Anna,” the Hulder repeated.
paras.zh: “安娜，”胡尔德重复。

paras.en: “Wait.” Anna rubbed her forehead. “Your name is Anna, too?”
paras.zh: “等等。”安娜揉了揉额头。“你也叫安娜？”

paras.en: “Wait.” The Hulder mimicked her again. “Your name is Anna, too!”
paras.zh: “等等。”胡尔德又学了一遍她的话。“你也叫安娜！”

paras.en: “Like I said,” Elsa said, her lips twitching, “hyper.”
paras.zh: “我说什么来着，”艾莎说，嘴角微微抽动，“亢奋。”

paras.en: “I might be wrong,” Kristoff observed, “but I think they’re just repeating everything you say.”
paras.zh: “可能是我看错了，”克里斯托夫说，“但我觉得他们只是把你说的每句话都重复一遍。”

paras.en: “Hyper! Everything you say!” the Hulder echoed back.
paras.zh: “亢奋！你说的每句话！”胡尔德照原样奉还。

paras.en: Taking a deep breath, Anna spoke as quickly as she could, giving the Hulder no chance to repeat her words until she was done. “Hi, I’m Anna! My home is Arendelle, like you, but above the ground.”
paras.zh: 安娜深吸一口气，用最快的语速说话，不给胡尔德留下任何重复的机会，直到把话说完。“嗨，我是安娜！我的家在阿伦黛尔，和你一样，只不过在地面之上。”

paras.en: The Hulder looked at her in complete astonishment. “Home?”
paras.zh: 胡尔德难以置信地望着她。“家？”

paras.en: Anna nodded. “Yes, home. Where do you live? We’d like to meet your family.”
paras.zh: 安娜点点头。“对，家。你们住在哪儿？我们想见见你的家人。”

paras.en: The Hulder looked at Anna, then nodded. “Home!” And then the Hulder was off—running backward as easily as if they had eyes in the back of their head. And maybe they did. After all, as Anna knew from old bedtime stories, no one had ever seen a Hulder’s back.
paras.zh: 胡尔德看看安娜，然后点了点头。“家！”话音未落，胡尔德已经跑了起来——倒退着跑，轻松得仿佛后脑勺上也长着眼睛。也许真长着呢。毕竟，安娜从古老的睡前故事里知道，从没有人见过胡尔德的背影。

paras.en: “Come on!” Anna shot to her feet. “We have to follow!”
paras.zh: “快！”安娜一跃而起。“我们得跟上！”

paras.en: The Hulder ran impossibly fast—and unlike Anna and the others, the Hulder was short enough to avoid low-hanging rocks, while Kristoff had to run at a crouch. Up, down, and down again, they sprinted through seemingly endless corridors of crystals and sparkling rocks. Anna couldn’t understand how the Hulder—Dash, as she mentally nicknamed them, taking a page from Olaf’s book—was able to tell the difference between the tunnels. Maybe it was some special Huldrefólk trick. After all, Huldrefólk could always find lost things. Maybe it meant they could never become lost themselves.
paras.zh: 胡尔德跑得快得不可思议——而且与安娜他们不同，胡尔德个子矮小，足以避开低垂的岩石，克里斯托夫却只能弓着身子跑。上坡、下坡、再向下，他们冲过一条条似乎没有尽头的、缀满水晶与闪石的长廊。安娜想不明白，这胡尔德——她心里照着雪宝的做派给它起了个诨名叫“飞毛腿”——是怎么分辨得出这些隧道的。也许那是胡尔德精灵的某种独门本事。毕竟，胡尔德精灵总能找到失落之物。也许这意味着，他们自己永远不会迷路。

paras.en: A strange thought crossed her mind, and she wondered if that meant the Huldrefólk always knew what they should do next. How fantastic would that be? Maybe that’s how Dash had found them so quickly. Or maybe Dash had found them because Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff were the lost things.
paras.zh: 一个古怪的念头掠过她心头，她暗自琢磨，这是否意味着胡尔德精灵永远知道自己下一步该做什么。那该有多妙？也许飞毛腿就是这样才这么快找到他们的。又或者，飞毛腿找到他们，正是因为安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫本身就是“失物”。

paras.en: Anna shook her head. She had so many questions, and there was so little time to attend to them all.
paras.zh: 安娜摇了摇头。她心里装着太多疑问，却几乎没有工夫一一去想。

paras.en: But there was one thing she could do. “Kristoff? Elsa?” Anna waited until they both looked at her, and then said, “I think I know what happened to the missing trolls. I read in Sorenson’s tower that they always flee the land when a Nattmara appears.”
paras.zh: 但有一件事她做得到。“克里斯托夫？艾莎？”安娜等到两人都望向她，才开口：“我想我知道失踪的岩精是怎么回事了。我在索伦森的高塔里读到过，纳特玛拉一出现，他们就会逃离这片土地。”

paras.en: Anna heard Kristoff let out a great sigh of relief. “Good,” he said. “Then that means they’re safe.”
paras.zh: 安娜听见克里斯托夫长长地舒了一口气。“太好了，”他说。“那就说明他们是安全的。”

paras.en: Soon enough, another sound began to play under the staccato of their footsteps. A strange, shuffling, creaking sound.
paras.zh: 不多时，在急促的脚步声之下，又浮现出另一种声响。一种奇怪的、拖沓的、吱呀作响的声音。

paras.en: “Do you hear that?” Anna called back between breaths.
paras.zh: “你们听见了吗？”安娜在喘息的间隙回头喊道。

paras.en: “Yeah,” Kristoff said. “Do you think—?”
paras.zh: “听见了，”克里斯托夫说。“你觉得是不是——？”

paras.en: “Maybe,” Anna replied, slowing to a walk. She didn’t need him to finish his sentence to know what he was thinking: Nattmara.
paras.zh: “也许吧，”安娜答道，放缓脚步改成了走。她不必等他说完就知道他在想什么：纳特玛拉。

paras.en: “We should stop,” Elsa said. “Take a moment to scout out what’s happening. Huldrefólk can be mischievous…especially if they think we’re here to take something that doesn’t belong to us.”
paras.zh: “我们该停下，”艾莎说。“花点工夫侦察一下情况。胡尔德精灵可能很爱恶作剧……尤其是当他们以为我们是来夺取不属于自己的东西时。”

paras.en: “But if we stop,” Anna said, “we’ll lose Dash!”
paras.zh: “可我们要是一停，”安娜说，“就跟丢飞毛腿了！”

paras.en: The corners of Elsa’s eyes crinkled in confusion as she navigated around a large boulder that Anna had simply scrambled over. “Dash?” she asked.
paras.zh: 艾莎绕过一块大圆石——那石头安娜方才可是手脚并用爬过去的——眼角困惑地皱起。“飞毛腿？”她问。

paras.en: “The Hulder,” Anna explained. She turned back to see if Kristoff needed any help with the boulder, but he’d simply shoved it to the side, clearing the way.
paras.zh: “就是那胡尔德，”安娜解释道。她回头想看看克里斯托夫搬石头要不要帮忙，可他早已把石头推到一旁，清出了路。

paras.en: “It’s too late,” he said. “We already lost them.”
paras.zh: “太迟了，”他说。“我们已经跟丢了。”

paras.en: In the two seconds Anna had taken her eyes off Dash, the child had sped out of sight. “No,” Anna breathed. “We have to keep up!” She broke into a run again, fresh fear giving her newfound speed. “Dash doesn’t know about the Nattmara!”
paras.zh: 就在安娜移开视线的那两秒里，孩子已经飞快地没了踪影。“不，”安娜低声道。“我们得跟上！”她重新拔腿狂奔，新生的恐惧给了她新添的速度。“飞毛腿还不知道纳特玛拉的事！”

paras.en: But as Anna rounded the final bend, she saw where the sound had been coming from: an underground city carved out of the rock itself.
paras.zh: 可当安娜转过最后一个弯，她看到了那声响的来处：一座从岩体中凿出的地下之城。

paras.en: The secret home of the Huldrefólk.
paras.zh: 胡尔德精灵的秘密家园。

paras.en: Just as the world above, so was the world below. Cozy homes were carved into the blue-gray stone, and orange light spilled out from them, as welcoming as a smile. The pebble-lined streets were alight with glowworms, so it was easy to see what various mine carts pulled: one held a pile of stalactites bundled like firewood, another was filled to the brim with glowing mushrooms the size of sun hats, and another was heaped with water-clear rocks that Anna thought might be large diamonds.
paras.zh: 地上世界如何，地下世界也如何。温馨的屋舍凿在蓝灰色的石头里，橙色的光从屋中漫溢出来，亲切得如同一个微笑。铺满卵石的街道被萤虫照得透亮，各辆矿车拉着什么一览无余：一辆上堆着像柴火般捆扎好的钟乳石，一辆满得冒尖地装着太阳帽大小的发光蘑菇，还有一辆堆着水一般清透的石头，安娜猜想那或许是巨大的钻石。

paras.en: And the Huldrefólk. The adults appeared to be tall, built more like sapling trees than people, with long limbs and long necks. And similar to Dash, they were hard to see in the light of the underneath realm.
paras.zh: 还有胡尔德精灵。成年精灵显得很高，身形与其说像人，不如说更像一棵棵幼树，四肢修长，脖颈颀长。和飞毛腿一样，他们在地下王国的光线下也很难看清。

paras.en: The glow-light wasn’t the same as sunlight, bright and revealing, but the kind of soft glow that Anna associated with romantic candlelit dinners. It illuminated at the same time as it concealed, casting shadows that again helped to obscure the Huldrefólk. Still, even in the dimness, Anna could tell that they camouflaged into whatever it was that they were standing near, from onyx black to marble white and every shade in between. Some of the Huldrefólk looked as though they could be purple, others orange and green with sparkling, black-veined skin. The Huldrefólk—the hidden folk—could blend into any surrounding.
paras.zh: 那幽光不同于明亮而无所遁形的日光，而是那种让安娜联想到浪漫烛光晚餐的柔光。它既照亮，又遮掩，投下的阴影再度帮着藏起了胡尔德精灵。即便在昏暗之中，安娜仍看得出，他们能融入身边任何东西的颜色，从乌黑到云石白，中间的每一种色调皆有。有些胡尔德精灵看上去似是紫色，有些则是橙绿相间，皮肤上闪着黑色的脉络。胡尔德精灵——隐世之民——能融入任何周遭。

paras.en: Which was great, Anna thought, but most important, they were real. Real creatures who would have real answers to where they could find the real lost sword of Aren. The thing of myth they needed to save the day.
paras.zh: 这固然了不起，安娜想，但最重要的是，他们真实存在。真实的生灵，才会给出真实的答案，告诉他们去何处寻找阿伦那把真正失落的神剑。那件他们赖以拯救一切的神话之物。

paras.en: “Wow,” Elsa whispered. “How beautiful. And peaceful.”
paras.zh: “哇，”艾莎低声说。“真美。真安宁。”

paras.en: “If Sven were here,” Kristoff said, “I bet he’d eat all those mushrooms, and then his teeth would probably glow for a week.”
paras.zh: “要是斯文在这儿，”克里斯托夫说，“我打赌他会把那些蘑菇吃个精光，然后他的牙大概得发光上一个礼拜。”

paras.en: Sven. Anna wished the reindeer were with them. The way down to the village looked steep, and Sven was always good about finding the surest path down a craggy mountain. She scanned the side of the rock, looking for a pathway to the dwellings. Somewhere below, she was sure they would find the answers to how to set things right and heal Sven, and the rest of Arendelle, from the Nattmara’s influence.
paras.zh: 斯文。安娜多希望驯鹿此刻与他们同在。下到村庄的路看起来很陡，而斯文向来最擅长在嶙峋的山上找到最稳妥的下山之路。她打量着岩壁，寻找通往那些屋舍的路径。她确信，就在下方某处，他们能找到拨乱反正的办法，治愈斯文以及阿伦黛尔其余地方，解除纳特玛拉的蛊惑。

paras.en: As she leaned forward to see better, Anna felt a sharp something prod her back.
paras.zh: 就在她往前探身想看得更清楚些时，安娜忽然感到背后被什么尖利的东西戳了一下。

paras.en: “Kristoff,” she said, swiping a hand behind her, “stop that. I’m just trying to see.”
paras.zh: “克里斯托夫，”她说道，反手向后一挥，“别闹了。我只是想看看。”

paras.en: “I’m not doing anything,” Kristoff said, standing to her left, a few feet away from easy poking distance.
paras.zh: “我什么都没做，”克里斯托夫说。他站在她左侧几英尺开外，远在够得着戳人的距离之外。

paras.en: The back of Anna’s neck prickled.
paras.zh: 安娜的后颈一阵发麻。

paras.en: Elsa stood to her right, her face pensive as she took in the city below them.
paras.zh: 艾莎站在她右侧，凝望着下方的城池，神色沉郁。

paras.en: Suddenly, Anna became very aware of the feeling that someone was watching her.
paras.zh: 忽然间，安娜无比清晰地感觉到，有人在注视着她。

paras.en: Maybe even a few someones.
paras.zh: 也许还不止一个人。

paras.en: “Oh,” she heard Elsa squeak.
paras.zh: “噢。”她听见艾莎轻轻叫了一声。

paras.en: Anna turned, only to come nose-to-nose with a spear. And not just one spear.
paras.zh: 安娜转过身，正撞上一支长矛，鼻尖离矛尖只有毫厘。而且不止一支长矛。

paras.en: Many spears.
paras.zh: 许多支长矛。

paras.en: WHILE ANNA, ELSA, AND KRISTOFF had been taking in the sights of the village below, it seemed as though a storm cloud had gathered around them.
paras.zh: 当安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫还在欣赏脚下村庄的景色时，仿佛一片暴风云在他们四周悄然聚集。

paras.en: Though, of course, storm clouds didn’t exist in the belly of the mines, nor were they capable of holding a spear to one’s throat.
paras.zh: 当然，矿井深处并不存在暴风云，暴风云也不可能把长矛抵在人的喉咙上。

paras.en: No.
paras.zh: 不。

paras.en: The roiling, shifting dark shapes gathering around them were none other than Huldrefólk warriors.
paras.zh: 在他们周围翻涌、游移的那些黑影，不是别的，正是岩精战士。

paras.en: Like the littler Dash, these ones, too, stuck to the shadows.
paras.zh: 和个头较小的达什一样，这些岩精也紧贴着阴影。

paras.en: In the glow, Anna could only make out the glint of an eye here, and the back of a hand there.
paras.zh: 在微光中，安娜只能勉强看清这里一只眼睛的反光，那里一只手背的轮廓。

paras.en: But she didn’t need to be able to see their faces to sense how they felt about three human trespassers in their secret city: they were not very happy at all. “H-h-hi,” Anna stuttered to the spear tips, trying to remember the etiquette of meeting a new group of people.
paras.zh: 不过，她不需要看清他们的脸，也能感受到这三位闯入他们秘密城市的人类惹来了怎样的情绪：他们一点也高兴不起来。“你、你、你们好，”安娜对着一根根矛尖结结巴巴地说，努力回想着结识一群新朋友时的礼节。

paras.en: It wasn’t the exact same as meeting the prime minister of Torres, but she knew that dignitaries were sensitive, so polite manners seemed the safest bet.
paras.zh: 这和会见托雷斯首相不太一样，但她知道达官贵人们都很敏感，所以礼貌相待似乎最稳妥。

paras.en: Step one: Introduce yourself, and announce you are a friend.
paras.zh: 第一步：自我介绍，并表明自己是朋友。

paras.en: She dipped into a curtsy. “My name is Anna of Arendelle, and this is my sis—” A spearpoint jabbed closer to her, and Anna went silent. “Stop,” a Hulder hissed. “Say no more, thief.” “I-I think there’s been a mistake,” Anna said, forcing a cheerful smile on her face. “We’ve come to ask for help.
paras.zh: 她行了个屈膝礼。“我是阿伦黛尔的安娜，这位是我的姐——”一支矛尖逼近她的脸，安娜顿时闭了嘴。“住口，”一名岩精嘶声道，“别再说了，小偷。”“我、我想是出了什么误会，”安娜勉强挤出一丝欢快的笑容说，“我们是来请求帮助的。

paras.en: We’re not here to take anything—” “Take,” the same Hulder spoke again, repeating Anna. “Take, take, take!” “No,” Kristoff said, his back against Anna’s. “We’re not here to take anything.
paras.zh: 我们不是来拿任何东西的——”“拿，”那名岩精又开口，重复着安娜的话，“拿，拿，拿！”“不，”克里斯托夫背靠着安娜说，“我们不是来拿任何东西的。

paras.en: We followed a little one—” “Take little one,” the Hulder repeated, and Anna could hear fury swell in the Hulder’s voice. “Take little one!” The cry was repeated by another Hulder, and then another, until the entire shifting mass of spear-wielding warriors took up the chant.
paras.zh: 我们只是跟着一个小家伙——”“掳走小家伙，”岩精重复道，安娜听得出他声音里的怒火在升腾。“掳走小家伙！”另一名岩精跟着喊，接着又一名，直到整片持矛游移的战士都齐声念起了这句咒语般的口号。

paras.en: Anna had a bad feeling.
paras.zh: 安娜有一种不祥的预感。

paras.en: A very bad feeling. “I think that they’re accusing us of trying to steal Dash,” she whispered. “Ah,” Kristoff said in a low voice, “well, that’s not accurate.” “Wait!” Anna told the Huldrefólk, holding up her hand. “We weren’t trying to kidnap anyone!” The Huldrefólk’s chant changed. “Liar, liar, every word!” Anna shook her head, trying to make sense of them. “We’re not,” Elsa spoke up, her voice smooth as ice, though Anna could hear the friction beneath the surface. “The little one found us.
paras.zh: 一种非常糟糕的预感。“我觉得他们在控诉我们想偷走达什，”她低声说。“啊，”克里斯托夫压低声音说，“嗯，这可不对。”“等等！”安娜举起手对岩精们说，“我们根本没想绑架谁！”岩精们的口号变了。“骗子，骗子，句句谎言！”安娜摇着头，想弄明白他们的意思。“我们不是，”艾莎开口了，声音如冰般平滑，但安娜听得出表面之下的摩擦。“是小家伙自己找到我们的。

paras.en: We were singing, and then my sister rescued the child from falling into a dark abyss—” “The abyss!” another Hulder with a higher voice interrupted. “The abyss!
paras.zh: 我们当时在唱歌，然后我妹妹把孩子从坠入黑暗深渊的危险中救了回来——”“深渊！”另一名声音更尖的岩精打断道，“深渊！

paras.en: Take to abyss!
paras.zh: 扔进深渊！

paras.en: Take to abyss!
paras.zh: 扔进深渊！

paras.en: Liar, liar, every word!” Uh-oh. “Um,” Anna said with a gulp. “I think they want to—” “Drop us off in the abyss?” Kristoff finished. “Yeah.
paras.zh: 句句谎言！”糟了。“呃，”安娜咽了口唾沫说，“我想他们是想——”“把我们丢进深渊？”克里斯托夫接了下去，“没错。

paras.en: I got that, too.” “Wait!” Anna tried again. “There’s a giant wolf out there that’ll be here before you know—” Anna’s sentence was cut short as a warrior rushed forward and tied what felt like a handkerchief around Anna’s mouth, making it impossible for her to shout.
paras.zh: 我也听出来了。”“等等！”安娜又试了一次，“外面有只巨狼，迟早会到这儿——”一名战士冲上前，用一块像是手帕的东西勒住安娜的嘴，让她没法喊叫，她的话戛然而止。

paras.en: But even if she could, would it help?
paras.zh: 可就算她能喊，又有用吗？

paras.en: They were so far underground, and the villagers who were still awake were far away, likely and hopefully already onboard Elsa’s royal ship.
paras.zh: 他们身处地下那么深，而还醒着的村民离得很远，多半——也希望——已经上了艾莎的皇家船只。

paras.en: Sorenson was gone, having been left to face the Nattmara.
paras.zh: 索伦森不见了，他被留下来独自面对纳特玛拉。

paras.en: And next to her, Elsa and Kristoff were also being gagged.
paras.zh: 而在她身旁，艾莎和克里斯托夫也都被堵住了嘴。

paras.en: Hard roots pressed into the soft skin of Anna’s wrists as her hands were pulled behind her back and bound.
paras.zh: 粗糙的树根勒进安娜手腕柔软的皮肤，她的双手被反剪到背后绑了起来。

paras.en: After checking to make sure the knot was tight, the Hulder who had bound her nodded. “March.” Single file, they walked in front of the Huldrefólk.
paras.zh: 绑住她的那名岩精确认绳结够紧后，点了点头。“走。”他们排成一列，走在岩精们的前面。

paras.en: Anna kept her eye on Elsa’s braid as it swung, and was grateful when Kristoff accidentally stepped on her heel.
paras.zh: 安娜一直盯着艾莎随步伐晃动的辫子，当克里斯托夫不小心踩到她的脚后跟时，她反而感到一丝安慰。

paras.en: It made her feel better knowing they were both there.
paras.zh: 知道他们俩都在身边，让她安心了些。

paras.en: At least they were all in this mess together.
paras.zh: 至少他们是一同陷进这团乱麻里的。

paras.en: Anna thought the Huldrefólk would take them away from their hidden city, back to the abyss from which they’d saved Dash, but instead, the warriors marched them down a narrow path, away from the abyss and the swarm of glowworms and fluorescent gardens.
paras.zh: 安娜以为岩精们会把他们带离秘密城市，回到他们救下达什的那个深渊去，可战士们却押着他们走上一条狭窄的小径，远离了深渊，也远离了成群的发光虫和荧光花园。

paras.en: Anna’s bad feeling only grew more insistent the longer they walked away from the city.
paras.zh: 离城市越远，安娜那不祥的预感就越发强烈。

paras.en: Sweat beaded on her forehead, and her ribcage felt too tight as she breathed in the stale and stuffy air.
paras.zh: 汗珠在她额头沁出，吸入沉闷混浊的空气时，她的胸腔闷得发紧。

paras.en: How far underground were they?
paras.zh: 他们究竟在地下多深的地方？

paras.en: Then the smell of rotten eggs punched her nose, and her eyes watered.
paras.zh: 接着，一股臭鸡蛋味猛地冲进她的鼻子，熏得她眼泪都出来了。

paras.en: It was the smell of sulfur, or else the Huldrefólk had some major issues with their plumbing.
paras.zh: 那是硫磺的味道，否则就是岩精们的管道出了大问题。

paras.en: The air grew hotter still until it almost seemed to take on a rosy glow.
paras.zh: 空气越来越热，几乎仿佛泛起了一层玫瑰色的微光。

paras.en: A red light danced along the walls ahead of them, an unusual color that typically could only be found in the most spectacular summer sunsets, or in Tuva and Ada’s forge, or…no.
paras.zh: 前方墙壁上跃动着红光，那是一种罕见的颜色，通常只出现在最壮丽的夏日落霞里，或是图娃和艾达的铁匠铺中，又或者……不。

paras.en: Anna’s heart flipped.
paras.zh: 安娜的心猛地一沉。

paras.en: Or in the center of an active volcano.
paras.zh: 或者是正喷发的火山中心。

paras.en: Liar, liar, every word plus abyss apparently equaled throwing the group of human trespassers from Arendelle into molten rock.
paras.zh: 骗子、骗子、句句谎言，再加上深渊——看来这等于要把这群来自阿伦黛尔的人类闯入者扔进熔岩里。

paras.en: The red glow grew brighter, and while the Huldrefólk seemed as cool as ice cream in the middle of an eternal winter, sweat now drenched Anna.
paras.zh: 红光越来越亮，岩精们仿佛置身于永冬中的冰淇淋般镇定自若，可安娜此刻已被汗水浸透。

paras.en: She imagined that if it got any hotter, her eyebrows would slide right off her face.
paras.zh: 她心想，要是再热下去，自己的眉毛恐怕都要从脸上滑落了。

paras.en: Even if Elsa could use her magic here—even if it wouldn’t draw the Nattmara straight to them—what chance did winter’s cold have against the melting powers of red-hot magma?
paras.zh: 就算艾莎能在这里用魔法——就算那不会把纳特玛拉直接引到他们身边——寒冬的冰冷又怎么敌得过炽热岩浆的融化之力？

paras.en: Now it was in front of them, a round circle of red that pulsed like a beating heart.
paras.zh: 此刻它就在他们眼前，一团红色的圆圈如心跳般搏动着。

paras.en: Anna stumbled to a stop, but the Huldrefólk shoved her forward, and though she could not believe it was possible, she grew even hotter. “Stop,” Anna garbled through her gag, her mind racing as she skipped over steps two through ten of diplomacy. “We’ll give you chocolate!” The words came out muffled.
paras.zh: 安娜踉跄着停下，岩精却把她往前推，而尽管她难以置信，她却觉得更热了。“住手，”安娜透过塞嘴的东西含糊地喊，脑子里飞快转着，直接跳过了外交步骤里的第二到第十步。“我们给你们巧克力！”这话听来闷闷的。

paras.en: It wasn’t actually a step of etiquette—truly, bribery didn’t belong on the list at all—and nothing in all her reading had prepared Anna for the possibility of being thrown into a river of lava by a hosting nation.
paras.zh: 这其实并不算什么礼节——说真的，贿赂根本不该列在清单上——她读过的书里，没有半本能让她料到会被东道主扔进熔岩河里。

paras.en: But it didn’t work.
paras.zh: 但这并不管用。

paras.en: They pushed her forward.
paras.zh: 他们把她往前推。

paras.en: Even though it was hotter than Oaken’s sauna, Anna went numb as she saw Elsa’s boot hang over the edge, the toe turning red in the glow.
paras.zh: 尽管这里比奥肯的桑拿房还热，可当安娜看见艾莎的靴子悬在边缘、靴尖在红光中泛红时，她却一阵麻木。

paras.en: Anna struggled harder.
paras.zh: 安娜挣扎得更猛烈了。

paras.en: If they disappeared on their mission, no one would ever know how the Nattmara came to be or how it could be stopped.
paras.zh: 如果他们就此消失在任务途中，就再没人会知道纳特玛拉是如何诞生的，又该如何阻止它。

paras.en: No one would survive it.
paras.zh: 没人能活着熬过去。

paras.en: Being thrown into lava wouldn’t just mean the end of Kristoff, Elsa, and Anna—it would mean the end of Arendelle.
paras.zh: 被扔进熔岩不只意味着克里斯托夫、艾莎和安娜的终结——那意味着阿伦黛尔的终结。

paras.en: They would have failed.
paras.zh: 他们就失败了。

paras.en: She would have failed.
paras.zh: 她就失败了。

paras.en: Emptiness yawned in Anna, threatening to swallow her whole.
paras.zh: 安娜心中豁开一片空洞，仿佛要将她整个人吞没。

paras.en: All she had wanted— ever wanted—was to always do more and, out of true love for her sister, help her.
paras.zh: 她所想要的——一直想要的——不过是多做些事，出于对妹妹真挚的爱，去帮她。

paras.en: Although the whole kingdom had seen Anna save her sister three years ago, she had since wondered who wouldn’t save their sister.
paras.zh: 尽管三年前全王国都见证了安娜救下妹妹，可自那以后，她常常想，换作谁又不会去救自己的妹妹呢。

paras.en: And still, Anna couldn’t get past that she was the one who had provoked Elsa into casting an eternal winter then, and now she was the one who had called a Nattmara to the land.
paras.zh: 然而安娜始终无法释怀：当年是她激得艾莎降下永冬，如今又是她把纳特玛拉召唤到了这片土地上。

paras.en: She would never feed Sven a carrot again.
paras.zh: 她再也不能给斯文喂胡萝卜了。

paras.en: She would never hear more about Olaf’s warm philosophy on life.
paras.zh: 她再也听不到雪宝那些温暖的人生哲理了。

paras.en: She would never get a chance to learn about the natural and celestial worlds from Sorenson.
paras.zh: 她再也没机会从索伦森那儿了解自然与星空的世界了。

paras.en: And it was all her fault.
paras.zh: 而这一切都是她的错。

paras.en: From the corner of her eye, she saw Elsa whip her head so fast that her braid slapped her Hulder captor’s nose, taking them by surprise, while Kristoff flung himself backward, slamming his captor into the wall.
paras.zh: 眼角余光里，她看见艾莎猛地一甩头，辫子抽中了岩精俘获者的鼻子，打了他们一个措手不及；与此同时克里斯托夫向后一仰，把抓他的岩精狠狠撞在墙上。

paras.en: The two managed to wrestle out of their binds in the process.
paras.zh: 两人趁势挣脱了捆绑。

paras.en: Come on!
paras.zh: 加油！

paras.en: Anna told herself.
paras.zh: 安娜对自己说。

paras.en: They’re still fighting.
paras.zh: 他们还在反抗。

paras.en: You can, too!
paras.zh: 你也可以！

paras.en: She wanted to cheer them on, but she needed to save her breath.
paras.zh: 她想为他们呐喊助威，可她得省着点力气。

paras.en: And besides, there was still a gag in her mouth.
paras.zh: 更何况，她嘴里还塞着东西。

paras.en: Her guard dragged her forward, closer to the edge of the molten lake, while Anna freed her hands. “HALT!” A deep voice reverberated around the rock, sending tremors through the earth.
paras.zh: 押着她的岩精拖着她前行，离熔岩湖的边缘更近了，安娜却趁机松开了自己的手。“止步！”一个低沉的声音在岩石间回荡，震得大地都颤了起来。

paras.en: But there was no way Anna was going to stop fighting.
paras.zh: 但安娜绝不肯就此停下反抗。

paras.en: She lunged to the side, free of the Hulder’s stony grip, and tore off her gag.
paras.zh: 她朝一侧猛冲，挣脱了岩精石头般的手，扯下了嘴里的塞布。

paras.en: She took a few running steps away from them before realizing she wasn’t being chased.
paras.zh: 她跑开几步，才发现自己并没有被追赶。

paras.en: Instead, the Huldrefólk knelt to the ground as a fourth Hulder appeared in the red haze.
paras.zh: 相反，岩精们纷纷跪倒在地，一名第四位岩精在红色雾霭中现身。

paras.en: This Hulder seemed to be the tallest of them all, their hair a wild black mane surrounding their face, and on their head they wore a circlet of something shiny.
paras.zh: 这名岩精似乎是他们中最高的，乱蓬蓬的黑发如鬃毛般围住面孔，头上戴着一圈闪亮的东西。

paras.en: It took Anna a minute to realize it was gold.
paras.zh: 安娜过了一会儿才反应过来，那是黄金。

paras.en: The leader of the Huldrefólk.
paras.zh: 岩精的首领。

paras.en: And on the Hulder leader’s shoulders sat a small, familiar figure. “Horse!” Dash yanked on the Hulder leader’s hair.
paras.zh: 而岩精首领的肩膀上，坐着一个小小又熟悉的身影。“马！”达什扯着岩精首领的头发。

paras.en: Anna sank into a curtsy, and after she coughed pointedly in Kristoff’s direction, he bowed.
paras.zh: 安娜行了个屈膝礼，又故意朝克里斯托夫的方向咳了一声，于是他也鞠了躬。

paras.en: Elsa, however, stayed as upright as an icicle, befitting her rank. “Psst!
paras.zh: 然而艾莎却像冰柱般笔直挺立，与她的身份相称。“嘘！

paras.en: Rule number one,” Anna murmured loud enough so that Elsa could hear.
paras.zh: 第一条规矩，”安娜低语道，声音刚好能让艾莎听见。

paras.en: Elsa nodded and spoke. “Greetings.
paras.zh: 艾莎点点头，开口道：“问候各位。

paras.en: I am Queen Elsa of Arendelle, and this is my sister, Princess Anna, and her…er, our guard, Kristoff Bjorgman of Nowhere in Particular.
paras.zh: 我是阿伦黛尔的艾莎女王，这位是我的妹妹安娜公主，以及她的……呃，我们的护卫，来自无名之地的克里斯托夫·比约格曼。

paras.en: We greet you in friendship.” Anna held her breath, wondering if the leader would accept. “Friendship,” the Hulder leader repeated.
paras.zh: 我们以友人的身份向你们致意。”安娜屏住呼吸，不知首领会不会接受。“友谊，”岩精首领重复道。

paras.en: And then, to Anna’s utter astonishment, the Hulder continued in full sentences. “I apologize for my family.
paras.zh: 接着，令安娜万分惊讶的是，那名岩精竟用完整的句子继续说了下去。“我为我的族人格外抱歉。

paras.en: They can be a bit overprotective.” In the dim light, Anna saw the Hulder pat Dash’s dangling knee. “Young Echo, however, has cleared up the misunderstanding, and she and I welcome you to our domain.
paras.zh: 他们有时候是有点过度保护。”昏暗的光里，安娜看见那名岩精拍了拍达什悬着的膝盖。“不过，小埃科已经解开了误会，她和我都欢迎你们来到我们的领地。

paras.en: I am the king of the Huldrefólk.” “You’re not repeating everything,” Elsa said, clearly too surprised to worry about manners.
paras.zh: 我是岩精之王。”“你并没有句句重复，”艾莎说，显然惊讶得顾不上礼节了。

paras.en: The imposing Hulder king inclined his head. “We like to use other people’s words so that we can wrap ourselves up and hide within them.
paras.zh: 威严的岩精之王微微颔首。“我们喜欢借用别人的话，好把自己包裹起来，藏身其中。

paras.en: It’s very rare for Huldrefólk to actually have to compose something new.
paras.zh: 岩精真正需要自己构思新话的时候，少之又少。

paras.en: That’s part of the reason why Echo found you—she wanted to collect your song.
paras.zh: 这也正是埃科找到你们的部分原因——她想收集你们的歌。

paras.en: Songs are easy to remember.
paras.zh: 歌声最容易记住。

paras.en: Easy to echo back.” “Echo!” Dash—now Echo, Anna realized—repeated the word from her perch.
paras.zh: 也容易回响。”“回声！”达什——现在安娜意识到她叫埃科了——在首领肩头重复着这个词。

paras.en: Anna knew she should probably let Elsa do all the talking, but her curiosity was too much. “Why do you talk in your own words?” she asked. “Because I am not only the king, but also the librarian,” said the Hulder leader. “I’ve spent years visiting the world above, collecting items as well as stories, and I have enough words at my disposal.
paras.zh: 安娜知道自己本该让艾莎全权交谈，可她的好奇心太强了。“你为什么用你自己的话说话？”她问。“因为我不只是国王，还是图书管理员，”岩精首领说，“我花了多年游历地面世界，收集物品也收集故事，手头的词足够用了。

paras.en: And so, I would like to apologize again for your initial greeting.” The Librarian King reached for Echo and set the child on the ground. “That’s it?” Kristoff burst out. “We’re almost thrown into a lake of lava, and all you can say is ‘I’m sorry’?” “I’m sorry!” Echo squealed, moving toward Kristoff. “Does ‘We’re very sorry’ make it any better?” the Librarian King asked. “Usually, the only humans who make it down this far want to take precious stones and gems from our mountain, or to capture a member of our domain to make them find iron ore deposits for their weapons and the like.” “We’re not looking for stones, gems, or iron,” Elsa said. “We’re looking for a sword of myth, the Revolute Blade.
paras.zh: 所以，我想再次为你们起初受到的招待道歉。”图书管理员国王伸手把埃科抱下，放到地上。“就这样？”克里斯托夫脱口而出，“我们差点被扔进熔岩湖，你所能说的就只有‘对不起’？”“对不起嘛！”埃科尖声叫着，朝克里斯托夫走去。“那‘我们非常抱歉’会不会好一点？”图书管理员国王问，“通常，能下到这么深的人类，要么是想从我们的山里拿走宝石珍矿，要么就是想抓我们领地的人去替他们找铁矿，好打造兵器之类。”“我们不是来找石头、宝石或铁的，”艾莎说，“我们找的是一把神话中的剑，回旋之刃。

paras.en: Can you please help us find it?” The Librarian King’s eyes flashed. “‘Revolving moon and spinning sun, forged a crescent blade.
paras.zh: 你能帮我们找到它吗？”图书管理员国王眼中精光一闪。“‘旋转的明月，飞转的烈日，铸成弯月之刃。

paras.en: From light and dark within the heart, the burnished sword was made.’” He looked down at them. “That’s the one, yes?” Anna nodded, feeling this was a good sign. “And,” he continued, “I suppose this has something to do with the Nattmara that has come to Arendelle?” Anna gaped. “How did you know about the Nattmara?” “Just because you can’t see us doesn’t mean we’re not always there.” The Librarian King studied them a second more.
paras.zh: 由心中光与暗，铸成这把亮剑。’”他低头看着他们。“就是它，对吗？”安娜点头，觉得这是个好兆头。“而且，”他继续道，“我想这和我们阿伦黛尔来的纳特玛拉脱不了干系吧？”安娜张大了嘴。“你怎么知道纳特玛拉的事？”“你们看不见我们，不代表我们就不在那儿。”图书管理员国王又打量了他们片刻。

paras.en: It was impossible to make out any expression on the leader’s face.
paras.zh: 根本无从辨认首领脸上的表情。

paras.en: The Hulder’s textured skin had taken on the appearance of the cracked rivulets of lava, and was hard to see against the molten backdrop.
paras.zh: 那岩精布满纹理的皮肤已变得如同熔岩龟裂的纹路，在熔岩背景映衬下几乎看不分明。

paras.en: But then, he must have made a secret signal, because the guards bowed before each of them and then hurried away, keeping their backs to Anna and her friends.
paras.zh: 但接着，他一定发出了某种暗号，因为那些卫兵在他们每人面前鞠了一躬，便匆匆退下，背对着安娜和她的朋友们。

paras.en: It only took the hidden people a couple of steps until they seemed to have disappeared entirely, though Anna knew they must still be there, great masters of camouflage that they were.
paras.zh: 这些隐身之人只走了几步，仿佛就彻底消失了，尽管安娜知道他们一定还在那儿——毕竟他们是伪装的大师。

paras.en: The Librarian King turned. “Now, all of you, come with me.” Anna’s heart leapt.
paras.zh: 图书管理员国王转过身。“现在，你们都跟我来。”安娜心头一喜。

paras.en: At last—she had not led them astray! “We don’t always know the answer—but we do know where to find it,” the Librarian King continued.
paras.zh: 终于——她没有把他们带错路！“我们并不总是知道答案——但我们知道去哪里找答案，”图书管理员国王继续说。

paras.en: Allowing the humans to walk in front of them, the Librarian King and Echo escorted Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff away from the lake of molten rock and toward a tranquil tributary of water where rafts bumped and prodded against each other.
paras.zh: 图书管理员国王和埃科让人类走在前头，护送安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫离开熔岩湖，走向一条平静的水渠，那里一只只木筏互相碰撞着。

paras.en: Anna looked at Elsa and Kristoff in the gloom, and a smile spread across her face. “This could be it!” she whispered. “We may finally find the sword!” “Let’s wait and see,” said Elsa, ever the one to freeze the excited mood.
paras.zh: 安娜在昏暗里看看艾莎和克里斯托夫，脸上绽开笑容。“可能就是这儿了！”她低声说，“我们终于可能找到那把剑了！”“先看看再说吧，”艾莎说，她总是那个给兴奋降温的人。

paras.en: Echo tugged at Kristoff’s tunic, and they began to toss stones into the water. “My assistant will help.
paras.zh: 埃科拽着克里斯托夫的衣衫，两人开始往水里扔石头。“我的助手会帮忙。

paras.en: She will take you to the Library of Lost Things,” the Librarian King told them. “If my people ever came across the legendary sword, it will be there—that is, if the sword truly exists.” Elsa shot Anna a look, and Anna bit her lip.
paras.zh: 她会带你们去失物图书馆，”图书管理员国王对他们说，“如果我的族人曾遇到过那把传奇之剑，它就在那里——当然，前提是这把剑真存在。”艾莎瞥了安娜一眼，安娜咬了咬嘴唇。

paras.en: She hoped against hope that it did. “We are sorry for bringing the Nattmara to your door,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: 她抱着一丝希望，盼它真的存在。“把纳特玛拉引到你们家门口，我们很抱歉，”艾莎说。

paras.en: It wasn’t lost on Anna that her sister had used the word we .
paras.zh: 安娜敏锐地注意到，妹妹用的是“我们”这个词。

paras.en: The Librarian King shook his head. “The Nattmara is one of the many natural enemies of the Huldrefólk—we both seek to reign the dark.
paras.zh: 图书管理员国王摇了摇头。“纳特玛拉是岩精诸多天敌之一——我们都想在黑暗中称王。

paras.en: But while the Huldrefólk love the night for its quiet privacy, the Nattmara prefers to use the dark as a weapon.
paras.zh: 但岩精喜爱夜晚，是因为它的静谧与私密；而纳特玛拉却喜欢把黑暗当作武器。

paras.en: Fear not: the Nattmara cannot pass into the borders of our domain.
paras.zh: 不必害怕：纳特玛拉无法越过我们领地的边界。

paras.en: As long as you’re within the Huldrefólk realm, the Nattmara cannot touch you.
paras.zh: 只要你们身在岩精的领地之内，纳特玛拉就碰不到你们。

paras.en: We are the hidden people.
paras.zh: 我们是隐身之人。

paras.en: We keep ourselves hidden, and now that you’re with us, we’ll keep you hidden as well.” Relief filled Anna, and then a thought stirred. “Umm, I have a question for you,” she said. “We lost a member of our group.
paras.zh: 我们隐藏自己，而既然你们和我们在一起，我们也会把你们藏好。”安娜心中一块石头落了地，接着一个念头浮起。“嗯，我有件事想问你，”她说，“我们队伍里走失了一个人。

paras.en: Is it possible for the Huldrefólk to find him?
paras.zh: 岩精有可能找到他吗？

paras.en: He’s kind of short and stocky, with a long silver beard that touches the floor, and he’s grumpy.” Anna paused, then added, “He’s nice!” The Librarian King inclined his head. “As you know, Huldrefólk are seekers of lost things.
paras.zh: 他有点矮壮，留着垂到地板的长长银须，脾气还有点暴躁。”安娜顿了顿，又补充道，“不过人很好！”图书管理员国王微微颔首。“如你所知，岩精是寻回失物的人。

paras.en: Collectors.
paras.zh: 是收藏者。

paras.en: If your friend is still free of the Nattmara, then I’m sure we can locate him.” “Land ahoy!” Anna looked to the water, where a gray raft glided in front of them and bumped against the bank.
paras.zh: 只要你的朋友还没被纳特玛拉附身，我确信我们能找到他。”“陆地，前方有陆地！”安娜朝水面望去，一只灰色木筏滑到他们面前，撞上了河岸。

paras.en: A cheery-looking Hulder (as Anna thought she could make out a smile in the dim glowworms’ light) waved at them and leaned against the long pole she’d been using to steer the vessel. “Ahoy!
paras.zh: 一名神情欢快的岩精（安娜觉得在昏暗的萤光虫微光里，她似乎能辨认出一丝笑容）朝他们挥手，倚着撑船的长篙。“你好啊！

paras.en: Ahoy!
paras.zh: 你好啊！

paras.en: Ahoy!” Echo cried out, and left the game of skipping rocks with Kristoff to fling herself onto the raft and into the new Hulder’s arms. “This is my assistant, Obscuren,” the Librarian King proclaimed. “She will help you find what you are looking for and will be your guide in my domain.” Anna scrambled onto the raft, settling herself next to Kristoff.
paras.zh: 你好啊！”埃科喊着，丢下和克里斯托夫玩的打水漂游戏，扑到木筏上，扑进那名新岩精的怀里。“这是我的助手奥布斯科伦，”图书管理员国王宣布，“她会帮你们找到要找的东西，并做你们在我领地里的向导。”安娜爬上木筏，在克里斯托夫身旁坐下。

paras.en: It was only then that she noticed the unusual material it was made of.
paras.zh: 直到这时，她才注意到木筏所用材料的奇特。

paras.en: While rafts were almost always constructed of wood, this one seemed to be made of floating stone.
paras.zh: 木筏几乎总是由木头制成，可这只却像是用会浮的石头做的。

paras.en: As she peered closer, she saw tiny holes perforating the surface, making the texture of the raft seem more like bread than rock. “I think this is a pumice raft,” Anna said to Kristoff, who nodded. “It is,” he said. “Rock from the volcano.” Anna felt a tug on her hair as Echo crawled into her lap, quietly chanting, “Row, row, row your raft!” “Say your goodbye,” the Librarian King instructed Echo. “It’s time for dinner.” The little Hulder’s eyes swam with tears. “Stay!” “I wish you could,” Anna said, and was surprised when she realized she meant it.
paras.zh: 她凑近细看，发现表面布满细密的小孔，让木筏的质地更像面包而非石头。“我想这是浮石筏，”安娜对克里斯托夫说，他点了点头。“是浮石，”他说，“火山里的石头。”安娜感到头发被扯了一下——埃科爬进了她怀里，轻轻念着：“划呀，划呀，划你的筏！”“跟人家道别吧，”图书管理员国王吩咐埃科，“该吃晚饭了。”小岩精的眼里泛起泪光。“留下来！”“我也希望你能留下，”安娜说，而当她意识到自己是真心这么想时，自己都有些惊讶。

paras.en: Miner’s Mountain was beautiful, full of unexpected surprises and even more unexpected friendships.
paras.zh: 矿工山真美，充满了意想不到的惊喜，还有更意想不到的友谊。

paras.en: She liked the little Hulder and her penchant for flying ahead as fast as possible.
paras.zh: 她喜欢这个小岩精，喜欢她总是拼命往前冲的性子。

paras.en: Anna bet Echo could show her many things—glowing crystals, ice caves, maybe even a sleeping bat or two—but she needed to fix her mistake before she could explore the wonders of the mountain further. “Besides, you’d be bored if you joined us,” Anna said. “We won’t be singing anymore, and being on a raft makes it hard for you to dash anywhere.” Head tilted, the little Hulder considered this bleak reality, then clambered out of the raft to join one of the Huldrefólk guards who’d seemingly materialized out of nowhere. “Bye!” Echo proclaimed from the riverbank, waving. “Bye-bye-bye!” Anna’s heart squeezed. “See you later.
paras.zh: 安娜打赌，埃科能带她看许多东西——发光的晶体、冰洞，说不定还有一两只睡着的蝙蝠——可她得先弥补自己的错误，才能继续探索这座山的奇妙。“再说，你跟我们去也会无聊的，”安娜说，“我们不会再唱歌了，而且坐在筏上也让你没法到处飞奔。”小岩精歪着头想了想这黯淡的现实，然后爬出木筏，去加入一名仿佛凭空出现的岩精卫兵。“再见！”埃科在河岸上挥着手宣布，“再见再见再见！”安娜心头一紧。“回头见。

paras.en: Stay out of dark abysses, okay?” Elsa was the last to step onto the raft.
paras.zh: 别去黑暗的深渊，好吗？”艾莎是最后一个踏上木筏的。

paras.en: When she’d settled her cloak around her, she looked back at the Librarian King. “Thank you,” she said. “For all your help.
paras.zh: 等她把斗篷裹好，回头望向图书管理员国王。“谢谢你，”她说，“谢谢你所有的帮助。

paras.en: I promise we’ll keep your secret, and we will keep the mines closed.
paras.zh: 我保证会替你们保守秘密，也会让矿井继续封闭。

paras.en: Your city will remain hidden.” The Librarian King bowed in thanks, and then Obscuren pushed them across the glassy surface of the river.
paras.zh: 你们的城市会一直隐秘。”图书管理员国王鞠躬致谢，随后奥布斯科伦撑着他们滑过如镜的河面。

paras.en: The raft rocked as they navigated the underground waterway, the air refreshingly cooler now.
paras.zh: 木筏在地下水道中摇晃前行，空气此刻清爽了许多。

paras.en: Obscuren took in their drooping eyelids. “You can sleep,” she said. “I know my way around the river.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦注意到他们耷拉的眼皮。“你们可以睡，”她说，“我认得河路的去向。

paras.en: And as the Librarian King said, you are hidden here with me, even from the Nattmara.” “Are you absolutely…” Whatever Kristoff had been going to say was lost in a yawn. “The Nattmara cannot find our domain,” Obscuren reminded them. “We are cloaked from it.
paras.zh: 而且就像图书管理员国王说的，你们和我在一起是隐身的，连纳特玛拉也看不见。”“你百分之百……”克里斯托夫本要说什么，却化作一个大哈欠。“纳特玛拉找不到我们的领地，”奥布斯科伦提醒他们，“我们被遮蔽在它之外。

paras.en: You can rest here, safely, without any fear of losing yourself over to its influence.
paras.zh: 你们可以在这儿安心休息，不必担心被它的力量吞噬。

paras.en: Sleep.
paras.zh: 睡吧。

paras.en: Rest.
paras.zh: 歇着吧。

paras.en: I’ll wake you when we reach our destination.” Obscuren had barely finished before a snore ripped out of Kristoff, and in the next second, Elsa, too, was asleep.
paras.zh: 到了目的地我会叫醒你们。”奥布斯科伦话音未落，克里斯托夫已经打起呼噜，下一秒，艾莎也睡着了。

paras.en: Anna, however, stayed awake.
paras.zh: 然而安娜还醒着。

paras.en: Though she had been daydreaming about sleeping, she found she couldn’t close her eyes.
paras.zh: 尽管她刚才还做着睡觉的白日梦，此刻却发现怎么也闭不上眼。

paras.en: Every time she did, her stomach hurt too much.
paras.zh: 每次闭眼，她的胃就疼得厉害。

paras.en: Because each moment asleep was a moment she wasn’t fixing her biggest mistake: the Nattmara she’d accidentally welcomed into Arendelle with a spell.
paras.zh: 因为每睡过去一刻，她就少一刻去弥补自己最大的错误：那道咒语，是她不小心把纳特玛拉招进阿伦黛尔的元凶。

paras.en: Obscuren’s voice interrupted her thoughts, and Anna pulled herself out of them. “Sorry, what was that?” Anna asked. “I said,” the Hulder repeated, “that you should sleep, too.” Obscuren pushed on the pole, and the water sighed as the raft sliced through it.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦的声音打断了她的思绪，安娜回过神来。“抱歉，你刚才说什么？”安娜问。“我说，”岩精重复道，“你也该睡了。”奥布斯科伦撑了一篙，木筏破水而行，水声仿佛一声叹息。

paras.en: The river flowed through winding tunnels with low ceilings, though here and there little beaches seemed to jut into the waterway, and Anna thought she could make out the distant shape of a Hulder or two watching them.
paras.zh: 河流穿过低矮蜿蜒的隧道，尽管这儿那儿有些小滩地探入水道，安娜觉得自己能辨认出远处一两个岩精注视着他们的身影。

paras.en: This close to a Hulder who was not trying to kill her, she could finally make out a more definite shape.
paras.zh: 离一个不想杀她的岩精这么近，她终于能看清更明确的轮廓。

paras.en: Obscuren looked almost human but for an overall spindly appearance, pointed ears, and changing skin.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦看起来几乎像人，只是整体瘦长得怪，耳朵尖尖，皮肤还会变色。

paras.en: At the moment, the Hulder’s eyes were a beautiful shade of orange, a color that made Anna think of the end of autumn or the start of spring.
paras.zh: 此刻，那岩精的眼睛是一种美丽的橙色，让安娜想起晚秋将尽或初春伊始的颜色。

paras.en: They seemed to take in everything around them, and as Obscuren looked at Anna, Anna wondered if the seeker of things could find Anna’s deepest secret in her eyes. “Obscuren,” Anna said, “do you know how the Nattmara came to Arendelle?
paras.zh: 那双眼睛仿佛将周遭一切尽收眼底，而当奥布斯科伦望向安娜时，安娜不禁想，这位寻物者能否从自己眼里看穿最深的秘密。“奥布斯科伦，”安娜说，“你知道纳特玛拉是怎么来到阿伦黛尔的吗？

paras.en: I think I know, but I’m not entirely sure.
paras.zh: 我想我知道，但不完全确定。

paras.en: The Blight started before the Nattmara arrived.
paras.zh: 枯疫在纳特玛拉到来之前就开始了。

paras.en: I’m a bit murky on the details.” She held her breath, waiting for Obscuren to somehow say the words that were blaring through her mind as loudly as a goatherd playing the tungehorn: the spell .
paras.zh: 细节上我有点模糊。”她屏住呼吸，等着奥布斯科伦说出那几个在她脑中轰鸣如牧羊人吹响号角的字：那道咒语。

paras.en: It must have been the spell, as much as it didn’t make sense that the animals and crops had grown sick before she’d read it.
paras.zh: 一定就是那道咒语——尽管说不通的是，动物和庄稼在她念它之前就已经病倒了。

paras.en: But after she read the spell, the wolf appeared.
paras.zh: 可她念过咒语之后，那头狼就出现了。

paras.en: Of that much Anna was certain—just as she was certain it was her fault.
paras.zh: 这一点安娜很确定——就像她确定那是自己的错一样。

paras.en: Obscuren was silent, but it wasn’t the kind of sharp silence of being ignored.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦沉默着，但那不是被无视时那种尖锐的沉默。

paras.en: This quiet had a thoughtful quality to it, as though she were weighing each word before speaking. “A Nattmara doesn’t appear out of thin air,” the Hulder said. “They are made, formed from an event in a person’s life that grows so big they can’t keep it inside anymore, and the fear becomes so large that it takes on a life of its own.” Anna nodded.
paras.zh: 这份安静带着思索的意味，仿佛她在开口前掂量着每一个字。“纳特玛拉不会凭空出现，”岩精说，“它们是被‘造’出来的，由一个人生命中某件不断膨胀、大到再也无法藏于心底的事所成形，恐惧变得如此巨大，便有了自己的生命。”安娜点了点头。

paras.en: Yes, that was what Sorenson had said.
paras.zh: 对，索伦森也是这么说的。

paras.en: The fear is too big to keep inside. “Sooo,” Anna said, “you don’t think that someone could have, I don’t know”—she tucked a strand of ruddy hair behind her ear—“said a spell, or something, and brought the Nattmara to Arendelle?” Obscuren gave a shake of her head. “I don’t believe the poems that humans call spells are really anything other than just that: poems.
paras.zh: 恐惧太大，藏不住了。“那——”安娜说，“你觉得，有没有可能是某人——我也不知道，”她把一缕红发别到耳后，“念了什么咒语之类的，把纳特玛拉带到了阿伦黛尔？”奥布斯科伦摇了摇头。“我不认为人类称作‘咒语’的那些诗，除了诗本身之外还能是什么。

paras.en: They may be able to conjure a beautiful image or a moment of time, but that is a different kind of magic entirely.” Anna wasn’t sure what to say, but she was comforted.
paras.zh: 它们或许能召唤出美丽的意象或某一瞬间，但那完全是另一种魔法。”安娜不知该说什么，却感到一丝安慰。

paras.en: Because Anna had read a spell…but it sounded like even if she had never said it out loud, the Nattmara still would have come to the kingdom.
paras.zh: 因为安娜确实念过一道咒语……但听这意思，即便她从没念出声，纳特玛拉也照样会降临王国。

paras.en: Anna still would have accidentally called it, with or without a poem.
paras.zh: 无论有没有那首诗，安娜还是会在不经意间把它招来。

paras.en: Because the night that it had materialized from her dreams was the same night she’d heard Elsa holding a council meeting without her, and she had felt her heart break a little.
paras.zh: 因为那夜它从她的梦中具象成形，正是她听见艾莎撇下她召开御前会议的那一夜，那一刻她的心微微碎了。

paras.en: It was the moment she had realized her greatest fear had come true: that Elsa really and truly had no need for her at all.
paras.zh: 就在那一刻，她意识到自己最大的恐惧成真了：艾莎真的、真的完全不需要她了。

paras.en: And because of that, her nightmare—her fear —had manifested in the form of the Nattmara that was now stalking them all. “And I guess,” she said, trying to keep her voice light, “if there’s no spell to call a Nattmara, then there’s probably no spell to banish one, right?” Obscuren shook her head. “I wouldn’t think so.
paras.zh: 正因如此，她的噩梦——她的恐惧——才以纳特玛拉的形态显现，如今正尾随着他们所有人。“那么我想，”她努力让声音听起来轻松，“既然没有召唤纳特玛拉的咒语，大概也就没有驱散它的咒语，对吧？”奥布斯科伦摇了摇头。“我想没有。

paras.en: I’ve only ever heard of one warrior willing to face the Nattmara, and that was Aren, with his mythical Revolute Blade that contained a strange power.” Revolute.
paras.zh: 我只听说过一位敢直面纳特玛拉的勇士，那就是阿伦，凭着他的神剑回旋之刃，其中蕴含着奇异的力量。”回旋。

paras.en: With Kristoff and Elsa asleep and nestled against her back, and Obscuren in the front, keeping an eye on Anna and her friends, the mythical curved sword shone like a lighthouse in the dark river of Anna’s worry, and, at last, she let her eyes drift shut to sleep.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫和艾莎睡着靠在她的背脊上，奥布斯科伦在前头留意着安娜和她的朋友们，这把神异的弯剑如同灯塔，照亮安娜忧心如暗河般的心，而终于，她任双眼缓缓合上，睡了过去。

paras.en: WHEN OBSCUREN WOKE ANNA, she felt better rested than she had in a long, long time.
paras.zh: 当奥布斯科伦叫醒安娜时，她觉得比很久很久以来都要精神焕发。

paras.en: Next to her, Kristoff stretched, half his hair smooshed against his cheek where he’d lain on it. “Up, up, and away,” Kristoff said with a yawn.
paras.zh: 身旁，克里斯托夫伸了个懒腰，压在脸颊上的那半边头发都睡扁了。“起喽，起喽，出发喽，”克里斯托夫打了个哈欠说。

paras.en: Elsa, however, still managed to look regal, even though Anna could see the pattern of pumice pores on her face.
paras.zh: 然而艾莎却依旧显得高贵，尽管安娜能看见她脸上浮石孔隙压出的印子。

paras.en: Anna giggled, motioning to her sister’s cheek. “You should take a look at yourself,” Elsa grumbled with half a smile.
paras.zh: 安娜咯咯笑起来，指了指妹妹的脸颊。“你也该照照自己，”艾莎半带笑意地嘟囔道。

paras.en: Anna peered into the river.
paras.zh: 安娜朝河里望去。

paras.en: Sure enough, she looked the same as she always did when she woke up: a bit like a woodland creature with a slobber problem.
paras.zh: 果不其然，她醒来时的模样和以往一样：活像个有流口水毛病的林中小兽。

paras.en: Anna patted down her stray hairs with river water, and she found comfort in the way that some things stayed the same.
paras.zh: 安娜用河水拍平乱翘的头发，从某些事物始终如一中找到了慰藉。

paras.en: Elsa smiled at her, and Anna guessed she was thinking the same thing, too. “We’re here,” Obscuren said as they glided up to a post.
paras.zh: 艾莎朝她笑了笑，安娜猜她想的也是同一件事。“我们到了，”奥布斯科伦说着，撑着筏子靠上一根木桩。

paras.en: While they waited for Obscuren to secure the raft, Anna looked around, but even holding out her wrist with the glowworm bracelet, she couldn’t see any sign of a library…or where one could possibly be.
paras.zh: 他们等着奥布斯科伦把筏子系牢，安娜四下张望，可即便举着手腕上萤光虫做成的手环，她也看不出半点图书馆的影子……更不知它能在何处。

paras.en: The banks of the underground river were narrow, no wider than a foot or two, and as far as she could tell, nothing had been carved into the rock’s surface except for a few crumbly-looking steps. “Where is it?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: 地下河的河岸很窄，不过一两尺宽，而据她所见，岩石表面除了几级看着酥脆易碎的台阶，什么也没凿出来。“它在哪儿？”安娜问。

paras.en: It had been nice to sleep and all, but being awake again meant she was more aware than ever of the time that was slipping away.
paras.zh: 睡上一觉固然好，可重新清醒意味着她比以往更清楚地感到时光正在溜走。

paras.en: They had only one more day of sun and a single night left before the third sunrise made the Nattmara’s reality permanent—assuming that the spell really had been what brought the Nattmara to Arendelle in the first place.
paras.zh: 在第三个日出让纳特玛拉的存在永久固化之前，他们只剩最后一天日照和一个夜晚了——前提是那道咒语真的是最初把纳特玛拉带到阿伦黛尔的元凶。

paras.en: Obscuren hadn’t though so, but Anna couldn’t shake Sorenson’s words.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦不这么认为，可安娜挥不去索伦森的话。

paras.en: All myths contain a kernel of hard truth.
paras.zh: 所有神话都含有一粒坚硬的真相。

paras.en: The spell might not have been real magic, but that didn’t mean the warning wasn’t true.
paras.zh: 那道咒语或许不是真正的魔法，但那不代表警告不是真的。

paras.en: At any rate, Anna was not willing to risk it. “Up, up, up and away,” Obscuren said, seeming to settle into another’s words comfortably, as if the conversation of the previous night had been a bit of a strain for her.
paras.zh: 无论如何，安娜都不愿拿这个去冒险。“起喽，起喽，起喽，出发喽，”奥布斯科伦说，仿佛惬意地借用着别人的话，好像前一晚的对话让她颇有些吃力。

paras.en: Elsa wobbled out of the raft first, followed by Kristoff.
paras.zh: 艾莎先晃晃悠悠地下了筏，接着是克里斯托夫。

paras.en: When he turned to offer his hand to help Anna step out, she ignored it and leapt over the side.
paras.zh: 他转身伸手想扶安娜下筏，她却没理，直接从侧面跳了下去。

paras.en: Obscuren indicated with a nod that they should take off their glowworm bracelets and leave the little creatures on the post.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦点点头示意，他们该取下萤光虫手环，把小虫留在木桩上。

paras.en: With a wistful sigh, Anna unwrapped the glowworm and gave it a little pat in thanks. “Will it be okay here?” she asked. “Home is where the heart is,” Obscuren said, and when Anna looked for clarification, the Librarian King’s assistant explained, “I’ll take them back with me.
paras.zh: 安娜怅然叹了口气，解下萤光虫，轻轻拍了拍以示感谢。“它留在这儿没事吧？”她问。“心在处便是家，”奥布斯科伦说，见安娜一脸疑惑，这位图书管理员国王的助手解释道，“我会把它们带回去。

paras.en: They’re not needed where we’re going.” And with that, Obscuren left the raft behind and stepped off into the darkness, silent as the moon sailing through the night sky.
paras.zh: 我们要去的地方用不着它们。”说罢，奥布斯科伦丢下木筏，步入黑暗，静默如划过夜空的月亮。

paras.en: Anna, Elsa, and Kristoff followed her, not nearly as gracefully, but they managed to reach the beginning of the steps and started to feel their way up the side of the rock, following the carved path that wound its way to the cave ceiling. “Stop a moment,” Obscuren said, and there were a few quick taps, and then a creak as the Hulder pushed open a square hatch in the ceiling.
paras.zh: 安娜、艾莎和克里斯托夫跟着她，虽然远没那么优雅，但也设法走到台阶起始处，沿着蜿蜒通向洞顶的凿路，摸着岩壁往上爬。“停一下，”奥布斯科伦说，接着是几下轻快的敲击，随后是一声吱呀——岩精推开了洞顶上一扇方形的活门。

paras.en: Light streamed through.
paras.zh: 光线倾泻而下。

paras.en: Squinting her eyes against the unexpected brightness, Anna emerged from the dirt floor of a round room with stone walls carved with runes and windows blocked by grassy tussocks.
paras.zh: 安娜眯起眼，抵御这突如其来的亮光，从一间圆形房间的泥地中钻了出来——石墙上刻着符文，窗户被草丛堵住。

paras.en: She caught a glimpse of blue in the window.
paras.zh: 她在窗口瞥见一抹蓝色。

paras.en: Her heart leapt. “Wait, is that sky ?” she asked. “We’re in a turf house,” Elsa said as she shrugged off her cloak and her mother’s scarf before stepping aside from the trapdoor to make space for Kristoff to climb up beside them.
paras.zh: 她心头一跳。“等等，那是天空吗？”她问。“我们在一间草皮屋里，”艾莎说着，卸下斗篷和母亲的围巾，从活门旁退开，好让克里斯托夫爬上来站在他们身边。

paras.en: Of course!
paras.zh: 当然了！

paras.en: Turf houses dotted Arendelle’s wilderness of scraggly birches and spruces.
paras.zh: 在阿伦黛尔那片遍布歪脖子桦树和云杉的荒野上，草皮屋星罗棋布。

paras.en: They were made by digging a dwelling-sized hole deep into the ground, which was then covered by a roof made of grass.
paras.zh: 它们是在地下挖出一间屋子大小的深坑，再覆以草做的屋顶建成的。

paras.en: Turf houses came in all shapes and sizes, but Anna’s favorites were the ones that looked like Earth Giants sunk into the soil, the green grass of the roofs resembling troll hair.
paras.zh: 草皮屋有各种形状和大小，可安娜最喜欢那些像大地巨人陷进土里的样式，屋顶的绿草仿佛地精的头发。

paras.en: Anna looked around, hoping to see a neat row of books. “Um, Obscuren, are you sure this is your library?” she said.
paras.zh: 安娜环顾四周，盼着能看见一排整齐的书。“嗯，奥布斯科伦，你确定这就是你的图书馆？”她说。

paras.en: It didn’t look so much like a library as it did a too-crammed gift shop.
paras.zh: 这地方不像图书馆，倒更像个塞得太满的礼品店。

paras.en: Sure, there were a few books scattered here and there, with bleached covers that looked like they’d been forgotten long ago and left out to wither in the sun.
paras.zh: 当然，这儿那儿散落着几本书，封面泛白，像是早被遗忘、丢在太阳下晒得发蔫。

paras.en: But mostly there were items .
paras.zh: 但更多的是物品。

paras.en: There were sideways chairs lying on top of rolled-up rugs next to a careful stack of mirrors.
paras.zh: 横倒的椅子压在卷起的毯子上，旁边是一摞码放整齐的镜子。

paras.en: There was a pile of gardening tools, broken clay figurines, and more than one pile of rusted old keys.
paras.zh: 有一堆园艺工具、破碎的泥塑小人，还有不止一堆生锈的旧钥匙。

paras.en: And there were socks—lots and lots of mismatched socks. “Welcome to the Library of Lost Things,” Obscuren said.
paras.zh: 还有袜子——许许多多配不成对的袜子。“欢迎来到失物图书馆，”奥布斯科伦说。

paras.en: Above the ground and in the warm light of the turf house, the Hulder seemed to look less like rock and more like a tree, softly sprouting leaves where before there had been the rough texture of a pebble. “Before you say anything, we did not steal any of these things.
paras.zh: 到了地面上，在草皮屋温暖的光线里，这岩精看起来少了些石头味，多了些树的神韵，原本粗糙如卵石的纹理上，柔柔地“长”出了叶子。“在你开口之前，我们可没偷过这些东西里的任何一件。

paras.en: We simply find things that are lost and give them homes.
paras.zh: 我们只是找到遗失的东西，给它们一个家。

paras.en: That includes everything from missing spectacles, to hair bands, to legendary swords.
paras.zh: 从丢失的眼镜、发带，到传奇的宝剑，全都包括在内。

paras.en: Please,” the Hulder continued, stepping aside, “feel free to roam.” “Thank you!” Anna cheered. “Can the Nattmara find us up here ?
paras.zh: 请吧，”岩精侧过身继续说，“随意逛逛。”“谢谢！”安娜欢呼道，“纳特玛拉能在这儿找到我们吗？

paras.en: Or are we still hidden and all that?” Kristoff asked, peering out a window. “With me, you are still hidden from the Nattmara,” Obscuren said. “Phew!” Kristoff said. “That’s a relief,” said Elsa, peering through the mess of objects. “We should split up,” Anna said, then looked at Elsa. “Right?” Elsa nodded, and so the three of them began their search.
paras.zh: 还是说我们依旧是隐身的？”克里斯托夫从窗口往外张望着问。“有我在，你们仍对纳特玛拉隐身，”奥布斯科伦说。“呼！”克里斯托夫说。“这下松口气了，”艾莎边在杂物堆里张望边说。“我们该分头找，”安娜说，又看看艾莎，“对吧？”艾莎点点头，于是三人开始分头搜寻。

paras.en: Some of the lost objects were beautiful—bronze vases from another age and even a necklace of heavy sapphires that Anna thought would complement Gerda’s eyes—if Anna were able to turn them back from yellow, that is.
paras.zh: 有些失物十分精美——来自另一个时代的青铜花瓶，甚至还有一条沉甸甸的蓝宝石项链，安娜觉得配格尔达的眼睛正合适——当然，前提是她能把人们的眼睛从黄色变回原样。

paras.en: She set the necklace down and hurried to the next pile.
paras.zh: 她放下项链，赶忙走向下一堆。

paras.en: She picked up a round mirror.
paras.zh: 她捡起一面圆镜。

paras.en: It was little, meant to slip into a pocket, and clasped cleverly to look like a clamshell.
paras.zh: 它很小，是揣进兜里的那种，扣合得巧，看上去像只蛤壳。

paras.en: She opened it, then set it to the side.
paras.zh: 她打开看了看，又放到一边。

paras.en: It was pretty, but not what she was looking for.
paras.zh: 是很漂亮，可不是她要找的东西。

paras.en: Scanning the room, Anna searched for a glint of metal, trying to find anything that could possibly be the sword of myth.
paras.zh: 安娜扫视房间，搜寻着金属的闪光，想找出任何可能是那把神话之剑的东西。

paras.en: She moved aside a rickety chair and a mountain of missing socks and tried to push down her disappointment, but it kept rising, like a hot-air balloon, not wanting to be weighed down.
paras.zh: 她挪开一把摇摇晃晃的椅子和一座“失踪袜子”山，努力压下心头的失望，可它却像热气球般不断上升，不愿被压下。

paras.en: There had to be something in this library.
paras.zh: 这图书馆里一定有线索。

paras.en: Anna’s thoughts skidded to a halt.
paras.zh: 安娜的思绪猛地刹住。

paras.en: Her eye had caught on a statue in the center of the room.
paras.zh: 她的目光被房间中央的一座雕像攫住。

paras.en: It was a figure of a human girl in a sky-blue dress with a glittering train, and a platinum blond braid.
paras.zh: 那是一个人类女孩的塑像，穿着天蓝色礼服，拖着闪亮的裙裾，还有一条白金色的辫子。

paras.en: It looked to be about as tall as Elsa’s knee, and it also happened to look a lot like Elsa.
paras.zh: 它差不多到艾莎膝盖高，而且碰巧长得非常像艾莎。

paras.en: Anna gasped as she stepped closer.
paras.zh: 安娜走近时倒吸一口气。

paras.en: It was a statue of Elsa.
paras.zh: 那是艾莎的雕像。

paras.en: Specifically, the one the sisters had installed in the town cuckoo clock a few years before.
paras.zh: 确切地说，是姐妹俩几年前装进镇上布谷鸟钟里的那一尊。

paras.en: Last spring, the Elsa figure had disappeared in a sudden storm, blown away by unusually strong winds.
paras.zh: 去年春天，这尊艾莎像在一场突如其来的风暴中失踪，被异常强劲的风吹走了。

paras.en: Anna peered at the statue.
paras.zh: 安娜端详着雕像。

paras.en: A little green wreath with candles had been perched on top of statue Elsa’s head, and Anna had the briefest thought that the statue looked more comfortable here, surrounded by other wondrous things, than it had looming above the masses, day in and day out.
paras.zh: 雕像艾莎的头顶上搁着一圈插着蜡烛的小绿冠，安娜闪过一个念头：这雕像待在这儿，被其他奇珍环绕，比日复一日高高凌驾于人群之上要自在得多。

paras.en: She was glad the Huldrefólk had found a new home for it, and so she kept searching.
paras.zh: 她很高兴岩精为它找了个新家，于是继续搜寻。

paras.en: But no matter how hard or long they looked, they did not find the coveted sword in the turf house.
paras.zh: 但无论他们找得多卖力、多久，都没在这间草皮屋里找到那把梦寐以求的剑。

paras.en: The closest things to a mythical sword they’d managed to unearth were a few shields and helmets from the time of King Runeard, but nothing older than that.
paras.zh: 他们挖出来的、最接近神话之剑的东西，不过是几面鲁纳德王时代的盾牌和头盔，再没有更古老的了。

paras.en: Anna’s shoulders slumped.
paras.zh: 安娜的肩膀垮了下来。

paras.en: If the Huldrefólk didn’t have Revolute, and if Sorenson was lost, and if the trolls had fled the Nattmara…what were they going to do?
paras.zh: 如果岩精没有回旋之刃，而索伦森又失踪了，地精们也逃离了纳特玛拉……他们该怎么办？

paras.en: They were running out of places to find answers. “There’s not a single sword in this library!” Elsa said to Obscuren an hour later as the gang flopped in front of a large fireplace to eat from Kristoff’s traveler’s pack.
paras.zh: 他们能找答案的地方快用光了。“这图书馆里一把剑都没有！”一小时后，艾莎对奥布斯科伦说，此时大家瘫坐在巨大的壁炉前，吃着克里斯托夫的行囊里的干粮。

paras.en: Obscuren sighed. “So it appears.” The Hulder’s skin had taken on the runes of the turf house walls, and speaking to Obscuren now almost felt like talking to alphabet soup.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦叹了口气。“看来是这样。”岩精的皮肤已变成草皮屋墙上的符文模样，此刻跟奥布斯科伦说话，几乎像是在和一锅字母汤对话。

paras.en: She seemed to droop slightly, and it was clear to Anna that Obscuren wasn’t used to having to converse so much. “Why not?” Kristoff asked. “Arendelle’s history seems to be full of swords, as far as I can tell.
paras.zh: 她似乎微微垂着头，安娜看得出奥布斯科伦不习惯要说这么多话。“为什么没有？”克里斯托夫问，“据我所知，阿伦黛尔的历史里好像到处都是剑。

paras.en: Why didn’t the Huldrefólk ever find one?
paras.zh: 岩精怎么从没找到过一把？

paras.en: Maybe it’s at another location?” “Sometimes,” Obscuren said, settling down onto the dirt floor to rest, “great swords are buried with their heroes.” “ARRGH!” Anna’s heart began to pound furiously as a cry that sounded a bit like a seagull reverberated through the turf house.
paras.zh: 也许在别的地方？”“有时候，”奥布斯科伦在泥地上坐下歇息，说道，“伟大的剑会与它们的英雄一同下葬。”“啊——！”一声有点像海鸥的叫喊在草皮屋里回荡，安娜的心狂跳起来。

paras.en: Wide-eyed, Anna turned to see what had made such a terrifying sound—expecting to see the Nattmara or a mob of yellow-eyed villagers coming for them—but all she saw was Elsa, who’d leapt to her feet. “Well, that’s just great!” Elsa’s blue eyes flashed and her cheeks reddened.
paras.zh: 安娜瞪大眼睛转头，想看看是什么发出这可怕的声音——本以为会看见纳特玛拉或一群黄眼村民冲过来——可她只看见一跃而起的艾莎。“哎呀，这可真妙！”艾莎的蓝眼睛冒着火，脸颊涨得通红。

paras.en: For the first time in a long time, Anna thought that her sister looked visibly upset. “What’s wrong?” Anna scrambled to her feet, too. “We just need to find out where Aren was buried—” Elsa snorted, and it was such an un-Elsa-like sound that Anna grew quiet. “We can’t find where he was buried.” Elsa paced the floor. “Don’t you remember the story?
paras.zh: 这是很久以来头一回，安娜觉得妹妹明显心烦意乱。“怎么了？”安娜也慌忙站起。“我们只要弄清阿伦葬在哪儿——”艾莎嗤笑一声，那声音如此不像艾莎，令安娜安静下来。“我们找不到他葬在哪儿。”艾莎在地板上踱步。“你不记得那个故事了？

paras.en: Aren was swallowed by a dragon!” Anna blinked. “He was ?” She’d forgotten that.
paras.zh: 阿伦被一条龙吞了！”安娜眨眨眼。“他被吞了？”她把这事给忘了。

paras.en: She glanced over at Kristoff, who was looking at Elsa with something like awe, as though he couldn’t quite believe that calm and collected Elsa was panicking. “Yes,” Elsa said, exasperated. “A dragon came to the fjord, and it threatened to eat everyone!
paras.zh: 她瞥了克里斯托夫一眼，他正带着几分敬畏望着艾莎，仿佛不敢相信一向镇定的艾莎竟在慌乱。“是的，”艾莎恼火地说，“一条龙来到峡湾，威胁要把所有人都吃掉！

paras.en: And so Aren, our greatest leader besides King Runeard, who loved his home and people more than anything, decided to go face the dragon…who”—Elsa paused, then changed to her most dramatic voice—“‘lives where the sea is a sky,’ and never came back.” Elsa took a deep breath. “Because the dragon swallowed him.
paras.zh: 于是阿伦——除鲁纳德王外我们最伟大的领袖，他爱家乡与百姓胜过一切——决定去直面那条龙……那条龙，”艾莎顿了顿，换上最戏剧化的嗓音，“‘栖于海即是天之处’，从此再没回来。”艾莎深吸一口气。“因为龙把他吞了。

paras.en: And dragons don’t exist, and neither does this sword, and Anna, oh, I’ve tried listening, but there’s nothing we can do!” “Curious,” Obscuren called out.
paras.zh: 而龙根本不存在，这把剑也不存在，安娜，哦，我努力去听了，可我们无能为力！”“奇怪，”奥布斯科伦喊了一声。

paras.en: During Elsa’s tirade, the Hulder had gone to a stone wall. “That’s not what all stories say.” She waved a delicate arm at the walls around them. “In that long-ago time when Huldrefólk and humans were more comfortable with each other, we would meet here, in a place of compromise between earth and sky.
paras.zh: 在艾莎长篇大论时，岩精走到一面石墙前。“并非所有故事都这么讲。”她纤细的手臂朝四周的墙壁一挥。“在久远的从前，岩精与人类彼此还更亲近，我们会在此相会，在这天地之间的折中之地。

paras.en: Each community carved their stories into these walls.
paras.zh: 每个族群都把自己的故事刻进这些墙里。

paras.en: This is one of the oldest turf houses.
paras.zh: 这是最古老的草皮屋之一。

paras.en: And here, the myth of Aren changes, slightly. “This”—the Hulder pointed at a carved rune that looked like a sideways S -shape—“according to our legend, says that a great danger came from the waters, and in order to save his home and people that he loved, Aren set out in a boat and was never seen again.” “How is that any better?” Elsa asked, and Anna was shocked to see her sister’s foot twitch, as though she had just resisted the urge to stomp her feet. “That just means Revolute is probably somewhere at the bottom of the ocean, and even if it were possible to scour all the waters, we just don’t have time.” Elsa turned sharply, sending her braid whipping out behind her and almost smacking a shocked Kristoff across the nose. “So you see,” she addressed Anna, “we’re never going to find Revolute!” But actually…Anna did see.
paras.zh: 而在这里，阿伦的神话略有不同。“这——”岩精指着一道像横写S形的刻符——“按我们的传说，是说巨大的危险来自水中，为了拯救他深爱的家乡与百姓，阿伦乘船出海，从此杳无音信。”“这有什么好一点的？”艾莎问，安娜惊讶地看见妹妹的脚抽动了一下，仿佛刚忍住跺脚的冲动。“那只不过意味着回旋之刃大概沉在海底某处，而就算能搜遍所有水域，我们也根本没时间。”艾莎猛地转身，辫子甩到身后，差点抽中吓了一跳的克里斯托夫的鼻子。“所以你看，”她对安娜说，“我们永远也找不到回旋之刃了！”可实际上……安娜看清了。

paras.en: Anna opened her mouth. “Elsa—” “The Nattmara is still out there, the Blight chokes the land, and all of our friends are probably stuck in a nightmare by now!” Kristoff flinched at her words. “You wanted to visit the Huldrefólk because they were supposed to be able to tell us something,” Elsa continued, “to show us the way to a made-up sword.
paras.zh: 安娜张开嘴。“艾莎——”“纳特玛拉还在外面，枯疫扼住了大地，我们所有的朋友现在大概都困在噩梦里了！”克里斯托夫被她的话刺得一缩。“你当初想拜访岩精，是因为他们本该能告诉我们些什么，”艾莎继续道，“给我们指一条去找一把虚构之剑的路。

paras.en: Is there anything else, any other clue—” “Elsa—” Her sister threw her hands in the air. “The people are all counting on me!” “ELSA!” Elsa’s furor stumbled to a halt, and, panting, she looked over at Anna, who pushed away a smile. “How can you be so calm at a time like this?” Elsa demanded, and Anna had to stop from giggling. “I’m calm because I learned from the best,” Anna said, and she could feel a fiery hope burning bright in her chest. “And because I know where Revolute is.”
paras.zh: 还有什么别的吗，任何别的线索——”“艾莎——”妹妹把手一摊。“百姓们都指望着我呢！”“艾莎！”艾莎的怒火戛然而止，她喘着气看向安娜，安娜憋住了笑。“这种时候你怎么还能这么镇定？”艾莎质问道，安娜差点笑出声。“我镇定，是因为我向最棒的人学来的，”安娜说，感到胸中燃起一团明亮的希望之火，“更因为，我知道回旋之刃在哪里。”

paras.en: “WAIT, WHAT?” ELSA SAID.
paras.zh: “等等，你说什么？”艾莎说。

paras.en: Anna couldn’t help smiling now at hearing her signature line coming from Elsa’s mouth. “What do you mean, you know where Revolute is ?” Somewhere along the way, it had clicked as Anna stared at the carvings on the walls and listened to Obscuren’s tale.
paras.zh: 听到自己的招牌台词从艾莎嘴里冒出来，安娜忍不住笑了。“你说知道回旋之刃在哪，是什么意思？”不知从何时起，当安娜盯着墙上的刻纹、听着奥布斯科伦的讲述时，一切忽然接通了。

paras.en: The Arendellians’ story and the Huldrefólk’s story were different, but the same.
paras.zh: 阿伦黛尔人的故事和岩精的故事不同，却又相同。

paras.en: Like Anna and Elsa.
paras.zh: 就像安娜和艾莎。

paras.en: And just like the royal sisters, the stories made the most sense when they were together. “Why can’t both things be true?” Anna suggested. “Why can’t he have been eaten by a dragon, as our story says, and be sent out on a boat?
paras.zh: 而正如这对王室姐妹，两个故事放在一起才最讲得通。“为什么不能两件事都是真的？”安娜提议，“为什么不能既像我们的故事所说被龙吞了，又乘船出海了？

paras.en: It’s all in the stories—Aren was swallowed by a dragon who lived in a place where the sea is a sky.” “But for the sea to be a sky, you have to be under the…” Elsa’s voice trailed off and her eyes lit up. “The Earth Giant’s Passage!
paras.zh: 故事里都写着呢——阿伦被一条住在‘海即是天之处’的龙吞了。”“可要让海变成天，你得在……的下面，”艾莎的声音淡了下去，眼睛却亮了起来，“大地巨人通道！

paras.en: It goes under the fjord, which means the sea is the sky.
paras.zh: 它从峡湾底下穿过，也就是说，海就是天。

paras.en: And that’s where the dragon boat is!” Elsa’s hand flew to her mouth in wonder. “The tumulus,” she said softly. “It’s Aren’s tumulus, which means…” “That’s where Revolute is buried,” Anna finished with a nod. “Exactly.” “Way to go, Anna!” Kristoff said. “You solved it!” “Thanks!” She flashed him a smile. “This means we have to go back to the castle,” Anna said, looking up at the Hulder, who stood there tall and impassive as they spoke. “And we need to get there as soon as possible!
paras.zh: 而那就是龙船所在！”艾莎惊讶地掩住嘴。“是陵冢，”她轻声说，“那是阿伦的陵冢，也就是说……”“回旋之刃就葬在那里，”安娜点头接了下去，“没错。”“干得漂亮，安娜！”克里斯托夫说，“你解开了谜题！”“谢谢！”她朝他粲然一笑。“这意味着我们得回城堡去，”安娜抬头看着那名岩精说，对方正高高地站着，面无表情地听他们说话，“而且我们得尽快赶到！

paras.en: Elsa, can you…” Anna twirled her finger. “ Magic?
paras.zh: 艾莎，你能……”安娜指尖一转，“用魔法？

paras.en: But it’ll draw the Nattmara right to us,” Elsa said.
paras.zh: 可那会把纳特玛拉直接引到我们这儿，”艾莎说。

paras.en: Obscuren chimed in. “If you wanted to use your magic without the Nattmara sensing it, I think it would need to be now.” Elsa nodded.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦插话道：“如果你们想用魔法又不让纳特玛拉察觉，我想就得趁现在。”艾莎点了点头。

paras.en: In the safety of the turf house, she crafted a sleigh of ice—ice so clear that Anna could see right through it.
paras.zh: 在草皮屋的安全之中，她造出一辆冰橇——冰清透得让安娜能一眼看穿。

paras.en: It was practically invisible.
paras.zh: 它几乎隐形。

paras.en: And then Anna felt a whoosh of cold air blow by her, and she shivered as snowflakes danced in the air, shaping themselves into a massive snow bear, who loomed much too large in the tiny turf house. “Elsa,” Anna said, taking in the snow bear with wonder, “he’s beautiful.” The bear growled. “He says his name is Bjorn,” Obscuren translated. “I can hear my reindeer, Sven, talk, too,” Kristoff said to the Hulder.
paras.zh: 接着安娜感到一阵冷风掠过，她打了个寒颤，只见雪花在空中飞舞，渐渐塑成一只巨大的雪熊，在狭小的草皮屋里显得过于庞大。“艾莎，”安娜惊赞地望着雪熊说，“他真美。”雪熊低吼一声。“他说他叫比约恩，”奥布斯科伦翻译道。“我也能听懂我的驯鹿斯文说话，”克里斯托夫对岩精说。

paras.en: His voice sounded glum, and Anna knew he was still worried about his best friend.
paras.zh: 他的声音听来闷闷不乐，安娜知道他还在担心最好的朋友。

paras.en: She hoped Sven was all right, and, at the very least, safe on the royal ship.
paras.zh: 她希望斯文安然无恙，至少，已在皇家船只上平安无事。

paras.en: Obscuren rested a hand on Kristoff’s arm and flashed a sad smile. “The Huldrefólk are known for finding things that are lost, because we know how to listen,” she said. “But we’re not the only beings who listen.
paras.zh: 奥布斯科伦把手搭在克里斯托夫臂上，露出一抹忧伤的微笑。“岩精以寻回失物闻名，因为我们懂得倾听，”她说，“但我们并非唯一会倾听的生灵。

paras.en: Animals can, too.
paras.zh: 动物也能。

paras.en: They can tell a kind heart from one filled with cruelty.
paras.zh: 它们能分辨出善良的心与残忍的心。

paras.en: And I suspect, Kristoff, that you’re someone who knows exactly what Sven is saying to you.” Kristoff shook his head. “I just hope he’s okay.” “If we leave right now, he will be,” Anna said, trying to say it with so much confidence that it would just have to be true.
paras.zh: 而我猜，克里斯托夫，你正是那个完全懂得斯文在对你说什么的人。”克里斯托夫摇了摇头。“我只希望他没事。”“如果我们现在就出发，他会没事的，”安娜说，用十足的把握说出这话，仿佛这样就必定成真。

paras.en: As quickly as they could, they buckled the snow bear up to the sleigh, and then said their farewells to Obscuren. “In my family,” the Hulder said, “we don’t say goodbye.” “What do you say, then?” Anna asked. “We say, ‘Till we see you again.’” Anna smiled. “Till we see you again.” “Maybe,” Obscuren said, already disappearing behind a stack of lost and broken plates. “But I’ll probably see you first.
paras.zh: 他们尽快给雪熊套上冰橇，然后向奥布斯科伦道别。“在我们族里，”岩精说，“我们不说再见。”“那你们说什么？”安娜问。“我们说，‘后会有期’。”安娜笑了。“后会有期。”“也许吧，”奥布斯科伦说，人已隐没在一摞失落又破碎的盘子后面，“不过大概率是我先看见你们。

paras.en: Unless you look very, very closely.” Obscuren reached out an arm and cracked open the door.
paras.zh: 除非你们看得非常、非常仔细。”奥布斯科伦伸出手臂，吱呀一声推开门。

paras.en: There was a second while the Hulder took in the land, and then she flung the door open wide for the bear and the sled. “Remember,” the Hulder called as they slipped from the safety of the turf house and slid out under the sky. “Home is where the heart is.
paras.zh: 岩精打量了大地片刻，随即把门彻底敞开，让雪熊和雪橇出去。“记住，”他们从草皮屋的安全中溜出、滑向天空之下时，岩精喊道，“心在处便是家。

paras.en: Good luck, friends of Arendelle.” “Goodbye, friend,” Anna said.
paras.zh: 祝好运，阿伦黛尔的朋友们。”“再见，朋友，”安娜说。

paras.en: But Obscuren was gone.
paras.zh: 但奥布斯科伦已经不见了。

paras.en: As Bjorn loped away from the turf house, home did not look like home anymore.
paras.zh: 当比约恩大步离开草皮屋时，家园已不再是原来的模样。

paras.en: Anna saw a haze had settled over Arendelle as color drained from the world.
paras.zh: 安娜看见一层阴霾笼罩阿伦黛尔，世界的颜色正在褪去。

paras.en: It was as though the earth itself were afraid, turning pale with fear.
paras.zh: 仿佛大地自己也害怕了，吓得脸色苍白。

paras.en: Anna held out her hand, studying it in the sunlight.
paras.zh: 安娜伸出手，在阳光下端详。

paras.en: It still looked pink in the cold.
paras.zh: 在冷意中，它仍显得粉粉的。

paras.en: Glancing at Elsa, Anna was comforted by the fact that her mother’s scarf, wrapped around Elsa’s shoulders, was still burgundy, while Kristoff’s hair was still the color of wheat.
paras.zh: 瞥了眼艾莎，安娜感到安慰：母亲那圈围在艾莎肩上的围巾仍是酒红色，而克里斯托夫的头发仍是麦子的颜色。

paras.en: The color that wheat was supposed to be, Anna corrected herself.
paras.zh: 是小麦本该有的颜色，安娜纠正自己。

paras.en: But there was still time before sunset.
paras.zh: 但离日落还有时间。

paras.en: There was still time to remedy this all. “It looks like the forest after a fire,” Kristoff said, glancing at the terrain as he guided the snow bear around a bend with a careful tug of the reins. “What do you mean?” Elsa asked. “The way the ash drifts,” Kristoff explained. “It floats on the air instead of falling.” “Maybe,” Anna said, trying to force cheer into her words, “that’s a good thing.
paras.zh: 还有时间扭转这一切。“这看起来像火灾后的森林，”克里斯托夫一边说，一边小心地一勒缰绳，引着雪熊绕过一道弯。“什么意思？”艾莎问。“灰烬飘移的样子，”克里斯托夫解释，“它是浮在空气里，而不是落下来。”“也许，”安娜说，努力让语气欢快些，“这是件好事。

paras.en: I read in the library that forest fires are necessary to clear the bramble and make way for new life.” Kristoff shook his head. “Tell that to the people who’ve lost their homes.” He jounced the reins, and the sleigh went faster.
paras.zh: 我在图书馆读到过，林火是清除荆棘、为新生命开路所必需的。”克里斯托夫摇摇头。“去跟那些失去家园的人说这话吧。”他抖了抖缰绳，雪橇更快了。

paras.en: Anna held a spyglass of ice from Elsa up to her eye, scanning the horizon for any sign of the Nattmara.
paras.zh: 安娜举起艾莎用冰做的望远镜凑到眼前，扫视地平线，寻找纳特玛拉的任何踪迹。

paras.en: So far, so good.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，一切尚好。

paras.en: There was no sign of the wolf.
paras.zh: 没有那头狼的影子。

paras.en: Well, no signs other than this pale shadow of their home and the fearful thump of Anna’s own heart.
paras.zh: 嗯，除了家园这惨淡的阴影，以及安娜自己那颗恐惧乱跳的心。

paras.en: Except, what was that?
paras.zh: 不过，那是什么？

paras.en: A dark smudge seemed to move from the washed-out green of the spruces. “Elsa,” Anna whispered, and slipped the spyglass back to her sister. “Something’s moving.
paras.zh: 一团黑斑似乎从褪了色的云杉绿中移动。“艾莎，”安娜低语，把望远镜递回妹妹，“有东西在动。

paras.en: Over there.” Elsa peered over her shoulder, then looked ahead again. “You’re right,” she said. “I think it’s following us.” Kristoff snapped the reins harder and Bjorn veered right, sending a swirl of pale white leaves into the air.
paras.zh: 在那边。”艾莎扭头望了望，又看向前方。“你说得对，”她说，“我觉得它在跟着我们。”克里斯托夫猛地一甩缰绳，比约恩向右一转，卷起一团惨白的叶子飞上空中。

paras.en: Anna looked back.
paras.zh: 安娜回头望去。

paras.en: The smudge also veered right.
paras.zh: 那团黑斑也向右转了。

paras.en: Yes.
paras.zh: 没错。

paras.en: Whatever it was, it was definitely following them.
paras.zh: 不管那是什么，它确实在尾随他们。

paras.en: Bjorn’s ears swiveled, and then Anna heard it.
paras.zh: 比约恩的耳朵转了转，接着安娜听见了。

paras.en: A cry: Ahhhhhhhh!
paras.zh: 一声喊：啊————！

paras.en: It seemed to come from the direction of the smudge.
paras.zh: 它似乎来自那团黑斑的方向。

paras.en: And it wasn’t the bone-cold howl of the Nattmara.
paras.zh: 而且那不是纳特玛拉骨寒般的嚎叫。

paras.en: This noise sounded almost human, as though someone were trying to call out a name.
paras.zh: 这声音几乎像人声，仿佛有人在竭力喊出一个名字。

paras.en: In fact… Ahhhhhh!
Naaaaaaaa! “Stop!” Anna lurched upright. “It’s Sorenson!” Elsa gasped. “What?” Kristoff pulled the reins, flinging Anna into Elsa as they sped back to the scientist.
paras.zh: 娜————娜！“停下！”安娜猛地挺身。“是索伦森！”艾莎倒吸一口气。“什么？”克里斯托夫一拉缰绳，雪橇掉头冲向那位学者，把安娜甩进艾莎怀里。

paras.en: As they got closer, the cry became clearer. “Annaaaa!
paras.zh: 靠近后，那喊声更清楚了。“安————娜！

paras.en: Elsaaaaa!” “Sorenson!” Anna shouted, relieved he was okay.
paras.zh: 艾————莎！”“索伦森！”安娜喊道，为他安然无恙而松了口气。

paras.en: Or was he?
paras.zh: 可他真的没事吗？

paras.en: The scientist looked the worse for wear.
paras.zh: 这位学者看上去狼狈不堪。

paras.en: His coat was torn, shredded by the Nattmara’s claws, and he limped, his ankle swollen.
paras.zh: 他的外套被撕破了，是纳特玛拉的爪子扯的，他一瘸一拐，脚踝肿着。

paras.en: But he was alive, and not only that, his eyes didn’t appear to be either pitch black or yellow. “Stop the sleigh!” Anna said, and Kristoff pulled Bjorn to a walk.
paras.zh: 但他还活着，而且不止如此，他的眼睛既不像全黑，也不像黄色。“停下雪橇！”安娜说，克里斯托夫让比约恩放慢成步子。

paras.en: The snow bear snorted, protesting the change in pace. “Sorenson!” Anna called as she swung out of the sleigh and hurried toward him. “We’re so glad to see you!
paras.zh: 雪熊喷了喷鼻息，对速度变化表示抗议。“索伦森！”安娜边喊边跳下雪橇，朝他快步走去，“见到你我们太高兴了！

paras.en: How did you escape?” “Hello to you, Anna, and to you, Your Majesty,” Sorenson said.
paras.zh: 你是怎么逃出来的？”“向你问好，安娜，也向陛下问好，”索伦森说。

paras.en: He spoke in a strange cadence, as if he had somehow managed to twist his tongue as well as his ankle. “I’ll tell you all about it in a minute.
paras.zh: 他说话节奏古怪，仿佛舌头和脚踝一样不知怎么扭到了。“我待会儿全告诉你们。

paras.en: Just let me catch my breath.” “We don’t really have time,” Elsa said, looking to the sky.
paras.zh: 先让我喘口气。”“我们真没多少时间，”艾莎望着天空说。

paras.en: The sun was definitely low now, approaching dinnertime. “How about you tell us in the sleigh?” He nodded. “That’s a good idea, but we can’t take a sleigh where we need to go.” “And where do we need to go?” Anna asked.
paras.zh: 太阳此刻确实低了，快到晚饭时分。“你在雪橇上跟我们说不行吗？”他点点头。“好主意，可我们要去的地方，雪橇进不去。”“那我们得去哪儿？”安娜问。

paras.en: She stepped over to Kristoff’s traveler’s pack and sifted around for a spare splint.
paras.zh: 她走到克里斯托夫的行囊边，翻找备用的夹板。

paras.en: Aha!
paras.zh: 啊哈！

paras.en: There it was.
paras.zh: 找到了。

paras.en: She knew Kristoff rarely left home without it.
paras.zh: 她知道克里斯托夫出门几乎从不落下它。

paras.en: The splint was for ice mountain emergencies, but Kristoff liked to tease her that he needed to make sure he had one on hand at the castle for the amount of times she’d managed to trip or stumble over something.
paras.zh: 这夹板本是为冰山突发状况备的，可克里斯托夫爱拿她打趣，说她在城堡里绊倒或磕碰的次数那么多，他得确保手边常备一个。

paras.en: Anna sat down and offered the scientist the splint. “How did you escape the Nattmara?” Sorenson said, “I found a thing of myth.” Anna’s eyebrows shot upward. “You found Revolute?” Sorenson tilted his head, and with his long silver beard, he looked a little bit like a confused dog. “Did you figure out where it was hidden?” Anna grinned. “Yes!
paras.zh: 安娜坐下，把夹板递给学者。“你是怎么逃过纳特玛拉的？”索伦森说：“我找到了一件神物。”安娜眉毛一挑。“你找到了回旋之刃？”索伦森偏了偏头，配上他那把长银须，样子有点像只困惑的狗。“你们猜到它藏在哪儿了？”安娜咧嘴一笑。“猜到了！

paras.en: Well, we know where to look.
paras.zh: 嗯，我们知道去哪儿找了。

paras.en: It’s in—” “What did you find, Sorenson?” Elsa asked, stepping in between them.
paras.zh: 它就在——”“你找到了什么，索伦森？”艾莎插到两人中间问。

paras.en: She’d arranged their mother’s scarf around her shoulders like a cape. “Ah, I found a cure,” Sorenson said, and he tapped his fingertips excitedly together. “But it’s hard to explain.
paras.zh: 她把母亲的围巾像披风般搭在肩上。“啊，我找到了解药，”索伦森说，兴奋地指尖相叩，“可这很难解释。

paras.en: I’d rather show it to you first.
paras.zh: 我更想先给你们看。

paras.en: It won’t defeat the Nattmara, but I believe it will clear up the Blight from the animals and the crops.” “What?” Kristoff, who’d been waiting in the sleigh, jumped out. “There’s a cure?
paras.zh: 它灭不了纳特玛拉，但我相信它能清除动物和庄稼上的枯疫。”“什么？”一直在雪橇里等的克里斯托夫跳了下来，“有解药？

paras.en: We can help Sven?” “Allegedly, yes,” Sorenson said. “And the Huldrefólk have it.” “I don’t know about that,” Elsa said, tugging on the fringe of her scarf. “They’re our friends, I think, and they didn’t say anything about having a cure.” “Yes.” Anna nodded. “And they are definitely our friends.” Sorenson’s face crinkled and he shook his head while he sighed. “Whatever they told you is wrong,” he said. “The Huldrefólk are thieves.
paras.zh: 我们能救斯文了？”“据说是的，”索伦森说，“而且岩精就有这东西。”“这我可不知道，”艾莎扯着围巾的流苏说，“他们是我们朋友，我想，而且他们从没提过有解药。”“是啊，”安娜点头，“而且他们绝对是我们的朋友。”索伦森眉头皱起，摇着头叹气。“他们告诉你们的都是错的，”他说，“岩精是贼。

paras.en: You should not have trusted them.” “No,” Anna said, standing up for Echo, the Librarian King, and Obscuren. “They find lost, unwanted things and give them homes.
paras.zh: 你们本不该相信他们。”“不，”安娜说，为埃科、图书管理员国王和奥布斯科伦撑腰，“他们找到失落、被人遗弃的东西，给它们一个家。

paras.en: They find ‘that which is lost,’ like your book says, sir.” But Sorenson kept shaking his head, his long beard waving like one of the windswept pennants on the castle wall.
paras.zh: 他们找的是‘失落的之物’，正如你书里写的，先生。”可索伦森仍摇着头，长须如城堡墙上被风吹动的旌旗般晃动。

paras.en: In the lengthening light, his beard looked more white than silver. “Then my book must be wrong, because the Huldrefólk have a thing of myth hidden in their hot springs, not more than a mile away.
paras.zh: 在渐长的光线里，他的胡须看着更白而非银。“那我的书一定是错的，因为岩精有一件神物藏在他们的温泉里，离这儿不到一英里。

paras.en: I discovered that if a Nattmara-touched animal drinks the water, they will be cured, even if you don’t defeat the Nattmara by sunrise of the third day.” “Let’s go!” Kristoff said, the hope so bright on his face that it hurt Anna to see. “If it’s only a mile, we could get a cup of the water from the hot springs, just in case, and still make it back without losing that much time!” Bjorn’s snuffle was louder now.
paras.zh: 我发现，被纳特玛拉碰过的动物只要喝了那水，就会痊愈，哪怕你们没在第三个日出前打败纳特玛拉。“走吧！”克里斯托夫说，脸上希望之光那么亮，看得安娜心疼。“如果只有一英里，我们大可去温泉取一杯水防身，还能赶回来，耽误不了多少时间！”比约恩的喷鼻声更响了。

paras.en: The bear wanted to move.
paras.zh: 熊想动身。

paras.en: He wanted to go .
paras.zh: 他想走。

paras.en: Yet Anna was torn…until she saw the expression on Kristoff’s face.
paras.zh: 然而安娜陷入了纠结……直到她看见克里斯托夫脸上的神情。

paras.en: Kristoff’s best friend was sick.
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫最好的朋友病了。

paras.en: And he had no way to know what had happened to Sven in the time they’d been gone, but he’d risked his life over and over again just for the chance that he could help make Sven feel better.
paras.zh: 他无从得知他们离开的这段时间斯文发生了什么，可为了能有机会让斯文好起来，他已一次又一次拿命去赌。

paras.en: How could Anna say no to that? “Elsa,” she said, turning from Sorenson, who still nursed his ankle on the splint, and from Kristoff, who looked like he was about to go sprinting in any direction as soon as he heard where these curing springs were. “I think we should get the water, as a precaution.” Again, Elsa looked at the sky and bit her lip.
paras.zh: 安娜怎么忍心拒绝？“艾莎，”她说，转过身，不再看仍用夹板护着脚踝的索伦森，也不看克里斯托夫——一听治愈温泉在哪儿，他简直要往任意方向冲刺了，“我想我们应该去取水，以防万一。”艾莎又望向天空，咬住嘴唇。

paras.en: As Anna saw her sister take a deep breath, she knew she wasn’t going to like whatever she was about to hear. “We can’t risk it,” Elsa said, still keeping her gaze on the sky, and on the floating bits of ash that looked like snow but weren’t. “I’m so sorry, Kristoff, but we can’t.
paras.zh: 安娜看见妹妹深吸一口气，便知道自己不会喜欢接下来听到的话。“我们不能冒这个险，”艾莎说，目光仍停留在天空，停留在那些看似雪却不是雪的浮灰上，“非常抱歉，克里斯托夫，但我们不行。

paras.en: Even if the spring water does work, there’s no way we can bring back enough for everyone in all the kingdom…and what about the sword?” The look on Kristoff’s face was unbearable. “So now you think the sword is real?” “Elsa!” Anna said, looking between her sister and the man she loved. “I understand your responsibility to the kingdom,” Kristoff told Elsa, “but Sven is family to me.” “Kristoff,” Elsa cut in, and her eyes were wide with hurt, though Anna didn’t know why her sister would be upset. “I’m saying no because it endangers too many people!” Anna took a deep breath, ready to argue more, when Bjorn let out a great bellow.
paras.zh: 就算泉水真有效，我们也带不回够全王国每个人用的量……那剑又怎么办？”克里斯托夫脸上的神情令人不忍。“所以你现在相信那把剑是真的了？”“艾莎！”安娜说，目光在妹妹与她所爱的人之间游移。“我理解你对王国的责任，”克里斯托夫对艾莎说，“但斯文是我的家人。”“克里斯托夫，”艾莎打断他，眼里满是受伤，尽管安娜不懂妹妹为何心烦，“我说不行，是因为这会危及太多人！”安娜深吸一口气，正要再争，比约恩却发出一声巨吼。

paras.en: Whirling around, she turned to see that Sorenson had taken Kristoff’s pickax from the sleigh and was trying to yank the bear out of his harness. “Sorenson?” Anna said, forgetting her frustration with Elsa as she took in the man’s peculiar actions. “What are you doing?” “Nothing, nothing,” Sorenson said, reaching down to fiddle with a buckle.
paras.zh: 她猛地转身，看见索伦森从雪橇上拿走了克里斯托夫的镐，正想把熊从挽具里拽出来。“索伦森？”安娜说，顾不上对艾莎的恼火，盯着这人怪异的举动，“你在干什么？”“没什么，没什么，”索伦森说着，弯腰去摆弄一个扣环。

paras.en: But as he bent down, Anna noticed something falling from his pocket.
paras.zh: 可他弯腰时，安娜注意到有东西从他口袋里掉了出来。

paras.en: If the world had been its normal color—dark emerald hues mixed with the rich blue of the mountains and the oncoming colors of fall—she would never have noticed it.
paras.zh: 若世界还是平常的色彩——深翠绿混着群山浓郁的蓝，以及渐近的秋色——她绝不会注意到它。

paras.en: But the world had turned ashy white, so what tumbled from Sorenson’s pocket stood out like a stain.
paras.zh: 可世界已变成灰白，于是从索伦森口袋里滚落的东西，醒目得像一块污迹。

paras.en: It was sand.
paras.zh: 那是沙。

paras.en: Black sand.
paras.zh: 黑沙。

paras.en: “NATT—NATT,” ANNA SPUTTERED, trying to get the warning out.
paras.zh: “纳特——纳特，”安娜结巴着，想把警告喊出口。

paras.en: But it was too late.
paras.zh: 可已经太迟了。

paras.en: Already, as she watched, sand swirled from out of Sorenson’s eyes to reveal not dark brown irises as Anna had thought, but eyes the color of a hornet’s jacket.
paras.zh: 就在她注视之时，沙子从索伦森的眼中旋涌而出，露出的不是安娜原以为的深棕色虹膜，而是如马蜂甲壳般的眼睛。

paras.en: And then the sand swirled into Sorenson’s heart.
paras.zh: 接着，沙子旋入索伦森的心口。

paras.en: A place for the Nattmara to roost until the sunset.
paras.zh: 那是纳特玛拉栖身之处，直到日落。

paras.en: Trolls tremble at the Nattmara’s howl while the Nattmara flees from the sun like a shadow.
paras.zh: 地精在纳特玛拉的嚎叫中战栗，而纳特玛拉却如影子般逃离阳光。

paras.en: But nightmares could still hurt, even in the day. “Nattmara!” Anna finally bellowed, and it was as if her shout had broken some strange enchantment.
paras.zh: 但噩梦即便在白天也能伤人。“纳特玛拉！”安娜终于吼出声，仿佛这一吼打破了某种奇怪的魔咒。

paras.en: A moment ago, she’d felt utterly suspended outside of herself, and now she was moving faster than she could think. “Run!” But Kristoff and Elsa had already seen what Anna had not been able to say.
paras.zh: 片刻前，她还觉得自己完全抽离在身体之外，此刻却动得比思考还快。“快跑！”可克里斯托夫和艾莎早已看懂了安娜没能说出口的事。

paras.en: Kristoff took a running leap for the driver’s seat of the sleigh while Elsa grabbed Anna’s hand and pulled her safely inside. “Mush!” Kristoff shouted, and Bjorn, already deeply unhappy about the break from the run and nervous around the man who did not smell quite right to him, shot off. “Go!
paras.zh: 克里斯托夫一个助跑跳上雪橇的驭手座，艾莎则抓住安娜的手把她拉进橇里。“驾！”克里斯托夫喊，比约恩本就因被迫停下而不快，又对那气味不对的男人感到不安，顿时窜了出去。“走！

paras.en: Go!
paras.zh: 走！

paras.en: Go!” Anna yelled when she was able to make her mouth move again.
paras.zh: 走！”等嘴巴又能动时，安娜喊道。

paras.en: She twisted around just in time to see Sorenson bare his teeth, and then he reached into his coat pocket and pulled out a glittering vial of violet powder—the Highly Flammable and Very Dangerous Combustion Powder.
paras.zh: 她扭身回头，正看见索伦森龇出牙，接着把手伸进外套口袋，掏出一个闪亮的小瓶，里面是紫色的粉末——高度易燃且极度危险的燃烧粉。

paras.en: The scientist, now the Nattmara’s puppet, raised the vial high into the air. “FASTER!” Anna cried, just as an explosion fell short of them, barely missing the sleigh.
paras.zh: 这位学者如今是纳特玛拉的傀儡，将小瓶高高举起。“再快！”安娜喊道，就在此刻一声爆炸落在他们身后不远处，险些击中雪橇。

paras.en: They careened out of control, the ride far from smooth as it was still early fall, and the ground was only just hard enough for the sleigh’s runners to work.
